18.x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: Sankalia held that rice was first harvested in AP in the Iron Age (Megalithic) era.

18.s: The Upanishadic thinkers criticised which tendency of Later Vedic religion?
18.x: Later Vedic worship became centred on elaborate rituals, which prompted the Upanishadic critique.
xa: The Upanishads (**c. 800-600 BCE**) dealt with **Atman, Brahman, Karma, Moksha**.
**Prajapati** became the supreme god.

18.s: Which Later Vedic god of animals later merged with Shiva?
18.x: Rudra, god of animals, later merged with Shiva.

18.s:
Match List-I (Later Vedic god) with List-II (Position):
List-I | List-II
a. Prajapati | i. Rose as preserver
b. Vishnu | ii. Creator; became supreme
c. Rudra | iii. Cattle god; god of the Shudras
d. Pushan | iv. God of animals, later merged with Shiva
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
18.x: Prajapati – creator, became supreme; Vishnu – rose as preserver (minor in the Rigveda); Rudra – god of animals, later merged with Shiva; Pushan – cattle god, god of the Shudras. Indra, Agni and Varuna lost importance.

18.s:
Match List-I (Priest) with List-II (Veda / role):
List-I | List-II
a. Hotri | i. Chanted the Samaveda
b. Adhvaryu | ii. Atharvaveda; supervised
c. Udgatri | iii. Yajurveda; practical, manual work of the sacrifice
d. Brahman | iv. Recited the Rigveda
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
18.x: Hotri – recited the Rigveda; Adhvaryu – Yajurveda, did the manual work; Udgatri – chanted the Samaveda; Brahman – Atharvaveda, supervised the sacrifice.

19.s: King Asvapati of the Upanishadic period was the ruler of:
19.x: Ashvapati, a Kshatriya scholar-king of the Upanishads who taught Brahmins, ruled Kekaya; Janaka ruled Videha, Pravahana Jaivali Panchala and Ajatashatru Kashi.

19.s: Which development contributed to the emergence of the Mahajanapadas?
o: The exclusive expansion of Kuru power into the Deccan
The rise of Kosala, Kashi and Videha in the east after Kuru–Panchala dominance in the upper Ganga valley
The replacement of agriculture by maritime trade in North India
The disappearance of all territorial kingdoms in favour of tribal units
19.x: The Kuru–Panchala alliance dominated the upper Ganga valley, while Kosala, Kashi and Videha rose in the east. This political development contributed to the emergence of the Mahajanapadas.
19.tq: Connect regional political change with the larger process of state formation.
xs: The **rise of Kosala, Kashi and Videha in the east** after **Kuru–Panchala** dominance led towards the Mahajanapadas — option **(2)**.
Kuru-Panchala held the **upper Ganga valley** through marriage and military links.
xa: The shift to **hereditary territorial monarchy** prepared the way for the **Mahajanapadas** of the **6th century BCE**.
**Videha** lay beyond the **Sadanira/Gandak**.

19.s:
Match List-I (Later Vedic kingdom) with List-II (Association):
List-I | List-II
a. Kuru | i. Hastinapur and Kurukshetra
b. Panchala | ii. Ahichchhatra
c. Videha | iii. Beyond the Sadanira; King Janaka
d. Kashi | iv. Varanasi region
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
19.x: Kuru – Delhi–Meerut / upper Doab (Hastinapur, Kurukshetra); Panchala – middle Doab–Rohilkhand (Ahichchhatra); Videha – north Bihar beyond the Sadanira (Gandak), King Janaka; Kashi – Varanasi region.

19.s:
Match List-I (Upanishadic scholar-king) with List-II (Kingdom):
List-I | List-II
a. Janaka | i. Kashi
b. Ashvapati | ii. Kekaya
c. Ajatashatru | iii. Videha
d. Pravahana Jaivali | iv. Panchala
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
19.x: Janaka – Videha; Ashvapati – Kekaya; Ajatashatru – Kashi (not the Magadha king); Pravahana Jaivali – Panchala. These Kshatriya kings taught Brahmins.

19.s: Which of the following was not a type of sacrifice performed by kings in ancient India to establish their position?
19.x: Rajasuya, Ashvamedha and Vajapeya were the royal sacrifices by which kings asserted their position; Muvendavelan is a Chola-period title, not a sacrifice.

19.s: Over whom did the Ashvamedha sacrifice proclaim the king's supremacy?
19.x: Ashvamedha asserted supremacy over other kings; the Vajapeya chariot race was over kinsmen.

19.s:
Match List-I (Later Vedic royal sacrifice) with List-II (Feature):
List-I | List-II
a. Rajasuya | i. Horse sacrifice; supremacy over other kings
b. Ashvamedha | ii. 'Drink of strength'; chariot race won over kinsmen
c. Vajapeya | iii. Second anointing at the end of the Rajasuya
d. Punarabhisheka | iv. Royal consecration conferring supreme power
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
19.x: Rajasuya – royal consecration (includes the Ratnahavimshi); Ashvamedha – horse sacrifice, supremacy over other kings and the area the horse roamed; Vajapeya – 'drink of strength', chariot race won over kinsmen; Punarabhisheka – second anointing at the end of the Rajasuya.

19.s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Large Shrauta sacrifices strengthened the position of the Brahmanas in the Later Vedic period.
Reason (R): Such sacrifices needed many priests and heavy dakshina, up to 2,40,000 cows in a Rajasuya.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
19.x: Both are true and R explains A: the elaborate Shrauta rites required many priests and enormous dakshina, which raised the power of the Brahmanas.

19.s:
Consider the following statements about Vedic royal sacrifices in Andhra:
1. The Satavahanas, Ikshvakus and Vishnukundins performed these rites.
2. Among the Ikshvakus, the Vajapeya brought the title Swarat.
3. An Ashvamedha altar has been found at Nagarjunakonda.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
19.x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: among the Ikshvakus the Vajapeya brought the title Samrat/Virat; the Ashvamedha brought Swarat.

19.s: The post-Vedic period tax was collected by king from people was called
19.x: In the Later Vedic period bali, earlier a voluntary gift, became an obligatory tribute collected by the king. Varman is armour and Vidatha an assembly that vanished.

19.s:
Consider the following statements about Later Vedic taxation:
1. Bhagadugha was the revenue collector.
2. Sangrahitri was the treasurer who managed the revenue.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
19.x: Bhagadugha collected the revenue and Sangrahitri, the treasurer, managed it. Vaishyas were the main tribute-payers.
xa: **Vaishyas** = main tribute-payers.
Taxes: **Bali, Bhaga, Shulka**.

19.s:
Consider the following statements about Later Vedic assemblies:
1. The Vidatha disappeared.
2. The Sabha and Samiti continued under chiefs, Brahmanas and rich nobles.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
19.x: The Vidatha vanished, while the Sabha and Samiti survived under chiefs, Brahmanas and nobles.

19.s:
Consider the following statements about Later Vedic taxes:
1. Bali, voluntary in the Rigveda, became a regular and compulsory tax.
2. Bhaga was the king's share of the produce, usually one-sixth.
3. Shulka was a land tax paid by the Brahmanas.
4. The Vaishyas were the main tribute-payers.
How many of the above statements are correct?
19.x: 1, 2 and 4 are correct. 3 is wrong: shulka meant customs / tolls; the Vaishyas were the main (only) tribute-payers.

19.s: What did Later Vedic society become, in contrast to the tribe-based Early Vedic society?
o: Urban and based on coined money
Territory-based with agriculture and compulsory taxes
19.x: The Early Vedic phase meant tribe, cattle and voluntary bali; the Later Vedic phase meant territory, agriculture and compulsory taxes.
xa: Later Vedic crops: rice (**vrihi**) and **wheat**.
Compulsory taxes: **Bali, Bhaga** (**1/6**), **Shulka**.
Collector = **Bhagadugha**.

19.s: The change from tribal chiefdom to hereditary territorial monarchy in the Later Vedic period prepared the way for which of the following in the 6th century BCE?
19.x: The shift to hereditary territorial monarchy during the Later Vedic period prepared the political ground for the rise of the Mahajanapadas in the 6th century BCE.
19.tq: Directly connect the major political transition with its historical consequence.
xs: The shift to **hereditary territorial monarchy** prepared the way for the **Mahajanapadas** of the **6th century BCE** — option **(3)**.
**Kosala, Kashi, Videha** rose in the east, leading to the Mahajanapadas.
xa: Shift: **jana** → **janapada**.
**Kuru-Panchala** dominated the upper Ganga valley.

19.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the state forms named in the Aitareya Brahmana?
19.x: The Aitareya Brahmana names Rajya, Bhojya, Swarajya, Vairajya and Samrajya. Ganatantra is not included in this list.
19.tq: Compare the option directly against the complete named list and avoid importing a later political term.
xs: **Ganatantra** is not in the Aitareya list — option **(4)**.
The forms are **Rajya, Bhojya, Swarajya, Vairajya, Samrajya**, by region.
xa: ⚠ East = **Samrat**; North = **Virat**; West = **Svarat**; South = **Bhoja**.
Middle country = **Raja** (hereditary Kshatriya).
**Ekarat** = sole/paramount ruler.

19.s:
Consider the following statements about the Shatapatha Brahmana's theory of kingship:
1. It linked the king with Prajapati.
2. It regarded the Rajasuya and Vajapeya as giving the king divine qualities.
3. It traced kingship exclusively to election by village assemblies.
Which of the above statements are correct?
19.x: The Shatapatha Brahmana linked the king to Prajapati and saw the Rajasuya and Vajapeya as conferring divine qualities; it did not trace kingship to village election.
xa: The **Aitareya** gives the war-leader origin of kingship.
The **Brahmanas' ritual monopoly** supported royal legitimacy.

19.s: Which of the following belongs to the Later Vedic polity rather than the Early Vedic polity?
19.x: Ratnins were part of the Later Vedic polity; an elective chief, voluntary bali and strong assemblies marked the Early Vedic polity.
xa: **Vidatha disappeared** in the Later Vedic period.
Ratnins were honoured in the **Ratnahavimshi** rite.

19.s:
Consider the following statements about Later Vedic kingship:
1. The word rashtra first appears in the Later Vedic texts.
2. Kingship was hereditary, usually passing to the eldest son.
3. Ekarat in the Aitareya Brahmana means a ruler elected by the Samiti.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
19.x: 1 and 2 are correct (traces of election survived). 3 is wrong: Ekarat (Atharvaveda, Aitareya Brahmana) means the sole / paramount ruler.

19.s:
Match List-I (Region, as in the Aitareya Brahmana) with List-II (Ruler's title):
List-I | List-II
a. East | i. Svarat
b. South | ii. Virat
c. West | iii. Samrat
d. North | iv. Bhoja
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
19.x: East – Samrat; South – Bhoja; West – Svarat; North – Virat.

19.s:
Consider the following statements about the origin of kingship in the Later Vedic texts:
1. The Aitareya Brahmana gives the earliest account: the gods, losing to the Asuras, chose a king to lead them.
2. The Aitareya Brahmana regards the king as the protector of Brahmins.
3. The Taittiriya Brahmana traces kingship to election by village assemblies.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
19.x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: the Taittiriya Brahmana gives the theory of the divine origin of kingship; kingship was not traced to election by village assemblies.

19.s: Which one of the following officials was responsible for collecting the king’s share of revenue?
19.x: Bhagadugha was the revenue or tax collector who collected the king’s share. Sangrahitri was the treasurer, Akshavapa the accountant and superintendent of dice, and Palagala the messenger.
19.tq: Apply the ‘who would do this job?’ method to distinguish related officials.
xs: The **Bhagadugha** collected the **king's share** of revenue — option **(3)**.
**Sangrahitri** = treasurer; **Akshavapa** = accountant / superintendent of dice; **Palagala** = messenger.
xa: Exam angle: Bhagadugha = **revenue collector** (**UPPSC 2023**).
⚠ Older notes say the **Sangrahitri** collected taxes.
**Bhaga** = king's share, **1/6** of produce.

19.s: Which of the following Ratnin – office pairs is NOT correctly matched?
19.x: Bhagadugha was the revenue collector; the treasurer was the Sangrahitri.

19.s:
Consider the following statements about the Later Vedic Ratnins:
1. They formed the king's council of 12 royal functionaries.
2. They were honoured in the Ratnahavimshi rite of the Rajasuya.
3. With them the Later Vedic king maintained a standing army.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
19.x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: there were more officers but no regular bureaucracy and no standing army.

19.s:
Match List-I (Ratnin) with List-II (Function):
List-I | List-II
a. Senani | i. Charioteer and herald
b. Suta | ii. Accountant; superintendent of dice
c. Sangrahitri | iii. Army chief
d. Akshavapa | iv. Treasurer
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
19.x: Senani – army chief; Suta – charioteer and herald; Sangrahitri – treasurer; Akshavapa – accountant and superintendent of dice. (Bhagadugha collects, Sangrahitri stores.)

20.s: Describing social stratification using the order of Brahmin, Kshatriya, Vaishya, Shudra is called
20.x: Ordering society as Brahmana, Kshatriya, Vaishya, Shudra is the varna system; caste (jati) is the later, multiple birth groups.

20.s: In ancient period, which Varna was also called as ‘Sarthavaha’?
20.x: Sarthavaha (Srenipramukh) was the head of a merchant guild or caravan, so the term belongs to the trading Vaishya varna; guild rules were called Samay and Srenidharma.

20.s: In which phase, the concept of untouchability was put clearly?
20.x: The Chhandogya Upanishad only calls the Chandala a person of despised birth; untouchability took definite shape in the Dharmashastra phase (early Christian era), not in the Rigvedic or Later Vedic phase.

20.s: On what did varna increasingly come to be based in the Later Vedic period?
20.x: Varna became increasingly birth-based in the Later Vedic period, and gotra exogamy became important.
xa: Rig Vedic society was **relatively fluid and egalitarian**.
**Harappan** society had differentiation but **no textual caste**.
In Rig Vedic times women attended the **Sabha**.

20.s: Varnashrama Dharma combines the varna system with which of the following?
20.x: Varnashrama Dharma denotes the combined framework of varna and Ashrama.
xa: It became the **normative frame** of later Hindu society.
AP angle: **Gautamiputra Satakarni** protected varnashrama dharma and opposed **varna-sankara**.

20.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Shudra in Later Vedic society?
o: Was called 'servant of another' in the Aitareya Brahmana
20.x: The dvija were the upper three varnas; Shudras had no upanayana and no Vedas.

20.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Chhandogya Upanishad refers to the Chandala as a person of despised birth.
2. Untouchability took a formal shape already in the Rigvedic period.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
20.x: Statement 1 is true. Formal untouchability belongs to the post-Vedic Dharmasutra and Dharmashastra phase, not the Rigvedic period.

20.s:
Consider the following statements about Later Vedic society:
1. The first statement of the four varnas is found in the Purusha Sukta of the Tenth Mandala of the Rigveda.
2. The Aitareya Brahmana describes the Shudra as 'a servant of another' who could be expelled or beaten at will.
3. The Vratyas and Nishadas were counted among the Dvija, the twice-born.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
20.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct as per the notes. Statement 3 is wrong: the Vratyas and Nishadas stood outside the varna order; the Dvija were the upper three varnas entitled to upanayana.

20.s:
Consider the following statements about guilds and money-lending in the Vedic age:
1. The rules of the guilds were called Samay and Srenidharma.
2. The Vaishya guilds (gana) were headed by a Gramani.
3. The first reference to money-lending is found in the Shatapatha Brahmana, which calls the usurer kusidin.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
20.x: Statement 2 is wrong: Vaishya guilds (gana) were headed by a Shreshthin, not a Gramani. Statements 1 and 3 are correct: guild rules were Samay/Srenidharma, and the Shatapatha Brahmana gives the first reference to money-lending (usurer = kusidin).

20.s:
Match the varnas of Later Vedic society with their roles:
List-I (Varna)
a. Brahmana
b. Kshatriya (Rajanya)
c. Vaishya
d. Shudra
List-II (Role)
i. Rulers and warriors
ii. Priests and teachers; the most powerful
iii. Service; no upanayana, no Vedas, no Sabha
iv. Farmers, herders, traders, artisans; the only tribute-payers
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
20.x: Brahmana = priests/teachers and most powerful; Kshatriya (also Rajanya) = rulers/warriors; Vaishya = farmers, herders, traders, artisans and the only tribute-payers; Shudra = service, with no upanayana, Vedas or Sabha.

20.s: Which of the followings customs emerged during the post-Vedic period :
20.x: The four ashramas (Brahmacharya, Grihastha, Vanaprastha, Sannyasa) emerged in the post-Vedic period; the four varnas already appear in the Rigveda's Purusha Sukta, and Indra, Surya, Rudra, Maruts are Rigvedic gods. (UPSC 1994 key: ashramas)

20.s: Which of the following custom emerged during the post-Vedic period?
o: Brahmacharya, Grihastha ashrama, Vanaprastha and Sannyasa
20.x: The full set of four ashramas emerged only in the post-Vedic period (first three in the Chhandogya, all four in the Jabala Upanishad / early Dharmasutras); the four varnas appear in the Rigveda's Purusha Sukta and the gods named are Rigvedic.

20.s: How many Ashrams are described in Vedas?
20.x: Four ashramas are described: Brahmacharya, Grihastha, Vanaprastha and Sannyasa.

20.s: Which ashrama involved gradual withdrawal from worldly life?
20.x: Vanaprastha was gradual withdrawal; Brahmacharya was Vedic study, Grihastha household life and Sannyasa complete detachment.
xa: The **Grihastha** performs the **Pancha Mahayajnas**.
Sannyasa was **added later**.
Women followed the ashrama chosen by their **husbands**.

20.s: For whom among the following were the Pancha Mahayajnas daily duties?
20.x: The Pancha Mahayajnas were daily duties of the Grihastha, or householder, Ashrama.
20.tq: Apply the social-role clue: regular family and ritual obligations belong to the householder.
xs: The **Pancha Mahayajnas** were daily duties of the **Grihastha** (householder) — option **(3)**.
Exam: **MPPSC 2025**.
xa: The five: **Brahma** (Vedic study), **Deva** (gods), **Pitri** (ancestors), **Bhuta** (living beings), **Nri/Manushya** (guests).
Grihastha duties: **marriage, family, economic** duties.

20.s:
Consider the following statements about the ashramas:
1. The first three ashramas are referred to in the Chhandogya Upanishad.
2. All four ashramas are first mentioned in the Jabala Upanishad.
3. Sannyasa was the first of the four ashramas to be established.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
20.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Sannyasa (complete renunciation) was added last; only the first three were established in Later Vedic times.

20.s:
Match the Pancha Mahayajnas with what they were meant for:
List-I (Yajna)
a. Brahma-yajna
b. Deva-yajna
c. Pitri-yajna
d. Nri (Atithi)-yajna
List-II (Meant for)
i. Hospitality to guests
ii. Study of the Vedas
iii. Duties towards the ancestors
iv. Offerings to the gods
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
20.x: Brahma = Vedic study; Deva = gods; Pitri = ancestors; Nri/Atithi = hospitality to guests (Bhuta-yajna is for living beings).

20.s:
Assertion (A): Moksha was one of the original trivarga of Purusharthas.
Reason (R): Moksha (liberation) was added to the Purusharthas later, under Upanishadic ideas.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
20.x: A is false: the trivarga was Dharma, Artha and Kama. R is true: Moksha was added later under Upanishadic ideas.

20.s: ‘Gotra’ System came into existance since
20.x: Gotra as a clan descended from a common ancestor appeared in Later Vedic (post-Vedic) times; in the Rigveda the word meant only a cow-pen.

20.s: In the context of ancient Indian society, which one of the following terms does not belong to the category of the other three?
20.x: Kula (family), vamsha (lineage) and gotra (clan) are kinship terms; kosa means treasury, so it is the odd one out.

20.s: In the context of ancient Indian society which one of the following terms does not belong to the category of the other three?
20.x: Vansha, gotra and kula are words of the family system; kosa is the treasury, so it does not belong.

20.s: In which text does the word 'gotra' first appear in the sense of lineage?
20.x: Gotra means cow-pen in the Rigveda; the lineage sense first appears in the Atharvaveda.

20.s:
Consider the following statements about gotra and kinship:
1. The word gotra literally means cow-pen and first occurs in the Rigveda.
2. Gotra exogamy prohibited marriage outside one's own gotra.
3. Irawati Karve's Kinship Organization in India (1953) divided India into four kinship zones.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
20.x: Statement 2 is wrong: gotra exogamy prohibited marriage WITHIN the same gotra. Statements 1 and 3 are correct as per the notes.

20.s: There was a provision for reciting which mantra in the Upanayana ritual of the Kshatriya castes?
20.x: The Grihya Sutras prescribe the Gayatri metre for a Brahmana's upanayana, Trishtubh for a Kshatriya and Jagati for a Vaishya.

20.s: What is the total number of Sanskaras?
20.x: Sixteen (shodasha) samskaras are traditionally counted, three before birth and the last (antyeshti) after death; Rocket lists Sanskaras = 16.

20.s:
Consider the following statements about Upanayana:
1. It was open to Shudras and women.
2. It was the sacred-thread initiation into Vedic study for the upper three varnas.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
20.x: Upanayana was the sacred-thread initiation into Vedic study for Brahmanas, Kshatriyas and Vaishyas; Shudras and women were excluded.
xa: Performed in the boy's **8th year**.
Elaborate description in the **Shatapatha Brahmana**.
It is one of the **16** samskaras.

20.s: Which of the following was true of the pupil in the gurukula system of education?
o: lived separately from the teacher and studied independently
received instruction only from guild heads
20.x: In the gurukula system, pupils lived with the guru. Education was confined largely to the Dvija communities.
20.tq: Test the defining institutional feature of the education system.
xs: In the **gurukula** the pupil **lived with the guru** — option **(1)**.
Education was confined largely to the **Dvija**.
xa: **Brahmacharya** = student stage — Vedic study under a guru.
**Acharya** initiated the pupil and taught **not for a fee**.

20.s:
Consider the following statements about the Upanayana:
1. It was performed in the boy's 8th year.
2. Its full description is found in the Aitareya Brahmana.
3. The metre prescribed for the Upanayana of a Vaishya was the Jagati.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
20.x: Statement 2 is wrong: the full description of the Upanayana is in the Shatapatha Brahmana. Statements 1 (8th year) and 3 (Vaishya = Jagati; Brahmana = Gayatri, Kshatriya = Trishtubh) are correct.

20.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Acharya taught the Veda to pupils for a livelihood.
2. The Upadhyaya taught the Veda and Vedangas for a livelihood.
3. Chudakarma (tonsure) was performed in the child's third year.
How many of the above statements are correct?
20.x: Statement 1 is wrong: the Acharya initiated the pupil and taught the whole Veda free; it was the Upadhyaya who taught for a livelihood (statement 2). Statement 3 is correct: Chudakarma, the tonsure samskara, came in the 3rd year. So two statements are correct.

20.s: What is marriage by purchase called?
20.x: Asura marriage is marriage by purchase: the groom paid a bride price to the girl's family. Arsha involved only a token cow and bull.

20.s: Marriage due to mutual love is called as?
20.x: Gandharva marriage rested on the mutual consent (love) of the two parties; Rakshasa was by capture and Asura by purchase.

20.s: Which Satavahana ruler claimed to have protected varnashrama dharma?
20.x: Gautamiputra Satakarni claimed to have protected varnashrama dharma.
xa: Jati proliferation is **post-Vedic** (Gupta-era diversification).
**Anuloma** offspring = **Ugra**; **pratiloma** = **Chandala**.

20.s: Which one of the following was regarded as the lowest form of marriage in the Dharmashastra classification?
20.x: Paishacha, involving the seduction of a sleeping or intoxicated girl, was regarded as the lowest form of marriage.
20.tq: Use the evaluative description to identify the exceptional form.
xs: **Paishacha** — seduction of a sleeping, intoxicated or incapacitated girl — is the **lowest form** — option **(3)**.
**Daiva, Prajapatya, Arsha** are **approved** forms.
xa: Disapproved forms: **Asura, Gandharva, Rakshasa, Paishacha**.
**Brahma** form: father gives daughter with gifts to a learned man.

20.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Paishacha — seduction of a sleeping or intoxicated girl
20.x: Rakshasa marriage involved capture or abduction. Marriage by purchase was known as Asura marriage.
20.tq: Find the swapped meaning among closely related marriage classifications.
xs: **Rakshasa — marriage by purchase** is wrongly matched — option **(1)**.

The rest are right: **Gandharva** = mutual consent; **Paishacha** = seduction; **Asura** = bride price.

Consider the following statements about the Ramayana:
1. It contains about 24,000 verses.
2. It is described as composed in five stages beginning from the 5th century BCE.
3. It contains about one lakh verses in 18 books.
Which of the above statements are correct?
21.x: The Ramayana has about 24,000 verses composed in five stages from the 5th century BCE; about one lakh verses in 18 books describes the Mahabharata.
xa: The Ramayana is attributed to **Valmiki**; the Mahabharata to **Vyasa**.
The Mahabharata is **older than the Ramayana** and is also called the **Jaya Samhita / Satasahasri Samhita**.
The Rigveda's **1,028 hymns** = **1,017** + **11 Valakhilya**.

21.s: Who wrote the Mitakshara, a commentary on the Yajnavalkya Smriti?
21.x: Vijnaneshwara wrote the Mitakshara, a commentary on the Yajnavalkya Smriti.
xa: Smritis, like the **Puranas**, are later texts; Vedic texts are **Shruti**.
Tradition counts **18 Mahapuranas**.
**Yajnavalkya** also appears in the **Brihadaranyaka Upanishad** dialogues with **Gargi** and **Maitreyi**.

21.s:
Consider the following statements about the Mahabharata:

2. Its original core, the Jaya, had 8,800 shlokas.
3. It is divided into 18 books (parvas).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
21.x: Statement 1 is wrong: the Harivamsa is appended to the Mahabharata. Statements 2 and 3 are correct (Jaya 8,800 shlokas; 18 parvas; later the Shatasahasri Samhita of about one lakh verses).

21.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Atharvaveda calls the Sabha and Samiti the twin daughters of Prajapati. Statement 4 is wrong: the Trayi is Rig, Yajur and Sama; the Atharvaveda was recognised later. So only two are correct.

21.x: Statement 3 is wrong: the Samaveda's priest is the Udgatri; the Adhvaryu belongs to the Yajurveda. Statements 1 and 2 are correct (shortest; compiled from the Rigveda, mostly Mandalas VIII and IX, all but about 75 verses).

22.s: Which of the following is not the part of “Ashtangayoga”?
22.x: The eight limbs are Yama, Niyama, Asana, Pranayama, Pratyahara, Dharana, Dhyana and Samadhi; Anusmriti (recollection) is a Buddhist meditation term, not a limb.

22.s:

2. Pratyahara belongs to the antaranga (inner) group.
3. Five limbs are bahiranga (outer).
Which of the statements given above is/are NOT correct?
22.x: Statement 2 is NOT correct: Pratyahara is the fifth and last bahiranga limb (the bridge to the inner limbs); antaranga = Dharana, Dhyana, Samadhi. Statements 1 and 3 are correct.

23.x: Ujjain (Ujjayini), capital of northern Avanti on the Shipra, was anciently called Avantika. Taxila was Gandhara's capital and Indraprastha Kuru's.

23.x: Suktimati (Sotthivati) was the capital of Chedi in eastern Bundelkhand.

23.x: Magadha covered the modern Patna and Gaya (and Nalanda) districts of Bihar; Anga lay east around Bhagalpur and Munger.

2. Mahapadma Nanda's title Sarvakshatrantaka means 'sole sovereign'.
3. The Hathigumpha inscription of Kharavela credits a Nanda king with a canal in Kalinga.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
25.x: Statement 2 is wrong: Sarvakshatrantaka means destroyer of the Kshatriyas; 'sole sovereign' is Ekarat. Statements 1 and 3 are correct.

25.s:
Assertion (A): Mahapadma Nanda is called Aparoparashurama, 'a second Parashurama'.
Reason (R): Mahapadma Nanda bore the title Sarvakshatrantaka, the destroyer of the Kshatriyas.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
25.x: Both are true and R explains A: like Parashurama he destroyed the Kshatriyas (Sarvakshatrantaka), hence Aparoparashurama.

25.s:
Consider the following statements about the last Nanda:
1. Dhana Nanda was called Agrammes by Greek writers.
2. Mahapadma Nanda was ruling Magadha at the time of Alexander's invasion.
3. Chandragupta Maurya overthrew Dhana Nanda in c. 321 BCE.
Which of the statements given above is/are NOT correct?
25.x: Statement 2 is NOT correct: the Nanda on the throne at Alexander's invasion (326 BCE) was Dhana Nanda (Agrammes/Xandrames). Statements 1 and 3 are correct.

25.s: In which century did the first Magadhan Empire rise?
25.x: The first Magadhan empire rose in the 6th century BC under Bimbisara (Haryanka), a contemporary of the Buddha.

25.s: Between the sixth and the fourth centuries BCE, ______ became the most powerful mahajanapada.
25.x: Between the 6th and 4th centuries BCE Magadha became the most powerful Mahajanapada (iron, elephants, fertile land, rivers).

25.s: Which one of the following was initially the most powerful city-state in India in the 6th century B.C.?
25.x: Of the four powers, Magadha emerged as the most powerful in the 6th century BC and founded the first empire; Gandhara, Kamboja and Kashi did not.

25.s: In contrast to the Vedic heartland, what was the nature of the society of Magadha?
25.x: Magadha's society was relatively unorthodox with little Vedic hold; iron, rivers, elephants and defensible capitals supported its rise.
xa: **Iron tools** raised **output + taxes**.
**Alluvial soil**, ample rainfall = agriculture.
**Ambitious rulers + able ministers** also helped.

25.s:
Match the following:
List-I (Buddhist Council)
A. First Council
B. Second Council
C. Third Council
List-II (Ruler)
1. Ashoka
2. Ajatashatru
3. Kalashoka
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
25.x: The First Council was held under Ajatashatru, the Second under Kalashoka and the Third under Ashoka.

25.s:
Consider the following statements about Magadha:
1. It was the most powerful and richest Mahajanapada of the 6th–4th centuries BCE.
2. According to the Puranas its first dynasty was the Brihadratha.
3. Jarasandha of the Brihadratha line ruled from Pataliputra.
How many of the above statements are correct?
25.x: Statement 3 is wrong: Jarasandha ruled from Girivraj (Rajgriha). Statements 1 and 2 are correct, and Magadha became the base of the Mauryan Empire. So only two are correct.

25.s:
Match the factors of Magadhan supremacy with their effects:
List-I (Factor)
a. Iron mines nearby
b. Alluvial soil, ample rainfall
c. Elephants from the eastern forests
d. Navigable Ganga and Son
List-II (Effect)
i. Agricultural surplus and taxes
ii. Weapons and tools; forest clearing
iii. First large-scale use of war elephants
iv. Cheap transport and trade
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
25.x: Iron mines = weapons, tools, forest clearing; alluvial soil and rainfall = surplus and taxes; eastern elephants = first large-scale war elephants; Ganga and Son = cheap transport and trade.

25.s:
Assertion (A): Control of the western sea ports was a main cause of the rise of Magadha.
Reason (R): Magadha had iron mines nearby for weapons and tools.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
25.x: A is false: the notes list control of western sea ports (like gold mines, superior cavalry or a republican system) as NOT a cause. R is true: nearby iron mines (Jharkhand) gave weapons and tools.

26.s: Identify the incorrect pair in the following.
26.x: Vimalanatha's emblem is the boar; the buffalo belongs to Vasupujya (12th). Ajitanatha–elephant, Naminatha–blue lotus and Arishtanemi (Neminatha)–conch are correct.

26.s: The 24th Jain Thirthankara was
26.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
26.x: Vardhamana Mahavira was the 24th and last Tirthankara; Rishabha was the 1st and Parshvanatha the 23rd. Siddhartha was Mahavira's father.

26.s: If Mahavira, the Jina, was the 24th Thirthankara, who was the first Thirthankara?
26.x: Rishabhadeva (Adinatha) was the first Tirthankara; Ajitanatha was the second.

26.s: Which one of the following statements is NOT correct?
o: The statue of Gomateshwara at Shravanabelagola represents the last Tirthankara of the Jains.
India's largest Buddhist monastery is in Arunachal Pradesh.
The Khajuraho temples were built under the Chandela Kings.
The Hoysalesvara Temple is dedicated to Shiva.
26.x: Gomateshwara at Shravanabelagola is Bahubali, son of the first Tirthankara Rishabhadeva, and not a Tirthankara at all, so (a) is NOT correct. Tawang (Arunachal) is India's largest Buddhist monastery, Khajuraho is Chandela, and the Hoysaleswara temple (Halebidu) is a Shiva temple.

26.s: Which one of the following was not a Jain Tirthankara?
26.x: Nathamuni was a Sri Vaishnava acharya who compiled the Alvar hymns, not a Tirthankara. Sambhavanatha (3rd), Chandraprabha (8th) and Nemi (22nd) are Tirthankaras.

26.s: Who was the last one in the order of Jain Tirthankaras?
26.x: Mahavira was the 24th and last Tirthankara; Parshvanatha was the 23rd and Rishabhadeva the 1st.

26.s: Which of the following place is known as a place of Pilgrimages because of being related to Parshvanath?
26.x: Parshvanatha attained nirvana on Sammed Shikhar (Parasnath hill, Jharkhand), which is why it is a pilgrimage centre for him; Pava is Mahavira's and Urjayanta (Girnar) Neminatha's nirvana place.

26.s: Parshvanatha, the Jain ‘Tirthankara’ was associated mainly with which of the following places?
26.x: Parshvanatha was born at Varanasi to King Asvasena and Queen Vama, so he is linked mainly with Varanasi.

26.s: Which of the following places is considered a Jain Siddha Kshetra on account of its association with Parshvanatha?
26.x: Parshvanatha attained nirvana at Sammed Shikhar (Parasnath hill), making it a Siddha Kshetra; Pava is Mahavira's.

26.s: Name the last Tirthankara.
26.x: Mahavira was the 24th and last Tirthankara; Parshvanatha was the 23rd.

26.s: The originator of the Jain religion is ……
26.x:
Most books and keys (UPPSC 2010): Rishabhadeva. Historians treat Parshvanatha as the earliest historical teacher and some books call Mahavira the founder (NextGen Indian History APPSC Part 1 p.42).
Jain tradition regards Rishabhadeva, the first of the 24 Tirthankaras, as the originator of the faith; Mahavira was the 24th and Parshvanatha the 23rd.

26.s: The Jainas believe that Jainism is the outcome of the teachings of twenty four Tirthankaras. In the light of this statement, which one among the following is correct of Vardhamana Mahavira?
o: He was the first Tirthankara and the founder of Jainism.
He was the twenty third Tirthankara, the first twenty two Tirthankaras being considerd legendary.
He was the last and twenty fourth Tirthankara, who was not considered as the founder of the new faith but a reformer of the existing religious sect.
He was not one of the twenty four Tirthankaras.
26.x: Mahavira was the 24th and last Tirthankara and a reformer of an older faith already taught by Parshvanatha (23rd), not its founder.

26.s: The word Tirthankara is related to –
26.x: Tirthankara ('ford-maker') is a Jain term for the 24 teachers who show the path to liberation.

26.s: Who was the first Tirthankara of Jain religion ?
26.x: Rishabhanatha (Rishabhadeva/Adinatha) was the first Tirthankara; Parshvanatha was the 23rd and Mahavira the 24th. Chetaka was a Lichchhavi chief.

26.s: Who among the following was twentieth Jain Tirthankar?
26.src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper General Studies
26.x: The 20th Tirthankara was Munisuvrata (emblem: tortoise).

26.s:
Consider the following statements about the Jain Tirthankaras:
1. The term 'Tirthankara' means 'conqueror of passions'.
2. The historicity of only the last two Tirthankaras, Parshvanatha and Mahavira, is confirmed by Jain and Buddhist texts.
3. Rishabhadeva, the first Tirthankara, was born at Ayodhya to Nabhi and Marudevi.
4. Munisuvrata was the 22nd Tirthankara.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
26.x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: Tirthankara means 'ford-maker' (one who shows the path across rebirth); 'conqueror' is the meaning of Jina. 4 is wrong: Munisuvrata was the 20th Tirthankara; the 22nd was Neminatha (Arishtanemi).

26.s:
Match List-I (Tirthankara) with List-II (Symbol / cognizance):
List-I | List-II
a. Rishabhadeva | i. Lion
b. Munisuvrata | ii. Tortoise
c. Parshvanatha | iii. Serpent
d. Mahavira | iv. Bull
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
26.x: Rishabhadeva (1st) – bull; Munisuvrata (20th) – tortoise; Parshvanatha (23rd) – serpent; Mahavira (24th) – lion. The conch belongs to Neminatha and the buffalo to Vasupujya.

26.s:
Match List-I (Tirthankara) with List-II (Place of nirvana):
List-I | List-II
a. Rishabhadeva | i. Mount Kailash (Ashtapada)
b. Vasupujya | ii. Pavapuri
c. Neminatha | iii. Girnar (Urjayanta)
d. Mahavira | iv. Champapuri
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
26.x: Rishabhadeva – Mount Kailash (Ashtapada); Vasupujya (12th) – Champapuri, not Pavapuri; Neminatha (22nd) – Girnar (Urjayanta); Mahavira – Pavapuri. Most other Tirthankaras, including Parshvanatha, attained nirvana at Sammed Shikhar.

26.s:
Consider the following statements about Parshvanatha:
1. He was born at Varanasi to King Asvasena and Queen Vama.
2. He renounced the world at 30 and died at 100, about 250 years before Mahavira.
3. He attained nirvana at Pavapuri.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
26.x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: Parshvanatha attained nirvana at Sammed Shikhar (Parasnath hill, Jharkhand); Pavapuri is Mahavira's place of death.

26.s:
Arrange the following Tirthankaras in the correct order of succession:
1. Munisuvrata
2. Vasupujya
3. Parshvanatha
4. Ajitanatha
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
26.x: Ajitanatha was the 2nd Tirthankara, Vasupujya the 12th, Munisuvrata the 20th and Parshvanatha the 23rd.

26.s: Who was the first follower of Mahavira?
26.x: Jamali, Mahavira's nephew and son-in-law, was his first disciple; Yashoda was his wife, Anojja his daughter and Trishala his mother.

26.s: What is not true in relation to Vardhamana Mahavir?
o: He is considered to be 24th and last Tirthankara
His mother was sister of Licchavi's king Chetaka
He did not marry in this lifetime
He left his body in 527 BCE at Pavapuri near Patna
26.x: 'He did not marry' is not true: Mahavira married Yashoda and had a daughter (NextGen; Svetambara tradition). He was the 24th Tirthankara, his mother Trishala was Chetaka's sister, and he died at Pavapuri (traditional date 527 BCE).

26.s: Which one of the following pair is correctly matched?
26.x: Chetaka was the chief of the Lichchhavis of Vaishali. Parshvanatha was not a Jnatrika (that was Mahavira's clan), Bindusara was a Maurya and Skandagupta a Gupta.

26.s:
Consider the following statements.

I. Vardhaman Mahavira’s mother was the daughter of Lichchhavi king Chetaka.

II. Gautama Buddha’s mother was a princess from the Koliyan dynasty.

III. Parshvanatha, the twenty-third Tirthankara, belonged to Banaras.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
26.x:
Most books and the UPSC key: Trishala was Chetaka's sister, so 'II and III'. The Digambara tradition makes her Chetaka's daughter (app notes 1:26; examrobot explanation).
I is wrong: Trishala was the sister of Chetaka, not his daughter (Svetambara account; UPSC key). II (Mahamaya was a Koliya princess) and III (Parshvanatha of Banaras) are correct.

26.x: Mahavira died at Pava (Pavapuri) near Rajagriha at the age of 72.

26.x: Arya Sudharma, the only Ganadhara to survive Mahavira, became the first Thera (head) of the Jain order; Bhadrabahu was the sixth Thera.

26.x: Jamali, Mahavira's son-in-law, was his first disciple; Bhadrabahu and Sthulabhadra came generations later.

26.s: Kundalpur is the birthplace of –
26.x: Kundagrama, modern Kundalpur near Vaishali, was the birthplace of Mahavira.

26.s: Mahavira Jain breathed his last at –
26.x: Mahavira died at Pava (Pavapuri) near Rajgir, aged 72; Rajgir is only the nearby town.

26.s: Where was Mahavira Swami born?
26.x: Mahavira was born at Kundagrama (Basukunda), a suburb of Vaishali; Vaishali itself is the nearby city.

26.s: The salvation place of Mahavirji, the originator of Jain religion, is located at -:
26.x: Mahavira attained nirvana at Pavapuri (Pava) near Rajgir.

26.s: Vardhamana Mahavira was:
26.x: Mahavira was a Kshatriya: his father Siddhartha belonged to the Jnatrika Kshatriya clan.

26.s: On the banks of which river did Mahavira Swami attain enlightenment?
26.x: Mahavira attained kaivalya at 42 under a sal tree at Jrimbhikagrama on the bank of the Rijupalika.

26.s: Who of the following was a contemporary of Gautama Buddha?
26.x: Vardhamana Mahavira was a contemporary of the Buddha; Parshvanatha lived about 250 years earlier, and Bhadrabahu and Chandragupta Maurya came later.

26.s: Which one of the following is NOT a title associated with Mahavira?
26.x: Jina, Kevalin, Nirgrantha, Mahavira and Arhat are titles associated with Mahavira. Tathagata is a title associated with the Buddha.
26.tq: Find the title belonging to another religious tradition rather than Jainism.
xs: **Tathagata** is **not** a title of Mahavira — option **(4)** is the answer.
Mahavira's titles: **Jina** (conqueror of passions), **Nirgrantha** (free from bonds), **Kevalin**, Mahavira, **Arhat**.
xa: **Jina** is the source of the word "**Jain**".
Followers were called **Nigranthas/Shravanas**.
**Kevalin** = one who has attained **Kevala jnana** (omniscience).

26.s: Which republic is described as the first to recognise Jainism?
26.x: The Lichchhavi republic is identified as the first republic to recognise Jainism.
26.tq: Recall the specific political community associated with early recognition of Jainism.
xs: The **Lichchhavi republic** was the **first to recognise Jainism** — option **(4)** is correct.
Mahavira's mother **Trishala** was the sister of Lichchhavi chief **Chetaka**.
xa: Mahavira was born at **Kundagrama**, near **Vaishali**.
Bimbisara's queen **Chellana** was also linked to this Lichchhavi house.
Contemporary rulers: **Bimbisara**, **Ajatashatru**, **Chetaka**, **Pradyota**.

26.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Mahavira?
o: He attained kaivalya under a sal tree
26.x: Mahavira died at Pavapuri, not Champapuri, which is linked with Vasupujya.

26.s:
Consider the following statements about the family of Mahavira:
1. He was born at Kundagrama near Vaishali.
2. His father Siddhartha was the chief of the Shakya clan.
3. His mother Trishala was a Lichchhavi princess.
4. Chetaka, chief of the Lichchhavis, was his maternal uncle, and Chetaka's daughter Chellana married Bimbisara.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
26.x: 1, 3 and 4 are correct. 2 is wrong: Siddhartha was the chief of the Jnatrika Kshatriya clan; the Shakyas were the Buddha's clan.

26.s:
Consider the following statements about Mahavira:
1. After renouncing the world at 30 he practised austerities for 12 years.
2. He attained Kaivalya at 42 under a sal tree at Jrimbhikagrama on the bank of the Rijupalika.
3. He died at Pavapuri at the age of 82.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
26.x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: Mahavira died at Pava (Pavapuri) near Rajgriha at the age of 72, not 82 (and not at Champapuri).

26.s:
Match List-I (Contemporary of Mahavira) with List-II (Kingdom / people):
List-I | List-II
a. Ajatashatru | i. Kosala
b. Chetaka | ii. Magadha
c. Pradyota | iii. Lichchhavis
d. Prasenajit | iv. Avanti
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
26.x: Bimbisara and Ajatashatru – Magadha; Chetaka – Lichchhavis of Vaishali; Pradyota – Avanti; Prasenajit – Kosala.

26.s:
Consider the following statements about Mahavira's companions and successors:
1. Makkhali Gosala, his companion for about six years, founded the Ajivika sect.
2. Ajita Kesakambalin was a materialist teacher of the time.
3. Bhadrabahu survived Mahavira and became the first Thera (head of the Sangha).
How many of the statements given above are correct?
26.x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: of the 11 Ganadharas only Arya Sudharma survived Mahavira and became the first Thera; Bhadrabahu was the 6th Thera.

26.s: Where did Mahavira deliver his first sermon?
26.x: Mahavira preached for 30 years in Kosala, Magadha and further east; his first sermon was at Rajgriha, and he visited the courts of Bimbisara and Ajatashatru.

26.s: Who preached the 'Syadvada' philosophical tradition?
26.x: Kundakundacharya, the Digambara monk of Konakondla (Anantapur), propagated Syadvada and Anekantavada (APPSC key). Somadeva Suri only held the title 'Syadvadachala Simha'; Nagarjuna was a Buddhist.

26.s: Who has the title "Syadvadachala Simha"?
26.x: Somadeva Suri held the title 'Syadvadachala Simha'; Kundakundacharya preached Syadvada but did not carry this title.

26.s: Which Jain philosopher wrote the text Samayasara?
26.x: Kundakundacharya, the Digambara philosopher, composed the Samayasara (also Pravachanasara, Panchastikayasara). Bavari was a Buddhist from Andhra and Kalakasuri a Jain monk of the Satavahana court.

26.s: Who preached the "Syadvada" philosophical tradition?
26.x: Kundakundacharya propagated Syadvada and Anekantavada (APPSC key); Somadeva Suri only held the title 'Syadvadachala Simha'.

26.s: "Syadwadachala Simha" was the title of:
26.x: Somadeva Suri held the title 'Syadvadachala Simha'. Kundakundacharya preached Syadvada, so he is the tempting wrong option.

26.s: Who has the title "Shyadwadachala Simha"?
26.x: Somadeva Suri held the title 'Syadvadachala Simha'.

26.s:
Consider the following statements about Jaina Philosophy.
(1) The Jaina philosophy revolves around two main doctrines, i.e., Anekantavada and Syadvada.
(2) According to anekantavada, every being has numerous properties. The permanent property that constitutes the nature of a thing is called attribute (guna). Which of the statement/s given above is/are correct?
26.x: Both are correct: Jain philosophy rests on Anekantavada and Syadvada, and under Anekantavada every being has many properties, the permanent one being its attribute (guna).

26.s: Which of the following Doctrines are associated with Jainism? (i) Anekantavada (ii) Sarvastivada (iii) Sunyavada (iv) Syadvada Select the correct answer using the code given below –
26.x: Anekantavada and Syadvada are Jain doctrines; Sarvastivada and Sunyavada are Buddhist.

26.x: Anekantavada, the many-sidedness of reality, is a core doctrine of Jainism.

26.s: Syadvad is a doctrine of
26.x: Syadvada, the doctrine of 'maybe' (conditioned predication), is Jain.

26.s: Which religion is related to 'Swadvada'?
26.x: Syadvada is a Jain doctrine.

26.s: Anekāntavāda is a core theory and philosophy of which one of the following?
26.x: Anekantavada is a core theory of Jainism (UPSC 2009 key: b).

26.s: The Jain philosopher who composed "Samayasara" was
26.x: Kundakundacharya, the Digambara philosopher, composed the Samayasara.

26.s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Anekantavada is regarded as a basis of tolerance and pluralism.
Reason (R): Anekantavada holds that reality is many-sided and no single view holds the whole truth.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true

26.s:

1. Kundakundacharya, a Digambara monk, wrote the Samayasara and Pravachanasara.

26.s: The doctrine of three jewels-Right faith, Right action and Right Knowledge, is the crowning glory of :
26.x: Right faith, right knowledge and right action are the Jain ratnatraya (three jewels), the path to moksha.

Triratna (ratnatraya: right faith, knowledge and conduct) is the Jain path to moksha. Nyaya and Yoga have no triratna.

26.x: Triratna (right faith, knowledge and conduct) is the Jain doctrine.

26.s: ‘Samadhi Marana’ is related to which Philosophy?
26.x: Samadhi Marana is another name for Sallekhana/Santhara, the Jain ritual fast unto death.

26.s: The Jain philosophy holds that the world is created and maintained by
26.x: Mahavira taught that the world was not created by a supreme creator but runs by an eternal law of decay and development, hence 'Universal Law' (UPSC 2011 key: a).

26.x: Jainism holds the universe to be eternal and uncreated, running by its own law of decay and development, so it has no 'final annihilation' of the world.

26.s: In Jain religion, which word is used for ‘Complete Intellect’?
26.x: Kaivalya (Kevala jnana) is the Jain term for complete knowledge (omniscience); Jina means conqueror and Nirvana is final liberation.

27.x: The earliest Jain canon (the Agamas) was compiled in Ardhamagadhi Prakrit. 'Prakrit' is the broader family, while Pali is the Buddhist canon's language.

Jain sacred texts (**Agamas / Siddhanta**) are in the eastern Prakrit **Ardhamagadhi**.

2. The Second Council at Vaishali (383 BCE) split the Sangha into Sthaviravadins and Mahasanghikas.
3. The Third Council at Pataliputra, presided over by Moggaliputta Tissa, was conducted in Sanskrit.

n: Vinaya Pitaka contains the rules and discipline of the Buddhist Sangha or monastic order. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #57 · pp 131-132]

3. The Vamsatthapakasini, which tells the Chanakya–Chandragupta legend, is a Jain text of the 10th century.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
33.x: Statement 3 is wrong: the Vamsatthapakasini (10th c.) is a Buddhist commentary, not a Jain text. Statements 1 and 2 are correct.

34.s: Megasthenes was the ambassador of -:
34.x: Megasthenes was the ambassador of Seleucus I Nicator to Chandragupta Maurya's court – not of Alexander or Darius.

34.s: Which Indian king defeated Seleucus, the administrator of Sindh and Afghanistan appointed by Alexander -
34.x: Chandragupta Maurya defeated Seleucus Nicator, Alexander's general, in 305 BCE and won his eastern provinces. Bindusara and Ashoka came later.

34.s: Deimachus came to India during the reign of –
34.x: Deimachus, envoy of the Syrian king Antiochus I, came to Bindusara's court (Strabo), succeeding Megasthenes.

34.s: Who one of the following had not come to India with Alexander?
34.x: Deimachus did not come with Alexander – he was Antiochus I's envoy to Bindusara. Nearchus, Onesicritus and Aristobulus were Alexander's companions.

34.s: Rulers of which of the following had diplomatic relations with distant countries like Syria and Egypt?
34.x: The Mauryas had diplomatic ties with Syria (Deimachus of Antiochus I) and Egypt (Dionysius of Ptolemy II) at Bindusara's court; Ashoka's RE XIII names these kings too.

34.s: During whose rule did Megasthenes come to India?
34.x: Megasthenes came to India as Seleucus's envoy during Chandragupta Maurya's rule, not Ashoka's, Harsha's or Kumaragupta's.

34.s: Famous Greek ambassador Megasthenes came to the court of which emperor?
34.x: Megasthenes, envoy of Seleucus Nicator, lived at the court of Chandragupta Maurya at Pataliputra – not Ashoka's or Harsha's.

34.s: In which year did Chandragupta Maurya defeat Seleucus Nicator?
34.x: Chandragupta defeated Seleucus about 305 BC, which led to the treaty.

34.s: Which one of the following was NOT included among the seven classes described by Megasthenes?
34.x: Megasthenes listed philosophers, farmers, herdsmen, artisans, soldiers, overseers and councillors. Merchants were not included in this seven-class description.
34.tq: Find the outsider by comparing every option with the complete named list.
xs: **Merchants** are not among Megasthenes' seven classes — option **(1)**.
The seven: **philosophers, farmers, herdsmen, artisans, soldiers, overseers (spies), councillors**.
xa: **Philosophers** = **Brahmanas and Sramanas** (ascetics).
⚠ **Overseers** were in effect **spies**.
He also wrongly claimed there were **no slaves**.

34.s: According to Megasthenes, how was the municipal administration of Palibothra conducted?
o: A 40-member body divided into four boards
A 30-member body divided into six boards
A council of 12 members divided into three boards
A council of 64 members divided into eight boards
34.x: Megasthenes described a 30-member municipal body organised into six boards at Palibothra.
34.tq: Separate the exact institutional composition from nearby city statistics.
xs: Palibothra was run by a **30-member municipal body in six boards** — option **(2)**.
**64** is the number of **gates**, not council members.
xa: Palibothra = **Pataliputra**, at the **Ganga-Son confluence**.
It had a **wooden wall**, **64 gates** and **570 towers**.
Megasthenes was sent by **Seleucus Nicator** to Chandragupta.

34.s:
Consider the following statements about the treaty between Chandragupta Maurya and Seleucus Nicator:
1. Seleucus ceded Aria, Arachosia, Paropanisadai and Gedrosia.
2. Seleucus also ceded Bactria.
3. Chandragupta gave Seleucus 500 war elephants.
4. Chandragupta's daughter was married to Seleucus.
How many of the above statements are correct?
34.x: Statements 2 and 4 are wrong: Bactria was not ceded, and it was Seleucus's daughter (Helena) who married Chandragupta, not the reverse. Statements 1 and 3 are correct, so only two are correct.

34.s:
Match the provinces ceded by Seleucus to Chandragupta Maurya with their present-day regions:
List-I (Province)
a. Aria
b. Arachosia
c. Paropanisadai
d. Gedrosia
List-II (Present-day region)
i. Kabul
ii. Balochistan
iii. Kandahar
iv. Herat
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
34.x: Aria = Herat; Arachosia = Kandahar; Paropanisadai = Kabul; Gedrosia = Balochistan.

34.s:
Consider the following statements about the Greek envoys to the Mauryan court:
1. Megasthenes, the first Greek envoy to an Indian court, came in the reign of Chandragupta Maurya.
2. Deimachus was sent by Antiochus I to the court of Bindusara.
3. Dionysius was sent by Ptolemy II Philadelphus to the court of Ashoka.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
34.x: Statement 3 is wrong: Dionysius, the envoy of Ptolemy II Philadelphus of Egypt, came to Bindusara's court. Statements 1 and 2 are correct.

34.s: Who of the following mentions about the meeting of Sandrokottos (Chandragupta Maurya) with Alexander, the Great
34.x: Justin described the meeting of Sandrokottos (Chandragupta Maurya) with Alexander. Pliny, Strabo and Megasthenes are not credited with this.

34.s: Who of the following mentions about the meeting of Sandrocottus (Chandragupta Maurya) with Alexander, the Great?
34.x: Justin, the Roman historian, described Sandrocottus (Chandragupta) meeting Alexander; Pliny, Strabo and Megasthenes are not credited with this.

34.s: Which among the following is India’s oldest dynasty?
34.x: The Maurya dynasty (321–185 BCE) is the oldest of the four; the Kushanas, Guptas and Vardhanas came later.

34.s: Who was called as 'Sandrocottos' by Justin, the Greek Writer?
34.x: Justin called Chandragupta Maurya 'Sandrocottus'; Sir William Jones identified the name with him. The Gupta kings are much later.

34.s: To which dynasty did Ashoka belong?
34.x: Ashoka belonged to the Maurya dynasty – grandson of its founder Chandragupta and son of Bindusara.

34.s: First Indian Empire was established by
34.x: Chandragupta Maurya founded the first Indian (pan-Indian) empire, the Maurya empire; Kanishka, Harsha and Samudragupta came later.

34.s: Who recognized Sandrokottos as Chandra Gupta Maurya?
34.x: Sir William Jones identified the Sandrokottos of the Greek writers with Chandragupta Maurya. This became the sheet-anchor of Indian chronology. Smith, Mookerji and D.R. Bhandarkar came later.

34.s:
Consider the following about the origin of the Mauryas:
1. Brahmanical sources link the name Maurya with the Shudra woman Mura.
2. Buddhist and Jain sources describe Chandragupta as a Kshatriya of the Moriya clan.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
34.x: Brahmanical sources connect the name Maurya with Mura, while Buddhist and Jain traditions make Chandragupta a Kshatriya of the Moriya clan.
xa: The **Parishishtaparvan** of **Hemachandra** gives the Jain account of his life.
**Mudrarakshasa** and **Devi Chandraguptam** preserve other traditions.
Greek name: **Sandrocottus**.

34.s: Which commentator on Mudrarakshasa made Chandragupta a descendant of the Nanda house?
34.x: Dhundiraja's commentary on Mudrarakshasa links Chandragupta with the Nanda house.

34.s:
Consider the following statements about the Greek accounts of Chandragupta Maurya:
1. Justin and Strabo call him Sandrocottus, while Arrian and Plutarch call him Androkottus.
2. Sir William Jones identified Sandrocottus with Chandragupta Maurya in 1793.
3. Pliny describes the meeting of Chandragupta with Alexander.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
34.x: Statement 3 is wrong: the meeting with Alexander is described by Justin, who also called Chandragupta's army a 'gang of dacoits'. Statements 1 and 2 are correct.

34.s:
Consider the following statements about Chandragupta Maurya:
1. He studied at Taxila in Gandhara, where he met Chanakya.
2. With the Himalayan chief Parvataka he overthrew Dhana Nanda and took the throne in 321 BCE.
3. Greek accounts credit him with 6,00,000 infantry and 30,000 cavalry.
4. He reigned from 297 to 273 BCE.
How many of the above statements are correct?
34.x: Statement 4 is wrong: 297–273 BCE is Bindusara's reign; Chandragupta reigned c. 324/321–297 BCE. Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct, so three are correct.

34.s:
Who among the following rulers paid attention to the resource management in Girnar region some centuries before the Christian era?
1. Mahapadma Nanda
2. Chandragupta Maurya
3. Ashoka
4. Rudradaman
Select the correct answer using the codes given below :
34.x: Before the Christian era Chandragupta Maurya (governor Pushyagupta built the Sudarshana lake) and Ashoka (governor Tushaspha added canals) managed Girnar's water. Rudradaman repaired it in c. 150 CE, after the Christian era, so codes 2, 3.

34.s: Who amongst the following Mauryan rulers did conquer the Deccan?
34.x:
Most books and keys: Bindusara conquered the Deccan. Some books credit Chandragupta (Jain tradition of his end at Shravanabelagola), and NextGen says Bindusara made no conquests.
Bindusara is credited with extending Mauryan rule over the Deccan up to Mysore (PMF); Ashoka only added Kalinga and Kunala was a later prince.

34.s: Who was the first king to conquer Malwa, Gujarat and Maharashtra?
34.x: Chandragupta Maurya was the first king to hold Malwa, Gujarat (Saurashtra, under governor Pushyagupta – Junagadh inscription) and Maharashtra; Skandagupta, Vikramaditya and Harsha came much later.

34.s: Realizing the need for water, the first ruler who got a lake constructed in the Girnar area, was
34.x: The first lake at Girnar, the Sudarshana, was built by Pushyagupta, governor of Chandragupta Maurya. Ashoka's governor only added canals; Rudradaman and Skandagupta repaired it later.

34.s: Who constructed the Sudarshana Lake?
34.x: The Sudarshana lake was built in Chandragupta Maurya's reign by his governor Pushyagupta (Junagadh inscription of Rudradaman). Samudragupta, Chandragupta Vikramaditya and Bimbisara are distractors.

34.s: With reference to Chandragupta Maurya's expansion, which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Mamulanar – Greek chronicler of the Mauryas
Seleucus – Ceded four provinces up to Afghanistan
Greek satraps – Expelled from the north-west
34.x: Mamulanar was a Tamil poet who referred to the Mauryas' southward expansion, not a Greek chronicler.
xa: **Western India**: Saurashtra under **Pushyagupta**, builder of the **Sudarshana lake**.
Army: **600,000 infantry, 30,000 cavalry**.
Ceded provinces: **Aria, Arachosia, Paropanisadai, Gedrosia**.

34.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Chandragupta Maurya is regarded as the Mauryan conqueror of the Deccan.
2. The Tamil poet Mamulanar refers to the southward push of the Mauryas.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
34.x:
Most books and keys: Bindusara conquered the Deccan. Some books credit Chandragupta (Jain tradition).
Only 2 is safely correct: the Sangam poet Mamulanar refers to the Mauryas' southward push. Statement 1 is not settled – PMF credits Bindusara with conquering the Deccan up to Mysore, so the old key 'Both' is changed.

34.s:
Match the Mauryan provincial capitals with their provinces:
List-I (Capital)
a. Taxila
b. Ujjain
c. Tosali
d. Suvarnagiri
List-II (Province)
i. East (Kalinga)
ii. West
iii. North
iv. South
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
34.x: Taxila – north; Ujjain – west; Tosali – Kalinga in the east; Suvarnagiri – south; Pataliputra was the centre.

34.s:
Consider the following statements about the southern reach of the Mauryas:
1. Brahmagiri, Siddapura and Jatinga-Rameshwara in Karnataka mark the southern reach of the empire.
2. The Pandya kingdom lay within the Mauryan Empire.
3. In Kurnool district, Yerragudi has both major and minor edicts while Rajula Mandagiri has only a minor edict.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
34.x: Statement 2 is wrong: the Tamil kingdoms – Chola, Pandya, Satyaputra, Keralaputra – stayed outside the empire. Statements 1 and 3 are correct.

34.s:
Assertion (A): The Satavahanas began their political career as feudatories of the Mauryas.
Reason (R): Ashoka's Rock Edict XIII names the Andhras among the peoples following Dhamma within his domain.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
34.x: Both are true: the notes say the Satavahanas began as Mauryan feudatories, and RE XIII names the Andhras among peoples within the domain. But R only shows the Andhra country lay within Ashoka's empire; it does not explain how the Satavahana dynasty began, so R is not the correct explanation of A.

34.s:
Consider the following statements about the Sudarshana lake at Girnar:
1. It was built by Pushyagupta, governor of Chandragupta Maurya.
2. Tushaspha, Ashoka's Yavana governor, added canals to it.
3. Rudradaman I repaired it using forced labour.
4. Skandagupta repaired it again.
How many of the above statements are correct?
34.x: Statement 3 is wrong: Rudradaman I repaired it (c. 150 CE) without forced labour, as his Junagadh inscription says. Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct, so three are correct.

34.s: Kautilya was prime minister of –
34.x: Kautilya (Chanakya, Vishnugupta) was the prime minister and guide of Chandragupta Maurya, not of Chandragupta Vikramaditya, Ashoka or Janaka.

34.s: By which name was Chanakya known in his childhood?
34.x: Chanakya's childhood name was Vishnugupta; one Arthashastra verse names its author Vishnugupta, while Chanakya and Kautilya are his other names.

34.s: The another name of Chanakya was
34.x: Chanakya, also called Kautilya, was known as Vishnugupta. Bhattaswami was a commentator, Rajasekhara a later poet and Vishakhadatta wrote Mudrarakshasa.

34.s: Another name of Chanakya was :
34.x: Chanakya, also called Kautilya, was known as Vishnugupta; Bhattaswami, Rajasekhara and Vishakhadatta are other authors.

34.s:
Consider the following statements about Chanakya:
1. One verse of the Arthashastra names its author Vishnugupta.
2. According to Taranath and Jain tradition, he stayed on as Ashoka's minister.
3. In the Mudrarakshasa his rival Rakshasa was the minister of the Nandas.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
34.x: Statement 2 is wrong: Taranath and Jain tradition make him Bindusara's minister. Statements 1 and 3 are correct.

34.s: The first Indian King who abdicated his throne, was:
34.x: Chandragupta Maurya is regarded as the first Indian king to abdicate – in favour of Bindusara – before becoming a Jain ascetic and dying by Sallekhana at Shravanabelagola.

34.s: Who came south with Chandragupta Maurya during the great famine in North India?
34.x: By Jain tradition the monk Bhadrabahu led the migration south in the 12-year famine, with Chandragupta Maurya, to Shravanabelagola. Sthulabhadra stayed in the north; Merutunga and Lakulisha are later figures.

34.s:
Consider the following about the Barabar caves:
1. They are located at Girnar.
2. They are the oldest surviving rock-cut caves.
3. They are carved in granite.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
34.x: The Barabar caves in Bihar are the oldest surviving rock-cut caves, carved in granite; they are not at Girnar.
xa: **Dasharatha** also gave the **Nagarjuni caves** to the Ajivikas.
**Rudradaman I** only repaired the Sudarshana lake.
Bindusara is the standard **Ajivika patron**.

34.s: To whom did Ashoka and Dasharatha dedicate the Barabar caves in Bihar?
34.x: Ashoka and Dasharatha dedicated the Barabar caves to the Ajivikas, the sect also patronised by Bindusara. Jainism is linked with Chandragupta and Samprati, and Buddhism with Ashoka's Lanka mission, but the Barabar dedications were to the Ajivikas; Vedic Brahmanas were not the recipients.
34.tq: Barabar and Nagarjuni caves = Ajivikas (Ashoka, Dasharatha).
xs: **Ashoka and Dasharatha** dedicated the **Barabar caves** to the **Ajivikas** — option **(1)**.
Barabar (**Bihar**) has the **oldest surviving rock-cut caves**, in **granite**.
**Jainism** is linked with Chandragupta and Samprati; the Barabar gifts were to the Ajivikas.
xa: **Dasharatha** was an Ajivika patron at **Nagarjuni**; personally counted a Buddhist (**CGPSC 2013** key).
**Bindusara** is the standard Ajivika patron.
**Ashoka** turned to **Buddhism** after Kalinga.

34.s: In which hills of Bihar is the Lomas Rishi cave, a Mauryan cave linked to the Ajivikas?
34.x: Lomas Rishi is one of the Barabar Hill caves in Bihar, famous for its carved facade.
n: Lomas Rishi Cave is located in the Barabar Hills of Bihar. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #76 · pp 154-155]
Lomas Rishi Cave is associated with the Ajivika religion. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #76 · pp 154-155]
Lomas Rishi Cave belongs to the Mauryan period. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #76 · pp 154-155]
xa: Lomas Rishi is famous for its **rock-cut façade**.
**Barabar Caves** contain **Ashokan inscriptions**; dedicated to Ajivikas by **Ashoka and Dasharatha**.
They are the **oldest surviving rock-cut caves**, carved in **granite**.

34.s: Which religion did Dasharatha, who gave the Nagarjuni caves to the Ajivikas, follow?
34.x: Dasharatha is taken as a Buddhist, though he patronised the Ajivikas with the Nagarjuni caves.

34.s:
Consider the following statements about Chandragupta Maurya's Jain end:
1. Bhadrabahu went south with him during the great famine.
2. After the twelve-year famine the followers of Sthulabhadra came to be called Digambaras.
3. He died by Sallekhana at Shravanabelagola in Karnataka.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
34.x: Statement 2 is wrong: Sthulabhadra's followers became the Svetambaras; Bhadrabahu's followers were the Digambaras. Statements 1 and 3 are correct (he abdicated for Bindusara – source Parishishtaparvan).

34.s:
Match the Mauryan rulers with their religious leanings:
List-I (Ruler)
a. Chandragupta
b. Bindusara
c. Ashoka
d. Samprati
List-II (Religion)
i. Ajivika
ii. Buddhism
iii. 'Ashoka of Jainism'; spread Jainism in Andhra
iv. Jainism, under Bhadrabahu
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
34.x: Chandragupta – Jainism (Bhadrabahu); Bindusara – Ajivika; Ashoka – Buddhism (though he gave the Barabar caves to the Ajivikas); Samprati – the 'Ashoka of Jainism', who spread Jainism in Andhra.

34.s: Which of the following Mauryan ruler is known as ‘Amitraghat’?
34.x: Amitraghata ('slayer of foes', Greek Amitrochates) was the title of Bindusara, not of Chandragupta, Samudragupta or Ashoka.

34.s:
Consider the following statements about Bindusara:
1. His birth name was Simhasena and his mother was Durdhara.
2. He ruled from 297 to 273 BCE.
3. Antiochus I sent him the philosopher he had asked for.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
34.x: Statement 3 is wrong: Bindusara asked Antiochus I for sweet wine, dried figs and a philosopher – the philosopher could not be sent. Statements 1 and 2 are correct.

34.s:
Consider the following statements about the Taxila revolts:
1. Under Bindusara, prince Susima failed to put down the Taxila revolt.
2. According to the Divyavadana, Ashoka was then sent to Taxila.
3. The later Taxila revolt in Ashoka's reign was also handled by Susima.
4. Ashoka had served as viceroy at Taxila and Ujjain.
How many of the above statements are correct?
34.x: Statement 3 is wrong: the later Taxila revolt under Ashoka was handled by Kunala. Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct, so three statements are correct.

34.s:
Assertion (A): Bindusara is identified with the 'Amitrochates' of the Greek writers.
Reason (R): Bindusara's title Amitraghata means 'slayer of foes'.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
34.x: Both are true: Amitrochates is the Greek form of Bindusara's title Amitraghata, which means 'slayer of foes' (Mahabhashya). But the meaning of the title does not explain the identification – it rests on the Greek form of the title – so R is not the correct explanation of A.

35.s: “In spite of being Buddhist, Ashoka did not leave belief in Hinduism” validation of this fact is:–
35.x: The epithet Devanampriya ('beloved of the gods') is read as proof that Ashoka, though a Buddhist, kept his regard for the gods; pilgrimages and veterinary hospitals show Buddhist piety and welfare.

35.s: Who established ‘Rajdharma’ on triplex bases of longanimity, liberty and compassion ?
35.x: Ashoka's Dhamma was a rajdharma based on longanimity (tolerance), liberty and compassion; Akbar, Ranjit Singh and Shivaji are distractors.

35.s: The central point in Ashoka's Dhamma is -:
35.x: The core of Ashoka's Dhamma is peace and non-violence – RE I bans slaughter and sacrifice; respect to elders and toleration are parts of it, not its centre.

35.s: India’s first hospital and herbal gardens were built by?
35.x: Ashoka's RE II records hospitals and medicinal herb gardens for men and animals – the first in India; Chandragupta, Mahavira and Dhanvantari are distractors.

35.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Ashoka:
1. The definition of Dhamma given by Ashoka has been taken from the "Rahulovada-Sutta".
2. In the 14th year of his reign, Ashoka appointed a new type of staffcalled Dhamma-Mahamatras.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
35.x: Both are correct: the spirit of Ashoka's Dhamma is drawn from the Rahulovada Sutta (with the Lakkhana Sutta and Dhammapada), and RE V appointed Dhamma Mahamatras 13 years after consecration, i.e. in his 14th regnal year.

35.s:
Consider the following statements about Ashoka's regnal years:
1. The Dhammayatra to Bodh Gaya was made in the 11th regnal year.
2. Dhamma Mahamatras were appointed in the 12th regnal year.
3. Rajukas received independent judicial authority in the 26th regnal year.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
35.x: The Dhammayatra was in the 11th year and rajukas got judicial authority in the 26th; Dhamma Mahamatras came in the 14th, the 12th being the quinquennial tours.

35.s: Which officials did Ashoka appoint to look after all sects, women and prisoners?
35.x: RE V's Dhamma Mahamatras worked among all sects, women and prisoners; Pativedakas were reporters.

35.s:
Consider the following statements about Ashoka's Dhamma:
1. It was a moral code and social ethic, not a new religion.
2. Its central point was peace and non-violence; Rock Edict I bans slaughter and sacrifice.
3. Pillar Edict II defines Dhamma as 'few faults, many good deeds'.
4. It named the Four Noble Truths and Nibbana.
How many of the above statements are correct?
35.x: Statement 4 is wrong: the Dhamma edicts name no Four Noble Truths or Nibbana – Dhamma was ethics, not Buddhist doctrine. Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct, so three are correct.

35.s:
Consider the following statements about the content of Ashoka's Dhamma:
1. Charity and truthfulness were among its virtues.
2. It asked for regard for both Brahmanas and Shramanas.
3. It encouraged festive gatherings called samajas.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
35.x: Statement 3 is wrong: wasteful festive gatherings (samajas) were to be avoided. Statements 1 and 2 are correct (also kindness, purity, respect for elders, courtesy to slaves and servants).

35.s:
Match Ashoka's measures with the edicts that record them:
List-I (Measure)
a. Appointment of Dhamma Mahamatras
b. Quinquennial tours of rajukas, pradeshikas and yuktas
c. Pativedakas may report at any time
d. Hospitals for men and animals
List-II (Edict)
i. Rock Edict VI
ii. Rock Edict V
iii. Rock Edict III
iv. Rock Edict II
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
35.x: Dhamma Mahamatras – RE V (14th regnal year); quinquennial tours – RE III (12th year); pativedakas reporting at any time – RE VI; hospitals, medicinal herbs, wells and trees – RE II.

35.s:
Consider the following statements about Ashoka's edicts:
1. Pillar Edict IV gave the rajukas independent judicial power in the 26th regnal year.
2. Pillar Edict IV gave condemned prisoners a respite of three days.
3. Pillar Edict V forbade the branding of cattle.
4. Rock Edict II limits its welfare measures to the empire and leaves out the Tamil lands.
How many of the above statements are correct?
35.x: Statement 4 is wrong: RE II extends the hospitals, herbs and wells also to the lands of the Cholas, Pandyas, Satyaputras and Keralaputras. Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct, so three are correct.

35.s: Which event brought about a profound change in Ashoka’s administrative policy?
o: His sending of missionary to Ceylon
35.x: The Kalinga War's carnage (RE XIII) made Ashoka give up conquest by war (Bherighosha) for conquest by Dhamma (Dhammaghosha). The Third Council and the Ceylon mission came later.

35.s:
Consider the following statements.
Assertion (A) Ashoka annexed Kalinga to the Mauryan Empire.
Reason (R) Kalinga controlled the land and sea routes to South India.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
35.x: Ashoka conquered Kalinga c. 261 BCE; Kalinga's control of the land and sea routes to the south explains why he wanted it, so R explains A.

35.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Kalinga War?
o: Rock Edict XIII is found at Dhauli and Jaugada
Bherighosha gave way to Dhammaghosha after it
Separate Edicts address officials at Tosali and Samapa
35.x: Dhauli and Jaugada have no RE XIII; they carry the Separate Edicts instead.

35.s:
Consider the following statements about the Kalinga War:
1. It was fought in c. 261 BCE, Ashoka's 8th regnal year.
2. Rock Edict XIII says about 1,50,000 were killed and 1,00,000 deported.

Consider the following statements about the Allahabad-Kosam pillar:

2. It also bears an inscription of the Mughal emperor Jahangir.
3. It was brought to the Allahabad fort by Firuz Shah Tughluq.

36.x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: the Kosam pillar went to the Allahabad fort traditionally under Akbar; Firuz Shah Tughluq brought the Topra and Meerut pillars to Delhi.

36.s:

3. Pillar Edict VII says that Dhamma spreads better by persuasion than by law.

36.x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: Lauriya Nandangarh (West Champaran, single lion capital) has PE I–VI; PE VII is only on the Delhi-Topra pillar.

36.s:
Consider the following statements about Ashoka's pillar edicts:

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
36.x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: the Schism edict is at Sarnath, Sanchi and Kaushambi; Girnar has the Major Rock Edicts.

36.s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Ashokan pillars cluster in the Ganga plain.
Reason (R): The Chunar sandstone for the pillars needed no transport, as it was quarried at each pillar site.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
36.x: A is true but R is false: the heavy Chunar sandstone monoliths had to be moved, and the pillars cluster in the Ganga plain because river transport made that easier.

36.s: Inculcating religious thought in the minds of disciples as the duty of teachers is found in which inscription of Ashoka?
36.x:
Most books and keys: Erragudi. Strictly: Rajula Mandagiri also carries the Minor Rock Edict text on gurus and disciples (AP History APPSC 01 p.11).
The Erragudi (Yerragudi) Minor Rock Edict tells teachers to instil Dhamma in their pupils. Bhattiprolu and Dhanyakataka are not Ashokan edict sites.
