54.s: Which region is indicated by the early records and forts as the original home of the Vishnukundins?
o: Telangana, including Amrabad, Keesaragutta and Indrapalanagara
The Krishna-Godavari coast after the Pallava wars
The coastal delta around Vengi alone
The southern Tamil region around Kandarapuram
54.x: Early records and forts at Amrabad, Keesaragutta and Indrapalanagara point to Telangana as the original home. The Vishnukundins later expanded into coastal Andhra.
54.tq: Infer the original homeland from the distribution of early forts and records.
xs: Early records and forts show **Telangana** — **Amrabad, Keesaragutta, Indrapalanagara** — as the original home — option **(1)**.
They first ruled Telangana **north of the Krishna**, then expanded to **coastal Andhra**.
xa: **Keesaragutta** = possibly their start as **Vakataka feudatories**.
**Indrapalanagara** = **Tummalagudem**, built by **Indravarma**.
**Amarapura** = **Munnanuru** (Amrabad, Nagarkurnool), where **yaga-vedikas** were found.

54.s: Keesaragutta may mark the beginning of the Vishnukundins as feudatories of which dynasty?
54.x: Keesaragutta may mark their start as Vakataka feudatories; the founder Indravarma was a Vakataka vassal.

54.s: With which place is the name of the Vishnukundin dynasty generally linked?
54.x: Historians generally take 'Vishnukundi' as the Sanskrit form of Vinukonda, a hill-fort town in the Guntur (now Palnadu) region.

Records span both Telugu states: **Godavari, Guntur, Telangana**.

54.s: The Vishnukundins formed a link between which two phases of Andhra history?

xs: The Vishnukundins link the **Ikshvaku age** and the **Eastern Chalukyas** — option **(3)**.

xa: Dynasty order: Ikshvakus → **Brihatpalayanas** → **Salankayanas** → Vishnukundins → Eastern Chalukyas.

xa: Buddhism too declined from **MV II** onward.
MV II turned Buddhist sites at **Undavalli** and **Mogalrajapuram** into Hindu shrines.
Family deity **Sriparvataswami** = **Srisaila Mallikarjuna**.

61.s: During the period of the South Indian Campaign of Samudragupta, who was the ruler of Vengi?
61.x: Hastivarman, the Salankayana king of Vengi (Pedavegi), was defeated by Samudragupta; Damana ruled Erandapalle, Mahendra Kosala and Vishnugopa Kanchi.

61.s: Devarashtra is identified with which place of Vishakapatnam district?
61.src: APPSC Asst. BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Mains Paper-II 2017
61.x: Devarashtra, the kingdom of Kubera in the Allahabad Prasasti, is the Yelamanchili area of Visakhapatnam district (NextGen). The old app note placing it at S. Kota (Vizianagaram) is not supported here.

61.s: The Allahabad Pillar Inscription of Samudragupta mentions a conflict between the Guptas and the Vengi king of the Salankayana dynasty. Who is the Salankayana king mentioned in that inscription?
61.x: The Allahabad Prasasti names Hastivarman of Vengi, a Salankayana, among the southern kings; Nandivarman and Chandravarman are other Salankayanas.

61.s:
Consider the following statements:
I. During the reign of Chandragupta-I, the Sakas were defeated.
II. Samudragupta's South Indian conquest did not lead to any permanent annexation.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
61.x: Statement I is false: the Saka (Western Kshatrapa) conquest was Chandragupta II's, not Chandragupta I's (one NextGen page wrongly credits Chandragupta I). Statement II is true: the southern kings were captured and reinstated (grahana-moksha-anugraha), so II only.

61.s: Which Pallava king was defeated by Samudra Gupta?
61.x: Samudragupta defeated Vishnugopa of Kanchi, a Pallava; Kubja Vishnuvardhana is the Eastern Chalukya founder of the 7th century.

61.s: What was the name of the ruler of Kosal in Samudragupta's "Prayag Prashasti"?
61.x: The Prayag Prashasti names Mahendra as king of (Dakshina) Kosala, first of the twelve southern kings; Mahendragiri ruled Pishtapura.

61.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Samudragupta's campaigns?
o: The southern kingdoms were permanently annexed.
Assam, Nepal and Bengal were frontier rulers who paid tribute.
The Ganga-Yamuna region was directly annexed.
The atavika (forest) kingdoms of central India were subdued.
61.x: The southern rulers were defeated and reinstated as tributaries, not permanently annexed; the other three are correct.
xa: **Distant** kings — **Kushanas, Sakas, Sri Lanka**, SE Asia — accepted suzerainty.
The Prashasti sorts opponents into **four groups**.
**12 kings** of Dakshinapatha were reinstated.

61.s: According to Gupta records, which powers paid homage to the Gupta ruler?
61.x: The Kushanas and Sakas were among the distant powers, with Sri Lanka and South-East Asia, that accepted Samudragupta's suzerainty and paid him homage.

61.s:
Consider the following statements about Samudragupta:
1. His empire was confined to Magadha and the middle Ganga valley.
2. His influence reached Simhala.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
61.x: Samudragupta's empire extended from Nepal and Punjab to Kanchi, and his influence reached Simhala.
xa: North: the **Ganga-Yamuna** region was annexed; **Atavika rajyas** subdued.
South: **12 kings** reinstated by **grahana-moksha-anugraha**.
**Meghavarman** of Sri Lanka sent a mission for a monastery at **Bodh Gaya**.

61.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
61.x: Ugrasena was associated with Palakka, not Devarashtra. Devarashtra was ruled by Kubera.
61.tq: Find the swapped ruler–kingdom pair among closely related southern campaign entries.
xs: **Ugrasena — Devarashtra** is wrong — option **(4)**.
**Ugrasena** ruled **Palakka** (Nellore area); **Devarashtra** was **Kubera's**.
Correct: **Nilaraja — Avamukta**, **Mantaraja — Kurala**, **Damana — Erandapalle**.
xa: Devarashtra = **S. Kota, Vizianagaram**.
Avamukta = **Guntur**; Erandapalle = **Srikakulam**.
**Dhananjaya** ruled **Kusthalapura (Arcot)**.

61.s: Vishnugopa, defeated in Samudragupta's southern campaign, was the ruler of which kingdom?
61.x: Vishnugopa was the Pallava king of Kanchi; Vengi was Hastivarman's and Kosala Mahendra's.

61.s:
Match the following:
List-I (King) - List-II (Kingdom)
A. Vyaghraraja - 1. Palakka
B. Ugrasena - 2. Kusthalapura
C. Dhananjaya - 3. Devarashtra
D. Kubera - 4. Mahakantara
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
61.x: Vyaghraraja - Mahakantara; Ugrasena - Palakka (Nellore area); Dhananjaya - Kusthalapura; Kubera - Devarashtra.

61.s:
Consider the following statements about the kingdoms in Samudragupta's southern campaign:
1. Vengi is identified with Pedavegi near Eluru.
2. Erandapalle lay in the Srikakulam area.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
61.x: Vengi = Pedavegi (Eluru) and Erandapalle = Srikakulam area; both were in coastal Andhra.

61.s:
Match List-I (Rulers in the Allahabad Prasasti) with List-II (Samudragupta's treatment):
List-I
a. Kings of Aryavarta
b. Atavika rajyas
c. Frontier kings of Assam, Nepal and Bengal
d. Twelve kings of Dakshinapatha
List-II
1. Paid tribute
2. Captured and released, reinstated as tributaries
3. Slain and their kingdoms annexed
4. Subdued (forest kingdoms)
Select the correct answer:
61.x: North - rulers slain, annexed; Atavika (forest) rajyas - subdued; frontier kings - paid tribute; the 12 southern kings - grahana-moksha-anugraha (captured, released, reinstated), so no permanent annexation in the south.

61.s:
Match List-I (King defeated by Samudragupta) with List-II (Kingdom):
List-I
a. Mahendragiri
b. Swamidatta
c. Damana
d. Kubera
List-II
1. Kottura
2. Devarashtra
3. Erandapalle
4. Pishtapura
Select the correct answer:
61.x: Mahendragiri - Pishtapura (Pithapuram); Swamidatta - Kottura; Damana - Erandapalle (Srikakulam); Kubera - Devarashtra (Yelamanchili area).

61.s:
Consider the following statements about Samudragupta and Andhra:
1. The Allahabad Pillar is the chief source for the 4th-century kings of Vengi, Avamukta and Devarashtra.
2. A Samudragupta-period record is found at Sankaram in Visakhapatnam.
3. Avamukta (Guntur area) was ruled by Ugrasena.
4. Mahendra of Kosala was one of the twelve southern kings he defeated.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
61.x: Statement 3 is wrong: Nilaraja ruled Avamukta; Ugrasena ruled Palakka (Nellore area). Mahendra of Kosala (Mahanadi region) was among the twelve southern kings.

61.s: The first Gupta ruler to assume the title of ‘Parama Bhagawat’ was
61.x:
Most books and the UPPSC official key give Chandragupta II, who used 'Parama Bhagavata' widely on coins and inscriptions. The NextGen Rocket Sheet gives Samudragupta, styled so in the Nalanda and Gaya copper plates (whose genuineness is doubted).
Samudragupta is the first Gupta styled Paramabhagavata, in his Nalanda and Gaya copper plates (NextGen Rocket); Chandragupta II used it regularly on coins and inscriptions, which is why some keys give him.

61.s: Which one of the following Gupta rulers is referred to as ‘Lichchhavi-Dauhitra’ (Son of the daughter of the Lichchhavis)?
61.x: Samudragupta, son of the Lichchhavi princess Kumaradevi, calls himself Lichchhavi-dauhitra in the Allahabad Prasasti; Chandragupta I was the Lichchhavis' son-in-law, not daughter's son.

61.s: Who is called ‘the Napoleon of Ancient India’?
61.x: V.A. Smith called Samudragupta the 'Napoleon of India' for his conquests.

61.s: Who is known as the Napoleon of India?
61.x: Samudragupta (c. 335-375 CE) was named the Napoleon of India by V.A. Smith; Chandragupta II and Ashoka are distractors.

61.s: The first Gupta ruler to assume the title of “Param Bhagavata” was
61.x:
Most books and the UPPSC official key give Chandragupta II, who used 'Parama Bhagavata' widely on coins and inscriptions. The NextGen Rocket Sheet gives Samudragupta, styled so in the Nalanda and Gaya copper plates (whose genuineness is doubted).
The Nalanda and Gaya copper plates style Samudragupta Paramabhagavata, making him the first Gupta with the title (NextGen Rocket). The official UPPSC key gave Chandragupta II, who used it widely on coins.

61.s: ‘Prithivyah Pratham Veer’ was the title of –
61.x: 'Prithivyah Pratham Veer' (first hero of the earth) was Samudragupta's title; Gangaikonda was Rajendra I's and Rajaraja Gautamiputra Satakarni's.

61.s: Who among the following rulers was called Kavi Raja?
61.x: Harisena calls Samudragupta Kaviraja (king of poets), and his lyrist coins show him with the veena.

61.s: Which title of Samudragupta reflected his Vaishnavite association?
61.x: Param Bhagavata, devoted follower of Vishnu, shows Vaishnavite faith and was used by the Gupta rulers, including Samudragupta. Devaputra was Kushana, Maharajadhiraja an imperial title and Satyashraya Chalukya.
61.tq: Link the title to its religious meaning.
n: Samudragupta was titled Param Bhagavata. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 53-55]
Param Bhagavata is a Vaishnavite title. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 53-55]
The recall association for Samudragupta's Param Bhagavata title is Param Bhagavata. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 53-55]
xs: **Param Bhagavata** was Samudragupta's **Vaishnavite title** — option **(1)**.
**Devaputra** was the imperial title of **Kanishka** and the **Kushana rulers**.
**Maharajadhiraja** (supreme king) was first adopted by **Chandragupta I**; **Satyashraya** was a **Chalukya** title of **Pulakeshin II**.
xa: Samudragupta was called the **Napoleon of India** by **V. A. Smith**.
He was **Kaviraja** (king of poets) and **Lichchhavi-dauhitra**.
His **Lyrist (veena-player)** coin type is the basis of **Kaviraja**.
Common imperial titles: **Parameshvara, Maharajadhiraja, Paramabhattaraka**.

61.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Ashoka was known as Devanampiya, meaning ‘Beloved of the Gods’.
Harshavardhana was also known as Shiladitya.
Chandragupta II was known as Satyashraya, meaning ‘Saka-conqueror’.
Kanishka and other Kushana rulers used the title Devaputra.
61.x: Option C is incorrect: Chandragupta II was called Sakari, the Saka-conqueror; Satyashraya was a title of Pulakeshin II. Ashoka as Devanampiya, Harsha as Shiladitya and Kushana Devaputra are right.
61.tq: Match each title with its ruler.
n: Chandragupta II was titled Vikramaditya. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 53-55]
Chandragupta II was titled Sakari. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 53-55]
Sakari means Saka-conqueror. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 53-55]
Ashoka was called Devanampiya or Devanampriya. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 53-55]
Devanampiya means beloved of the Gods. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 53-55]
Kanishka and Kushana rulers used the title Devaputra. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 53-55]
Devaputra was an imperial title. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 53-55]
Harshavardhana was also known as Shiladitya. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 53-55]
Shiladitya was an alternative title or name of Harshavardhana. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 53-55]
Pulakeshin II was titled Satyashraya. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 53-55]
Satyashraya was a Chalukya title. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 53-55]
The recall association for Ashoka's Devanampiya title is Devanampiya. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 53-55]
xs: The incorrect statement is **Chandragupta II as Satyashraya, 'Saka-conqueror'** — option **(3)**.
Chandragupta II's Saka-conqueror title was **Sakari**; **Satyashraya** was a **Chalukya** title of **Pulakeshin II**.
The rest are correct: **Ashoka** = **Devanampiya** (Beloved of the Gods); **Harshavardhana** = **Shiladitya**; **Kanishka** and Kushanas = **Devaputra**.
xa: Chandragupta II was also **Vikramaditya**, **Devagupta, Devaraja, Devashri**.
**Rajaraja I** = **Mummudi Chola**; **Rajendra I** = **Gangaikonda Chola**.
**Gautamiputra Satakarni** = **Rajaraja**; **Vima Kadphises** = **Sarvalokeshvara**.
Ashoka's inscriptional name: **Devanampiya Piyadassi**.

61.s: Which of the following titles was NOT of a Gupta ruler but of the Kushana Kanishka?
61.x: Devaputra was a Kushana title; the others were used by Gupta rulers.

61.s:
Match the following:
List-I (Title) - List-II (Gupta ruler)
A. Kaviraja - 1. Chandragupta II
B. Mahendraditya - 2. Samudragupta
C. Maharajadhiraja (first to assume) - 3. Chandragupta I
D. Sakari - 4. Kumaragupta I
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
61.x: Samudragupta was Kaviraja, Kumaragupta I was Mahendraditya, Chandragupta I was the first Maharajadhiraja and Chandragupta II was Sakari (Saka-conqueror).

61.s:
Consider the following statements about Gupta titles:
1. Sri Gupta and Ghatotkacha bore only the title Maharaja.
2. After the Ashvamedha, Samudragupta took the title Prithivyama Pratiratha ('no rival on earth').
3. V.A. Smith called Samudragupta the 'Napoleon of India'.
4. Kumaragupta I bore the title Vikramaditya.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
61.x: Statement 4 is wrong: Vikramaditya was Chandragupta II's title; Kumaragupta I was Mahendraditya.

61.s:
Consider the following statements about Gupta queens:
1. Duttadevi was the queen of Samudragupta.
2. Anantadevi was the queen of Kumaragupta I.
3. Chandragupta I married Kumaradevi, a Vakataka princess.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
61.x: Statement 3 is wrong: Kumaradevi was a Lichchhavi princess (hence Samudragupta = Lichchhavi-dauhitra).

61.s: Who founded Gupta Dynasty?
61.x: Sri Gupta founded the Gupta dynasty; Chandragupta I was the first great king and real founder of the empire.

61.s: The Gupta Era was Started at:
61.x: The Gupta era (319-20 CE) began with the accession of Chandragupta I; Sri Gupta founded the dynasty but not the era.

61.s: Who of the following was the first Gupta ruler to issue coins?
61.x: The first Gupta coins are the gold king-queen (Chandragupta I-Kumaradevi) type; no coins of Sri Gupta or Ghatotkacha are known. Some scholars think Samudragupta struck them to honour his parents.

61.s: Who established Gupta Samvat?
61.x: Chandragupta I started the Gupta Samvat in 319-20 CE, the year of his accession; Chandragupta II and Ghatotkacha did not.

61.s: The Gupta Samvat was founded by
61.x: The Gupta Samvat (319-20 CE) was founded by Chandragupta I and marks his accession.

61.s: Who was the first Gupta ruler to attain the title of ‘Maharaja Dhiraja’?
61.x: Chandragupta I was the first Gupta to take the title Maharajadhiraja; Sri Gupta and Ghatotkacha were only Maharaja.

61.s: Which of the following city was not the capital of the Guptas?
61.x: Gupta capitals were Pataliputra, with Ayodhya, Prayaga and Ujjayini (Chandragupta II's second capital) also named; Varanasi was never a Gupta capital.

61.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the caste origin of the Guptas?
o: They are described as originally Vaishyas
They were later treated as Kshatriyas
A Brahmana origin has been argued from the Dharana gotra
The Junagadh inscription settles their caste origin
61.x: The Junagadh inscription does not settle the question; the Vaishya-to-Kshatriya view and the Dharana gotra argument are both put forward.

61.s: Which ruler came immediately after Samudragupta in the Gupta line?
61.x: Samudragupta was followed by Ramagupta, whom Chandragupta II killed.

61.s:
Arrange the following Gupta rulers in chronological order:
1. Samudragupta
2. Ghatotkacha
3. Chandragupta I
4. Sri Gupta
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
61.x: Sri Gupta founded the line, Ghatotkacha followed, then Chandragupta I and then Samudragupta.

61.s:
Consider the following statements about Chandragupta I:
1. He defeated the Sakas and issued silver coins.
2. His capital was Pataliputra.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
61.x: Chandragupta I ruled from Pataliputra; the Saka victory and silver coins belong to Chandragupta II.

61.s:
Consider the following statements about the early Guptas:
1. Sri Gupta ruled a small area of North Bengal and South Bihar.
2. Sri Gupta was succeeded directly by Chandragupta I.
3. The Vayu Purana places the early Gupta territory in Magadha, Prayag and eastern Uttar Pradesh.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
61.x: Statement 2 is wrong: Sri Gupta was succeeded by Ghatotkacha; Chandragupta I came next.

61.s:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): The Gupta era (Gupta Samvat) begins in 319-320 CE.
Reason (R): Chandragupta I was the first Gupta ruler to take the title Maharajadhiraja.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
61.x: Both are true, but R does not explain A: the Gupta era of 319-320 CE marks the accession of Chandragupta I (c. 319-335 CE); his title Maharajadhiraja is a separate fact.

61.s:
Consider the following statements about Chandragupta I:
1. His queen Kumaradevi was a Lichchhavi princess.
2. His gold king-queen coins carry the legend 'Lichchhavayah'.
3. His capital was Ujjain.
How many of the above statements are correct?
61.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Chandragupta I's capital was Pataliputra.

61.s:
Consider the following statements about Gupta coins:
1. Most Gupta coins were gold dinaras.
2. Samudragupta's lyrist type shows him playing the veena.
3. His Ashvamedha type celebrated his conquests after the horse sacrifice.
4. The king-queen type was issued by Samudragupta.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
61.x: Statement 4 is wrong: the king-queen type (with Kumaradevi) belongs to Chandragupta I.

61.s: The first inscriptional evidence of the Satipratha has been found from –
61.x: The Eran inscription of 510 CE (Bhanugupta's time) records the sati of the wife of commander Goparaja – the first inscriptional evidence of sati; Junagadh, Mandsaur and Sanchi do not.

61.s: Which inscription records the repair of the Sudarshana lake by Parnadatta, the governor of Skandagupta?
61.x: The Junagadh, or Girnar, inscription records that Parnadatta repaired the Sudarshana lake while serving as Skandagupta’s governor.
61.tq: Use the public-works detail to identify the correct inscription.
xs: The **Junagadh (Girnar)** inscription records **Parnadatta's** repair of the **Sudarshana lake** — option **(3)**.
Parnadatta was **Skandagupta's** governor.
**Mehrauli** = Chandragupta II; **Udayagiri** = Virasena; **Bhitari** = Hunas repulsed.
xa: Skandagupta's **Bhitari** record mentions the **Hunas**.
Samudragupta's conquests are **not** in Junagadh but in the **Allahabad Pillar** (**APPSC 2025**).
**Mandsaur** records a silk-weavers' guild.

61.s: The Mehrauli Iron Pillar is correctly associated with which of the following sets of details?
61.x: The Mehrauli Iron Pillar was set up as a Vishnu Dhvaja (standard of Vishnu) on the hill called Vishnupada, so it is dedicated to Vishnu.
61.tq: Recall the deity of the pillar.
n: The Mehrauli Iron Pillar is devoted to Vishnu. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-17]
The Mehrauli Iron Pillar was established as a Vishnu Dhvaja. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-17]
The Mehrauli Iron Pillar is associated with Vishnupada. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-17]
xs: The **Mehrauli Iron Pillar** is linked with **Vishnu, Vishnu Dhvaja and Vishnupada** — option **(1)**.
It was **devoted to Vishnu**, **established** as a **Vishnu Dhvaja** and **associated** with **Vishnupada**.
It names a king **Chandra**, identified as **Chandragupta II**.
xa: It claims conquests in **NW India** and most of **Bengal**.
**Udayagiri** cave (near **Vidisha**) has a **Varaha** image and **Virasena's** record.
**Bhitari Pillar** — **Skandagupta**, **Huna** war.
Chandragupta II's title **Sakari** = Saka-conqueror.

61.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
61.x: The Bhitari Pillar records Skandagupta's war with the Hunas; Mehrauli is Chandragupta II, Junagadh is Skandagupta and Eran is Bhanugupta.

61.s:
Match List-I (Gupta inscription) with List-II (Key fact):
List-I
a. Eran
b. Udayagiri cave
c. Mandsaur
d. Junagadh
List-II

61.x: Eran (510 CE, Bhanugupta) - sati of Goparaja's wife; Udayagiri - Virasena; Mandsaur (Kumaragupta I) - Vatsabhatti, Bandhuvarman; Junagadh (Skandagupta) - Parnadatta repaired the Sudarshana lake.

61.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Mehrauli Iron Pillar records Chandragupta II's conquests in the north-west and Bengal.
2. The Mehrauli Iron Pillar stands in the yard of the Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque, Delhi.
3. The Bhitari Pillar of Skandagupta is in Varanasi district.

61.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Bhitari Pillar is in Ghazipur district, Uttar Pradesh.

61.s:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): Vishakhadatta wrote both the Mudrarakshasa and the Devichandraguptam.
Reason (R): The Mudrarakshasa deals with Ramagupta, Dhruvadevi and Chandragupta II.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
61.x: A is true. R is false: the Mudrarakshasa is about Chanakya and Chandragupta Maurya; the Ramagupta-Dhruvadevi-Chandragupta II story is the Devichandraguptam.

61.s: According to Chinese source, Meghavarman, the ruler of Sri Lanka, sent a missionary to which of the following Gupta Kings for permission to build a Buddhist temple at Gaya?
61.x: A Chinese source records that Meghavarman of Sri Lanka sent a mission to Samudragupta for permission to build a Buddhist monastery at Bodh Gaya.

61.s: Where did Meghavarman of Sri Lanka send a mission to Samudragupta to build a monastery?
61.x: Meghavarman's request to build a monastery at Bodh Gaya is known from a Chinese source.
xa: Meghavarman wanted a **monastery and rest house** at **Bodh Gaya**.
Chandragupta II's sea trade reached **Europe via Egypt**.
Samudragupta's minister: **Vasubandhu**.

62.s: Which Gupta ruler assumed the throne after killing his elder brother?
62.x: Chandragupta II killed his elder brother Ramagupta and married his widow Dhruvadevi (Devichandraguptam). Samudragupta and Skandagupta came to the throne without such a story, and Sri Gupta was the founder.

62.s: The second capital of the Gupta ruler, Chandragupta-II was
62.x: After conquering the Western Kshatrapas, Chandragupta II made Ujjain his second capital. Malwa and Saurashtra are regions, and Mehrauli is the site of his iron pillar.

62.s: After conquering the Shakas, which of the following metal coins were introduced by Chandragupta II?
62.x: After the Saka conquest Chandragupta II issued silver coins on the Western Kshatrapa model for the conquered west. The Guptas' usual gold coins existed before, so gold is the tempting wrong option.

62.s: Who was the first Gupta ruler to issue silver coins?
62.x: Chandragupta II was the first Gupta to issue silver coins, copying Western Kshatrapa coins after the Saka conquest. NextGen 03 p.2 wrongly credits Chandragupta I, whose coins were gold (king-queen type).

62.s: Who is known as ‘Saka-conqueror’?
62.x: Chandragupta II ended Western Kshatrapa (Saka) rule by defeating Rudrasimha III and took the title Sakari, 'Saka-conqueror'. Samudragupta only received homage from the Sakas.

62.s: Who among the following Gupta Kings had another name Devagupta ?
62.x: Devagupta (also Devaraja, Devashri) was another name of Chandragupta II, known from Sanchi and Vakataka records. Samudragupta and Kumaragupta did not bear it.

62.s:
With reference to Chandragupta – II, which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. The strongest evidence in the context of Saka Victory is the silver coins of this King.

64.s: The decline of trade and commerce in North India between 7th and 10th centuries was partly due to the
o: Decline in skills of Indian artisans
64.x: The collapse of the West Roman Empire cut the long-distance trade on which North India had prospered. China and SE Asia did not collapse, and artisans' skills did not decline.

64.s: The gradual decline of towns was an important feature of which period?
64.x: The gradual decline of towns is a feature of the Gupta period: Mathura, Hastinapur, Shravasti declined and Pataliputra became a village by Hiuen-Tsang's time. The other eras are not marked by it.

64.s: From the third century AD when the Huna invasion ended the Roman Empire, the Indian merchants relied more and more on the :
64.x: With the Roman market lost, Indian merchants turned more to South-East Asian trade. African, West European and Middle Eastern trade did not replace it.

64.s: The gradual decline of towns was a important feature of which period?
64.x: The gradual decline of towns is a recognised feature of the Gupta period, with Mathura, Hastinapur and Kaushambi declining. The Pratihara, Rashtrakuta and Satavahana eras are not characterised this way.

64.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. After the fall of Rome, Indian merchants relied more on South-East Asian trade through Tamralipti.
2. The shift to South-East Asian trade revived the economy of North India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
64.x: Merchants turned to South-East Asian trade via Tamralipti after Rome fell, but this did not revive the northern economy.

64.s:
Match List-I (Factor) with List-II (Effect on Indian trade):
List-I | List-II
a. Eastern Roman (Byzantine) trade | i. North-western route blocked; inflow of gold and silver cut
b. Huna invasions | ii. Overland trade hurt after the rise of Islam
c. Sassanid decline | iii. Silk and spice trade till c. 550 CE, ended when the Romans learnt to rear silkworms
d. Fall of the West Roman Empire | iv. Decline of North Indian trade in the 7th–10th centuries
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
64.x: Byzantine trade lasted till about 550 CE and fell when the Romans learnt sericulture; the Hunas blocked the north-west and cut the inflow of gold and silver; the Sassanid decline after Islam hurt overland trade; the fall of the West Roman Empire (476 CE) is the standard cause of the 7th–10th century decline.

64.s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Pataliputra had grown into the largest city of India by the time Hiuen-Tsang came.
Reason (R): R.S. Sharma's 'urban decay' thesis points to shrinking towns and few gold coins in the post-Gupta period.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
64.x: A is false: when Hiuen-Tsang came, Pataliputra had become a village – towns declined gradually in the Gupta period. R is true: it is the basis of Sharma's urban decay and feudalism thesis.

64.s:
Which of the following statements is/are correct about the caste system during the post Gupta period?

a. Abhira tribe fragmented into Abhira Brahmanas, Abhira Kshatriyas and Abhira Shudras

b. Brahmanas were not further divided in subcastes during this period

c. Peasants with unequal access to the economic powers were included in Shudra varna

d. Kayastha communities were involved in record keepings and as scribes
64.src: AP recruitment paper (header page missing in scan)
64.x: Tribes like the Abhiras split into Abhira Brahmanas, Kshatriyas and Shudras, peasants were placed in the Shudra varna and Kayasthas emerged as scribes (a, c, d). Brahmanas themselves split into many subcastes, so b is wrong.

64.s: "Kayastha" is the caste of?
64.x: Kayasthas were a caste of scribes who kept records and accounts. They were not traders or physicians.

64.s: A new sort of social structure known as the Jajmani system became prevalent in India during:
64.x: The jajmani system, linking service castes to landholding patrons, is traced to the post-Gupta period. It does not belong to the Satavahana, Gupta or Mauryan periods.

64.s: Which of the following lawgivers of the post Gupta period declared that Sudras were not slave by nature?
64.x: Medhatithi, the post-Gupta (9th c.) commentator on the Manusmriti, held that Shudras were not slaves by nature. Vijnaneshvara (Mitakshara), Narada and Jimutavahana (Dayabhaga) are other jurists.

64.s: During which age did women enjoy equality with men?
64.x: No period gave women equality with men; in the Gupta age their status fell (early marriage, no property rights), so 'None of these'.

64.s: Which of the following pairs of land types is correctly matched?
64.x: Maru meant desert. Urvara was fertile, usara barren and aprahata fallow land.
xa: **Amarakosha** lists **12 types of land**.
**Shadvala** = grassy; **Pankila** = muddy.
In another table **Aprahata** = forest / uncultivated.

64.s: How many types of land does the Amarakosha, attributed to Amarasimha, list?
64.x: Amarakosha lists 12 types of land.
64.tq: Use the exact numerical value and reject nearby counts from other classifications.
xs: **Amarakosha** of **Amarasimha** lists **12 types of land** — option **(2)**.
Examples: **urvara** (fertile), **usara** (barren), **maru** (desert), **aprahata** (fallow).
xa: Also **shadvala** (grassy) and **pankila** (muddy).
Other terms: **Kshetra** = cultivable; **Khila** = waste; **Vastu** = habitable.
The **Sudarshana lake** at **Girnar** was repaired under **Skandagupta**.

64.s:
Consider the following statements about Gupta and post-Gupta society:
1. Castes multiplied into sub-castes by absorbing foreigners and tribes.
2. The jajmani system tied hereditary service castes to landowning patrons for a share of the produce.
3. The Narada Smriti lists 12 types of slaves.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
64.x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: the Narada Smriti lists 15 types of slaves.

64.s:
Consider the following statements about women in the Gupta period:
1. The law books advised pre-puberty marriage of girls.
2. Stridhana, over which women had control, consisted of ancestral land.
3. Svayamvara gave way to marriages arranged by parents.
4. The Eran inscription of 510 CE records the sati of the wife of Bhanugupta.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
64.x: Two are correct (1 and 3). 2 is wrong: stridhana consisted of marriage gifts; women had no general property rights. 4 is wrong: the Eran record (510 CE) is of the wife of Goparaja, a general / friend of Bhanugupta.

64.s: Which of the following was NOT the feature of the Guilds during the Gupta Period ?
64.x: Gupta guilds were autonomous bodies with their own laws, judicial powers and even armed bodies. So 'non-autonomous bodies' is the feature they did not have.

64.s: In relation to the Dashpur inscription of Kumaragupta and Bandhuvarman, which statement is incorrect?
o: The inscription mentions the construction of the Sun
It is oldest example of the advertisement tradition in
The inscription also refers to Dashpur as Pashchimapur
The inscription was composed by Bhavabhuti
64.x: The Dashpur inscription was composed by Vatsabhatti, not Bhavabhuti, so option 4 is incorrect. It does record the Sun temple, praises silk cloth (oldest advertisement) and calls Dashpur Pashchimapur.

64.s: Which of the following inscription reveals information about Silk Weavers Guild?
64.x: The Dashpur (Mandsaur) inscription records the silk weavers' guild that built and repaired a Sun temple. The Prayag, Eran and Hathigumpha records do not.

64.s: Which of the following inscriptions is known as the first advertisement of the World?
64.x: The Dashpur (Mandsaur) inscription of Kumaragupta I's time, praising silk cloth, is called the first advertisement. Sohgaura, Supia and Eran are other records.

64.s: From where did the silk-weavers' guild of the Mandsaur (Dashpur) inscription migrate to Dashpur?
64.x: The guild came from Lata in Gujarat and built a Sun temple at Dashpur; weavers changing profession point to falling silk demand.
xa: Temple built **436–37 CE**, repaired **473 CE**.
Composed by **Vatsabhatti**, not Bhava.
Called the **oldest advertisement** in Indian tradition.

64.s:
Match List-I (Record) with List-II (Guild fact):
List-I | List-II
a. Dashpur (Mandsaur) inscription | i. Repair of the Sudarshana lake by Parnadatta
b. Indore copper plate | ii. Guilds acting as banks; town board
c. Damodarpur copper plates | iii. Silk weavers built a Sun temple
d. Junagadh inscription | iv. Guild of oil-men maintained a lamp in a Sun temple
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
64.x: Dashpur – silk weavers' Sun temple (Kumaragupta I, Bandhuvarman); Indore plate (Skandagupta) – oil-men's guild; Damodarpur plates – guilds as banks and the town board; Junagadh – Parnadatta's repair of the Sudarshana lake.

64.s:
Consider the following statements about Gupta guilds:
1. Some guilds maintained their own armed bodies.
2. The head of a guild was called the Sarthavaha.
3. The Dashpur inscription was composed by Vatsabhatti.
4. The Indore copper plate recording the oil-men's guild belongs to Skandagupta's reign.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
64.x: Three are correct. 2 is wrong: the head of a guild was the Sreshthi / Setti; the Sarthavaha was the caravan trader.

64.s: In his travels through India, Fahhien has mentioned a hospital, it was located at
64.x: Fa-hien described a free hospital at Pataliputra endowed by citizens, where the poor got doctors, food and medicine. Tamralipti was only his port of departure.

64.s: Fa-hien’s mission to India was to
o: learn about the administrative system of the Gupta kings.
understand the social position of women during the Gupta period.
visit the Buddhist institutions and to collect copies of Buddhist manuscripts.
get full knowledge about the condition of peasants during the period of Gupta kings.
64.x: Fa-hien came to visit Buddhist sites and collect Buddhist manuscripts; his focus on Buddhism is why he never named the king. He did not come to study administration, women or peasants.

64.s: In travel through India Fa-hien has mentioned a hospital, it was located at
64.x: Fa-hien recorded a free hospital at Pataliputra funded by citizens, giving poor patients doctors, food and medicine. Tamralipti was only his port of departure.

64.s: According to Fa-Hien, how did the Chandalas announce their approach?
64.x: Fa-Hien noted that Chandalas lived outside villages and towns and struck wood to warn others.
xa: Fa-Hien came in the reign of **Chandragupta II**, c. **399-414 CE**, but never named the king.
His account: **Fo-kwo-ki** ("Record of Buddhist Kingdoms").
He saw **free hospitals** at **Pataliputra** and **20 viharas at Mathura**.
**Cowrie shells** were used in daily exchange; he returned by sea via **Tamralipti and Sri Lanka**.

64.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about society as described by Fa-Hien?
o: Chandalas followed the same food restrictions as everyone else.
Cowrie shells were used in daily exchange.
Hindus and Buddhists lived in harmony.
The people were peaceful and prosperous.
64.x: The Chandalas were an exception to the general food restrictions; the other three are Fa-Hien's observations.
xa: Government was **mild** with **few taxes**.
**No death penalty**; fines instead.
**Free hospitals** at Pataliputra; **rest houses** on highways.

64.s: Which of the following places did Fa-Hien NOT describe as a centre of Buddhist decay?
64.x: Fa-Hien saw decay at Kapilavastu, Gaya and Kushinagar, but found 20 viharas flourishing at Mathura.

64.s:
Consider the following statements about Fa-hien:
1. He came overland via Central Asia and Gandhara and returned by sea via Sri Lanka.
2. His account is known as the Si-yu-ki.
3. He visited India during the reign of Kumaragupta I.
4. He saw 20 viharas at Mathura.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
64.x: Two are correct (1 and 4). 2 is wrong: his account is the Fo-kwo-ki; Si-yu-ki is Hiuen-Tsang's. 3 is wrong: he came c. 399–412 CE, under Chandragupta II.

64.s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Fa-hien records that ordinary daily exchange was carried on with cowries.
Reason (R): The Guptas issued gold coins only in very small numbers.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
64.x: A is true (Fa-hien). R is false: the gold dinara was issued in the largest numbers; it is copper coins that are very few.

65.s: The ornament in the chest of Lord Vishnu
65.x: The Kaustubha gem, which rose from the churning of the ocean, adorns Vishnu's chest. Marakatham (emerald), Manikyam (ruby) and Pagadam (coral) are ordinary gems.

65.s: Who were the first to worship Vasudeva Krishna :
65.x: The Bhagavatas (Vasudevakas) were the first worshippers of Vasudeva-Krishna, known from Panini's time. Vedic Aryans worshipped nature gods, and the Tamils and Abhiras are not credited with it.

65.s: Who contributes the most in the development of Bhagavata sect?
65.x: Bhagavatism peaked under the Guptas, who made it virtually the state religion and styled themselves Parama Bhagavata with Garuda as emblem. Indo-Greeks like Heliodorus were only early patrons.

65.s: The earliest known epigraphic evidence of Bhagvatism is :
65.x: The Besnagar Garuda pillar of Heliodorus (2nd c. BCE) is the earliest epigraphic evidence of Bhagavatism. The Prayag prashasti, Nasik and Ayodhya records are later.

65.s: Which incarnation of Vishnu is depicted as saving the Earth from the Sea?
65.x: In the Varaha (boar) avatar Vishnu killed Hiranyaksha and lifted the Earth from the cosmic ocean on his tusks. Matsya saved Manu from the flood, Kurma bore Mount Mandara and Narasimha killed Hiranyakashipu.

65.s: The earliest known epigraphic evidence of Bhagavatism is
65.x: The Garuda column at Besnagar, set up by the Greek envoy Heliodorus, is the earliest epigraphic evidence of Bhagavatism. Samudragupta's Prayag prashasti is much later.

65.s: The originator of Bhagavata Religion was –
65.x: The Bhagavata religion goes back to Vasudeva-Krishna of the Vrishni (Satvata) clan, son of Devaki. Janaka and Yajnavalkya are Upanishadic figures and Surdas a medieval poet.

65.s:

Avatar:
(A) Matsya (The Fish)
(B) Kurma (The Tortoise)
(C) Varaha (The Boar)
(D) Narasimha (The Man-Lion)
Sequence: (i) First (ii) Second (iii) Third (iv) Fourth

65.x: The Dashavatara order begins Matsya, Kurma, Varaha, Narasimha. Off-topic, moved.

65.s: The incarnation of Lord Vishnu in Dwapara Yuga was
65.x: Krishna is the avatar of the Dvapara Yuga (Dwarka is its dham); Rama belongs to the Treta Yuga, Vamana and Narasimha to earlier yugas.

65.s: Nandivarman II's Pedavegi inscription is regarded as the first inscription in Andhra Pradesh relating to which of the following?
65.x: The Pedavegi inscription of Nandivarman II is regarded as the first inscription in Andhra Pradesh concerning Vishnu temples.
xa: Salankayanas also used Shaiva **Parama Mahesvara** titles.
**Gudimallam's Parasurameswara** temple = oldest Shiva linga (APPSC G2 **2008**).
**Kapalikas**: **Bhairavakonda** caves.

65.s:
Consider the following statements about early Bhagavatism:
1. It centred on Vasudeva-Krishna of the Vrishni (Satvata) clan.
2. Heliodorus, who set up the Garuda pillar at Besnagar, was the envoy of the Indo-Greek king Menander.
3. Heliodorus served at the court of the Sunga king Bhagabhadra.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
65.x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: Heliodorus was the envoy of the Indo-Greek king Antialcidas.

65.s:
Consider the following statements about Gupta Vaishnavism:
1. Samudragupta was the first Gupta ruler to style himself Parama Bhagavata.
2. The dynastic emblem of the Guptas was Nandi.
3. Gupta Vaishnavism preached the theory of ten incarnations of Vishnu.
4. The colossal Varaha panel at Udayagiri was carved under Chandragupta II.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
65.x: Three are correct. 2 is wrong: the Gupta dynastic emblem was Garuda, Vishnu's mount.

65.s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): The Salankayana rulers of Andhra were Vaishnavas.
Reason (R): The Salankayanas used the title Parama Mahesvara.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
65.x: Both are true, but R does not explain A: Parama Mahesvara is a Shaiva title, used by the Vaishnava Salankayanas.

65.s: With which religion is Kalika Purana associated ?
65.x: The Kalika Purana is an upapurana of the Shakta (goddess) tradition, probably composed in Assam. It is not Vaishnava, Buddhist or Jain.

65.s: Kalika Purana is associated with which of the following religion?
65.x: The Kalika Purana belongs to Shaktism, the worship of the goddess. It is not a Vaishnava, Buddhist or Jain text.

65.s: Who are the worshippers of Kapalini?
65.x: Kapalini, the skull-bearing form of the goddess consort of Kapali-Bhairava, was worshipped by the Kapalikas. Kalika is a goddess, not a sect, and the Shaktas and Vaishnavas are broader traditions.

65.s: The Kapalikas emerged from the school of:
65.x: The NextGen APPSC fact list states that the Kapalikas emerged from the Misra Saivam school, which is the APPSC key. Pashupata is the oldest Shaiva sect, and Vaishnavam is a different tradition.

65.s: Which one of the following was a Shaiva sect in ancient India?
65.x: Mattamayura was a Shaiva sect known from Chedi (Kalachuri) inscriptions. The Ajivikas were a heterodox sect, Mayamata is an architecture text and Isanasivagurudeva Paddhati a ritual manual.

65.s: Ardhanarishvara, a figure of half Shiva and half Parvati, represents
o: Union of God with his Shakti
65.x: Ardhanarishvara, half Shiva and half Parvati, shows the god united with his Shakti. 'Union of male and female' and 'god and goddess' are looser versions of the same idea.

65.s: The five traditional subjects of the Puranas include which of the following?
o: Trade, taxation, diplomacy, warfare and agriculture
Creation, re-creation, genealogies, manvantaras and dynastic history
Ritual, pilgrimage, music, dance and sculpture
Grammar, logic, medicine, astronomy and architecture
65.x: The pancha-lakshana of the Puranas consists of creation, re-creation, genealogies, manvantaras and dynastic history.
65.tq: Recall the five-part classification as a complete group.
xs: **Pancha-lakshana**: **creation, re-creation, genealogies, manvantaras, dynastic history** — option **(2)**.
These are the Puranas' **five topics**.
xa: **18 Mahapuranas** (APPSC-G2 **2011**).
Final shape in the **Gupta period** (c. 4th–6th c. CE).
**Smriti** texts: **Yajnavalkya, Narada, Brihaspati, Katyayana**.

65.s:
Consider the following statements about the Kalika Purana:
1. It is one of the 18 Mahapuranas.
2. It was likely written in Assam.
3. It is associated with Shaktism.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
65.x: The Kalika Purana is a Shakta upapurana, likely written in Assam, not a Mahapurana.

65.s:
Match List-I (Sect) with List-II (Associated fact):
List-I | List-II
a. Pashupata | i. Bhairava worship; Bhairavakonda caves
b. Kalamukha | ii. Followers of Kalanana; Simha Parishat in Andhra
c. Kapalika | iii. Matsyendranath and Gorakhnath
d. Nathpanth | iv. Oldest Shaiva sect, founded by Lakulisha
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
65.x: Pashupata – oldest, founder Lakulisha; Kalamukha – followers of Kalanana, a disciple of Lakulisha, Simha Parishat in Andhra; Kapalika – skull-bearing Bhairava worshippers, Bhairavakonda caves, Srisailam; Nathpanth – Matsyendranath and Gorakhnath.

65.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Gudimallam in Tirupati district has the earliest known Shiva linga.
2. The Gupta ekamukhalinga is a linga bearing four faces of Shiva.
3. Tantrism, open to women and Shudras, spread from the fifth century.
4. The Kalamukha and Pashupata sects later flourished under the Kakatiyas.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
65.x: Three are correct. 2 is wrong: the ekamukhalinga is a linga with ONE face.

65.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Eighteen Mahapuranas are traditionally recognised.
2. The Puranas took their final shape in the Kushana period.
3. The silk-weavers' guild built the Sun temple at Mandsaur in the reign of Skandagupta.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
65.x: Only 1 is correct. 2 is wrong: the Puranas took their final shape in the Gupta period. 3 is wrong: the Mandsaur Sun temple was built under Kumaragupta I; Skandagupta's Indore plate endows a lamp in a Sun temple.

65.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Pashupata sect, the oldest Shaiva sect, was founded by Lakulisha.
2. The Kapalikas were an extremist Vaishnava sect.
3. Durga, Amba, Kali and Chandi were worshipped as mother goddesses.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
65.x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the skull-bearing Kapalikas were a Shaiva sect (Bhairava worship).

65.s: At which place out of the following a Gupta era temple is not found?
65.x: Gupta-period temples survive at Bhitargaon (brick temple, Kanpur), Deogarh (Dashavatara) and Bhitari (Ghazipur, Skandagupta's excavated Vishnu temples). Rajgir is known for Buddhist and earlier Magadhan sites, not a Gupta temple.

65.s: The Dasavatara Temple at Deogarh belongs to which period?
65.x: The Dashavatara temple at Deogarh is a Gupta temple (c. 6th c. CE) of the early Nagara style, depicting Vishnu's ten avatars. The Pallavas, Cholas and Vijayanagara built in the south and later.

65.s: With reference to the cultural history of India, the term 'Panchayatan' refers to
65.x: Panchayatana is a style of temple construction with the main shrine and four subsidiary shrines. It is not a village assembly, sect or office.

65.s: With reference to the cultural history of India, the term 'Panchayatan' refers to –
65.x: Panchayatana is a temple plan with a central shrine and four subsidiary shrines, as at Deogarh. It is not an assembly, a sect or a functionary.

65.s: The temple of Deogarh near Jhansi and the sculptures in the temple at Garhwa near Allahabad are the important remains of the
o: More than one of the above
65.x: The Deogarh temple near Jhansi and the Garhwa sculptures near Allahabad are remains of Gupta art. The Mauryas built no such temples and the Rashtrakutas worked in the Deccan.

65.s:
With reference to the temple of Bhitargaon, Kanpur, Uttar Pradesh, which of the following statements is/ are correct?
(1) This temple was constructed during 5th century A.D. to 6th century A.D.
(2) It is one of the oldest brick temples of India.
Select the correct answer using the code given below-
65.x: Both are correct: the Bhitargaon temple (Kanpur) is a Gupta brick temple of the 5th–6th century with terracotta panels, one of the oldest brick temples of India.

65.s: Which of the following temple – stage pairs is NOT correctly matched?
65.x: Deogarh belongs to the third stage, like Bhitargaon; Sanchi Temple 17 and Tigawa are first stage and Nachna second.

65.s:
Consider the following statements about the Bhitargaon temple:
1. It is a Buddhist chaitya.
2. It belongs to the third stage of Gupta temple architecture.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
65.x: Bhitargaon is a third-stage Gupta Hindu temple, not a Buddhist chaitya.

65.s: Which Gupta temple has two flanking shrines at the entrance?
65.x: Bhumara has flanking shrines; Sanchi 17 a flat roof, Nachna a covered ambulatory and Deogarh a shikhara with panchayatana plan.
xa: Sanchi 17 is in **Raisen**, MP; Tigawa (also stage 1) is in **Katni**.
Bhitargaon (Kanpur) is the stage 3 **brick** temple with **terracotta panels**.
Stage 3 = the **start of Nagara** style.

65.s: The stage-3 Gupta temple with a low square shikhara and panchayatana plan marks the start of which style?
65.x: Stage 3 (low shikhara, high jagati, panchayatana) marks the beginning of the northern Nagara style.

65.s:
Consider the following statements about the stages of Gupta temple building:
1. Stage 1 temples had a square sanctum and a flat roof.
2. Stage 2 temples added a covered ambulatory.
3. Stage 3 temples had no shikhara.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
65.x: Stage 1 had a flat roof and stage 2 a covered ambulatory; stage 3 had a low square shikhara, so statement 3 is wrong.

65.s:
Match List-I (Gupta temple) with List-II (Feature):
List-I | List-II
a. Temple 17, Sanchi | i. Low square shikhara and Panchayatana plan – third stage
b. Parvati temple, Nachna | ii. Flat roof and square sanctum – first stage
c. Shiva temple, Bhumara | iii. Covered ambulatory, two-storeyed – second stage
d. Dashavatara temple, Deogarh | iv. Two flanking shrines – second stage

65.x: Sanchi Temple 17 – flat-roofed first stage; Nachna (Parvati) – covered ambulatory; Bhumara (Shiva) – two flanking shrines; Deogarh (Dashavatara, Vishnu) – low shikhara and Panchayatana, third stage.

65.s:
Consider the following statements about Gupta temples:

2. The earliest surviving free-standing Hindu temples belong to the Kushana period.
3. The Dashavatara temple of Deogarh is in Kanpur district.
4. The Deogarh temple is the earliest Panchayatana temple of North India.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
65.x: Two are correct (1 and 4). 2 is wrong: the earliest free-standing Hindu temples survive from the Gupta age. 3 is wrong: Deogarh is in Lalitpur district near Jhansi; Bhitargaon is near Kanpur.

65.s: What was the name of weapon which was made from Dadhichi's back bone?
65.x: Indra's thunderbolt, the Vajrayudha, was made from the backbone of sage Dadhichi to kill Vritra. Pashupata was Shiva's weapon, Brahmastra Brahma's and Gandiva Arjuna's bow.

68.s: What was one important consequence of the exhaustion of all three powers involved in the struggle for Kannauj?

The immediate restoration of Harsha's empire
The emergence of new Rajput states such as the Chandelas and Chauhans

**Chauhans** were not a party to the struggle itself.

n: The Khalimpur Inscription is associated with Dharmapala. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-17]

69.x: The Lakshmana era (Lakshmana Samvat, reckoned from c. 1119 AD) is named after the Sena king Lakshmanasena of Bengal; the Pratiharas, Palas and Chauhans started no such era.

70.s: The Gurjar-Pratihara dynasty was founded by :
70.x: Nagabhata I (c. 730–760), who repulsed the Arabs, founded the imperial Gurjara-Pratihara line; Vatsaraja and Mihira Bhoja came later and Harsha was a Pushyabhuti.

70.s: Which one of the following ruler is not related to Gurjar-Pratihara dynasty?
70.x: Bhartripatta (Bharatrabhatta) I was a Guhila of Mewar; Nagabhata I, Mahendrapala I and a later Devapala (c. 948–954) were Pratihara kings.

70.s:
Arrange the names of the following historical personalities in correct chronological order and select the correct answer from the codes given below:
1. Nagabhatta II
2. Mahipala
3. Mahendrapala
4. Vatsaraja
Codes :
70.x: Vatsaraja (c. 780–800), Nagabhata II (800–833), Mahendrapala I (885–910), Mahipala (912–944): 4, 1, 3, 2.

70.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Kannauj around 916 CE — Mahipala I defeated Indra III
Bundelkhand campaign — Govinda III defeated Nagabhata II
Early ninth-century Kannauj — Nagabhata II defeated Chakrayudha
70.x: Around 916 CE, Indra III defeated Mahipala I and sacked Kannauj. The other three pairs correctly identify the campaigns and victors.
70.tq: Find the reversed victor–defeated pair in the battle table.
xs: "**Mahipala I** defeated **Indra III**" is wrong — option **(1)** is the answer.
Around **916**, **Indra III** sacked Kannauj, defeating Mahipala I.
**Govinda III** beat **Nagabhata II** (Bundelkhand); Nagabhata II ousted **Chakrayudha** and beat **Dharmapala** near **Monghyr**.
xa: **Mahmud of Ghazni** attacked Kannauj in **1018**.
⚠ **Vatsaraja** lost to Dhruva; **Nagabhata II** to Govinda III.
Rajashekhara served **Mahipala I** as well as Mahendrapala I.

70.s:
Match List-I (Pratihara ruler) with List-II (Event):
List-I | List-II
a. Vatsaraja | i. Ousted Chakrayudha and made Kannauj the capital
b. Nagabhata II | ii. Kannauj looted by Indra III c. 916
c. Mahendrapala I | iii. Bore the title 'Maharajadhiraja of Aryavarta'
d. Mahipala I | iv. Defeated by Dhruva, starting the tripartite struggle
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
70.x: Vatsaraja took Kannauj but was defeated by Dhruva; Nagabhata II ousted Chakrayudha and made Kannauj the capital; Mahendrapala I was 'Maharajadhiraja of Aryavarta'; under Mahipala I, Indra III looted Kannauj (c. 916).

70.s:
Consider the following statements about the early Pratiharas:
1. Nagabhata I, the founder, had his capital at Ujjain (Avanti).
2. Nagabhata II defeated the Pala Dharmapala near Bhagalpur.
3. Nagabhata II was defeated by the Rashtrakuta Govinda III.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
70.x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: Nagabhata II defeated Dharmapala near Monghyr, not Bhagalpur.

70.s: 'Aadi Varaha' was the title of which Gurjar Pratihara ruler?
70.x: Mihira Bhoja, a Vaishnava, took the titles Adivaraha and Prabhasa; Adivaraha appears on his coins.

70.s: The greatest Pratihara King was –
70.x: Mihira Bhoja (836–885) was the greatest Pratihara king. Dharmapala was a Pala, Harsha a Pushyabhuti, and Mahendrapala I was Bhoja's son.

70.s: What is/are not true about King Mihir Bhoja? (i) He was the son of Nagabhatta-II (ii) Kannauj was the capital of his kingdom. (iii)Arab traveller Al-Masudi gave him name of King Baura.
70.x: Only (i) is false: Mihira Bhoja was the son of Ramabhadra and grandson of Nagabhata II. Kannauj was his capital, and Al-Masudi called the king 'Baura'.

70.s:
Consider the following statements about Mihira Bhoja:
1. He was the son of Ramabhadra.
2. He was the grandson of Nagabhata II.
3. His coins carry a Shaiva legend.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
70.x: Mihira Bhoja was Ramabhadra's son and Nagabhata II's grandson. His coins carry the Vaishnava legend Adivaraha, not a Shaiva one.

70.s:
Consider the following statements about Mihira Bhoja:
1. Besides Adivaraha, he bore the title Prabhasa.
2. He recovered Kannauj around 836 AD and made it his capital.
3. His expansion was checked by Sankaravarman of Kashmir.
4. His Gwalior prashasti was composed by Rajashekhara.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
70.x: Three are correct. 4 is wrong: the Gwalior prashasti was composed by the court poet Baladitya; Rajashekhara lived at the court of Mahendrapala I and Mahipala I.

70.s: The great Sanskrit poet and dramatist Rajashekhara was in the court of:
70.x: Rajashekhara (Karpuramanjari, Kavyamimamsa) was the court poet of the Pratihara Mahendrapala I and also of his son Mahipala I; Mahendrapala I is the standard answer.

70.s: The great Sanskrit poet and dramatist, Raj Shekhara was in the court of
70.x: Rajashekhara was the court poet of Mahendrapala I (and later Mahipala I), not of Raja Bhoja of Dhar or the Rashtrakuta Indra III.

70.s: Which of the following works was NOT written by Rajashekhara?
70.x: Prabandhachintamani was written by Merutunga, whereas Kavyamimamsa, Karpuramanjari and Viddhasalabhanjika were works of Rajashekhara.
70.tq: Use the author–work distinction to identify the wrongly attributed work.
xs: **Prabandhachintamani** is not Rajashekhara's — it is by **Merutunga** — option **(3)** is the answer (MPPSC 2025).
Rajashekhara wrote **Kavyamimamsa**, **Karpuramanjari** and **Viddhasalabhanjika**.
xa: **Kavyamimamsa** is on poetics; **Karpuramanjari** is a **Prakrit play**.
Rajashekhara was court poet of **Mahendrapala I** (and **Mahipala I**).

70.s: Who wrote the Prabandhachintamani?
70.x: Prabandhachintamani is Merutunga's work, not Rajashekhara's.

70.s: The Arab traveller Suleman visited India in the reign of Pratihar King –
70.x: The Arab merchant Sulaiman (c. 851) wrote of the Pratihara kingdom in the reign of Mihira Bhoja (Bhoja I), praising his cavalry.

70.s:
Consider the following statements about Arab accounts of the Pratiharas:
1. Sulaiman called the Pratihara kingdom Juzr (Al-Juzr).
2. Al-Masudi called the Pratihara king Balhara.
3. Sulaiman named the Rashtrakuta Amoghavarsha I one of the four great kings of the world.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
70.x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: Al-Masudi called the Pratihara king (Bhoja) Baura.

70.s: Where was the early seat of the Gurjaras?
70.x: Bhinmal in Rajasthan was the early Gurjara seat; Ujjain and then Kannauj (Mahodaya) came later.

70.s: By what other name was Kannauj, the Pratihara capital from Nagabhata II's time, known?
70.x: Kannauj was also called Mahodaya; the Barah copper plate of Bhoja mentions a camp there.

70.s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): The Pratiharas claimed descent from Lakshmana.
Reason (R): The word 'Pratihara' means door-keeper, and Lakshmana was the door-keeper brother of Rama.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
70.x: Both are true and R explains A: 'Pratihara' means door-keeper, and the dynasty traced itself to Lakshmana, Rama's door-keeper brother.

70.s:
Match List-I (Source) with List-II (What it records):
List-I | List-II
a. Prithviraj Raso | i. A camp (skandhavara) at Mahodaya

Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
70.x: Prithviraj Raso – Agnikula legend (Pratiharas, Chaulukyas, Paramaras, Chauhans born at Mount Abu); Aihole inscription – first mention of the Gurjaras (with the Harshacharita); Barah copper plate – camp at Mahodaya; Gwalior prashasti of Mihira Bhoja – composed by Baladitya.

70.s:
Consider the following statements about resistance to the Arabs:
1. Muhammad bin Qasim took Sindh in 712, defeating and killing Raja Dahir.
2. The Gwalior inscription says Nagabhata I crushed the mleccha (Arab) army.
3. Thanks to the Pratiharas, Arab rule stayed confined to Gujarat and Malwa.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
70.x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: Arab rule stayed confined to Sindh and Multan; the Pratiharas were the main barrier.

70.s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Mahmud of Ghazni attacked Kannauj in 1018.
Reason (R): The Chandelas of Khajuraho were among the feudatories who broke away from the Pratiharas.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
70.x: Both are true, but R does not explain A: the Ghaznavid raid of 1018 and the break-away of feudatories like the Chandelas were separate factors in the Pratihara decline.

71.s: The magnificent temple of Kailasa was erected by
71.x: The monolithic Kailasa temple (Ellora Cave 16) was carved under the Rashtrakuta Krishna I, not Govinda II, Krishna II or Dantidurga.

71.s: Which of the following is wrongly matched with respect to Rashtrakutas?
o: Amoghavarsha: the first Kannada book writer
Dantidurga: the founder of Rashtrakuta kingdom
Krishna-III: the famous rock-cut temple of Shiva at Ellora
71.x: The wrong pair is Krishna III – Ellora: the Kailasa rock-cut Shiva temple was carved under Krishna I. Amoghavarsha's Kavirajamarga is the earliest available Kannada book, Dantidurga founded the dynasty, and Al-Masudi (915–16) wrote of the 'Balhara' (Vallabharaja).

71.s: Which among the following Rashtrakuta ruler built the Kailas temple of Ellora?
71.x: The Kailasa temple of Ellora was built by Krishna I; Govinda II, Amoghavarsha and Indra III are known for other things.

71.s: Who among the following was born in a military camp in the course of his father’s campaign?
71.x: Amoghavarsha I was born in 800 AD in a military camp at Shribhavan on the Narmada while his father Govinda III was returning from the north.

71.s: Which Rashtrakuta ruler built the famous Shiva temple of Ellora?
71.x: Krishna I built the rock-cut Shiva (Kailasa) temple at Ellora, not Dantidurga, Krishna II or Govinda III.

71.s: Kailasa temple of Ellora was constituted by
71.x: The Kailasa temple at Ellora was built by Krishna I; Krishna III is the usual trap.

71.s:
Consider the following statements about the order of Rashtrakuta rulers:
1. Dantidurga ruled from 753 to 756.
2. Dhruva ruled before Govinda III.
3. Amoghavarsha I ruled before Govinda III.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
71.x: The order is Dantidurga (753-756), Dhruva (780-793), Govinda III (793-814) and Amoghavarsha I (814-878). Amoghavarsha I came after Govinda III.

71.s: Amoghavarsha I is particularly associated with which of the following combinations?
71.x: Amoghavarsha I built Manyakheta, was associated with Kavirajamarga, and is described as a Jain ruler or patron.
71.tq: Use a cluster of contributions to identify the ruler rather than relying on a single isolated fact.
xs: Amoghavarsha I = **Manyakheta**, **Kavirajamarga** and **Jainism** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Kailasa** = Krishna I; **Takkolam** = Krishna III; **Gadayuddha** = **Ranna**; **Hiranyagarbha** = Dantidurga.
xa: Amoghavarsha won at **Vingavalli** (title **Viranarayana**); also titled **Nripatunga**.
He also wrote the Sanskrit Jain text **Prashnottara Ratnamalika**.
**Sulaiman** called him one of the **four great kings** of the world.

71.s:
Match List-I (Rashtrakuta ruler) with List-II (Achievement):
List-I | List-II
a. Dhruva | i. First Rashtrakuta to march into northern India
b. Govinda III | ii. Defeated the Cholas at Takkolam (949)
c. Indra III | iii. Defeated Nagabhata II and Dharmapala and reached the Himalayas
d. Krishna III | iv. Looted Kannauj c. 916
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
71.x: Dhruva was the first to go north (beat Vatsaraja and Dharmapala); Govinda III beat Nagabhata II and Dharmapala and reached the Himalayas; Indra III looted Kannauj c. 916; Krishna III beat the Cholas at Takkolam in 949.

71.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Kailasa temple of Krishna I is Cave 16 at Ellora.
2. Govinda III's campaign up to the Himalayas is described in the Sanjan plates.
3. The Kailasa temple at Ellora is built in the Vesara style.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
71.x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: the Kailasa temple is a Shaiva temple in the Dravidian style.

71.s: Which Telugu scholar wrote the poem "Vikramarjuna Vijayam" in Kannada?
71.x: Pampa (Pampana), a Jain poet of Telugu origin at the court of the Vemulavada Chalukya Arikesari II, wrote Vikramarjuna Vijayam (Pampa Bharata) in Kannada.

71.s: Which Telugu scholar wrote the poem "Vikramarjuna Vijayam" in Kannada?
71.x: Pampana (Adikavi Pampa) wrote Vikramarjuna Vijayam in Kannada under Arikesari II of Vemulavada; Rattaka, Narayana Bhattu and Bhimakavi did not.

71.s: Which one of the following pairs of composers in different languages and their works on the Mahabharata theme is correctly matched?
71.x: Pampa wrote the Kannada Mahabharata (Vikramarjuna Vijaya). Sarala Dasa wrote in Odia, Kasirama Das in Bengali and Tikkana in Telugu, so the other pairs are wrong.

71.s: 'Pampa', 'Ponna' and 'Ranna' are regarded as the three gems of
71.src: Grama Ward Sachivalayam Category-III Animal Husbandry Assist
71.x: Pampa, Ponna and Ranna are the Ratnatraya ('three gems') of Kannada poetry.

71.s: Whose contemporary was Pampakavi?
71.x: Pampa was the court poet of the Vemulavada Chalukya Arikesari II (Immadi Arikesari) and modelled Arjuna on him; Vishnugopa, Indrabhattaraka Varma and Kubja Vishnuvardhana lived centuries earlier.

71.s:
Consider the following statements about Rashtrakuta-era literature:
1. Kavirajamarga by Amoghavarsha I is in Kannada.
2. Prashnottara Ratnamalika is in Sanskrit.
3. Nalachampu was written by Halayudha.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
71.x: Kavirajamarga is in Kannada and Prashnottara Ratnamalika in Sanskrit. Nalachampu is by Trivikrama Bhatta; Halayudha wrote Kavirahasya.

71.s:
Consider the following statements about Pampa:
1. His Vikramarjuna Vijaya is also known as the Pampa Bharata.
2. His Kannada Adipurana describes the life of Mahavira.
3. The Kurkyala inscription of his brother Jinavallabha contains early Telugu verses.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
71.x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: Pampa's Kannada Adipurana describes the life of Rishabhadeva, the first Tirthankara.

71.s:
Match List-I (Work) with List-II (Author):
List-I | List-II
a. Santipurana | i. Trivikrama Bhatta
b. Gadayuddha | ii. Mahaviracharya
c. Ganitasarasangraha | iii. Ranna
d. Nalachampu | iv. Ponna
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
71.x: Santipurana – Ponna; Gadayuddha – Ranna; Ganitasarasangraha (Sanskrit mathematics) – Mahaviracharya; Nalachampu, the first champu – Trivikrama Bhatta (not Halayudha).

71.s:
Consider the following statements about patrons of Kannada poets:
1. Ponna was patronised by the Rashtrakuta Krishna III.
2. Ranna was patronised by the Vemulavada Chalukya Arikesari II.
3. The Vemulavada Chalukyas of the Karimnagar region were Rashtrakuta feudatories and strong patrons of Jainism.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
71.x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: Ranna was patronised by the Western Chalukya Tailapa II; Arikesari II was Pampa's patron.

71.s:
Consider the following pairs (Work – Author):
1. Kavirajamarga – Amoghavarsha I
2. Prashnottara Ratnamalika – Amoghavarsha I
3. Adipurana (Sanskrit) – Jinasena
4. Kavirahasya – Halayudha
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
71.x: All four pairs are correct: Amoghavarsha I wrote the Kannada Kavirajamarga (c. 850, the earliest available work on Kannada poetics) and the Sanskrit Prashnottara Ratnamalika; Jinasena wrote the Sanskrit Adipurana; Halayudha wrote the Kavirahasya.

71.s: Who among the following laid the foundation of the Rashtrakuta Empire?
71.x: Dantidurga, a Chalukya feudatory, overthrew Kirtivarman II and founded the Rashtrakuta empire (c. 753); Krishna I, Dhruva and Amoghavarsha were successors.

71.s: Who out of the following performed a ritual called ‘Hiranya-Garbha’?
71.x: Dantidurga performed the Hiranyagarbha ('golden womb') ritual at Ujjayini, believed to 'reborn' him a Kshatriya; Mayurasharma, Harishchandra and Harsha are not linked to it.

71.s: The Rashtrakuta kingdom assumed the independent status during the reign of?
71.src: APPSC Assistant Tribal Welfare Officer in A.P. Tribal Welfar
71.x: The Rashtrakutas became independent under Dantidurga, who threw off Chalukya overlordship by defeating Kirtivarman II.

71.s: Founder of Rashtrakutas
71.x: Dantidurga founded the Rashtrakuta empire; Pulakesin I and Vikramaditya II were Chalukyas and Vindhyasakti founded the Vakatakas.

71.s:
Consider the following statements about Dantidurga:
1. He overthrew the Badami Chalukya Kirtivarman II.
2. His inscription is in the Dashavatara cave (Cave 15) at Ellora.
3. He was a contemporary of the Eastern Chalukya Vijayaditya II.
4. He built Manyakheta.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
71.x: Two are correct (1 and 2). 3 is wrong: his Eastern Chalukya contemporary was Vijayaditya I. 4 is wrong: Manyakheta was built by Amoghavarsha I, not Dantidurga.

71.s: The capital city of the Rashtrakutas was
71.x: The Rashtrakuta capital was Manyakheta (Malkhed), built by Amoghavarsha I. Vijayapuri was Ikshvaku, Badami Chalukya and Bhattiprolu an early Buddhist site.

71.s: Which religion had Rashtrakuta protection?
71.x: The Rashtrakutas patronised Shaiva, Vaishnava and Shakta cults but leaned towards Jainism: Amoghavarsha I was a disciple of Jinasena and about a third of the Deccan was Jain.

71.s: 'Nripatunga' was a title of which Rashtrakuta ruler?
71.x: Nripatunga and Viranarayana were titles of Amoghavarsha I; Prabhutavarsha was associated with Govinda III.
xa: Balhara: contemporary of **Al-Masudi** (APPSC G1 2024).
Viranarayana came after the victory at **Vingavalli**.

71.s:
Consider the following statements about the Rashtrakuta capitals:
1. Manyakheta was built by Amoghavarsha I.
2. Manyakheta (Malkhed) is in present-day Maharashtra.
3. The early seat of the Rashtrakutas was Elapura (Ellora).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
71.x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: Manyakheta (Malkhed) is in Kalaburagi district, Karnataka.

71.s:
Consider the following statements about Rashtrakuta titles:
1. Prabhutavarsha was a title of Dhruva.
2. Amoghavarsha I took the title Viranarayana after his victory at Vingavalli.
3. The Arabs used 'Balhara' (from Vallabharaja) for the Rashtrakuta kings generally.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
71.x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: Prabhutavarsha was a title of Govinda III.

71.s:
Consider the following statements about Arab writers on the Rashtrakutas:
1. Sulaiman visited India in 916, in the reign of Amoghavarsha I.
2. Ibn Khurdadhbih called the Balhara the greatest king of India, the 'king of kings'.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
71.x: Only 2 is correct. 1 is wrong: Sulaiman visited in 851, in Amoghavarsha I's reign, and called him one of the four great kings of the world.

71.s: Famous South Indian ‘The Battle of Takkolam’ was fought between?
71.x: At Takkolam (949 CE) the Rashtrakuta Krishna III with the Western Gangas defeated the Cholas of Parantaka I; prince Rajaditya was killed.

71.s: The famous Battle of Takkolam of South India was fought between
71.x: Takkolam (949) was fought between the Cholas (Parantaka I, prince Rajaditya) and the Rashtrakutas under Krishna III, who won.

71.s:
Consider the following statements about the Battle of Takkolam (949 CE):
1. Krishna III defeated the Chola king Parantaka I.
2. Krishna III was helped by the Western Gangas and the Vaidumbas.
3. The Chola side was led by prince Rajaditya, who was killed.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
71.x: All three are correct: Krishna III, with the Western Gangas and Vaidumbas, defeated Parantaka I; the Chola prince Rajaditya led and was killed.

71.s: For about how long did the Rashtrakuta–Vengi conflict continue?
71.x: The Rashtrakuta–Vengi conflict lasted about 200 years, with repeated struggles against the Eastern Chalukyas.
xa: **Vijayaditya II** fought **108 battles**.
**Amoghavarsha** won at **Vingavalli**.
**Dhruva** won through **Vemulavada Arikesari I**.

71.s:
Consider the following statements about the Eastern Chalukya ruler Vijayaditya II:
1. He is associated with building 108 Shiva temples.
2. He is linked with the naming of Vijayawada.
3. He composed the Kavirajamarga in Kannada.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
71.x: Vijayaditya II is associated with 108 Shiva temples and the naming of Vijayawada. Kavirajamarga was written by the Rashtrakuta Amoghavarsha I.

71.s:
Match List-I (Eastern Chalukya ruler) with List-II (Rashtrakuta link):
List-I | List-II
a. Vishnuvardhana IV | i. Defeated Krishna II
b. Vijayaditya II | ii. Fought 108 battles against the Rashtrakuta forces
c. Gunaga Vijayaditya III | iii. Gave his daughter Shila Mahadevi to Dhruva
d. Vijayaditya I | iv. Contemporary of Dantidurga
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
71.x: Vishnuvardhana IV lost to Dhruva and gave him Shila Mahadevi; Vijayaditya II fought 108 battles (and built 108 Shiva temples); Gunaga Vijayaditya III defeated Krishna II; Vijayaditya I was Dantidurga's contemporary.

71.s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Tailapa II of the Kalyani Chalukyas overthrew the Rashtrakuta line around 973.
Reason (R): The Rashtrakuta Khottiga had defeated the Paramara Siyaka II and sacked his capital in 972.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
71.x: A is true, R is false: it was the Paramara Siyaka II who defeated Khottiga and sacked Manyakheta (972), after which Tailapa II overthrew the line (c. 973).

72.s: The Kailasa Temple at Ellora was carved during the reign of
72.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
72.x: The Kailasa temple at Ellora was carved under the Rashtrakuta Krishna I; Rajendra and Rajaraja were Cholas and Narasimha I a Pallava/Hoysala name.

72.s: Which dynasty constructed the Ellora Kailasa Temple?
72.x: The Kailasa temple (Ellora Cave 16) was carved under the Rashtrakuta Krishna I.

72.s: Which dynasty of rulers is associated with the construction of famous the Kailasa Temple of Ellora?
72.x: Kailasa at Ellora is a Rashtrakuta monument (Krishna I), not Chalukya, Chola or Pallava.

72.s: Which of the following temples is an example of rockcut architecture?
72.x: Kailasa at Ellora is carved out of the rock; the Shore Temple, the Thanjavur Rajarajeshwara and the Puri Jagannatha temples are structural (built of stone blocks).

72.s: Which of the following temples is considered as a wonder of rock-cut architecture ?
72.x: The Kailasa temple at Ellora, the largest single monolithic excavation in the world, is the wonder of rock-cut architecture; the others are structural temples.

72.s: The famous Kailasha temple, cut out of solid rock at Ellora, was built under the patronage of the
72.x: The monolithic Kailasa temple at Ellora was carved under Rashtrakuta patronage (Krishna I).

72.s: Among the cave temples, where is the famous Kailasa temple located?
72.x: The Kailasa temple is Cave 16 of Ellora; Ajanta, Elephanta and Kanheri are other cave sites.

72.s: The Kailasa temple of Ellora was built by –
72.x: Kailasa was carved under the Rashtrakuta king Krishna I, not the Chalukyas of Vatapi or the Gangas.

Match

The core region of the Eastern Chalukyas was Vengi in present-day Andhra Pradesh. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #145 · pp 254-255]
Rajamahendravaram, also known as Rajahmundry, later became an important centre. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #145 · pp 254-255]
Rajaraja Narendra was associated with Rajamahendravaram. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #145 · pp 254-255]
xa: First capital: **Pithapuram**; **Jayasimha I** moved it to **Vengi**.
Emblem: **Boar (Varaha)**; official language **Sanskrit**.
Greatest ruler: **Gunaga Vijayaditya III** (APHQ 2011).
Inscriptions use the matronymic **"Hariti Putra"**.

78.s: Who was the last king of the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi?
78.x: Vijayaditya VII (1070-1075) was the last king; his death in 1075 ended the Vengi line.

78.s: Which of the following was a title of Kubja Vishnuvardhana?
78.x: Besides Vishamasiddhi, Kubja Vishnuvardhana had the titles Sarvasiddhi and Makaradhwaja.

78.s: Which of the following title–ruler pairs is NOT correctly matched?
78.x: Chalukya Chandra was the title of Saktivarma I, not Vimaladitya. Vimaladitya bore the titles Rajamartanda and Mummadi Bhima.
78.tq: Find the swapped ruler in a title table, especially where two rulers belong to the same dynastic phase.
xs: **Chalukya Chandra — Vimaladitya** is wrong — option **(1)**: Chalukya Chandra was **Saktivarman I**.
Vimaladitya's titles were **Rajamartanda** and **Mummadi Bhima**.
The others are right: **Narendramrigaraja** — Vijayaditya II; **Rajamahendra** — Ammaraja I; **Vishamasiddhi** — Kubja Vishnuvardhana.
xa: **Kollabhiganda** — **Chalukya Bhima I** (G2 2012 key).
**Tripura Martya Maheshwara** — **Gunaga Vijayaditya III**.
**Rajaraja Narendra**: Kavyageetha Priyudu, Rajarajanarayana, Baraganda Bhairava.

78.s: In 1006 CE, Satyasraya sent Bayyalanambi against Vengi. Who defeated Bayyalanambi?
o: Vijayaditya VII with Rajendra Chola's assistance
78.x: Saktivarma I defeated Bayyalanambi with Chola help in 1006 CE. Satyasraya of the Kalyani Chalukyas had sent Bayyalanambi against Vengi.
78.tq: Track the combatant, the opposing commander and the external support separately.
xs: **Saktivarma I** beat **Bayyalanambi** with **Chola** help in **1006** — option **(4)**.
Bayyalanambi was sent by **Satyasraya** of Kalyani.
xa: Saktivarma's coins are found in **Arakan (Burma)**.
He and **Vimaladitya** had recovered Vengi from **Jatachoda Bhima** with Chola help.
Title: **Chalukya Chandra**.

78.s:

78.x: 1, 3 and 4 are correct. 2 is wrong: they ruled 624–1075 (over four centuries); after 973 the Kalyani Chalukyas were only their main rivals.
