91.x: Only statement 1 is correct. The promised revenue was that of Ellichpur (2); the 1307-08 campaign brought the submission of Ramachandra, not Harapaladeva (3); the Dnyaneshwari (1290, Nevasa) was written in Ramachandra's reign (4).

92.s: The ____ dynasty ruled over Andhra country from 12th to 13th centuries.
92.src: Social and Cultural History of A.P and Welfare Programmes 20
92.x: The Kakatiyas ruled the Andhra country in the 12th-13th centuries (independent from 1163 to 1323) from Hanumakonda and Orugallu. The Western Chalukyas and Cholas were earlier, the Yadavas ruled Maharashtra.

92.s: One of the major dynasties that ruled over Andhra
92.x: All four ruled parts of Andhra, so the question is loose; the intended answer is the Satavahanas, the first and greatest major dynasty of Andhra (the Kakatiyas were the second to unite all Telugu lands). Keyed as printed.

92.s: The Dynasty which had given ultimate design to Andhra culture and civilisation was
92.x: The Kakatiyas united the whole Andhra region and 'gave a comprehensive form to Andhraism' - Telugu identity, Orugallu as Andhranagari - so they gave Andhra culture its final shape. The Satavahanas, Pallavas and Chalukyas came earlier.

92.s: Which of the following clans the first rulers of Jains are believed?
92.x: The Kakatiyas were initially Jains and later embraced Shaivism, so they are the clan whose first rulers were Jains. The Satavahanas were Brahmanical, the Guptas Vaishnava, the Reddis Shaiva.

92.s: Bayyaram inscription tells about whose history?
92.x: The Bayyaram tank inscription of Mailamba (Ganapatideva's sister) gives the genealogy of the early Kakatiyas from Venna Bhupati. It has nothing to do with the Reddis, Badami Chalukyas or Satavahanas.

92.s: Who was the Raja Guru of Ganapatideva?
92.x: Visvesvara Sivacharya (Visvesvara Siva), head of the Golaki Matha, was Ganapatideva's raja guru. Vidyanatha was Prataparudra's court poet; Mallikarjuna Pandita and Sripati Pandita were Saiva teachers, not his guru.

92.s: Kakatiyas were feudatories of which Andhra dynasty?
92.x: The Kakatiyas first appear as Rashtrakuta vassals (Gundaya 'Rashtrakuta', Garuda emblem) and later served the Kalyani Chalukyas. The Eastern Chalukyas only issued the Magallu grant that first mentions them; they were never Kakatiya overlords.

92.s: To whom were the Kakatiyas feudatories before establishing their independent kingdom?
92.x: The early Kakatiyas were feudatories of the Rashtrakutas (Magallu: Gundaya 'Rashtrakuta'), then of the Kalyani Chalukyas. They were never vassals of the Yadavas, the Eastern Chalukyas or the Hoysalas.

92.s: To whom were the Kakatiyas feudatories before taking over the kingdom?
92.x: The Kakatiyas were originally feudatories of the Rashtrakutas (Garuda emblem) and later of the Kalyani Chalukyas (Varaha emblem). The Yadavas, Vengi Chalukyas and Hoysalas were neighbours or rivals.

92.s: Kakatiyas were subordinates of which dynasty in Andhra
92.x: The Kakatiyas were first subordinates of the Rashtrakutas, and only later of the Kalyani Chalukyas. The Eastern Chalukyas only issued the Magallu grant that first mentions them.

92.s: According to which of the following was 'Veena' the founder of the Kakatiya family?
92.x: The Bayyaram tank inscription of Mailamba traces the Kakatiyas from Venna (Venna Bhupati) as the first of the line. The Kazipet inscription names Beta I; Junagarh and Vijayawada are unrelated.

92.s: Who were the kings who had the title 'Mahamandaleswara'?
92.x: The Kakatiya rulers, as feudatories of the Kalyani Chalukyas, bore the title Mahamandaleswara (Beta II took it). It is a feudatory title, so the overlord Chalukya and Rashtrakuta kings did not use it as their style.

92.s: Who is the Guru of Ganapati Deva?
92.x: Visvesvara Sivacharya (Visvesvara Sambhu) of the Golaki Matha was Ganapatideva's guru. Vidyanatha was Prataparudra's court poet, Palkuriki Somanatha a Virasaiva poet.

92.s: Religious teacher of Ganapati Deva?
92.x: Visvesvara Sivacharya was Ganapatideva's guru. Rameswara Pandita was Beta II's guru and Dhruveshwara Pandita Mahadeva's.

92.s: According to which inscription was Beta Raja-I the first Kakatiya king?
92.x: The Kazipet (Dargah) inscription traces the Kakatiya line from Beta I and names him the first Kakatiya king. Junagadh is Rudradaman's record, Gantasala and Amaravati are Buddhist sites.

92.s: According to which inscription was Beta Raja I the first Kakatiya king?
92.x: The Kazipet (Dargah) inscription traces the Kakatiya line from Beta I and names him the first Kakatiya ruler. The other inscriptions are not linked to the Kakatiya genealogy.

92.s: Betha Raj-I was the first Kakatiya king according to the
92.x: The Kazipet Dargah inscription traces the Kakatiya line from Beta I, naming him the first Kakatiya ruler. Junagadh, Ghantasala and Amaravati are unrelated.

92.s: For the first time, in which inscription were the Kakatiyas mentioned?
92.x: The Kakatiyas are first mentioned in the Magallu inscription (c. 950-956) of the Eastern Chalukya king Danarnava, through Kakatiya Gundyana. Bayyaram (13th c.) is later; Polavaram and Pillalamarri are unrelated.

92.s: Which inscription mentioned about Kakatiyas for the first time
92.x: The Magallu grant of Eastern Chalukya Danarnava (c. 950-956) is the first mention of the Kakatiyas (Gundyana). Bayyaram is a later genealogy.

92.x: None of them was founded in the early 8th century: the Hoysalas rose in the 10th-11th c., the Gahadavalas in the 11th c., and the Kakatiyas and Yadavas became independent only in the 12th c. (1163, c. 1187). UPSC key: (d).

92.s: Which historian rightly pointed out that the kannada rule in Andhra came to an end with the establishment of Kakatiya Kingdom

92.s: Which Eastern Chalukya ruler issued the Magallu grant of 956, which contains the first mention of the Kakatiya family?
92.x: The Magallu grant of Eastern Chalukya Danarnava (956) first mentions the Kakatiya family through Gundyana.
xa: The Magallu grant names **Kakara Gundana** as progenitor; Bayyaram names **Venna**.

First sovereign = **Rudradeva 1163**; last = **Prataparudra II**.

92.s: Which dynasty ruled the Eastern Deccan during the 12th–14th centuries CE?
92.x: The Kakatiyas ruled the eastern Deccan from Warangal in the 12th–14th centuries. The Seunas (Yadavas) ruled the western Deccan, and the Eastern Gangas ruled Odisha.
92.tq: Discriminate the eastern and western Deccan dynasties.
n: The Kakatiya dynasty was located in the Eastern Deccan. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #150 · pp 261-261]
The Kakatiya dynasty existed during the 12th–14th centuries CE. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #150 · pp 261-261]
xs: The **Kakatiya Dynasty** ruled the **Eastern Deccan** in the **12th–14th centuries CE** — option **(3)**.
Their capital was **Warangal**.
The **Seuna / Yadava** dynasty ruled from **Devagiri** — they were the Kakatiyas' rivals.
xa: Rulers: **Rudradeva**, **Mahadeva**, **Ganapati Dev**, **Rudrama Devi**.
Rudrama Devi defeated the **Eastern Gangas** of **Orissa**.
The Kakatiyas were **Shudras** with **Sanskrit** as official language.
Clan deity: **Kakatamma (Kakati Devi)** = Jain **Kushmandini**.

92.s: Which of the following pairs (Saiva guru – Kakatiya ruler) is INCORRECTLY matched?
92.x: Dhruveshwara Pandita was Mahadeva's guru, not Ganapatideva's; Ganapatideva's Raja Guru was Visvesvara Sivacharya.

92.s: Under which dynasty did the Kakatiyas serve as feudatories after the Rashtrakuta phase?
92.x: After the Rashtrakutas, the Kakatiyas served the Kalyani Chalukyas as Mahamandaleswaras.

1. The chapters of the Ramayana are called Kandas, those of the Mahabharata Parvas.
2. During the Ajnatavasa in Virata's kingdom, Yudhishthira took the name Vallabha.
3. Arjuna took the name Brihannala during the Ajnatavasa.
4. Reading the Virata Parva is popularly believed to bring rain.
How many of the above statements are correct?
101.x: Only statement 2 is wrong: Yudhishthira took the name Kanka; Vallabha was Bhima. Kandas / Parvas, Brihannala and the rain belief about the Virata Parva are as in the notes. So three are correct.

101.s: "SarasangrahaGanita", a mathematical work in Telugu was composed by:
101.src: APPSC Group-II (Mains) Paper-II Social History & Constitutio
101.x: Pavuluri Mallana wrote the Telugu Sara Sangraha Ganitam (Ganitasara Sangrahamu), a verse rendering of Mahaviracharya's Sanskrit Ganitasarasangraha, the first mathematics book in Telugu.

101.s: Pavuluri Mallana, the mathematician, lived in the court of
101.src: Asst. B.C. Welfare Officer, Asst. Social Welfare Officer & A
101.x: Pavuluri Mallana lived in the court of the Eastern Chalukya Rajaraja Narendra, who granted him the Navakhandavada agrahara.

101.s: Who was the court mathematician of King Raja Raja Narendra?
101.src: APPSC Asst. BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Mains Paper-II 2017
101.x: Pavuluri Mallana, the mathematician who wrote the Telugu Ganitasara Sangrahamu, was in Rajaraja Narendra's court and received the Navakhandavada agrahara.

101.s: Which was the agraharam of the Chalukya mathematician Pavuluri Mallana?
101.x: Rajaraja Narendra granted the Navakhandavada agrahara to the mathematician Pavuluri Mallana. Nandampudi went to Narayana Bhattu, and Asanapuram was a ghatika centre.

101.s: Who received Navakhandavada from Rajaraja Narendra?
101.x: Pavuluri Mallana, author of the Telugu Ganitasara Sangrahamu, received Navakhandavada from Rajaraja Narendra. Narayana Bhattu received Nandampudi, and Nannaya only composed that grant.

101.x: Pavuluri Mallana translated Mahaviracharya's Ganitasarasangraha into Telugu, the first Telugu mathematics work. Nanne Choda wrote Kumarasambhavam, and Nannaya and Narayana Bhatta translated the Mahabharata.

101.x: Pavuluri Mallana translated Mahaviracharya's Ganitasarasangraha into Telugu, the first Telugu mathematics work. Nanne Choda wrote Kumarasambhavam, and Nannaya and Narayana Bhatta translated the Mahabharata.

101.x: Pavuluri Mallana, the mathematician who wrote Ganitasara Sangrahamu, lived in the court of Rajaraja Narendra and received the Navakhandavada agrahara from him.

101.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Nandampudi agrahara was granted to Nannaya.
2. Narayana Bhattu, who knew eight languages, was called Ashtabhasha Kavisekhara.
3. Someshwara I of Kalyani later made Narayana Bhattu his representative at Rajamahendravaram.
4. Pavuluri Mallana bore the titles Sukavi and Satkalasila.
How many of the above statements are correct?
101.x: Only statement 1 is wrong: Nandampudi was given to NARAYANA BHATTU for helping Nannaya 'Andhraise' the Mahabharata - Nannaya only composed the grant. The rest are as in the notes. So three are correct.

101.s: 'Ranganatha Ramayanam' was composed by
101.src: Asst. B.C. Welfare Officer, Asst. Social Welfare Officer & A
101.x: Ranganatha Ramayanam, the first Telugu Ramayana and a classic dwipada kavya, was composed by Gona Budda Reddy in the Kakatiya age.

101.s: Nirvachanottara Ramayanamu is the work of:
101.src: APPSC Junior Assistant in Dr. NTR University of Health Scien
101.x: Nirvachanottara Ramayanamu, the Uttara Ramayana told wholly in verse, is Tikkana's first work, dedicated to Manumasiddhi II; Gona Budda Reddi wrote Ranganatha Ramayanam and Baddena Sumati Satakam.

101.s: Who wrote the Telugu writings Niti Sastra Muktavali and Sumati Satakam?
101.src: APPSC Junior Assistant in Dr. NTR University of Health Scien
101.x: Baddena (Bhadra Bhupala) of the Kakatiya age wrote Sumati Satakam and Nitisastra Muktavali; Gona Budda Reddi wrote Ranganatha Ramayanam, and Kase Siddhappa and Vidyanatha other works.

101.s: Who was the first person to translate the Ramayana into Telugu?
101.src: APPSC Junior Assistant in Dr. NTR University of Health Scien
101.x: Gona Budda Reddy's Ranganatha Ramayanam (by c. 1250) is the first Telugu translation of the Ramayana. Tikkana's Nirvachanottara Ramayana covers only the Uttara Kanda, and Bhaskara's Ramayana came later.

101.s: Which among the following statements regarding Tikkana is incorrect?
o: Tikkana was the court poet of the Nellore Telugu Chodas.
Tikkana dedicated Nirvachanottara Ramayana to Manuma Siddhi II.
Marana and Ketana were the disciples of Tikkana.
Andhra Bhasha Bhushanam, the first work on Telugu Grammar, was written by Tikkana.
101.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
101.x: Andhra Bhasha Bhushanam, the first grammar written in Telugu, is Ketana's, not Tikkana's, so statement 4 is incorrect. Tikkana was court poet of the Nellore Chodas, dedicated Nirvachanottara Ramayana to Manumasiddhi II, and taught Marana and Ketana.

101.s: The Ramayana was translated from Sanskrit to Telugu for the first time by
101.src: Grama Ward Sachivalayam Category-III Village Agriculture Ass
101.x: Gona Budda Reddy's Ranganatha Ramayanam (by c. 1250) is the first Telugu translation of the Ramayana. Tikkana's Nirvachanottara Ramayana covers only the Uttara Kanda, and Bhaskara's Ramayana came later.

101.s: Who wrote the popular Telugu text 'Sumathi Shatakam'?
101.x: Baddena (Bhadra Bhupala) of the Kakatiya age wrote Sumati Satakam and Nitisastra Muktavali; Gona Budda Reddi wrote Ranganatha Ramayanam, and Kase Siddhappa and Vidyanatha other works.

101.s: Who was the first to translate the Ramayana epic into Telugu by 1250 AD?
101.x: Gona Budda Reddy's Ranganatha Ramayanam (by c. 1250) is the first Telugu translation of the Ramayana. Tikkana's Nirvachanottara Ramayana covers only the Uttara Kanda, and Bhaskara's Ramayana came later.

101.s: Which of the following is the work of Gona Buddha Reddy?
101.x: Gona Budda Reddy wrote the Ranganatha Ramayanam in dwipada metre. Vichitra Vijayam, Harishchandra Vijayam and Rajasekhara Charitra are other poets' works.

101.s: Ranganatha Ramayanam was written by?
101.x: Ranganatha Ramayanam was written by Gona Budda Reddy in dwipada metre; Molla wrote the Molla Ramayanam, and Chemakura Venkata Kavi and Rangajamma were 17th-century poets.

101.s: Which of the following poems is recognized as the greatest dwipada kavyam in Telugu literature?
101.src: APPSC Junior Assistants (Dr. NTR University of Health Scienc
101.x: Gona Budda Reddy's Ranganatha Ramayana is regarded as the greatest (and first) dwipada kavya in Telugu; Nirvachanottara Ramayana is in padyas and Bhaskara Ramayana is a champu.

101.x: Andhra Mahabharatam - Nannayya Bhattaraka (1), Markandeya Puranamu - Marana (2), Dasakumara Charita - Mulaghatika Ketana (4), Harivamsamu - Yerrana (3): A-1, B-2, C-4, D-3.

101.s: Who wrote Bhaskara Ramayanam?
101.x: Bhaskara Ramayanam is by Hulakki Bhaskara; Ranganatha Ramayanam is by Gona Budda Reddy.

101.s:
Match the following Kakatiya-age works with the fact about them:
List I

b. Nirvachanottara Ramayanam
c. Markandeya Puranam
d. Keyurabahu Charitra

ii. First Telugu Ramayana and the first dwipada kavya
iii. Tikkana's first work, dedicated to Manumasiddhi II
iv. Dedicated to the Kakatiya commander Gannaya (Ganna Reddy)
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
101.x: Ranganatha Ramayanam (Gona Budda Reddy) - first Telugu Ramayana and first dwipada kavya; Nirvachanottara Ramayanam - Tikkana's first work, to Manumasiddhi II; Markandeya Puranam (Marana) - dedicated to Gannaya; Keyurabahu Charitra (Manchana) - from Viddhasalabhanjika. So a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.

101.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Tikkana preached Harihara Advaita and dedicated his Bharatam to Hariharanatha.
2. Errana wrote both the Harivamsamu and the Uttara Harivamsa.
3. Errana's Narasimha (Nrusimha) Puranam is the first Kshetra-mahatmya kavya.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
101.x: Statement 2 is wrong: Errana wrote the Harivamsamu (to Prolaya Vema), but the Uttara Harivamsa is by Nachana Somana. Tikkana's Harihara Advaita and the Nrusimha Puranam as the first Kshetra-mahatmya kavya are as in the notes.

101.s: The oldest of the spoken and literary languages of South India
101.x: Tamil is the oldest of the spoken and literary Dravidian languages of South India (Sangam literature) and was the first to be declared a classical language (2004); Telugu, Kannada and Malayalam developed literatures later.

101.s: Telugu language belongs to
101.x: Telugu belongs to the Dravidian family (South-Central branch, with Gondi and Kui), not to the Aryan, Sanskrit or Pali families.

101.s: Which language is popularly known as the 'Italian of the East'?
101.x: Telugu, whose words end in vowels, was called the 'Italian of the East' by the 15th-century Venetian traveller Niccolo de' Conti.

101.s: Official languages of Andhra Pradesh state?
101.x: Telugu is the official language of Andhra Pradesh (since 1966) and Urdu is the second official language (all districts since the 2022 amendment); Hindi is not an official language of the state.

101.s: Hala, the 17th ruler of Satavahana Dynasty wrote Gathasaptasati in ___ language.
101.src: Social and Culture History & Welfare Programmes paper 2019
101.x: Hala's Gathasaptasati is a Prakrit (Maharashtri) anthology; Prakrit was the royal language of the Satavahanas, not Sanskrit or Telugu.

101.s: The earliest Telugu inscription seen at Vipparla was issued by
101.src: APPSC Asst. BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Mains Paper-II 2017
101.x: The Vipparla inscription was issued by the Eastern Chalukya Jayasimha Vallabha I; Vishnuvardhana I (Kubja) issued the Chejarla record, not Vipparla.

101.s: Which is the first inscription in Telugu?
101.x: The Kalamalla inscription (Kadapa, c. 575 CE) of the Renati Chola Erikal Mutturaju Dhananjaya is regarded as the first Telugu inscription; Chejarla and Addanki are later Eastern Chalukya-period records.

101.s: In which language are the Kakatiya inscriptions given?
101.x:
Most books and keys: Telugu. NextGen (Kakatiyas p.71) calls Sanskrit the Kakatiya royal language with most inscriptions in Sanskrit; the corpus is largely Telugu or bilingual.
Most Kakatiya-period inscriptions are in Telugu, which became the administrative language under them (many are bilingual Sanskrit-Telugu); Prakrit and Pali belong to the earlier Buddhist age.

101.s: What was the official language of the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi?
101.x:
Most books and keys: Telugu (NextGen previous papers, Rocket #11). Strictly: the grants' prasasti and much of the court record stayed in Sanskrit (NextGen Powerplay #1 Part 5.1 p.9; old app notes said Sanskrit).
APPSC keys and NextGen give Telugu as the official language of the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi: Telugu entered royal records and literature under them (grant details in Telugu, Nannaya at court). Sanskrit stayed the language of the prasasti.

101.s: Who was the exponent to state that the origin of Telugu is from Sanskrit?
101.src: APPSC Asst. BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Mains Paper-II 2017
101.x: Chilukuri Narayana Rao (Andhra Bhasha Charitramu) argued that Telugu was born of Sanskrit and the Prakrits; Bishop Caldwell held the opposite, that Telugu is a Dravidian language. (Moved: Telugu language and literature row.)

101.s: The Central Govt. has so far accorded classical language status to
101.src: APPSC Junior Assts. in Inter Board (APPSC Key) 2012
101.x: Tamil (2004), Sanskrit (2005) and Telugu (2008) all have classical status (now 11 classical languages, incl. Marathi, Pali, Prakrit, Assamese and Bengali added on 3 Oct 2024).

101.s: What are the languages, centre granted classical language status?
101.x:
on 3 Oct 2024 Marathi, Assamese, Bengali, Pali and Prakrit were added — now 11 classical languages, so option A is also classical today (Govt of India decision, 3 Oct 2024)
Telugu and Kannada were declared classical languages on 31 October 2008; Tamil and Malayalam are both classical but Malayalam came in 2013 (now Marathi and Assamese too, since 3 Oct 2024).

101.s: From which three Shaiva centres does the Trilinga theory derive the name Andhra?
101.x: The Trilinga theory refers to Srisailam, Kaleshwaram and Draksharama as the three Shaiva centres of Trilinga desa.
101.tq: Use a three-place association to distinguish the Trilinga theory from other regional lists.
xs: The **Trilinga theory** names **Srisailam, Kaleshwaram and Draksharama** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Andhra was called **Trilinga desa** after these three Shaiva centres, and "Telugu" is derived from **Trilinga**.
xa: Some derive **Tenugu** from **tene (honey)**.
**Andhra** / **Andhrika** are other names of the language.
**Draksharama Bhimeswara** is praised in **Srinatha's Bhimakhandam**.

101.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Telugu?
o: It has been a classical language of India since 2008
Telugu Language Day falls on 29 August
Telugu Language Day marks the birth anniversary of Gurajada Apparao
29 August is the birth anniversary of Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy
101.x: Telugu Language Day (29 August) marks Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy's birth anniversary, not Gurajada Apparao's.

101.s: Which of the following statements correctly describes the linguistic and literary situation during the Kakatiya period?
o: Telugu grammar, poetics and the desi-metre tradition developed, and Telugu became the main language of inscriptions.
Persian became the principal language of Kakatiya inscriptions.
Only Tamil was used for literary composition and inscriptions.
Telugu literature declined, while Sanskrit disappeared from inscriptions.
101.x: In the Kakatiya era most inscriptions were in Telugu, which grew as an administrative language, and Telugu grammar, poetics and the desi-metre tradition developed. Persian and Tamil were not the Kakatiya inscriptional languages, and Telugu literature flourished rather than declined.
101.tq: Separate the language of literary development from the language retained in inscriptions.

101.s: In June 2026, an ASI survey copied 25 inscriptions of the 2nd to 16th centuries in which tiger reserve?
101.x: In June 2026 an ASI survey of the Nallamala Tiger Reserve copied 25 inscriptions (2nd–16th centuries).

101.s:
Consider the following statements about Telugu:
1. It belongs to the South-Central branch of the Dravidian family, with Gondi and Kui.
2. The Venetian Niccolo de' Conti called it the 'Italian of the East' because its words end in vowels.
3. 'Desa bhashalandu Telugu lessa' occurs in Krishnadevaraya's Manucharitra.
4. Telugu Language Day (29 August) marks the birth anniversary of Gurajada Apparao.
How many of the above statements are correct?
101.x: Statement 3 is wrong: the line is from Krishnadevaraya's AMUKTAMALYADA (Manucharitra is Allasani Peddana's). Statement 4 is wrong: 29 August is the birth anniversary of Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy. Statements 1 and 2 are as in the notes. So only two are correct.

101.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Telugu has been the official language of Andhra Pradesh since 1966.
2. Since the 2022 amendment, Urdu is the second official language in all districts of Andhra Pradesh.
3. Telugu and Kannada were declared classical languages on 31 October 2008.
4. After the decision of 3 October 2024 there are 9 classical languages.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
101.x: Statement 4 is wrong: after 3 October 2024 there are 11 classical languages. The official-language facts (Telugu since 1966, Urdu in all districts since 2022) and classical status for Telugu and Kannada on 31 October 2008 are as in the notes.

101.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Hala's Gathasaptasati, in Prakrit, contains Telugu words such as atta, potta, pilla and pandi.
2. The first Telugu word, Nagabu, was found at Amaravati by Veturi Prabhakara Sastri.
3. The word Vepuru occurs in the Chikkulla plates.
4. The Chikkulla plates, with the Telugu plural '-ambul', were issued by the Vishnukundins.
How many of the above statements are correct?
101.x: Only statement 3 is wrong: Vepuru occurs in the MYAKADONI inscription; the Chikkulla plates (Vishnukundins) give '-ambul'. Gathasaptasati's Telugu words and Nagabu at Amaravati are as in the notes. So three are correct.

101.s:
Match the following early Telugu inscriptions with their issuer:
List I
a. Kalamalla
b. Erragudipadu
c. Chejarla
d. Bezawada
List II
i. Renati Chola Punyakumara
ii. Kubja Vishnuvardhana
iii. Yuddhamalla II
iv. Renati Chola Erikal Mutturaju Dhananjaya
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
101.x: Kalamalla - Renati Chola Erikal Mutturaju Dhananjaya (c. 575); Erragudipadu - Renati Chola Punyakumara; Chejarla - Kubja Vishnuvardhana; Bezawada - Yuddhamalla II. So a-iv, b-i, c-ii, d-iii.

101.s:
Match the following inscriptions with their literary feature:
List I
a. Addanki
b. Kandukur
c. Bezawada
d. Erragudipadu
List II
i. First Madhyakkara poem
ii. Geya (song) style
iii. Seesa metre
iv. First poetic inscription - Taruvoja metre
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
101.x: Addanki - first poetic inscription, in the Taruvoja metre; Kandukur (Gunaga Vijayaditya) - Seesa; Bezawada (Yuddhamalla II) - first Madhyakkara; Erragudipadu - first fully available, in geya (song) style. So a-iv, b-iii, c-i, d-ii.

101.s:
Consider the following statements about early Telugu inscriptions:
1. The Kalamalla inscription (Kadapa), the first Telugu inscription, is dated to about 775 CE.
2. The Addanki inscription was issued by Panduranga, commander of Gunaga Vijayaditya III.
3. The Chebrolu inscription shows the Marga and Desi forms.
4. The Motupalli record is among the inscriptions showing written Telugu before Nannaya.
How many of the above statements are correct?
101.x: Statement 1 is wrong: Kalamalla is dated c. 575. Statement 4 is wrong: Motupalli is a later Kakatiya record, not pre-Nannaya. Statements 2 and 3 are as in the notes. So only two are correct.

101.s:
Consider the following statements about the Telugu script:
1. The Pitikayagulla inscription (Prakasam, 8th c.) is the first Telugu poetic inscription.
2. The Bhattiprolu inscriptions (c. 400 BCE) are in Prakrit, in a variant of Brahmi, with early Telugu names.
3. In the Kadamba-Chalukya age Telugu was written in a common Old Kannada-Telugu script.
4. A separate rounded Telugu script emerged in the 11th-14th centuries.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
101.x: Statement 1 is wrong: Pitikayagulla shows post-Badami Chalukya influence on the script; it is NOT the first poetic inscription (that is Addanki, Taruvoja). The Bhattiprolu, Old Kannada-Telugu and 11th-14th century rounded-script statements are as in the notes.

101.s:
Given below are two statements, one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): In the bilingual grants of the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi, the grant details were written in Telugu.
Reason (R): The prasasti (praise) portion of their grants stayed in Sanskrit.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
101.x: Both are true (notes: the prasasti stayed in Sanskrit, grant details in Telugu), but the Sanskrit prasasti does not explain why the details were in Telugu - Telugu entered royal records as the official language under them. So R is not the explanation of A.

101.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Tamil is the oldest spoken and literary language of South India and was the first to get classical status (2004).
2. Tayumanavar was a Tamil Saiva saint-poet.
3. Kamban is known for a Telugu translation of the Mahabharata.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
101.x: Statement 3 is wrong: Kamban wrote the Tamil Ramayana; the Telugu Mahabharata translators were Nannaya and Tikkana. Statements 1 and 2 are as in the notes.

101.s: 'Kreedabhiramam' is a?
101.x:
Key: Poetry. Strictly it is a vidhi natakam (street play) in verse, not a poem (NextGen Kakatiyas p.3).
Kreedabhiramam is a Telugu vidhi natakam (street play) written in verse, so among the options it is poetry. 'Kreeda' means amusement, not sport, and it is no grammar.

101.s: Which of the following cities is described as the city of actors in Kreedabhiramam?
101.x: Kreedabhiramam describes Orugallu (Warangal) as the abode of actors and drama artists, with its markets, temples and nightlife. Dwarasamudram, Devagiri and Madhura were Hoysala, Yadava and Pandya capitals.

101.s: Prataparudra - Yashobhushana was written by
101.x: Prataparudra Yasobhushanam (Prataparudriyam) is a Sanskrit alankara work by Vidyanatha, court poet of Prataparudra II; it is not by Ketana, Baddena or Tikkana.

101.s: In which of the following works has the city of Warangal been very vividly described?
101.x: Vinukonda Vallabharaya's (Vallabhamatya's) Kreedabhiramam gives the most vivid description of Kakatiya Orugallu (Warangal), its streets, markets and temples. Rajasekhara Charitra and Kalapurnodayam are Vijayanagara-age kavyas.

101.s: Which city is described in 'Kridabhiramam'?
101.x: Vinukonda Vallabharaya's (Vallabhamatya's) Kreedabhiramam gives the most vivid description of Kakatiya Orugallu (Warangal), its streets, markets and temples. Rajasekhara Charitra and Kalapurnodayam are Vijayanagara-age kavyas.

101.s: Which of the following is the city described in Vallabhamatya's Kridabhiramam?
101.x: Vinukonda Vallabharaya's (Vallabhamatya's) Kreedabhiramam gives the most vivid description of Kakatiya Orugallu (Warangal), its streets, markets and temples. Rajasekhara Charitra and Kalapurnodayam are Vijayanagara-age kavyas.

101.s:
Assertion (A): Jayapa Senani authored Nrittaratnavali.
Reason (R): Jayapa Senani's profession was Gaja Sahini.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
101.x: Both are true but R does not explain A: Jayapa Senani was Gaja Sahini (elephant commander) under Ganapatideva, and his military post does not explain his writing the dance treatise Nrittaratnavali.
101.tq: Check whether R is the cause of A.
n: Nrittaratnavali was written by Jayapa Senani. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 9-11]
Jayapa Senani’s profession was Gaja Sahini. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 9-11]
xs: **Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A** — so option **(2)** is correct.
A: **Jayapa Senani** wrote **Nrittaratnavali**, a Sanskrit dance treatise (**8 prakaranas**).

xa: Jayapa also wrote **Geeta Ratnavali** and **Vadya Ratnavali**.
**Vidyanatha** wrote **Prataparudra Yashobhushanam**.

101.s:
Which of the following statements regarding Nannaya Bhattu are correct?
I. Nannaya Bhattu was a Telugu poet who translated the Sanskrit Mahabharata into Telugu as ' Andhra Mahabharatam '.
II. He is also credited with writing ' Andhra Shabda Chintamani ', a Sanskrit treatise on Telugu grammar.
III. Raja Raja Narendra donated Nandampudi Agrahara to Nannaya.
101.x:
Official key: I and III (Nandampudi to Nannaya). Strictly: the Nandampudi grant names Narayana Bhattu as donee and Nannaya as its composer, so I and II (NextGen Eastern Chalukyas p.20, p.33).
Statements I and II are right: Nannaya translated the Mahabharata (Andhra Mahabharatam) and is credited with Andhra Shabda Chintamani. Statement III is wrong, because Rajaraja Narendra gave Nandampudi to Narayana Bhattu and Nannaya only composed the grant (official key: I and III).

101.s: Who spread Veerashaivism in Andhra?
101.x:
Some keys: Basava (founder of Veerashaivism) or Somanatha (who popularised it in Telugu). Strictly: Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya propagated it in Andhra (NextGen Andhra Cholas p.3).
Veerashaivism was spread in Andhra by Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya (12th c.); Basava founded it in Karnataka, and Palkuriki Somanatha later popularised it through Telugu literature. The printed key (Basava) contradicts its own explanation.

Correct: **Ramabhyudayam — Ayyalaraju Ramabhadra**; **Kalahastiswara Satakam — Dhurjati**; **Rajasekhara Charitra — Madayagari Mallana**.

**Varadambika Parinayam** is by **Tirumalamba**.

101.x: The Nannaya age belongs to the 11th century, followed by the Tikkana age in the 13th century, the Srinatha age in the 15th century and the Prabandha or Rayala age in the 16th century.
101.tq: Place the periods by their century markers, then verify the sequence from earliest to latest.
xs: Order: **Nannaya (11th c.) → Tikkana (13th c.) → Srinatha (15th c.) → Prabandha/Rayala (16th c.)** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The other orders misplace these centuries.
xa: **Shiva Kavi Yugam** (**1060-1260**) lies between the Nannaya and Tikkana ages.
**Errana age** (14th c.) sits between Tikkana and Srinatha.
After the Prabandha age: **Dakshinatya** (**17th-18th c.**) and **Modern** (**19th c.** onward).

101.s: Who is identified as the first prabandha writer in Telugu?
101.x: Errana is identified as the first prabandha writer; Nannechoda began the tradition of the eight descriptions.
xa: ⚠ Other notes call **Srinatha** the prabandha pioneer (Sringara Naishadham, Haravilasam).
CDX names **Bhaskara Ramayanam** (Hulakki Bhaskara) the first champu kavya.
The **Prabandha** age peaked with the **Ashtadiggajas** at Krishnadevaraya's court.

101.s: Which of the following literary form–example pairs is correctly matched?
101.x: Ranganatha Ramayanam is identified as the earliest dwipada kavya. Sugriva Vijayam is associated with Yakshagana, Raghavapandaviyam with dvyarthi kavya, and Dasakumara Charitra with story kavya.
101.tq: Start from the sure genre–work pair and eliminate the swapped literary forms.
xs: **Dwipada — Ranganatha Ramayanam** is correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Yakshagana** → **Sugriva Vijayam** (Kandukuri Rudrakavi); **Dvyarthi kavya** → **Raghavapandaviyam** (Pingali Surana).
**Dasakumara Charitra** is the first **story kavya**; CDX names **Bhaskara Ramayanam** the first **champu**.
xa: Ranganatha Ramayanam is by **Gona Budda Reddy**.
Raghavapandaviyam tells the **Ramayana and Mahabharata** at once.

101.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Shiva Kavi Yugam of Telugu literature is dated 1060-1260.
2. The Dakshinatya (southern Nayaka) age covers the 15th and 16th centuries.
3. The Jain work Jinendra Kalyanabhyudayamu was written by Appayacharya in Prataparudra's time.

101.x: Statement 2 is wrong: the Dakshinatya age covers the 17th-18th centuries (15th is Srinatha's age, 16th the Prabandha/Rayala age). The Shiva Kavi Yugam (1060-1260) and Appayacharya's Jinendra Kalyanabhyudayamu are as in the notes.

102.s: Mohammad Gori was defeated by Prithvi Raj Chowhan in the battle of
102.x: Prithviraj Chauhan defeated Ghori in the First Battle of Tarain (1191); Chandawar (1194) was Ghori's win over Jaichand.

102.s: Who defeated Muhammad Ghori for the first time?
102.x: Ghori's first defeat came in 1178 at Kayadara near Mount Abu at the hands of Mularaja II of Gujarat, not Prithviraj (1191).

102.s: Whom had Muhammad Ghori defeated in 1194 in the Battle of Chandawar?
102.x: At Chandawar (1194) Ghori defeated Jaichand (Jayachandra), Gahadavala king of Kannauj.

102.s: Which one of the following kings was defeated by Muhammad Ghori in the battle of Chandawar?
102.x: Chandawar (1194) was Ghori's victory over Jayachandra of Kannauj; Prithviraj fell at Second Tarain (1192).

102.s: Who among the following rules is famous as “Prithvi Raj Chauhan”?
102.x: Prithviraj Chauhan was Prithviraja III (Rai Pithora), the Chahamana ruler of Ajmer.

102.s: Battle that laid the foundation of Muslim domination in India was :
102.x: Ghori's victory at the Second Battle of Tarain (1192) laid the foundation of Turkish rule in North India.

102.s: Which one of the following rulers from Central Asia conquered North India in 1192?
102.x: Shihabuddin Muhammad Ghori conquered North India after Second Tarain in 1192; Mahmud only raided.

102.s: In which battle Muhammad Ghori defeated Jayachandra-
102.x: Ghori defeated Jayachandra at Chandawar in 1194.

102.s: Who among the following rulers is famous as ‘Prithviraj Chauhan’?
102.x: Prithviraj Chauhan is Prithviraja III of Ajmer.

102.s: Who among the following Rajput Kings defeated Muhammad Ghori for the first time?
102.x: Ghori was first beaten in 1178 by the Gujarat Chaulukyas – Mularaja II (Bhimdev II), shown here as 'Baghel Bhim' – not by Prithviraj (1191).

102.s: In which battle did Prithviraj Chauhan defeated Muhammad Ghori?
102.x: Prithviraj won the First Battle of Tarain (1191); Ghori won the second (1192).

102.s: When was the first battle of Tarain fought?
102.x: The First Battle of Tarain was fought in 1191; the second in 1192.

102.s: The second battle of Tarain was fought between?
102.x: The Second Battle of Tarain (1192) was between Muhammad Ghori and Prithviraj Chauhan.

102.s: Which among the following was the central Asian ruler who conquered North India in 1192 AD?
102.x: Shihabuddin Muhammad Ghori won Second Tarain (1192) and conquered North India.

102.s: The battle from which Muslim rule in India established?
102.x: Muslim rule was established after Ghori's victory at the Second Battle of Tarain (1192).

102.s: Coins of which Muslim ruler bear an image of Devi Lakshmi?
102.x: Muhammad Ghori's coins carry Goddess Lakshmi on one side and the Kalma in Arabic on the other.

102.s: Muhammad Ghori suffered his first defeat at the hands of which ruler?
102.x: Ghori's first defeat (1178) was at the hands of Mularaja II / Bhima II of Gujarat, near Mount Abu.

102.s: ‘The last Sun of Indian glory’ has been used for –
102.x: Historian B.N. Luniya called Prithviraj Chauhan 'the last Sun of Indian glory'.

102.s:
Match List-I (Battle) with List-II (Year):
List-I | List-II
a. Kasahrada (Kayadara) near Mount Abu | i. 1191
b. First Battle of Tarain | ii. 1178
c. Second Battle of Tarain | iii. 1192

102.x: Kasahrada – 1178 (Mularaja II beat Ghori, his first defeat); First Tarain – 1191 (Prithviraj won); Second Tarain – 1192 (Ghori won); Chandawar – 1194 (Ghori, army under Aibak, beat Jaichand).

102.s:
Consider the following statements about Muhammad Ghori's battles:
1. Ghori's first defeat came in 1178 at Kasahrada near Mount Abu during his Gujarat campaign.
2. Mularaja II's queen mother Naika Devi acted as regent at that time.
3. The Battle of Chandawar was fought near Karnal in Haryana.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
102.x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: Chandawar (1194) was fought near Firozabad (UP) on the Yamuna; it is Tarain that lies near Karnal, Haryana.

102.s:
Consider the following statements about Muhammad Ghori:
1. He entered India by the Khyber Pass.
2. His first Indian invasion (1175) was against Multan.
3. He took Punjab and Lahore in 1186 from Khusru Malik, the last Ghaznavid.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
102.x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: Ghori entered India by the Gomal Pass.

102.s:
Consider the following statements about the Battles of Tarain:
1. The First Battle of Tarain arose over Ghori's attack on Tabarhinda (Bhatinda).
2. In the Second Battle, Jaichand of Kannauj sent troops to help Prithviraj.
3. The Turkish cavalry speed and mounted archery beat the larger Rajput army in 1192.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
102.x: Only two (1 and 3) are correct. 2 is wrong: Jaichand refused to help Prithviraj in 1192.

102.s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Unlike Mahmud of Ghazni's raids, Muhammad Ghori's invasions led to lasting Turkish rule in North India.
Reason (R): Ghori aimed at conquest and permanent occupation, and left his slave Aibak as his representative in India.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
102.x: Both are true and R explains A: Ghori sought conquest and permanent occupation (Mahmud only plundered), and Aibak, his representative after 1192, became the first Sultan in 1206.

102.s:
Consider the following statements about Qutbuddin Aibak:
1. He was a slave of Muhammad Ghori and held the post of Master of Stables.
2. He became the first Sultan when Ghori died near Jhelum in 1206.
3. His capital as the first Sultan was Delhi.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
102.x: Only two (1 and 2) are correct. 3 is wrong: Aibak's capital was Lahore.

102.s: “Chachnama” was translated to Persian by
o: Muhammad Ali Bin Abu Bakr Kufi
More than one of the above
102.x: The Arabic Chachnama on the conquest of Sindh survives only in the 13th-century Persian translation by Muhammad Ali bin Abu Bakr Kufi; Aufi and Shams-i-Siraj wrote other works.

102.s: The first Muslim invaders of India were –
102.x: The Arabs under Muhammad bin Qasim (Sindh, 712) were the first Muslim invaders, long before the Ghaznavids and Ghurids.

102.s: Muhammad-Bin-Qasim was a –
102.x: Muhammad bin Qasim was an Arab, nephew and son-in-law of Al-Hajjaj, sent by Caliph al-Walid – not a Turk or Mongol.

102.s: Who was the Hindu King at the time of invasion of Muhammad-bin-Qasim on Sindh?
102.x: Qasim defeated and killed Raja Dahir of Sindh, whose capital was Alor (Aror).

102.s: When did the first contact of India with Islam established?
o: After the arrival of Sufi Saints
In the 11th century after establishment of Turkish rule in India.
In the 7th century after conquest of sindh by Muhammad-bin-Qasim.
Arrival of Arab traders on the Malabar Coast.
102.x: Islam first reached India through Arab traders on the Malabar coast in the 7th century; the conquest of Sindh (712, 8th century – not 7th) was the first political contact and the Turks came later.

102.s: Who was Muhammad bin Qasim?
102.x: Muhammad bin Qasim, who led the Arab conquest of Sindh in 712, was an Arab.

102.s: Which among the following were first Muslim Invader in India?
102.x: The Arabs under Muhammad bin Qasim (712) were the first Muslim invaders of India, before the Ghurids.

102.s: First Muslim attack on India occurred in the year
102.x: Qasim's army set out in 711 but took Debal and defeated Dahir in 712, the date books give for the first Muslim invasion; so none of 674, 1013 or 711 is keyed.

102.s: First Muslim invader in India was
102.x: Muhammad bin Qasim (712) was the first Muslim invader; Mahmud, Ghori and Aibak came centuries later.

102.s: Arab writers said which Indian dynasty had the strongest cavalry in India?
102.x: Arab writers credited the Pratiharas, whose Nagabhata I drove back the Arabs, with the strongest cavalry.

102.s: What is the Chachnama, translated into Persian by Kufi, a chronicle of?
102.x: The Chachnama is an Arabic chronicle of the conquest of Sindh (680-718), later translated into Persian by Kufi.

102.s:
Consider the following statements about Muhammad bin Qasim:
1. He was the nephew and son-in-law of Al-Hajjaj bin Yusuf, the Umayyad governor of Iraq.
2. He was sent to Sindh by Caliph Harun al-Rashid.
3. The capital of Raja Dahir, whom he defeated, was Alor (Aror).
4. Debal, Sehwan and Somnath were among the places he took.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
102.x: Only two (1 and 3) are correct. 2 is wrong: he was sent by Caliph al-Walid. 4 is wrong: he took Debal, Nirun, Sehwan, Brahmanabad and Multan – Somnath was Mahmud's raid of 1025.

102.s:
Consider the following statements about the Arab conquest of Sindh:
1. Piracy against Arab ships was one of its causes.
2. It was followed by mass Islamisation of the Hindus and Buddhists of Sindh.
3. Through it Indian decimal and place-value mathematics reached the Islamic world and then Europe.

102.x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: there was no mass Islamisation; Hindus and Buddhists were given dhimmi status.

102.s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Arab rule in India remained confined to Sindh and Multan.
Reason (R): Nagabhata I of the Rashtrakuta dynasty drove the Arabs back.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
102.x: A is true: the Thar and Aravallis, strong Pratiharas, Rashtrakutas and Palas and weak Arab resources confined them. R is false: Nagabhata I was a Pratihara, not a Rashtrakuta.

102.s: After the attack of Mahmud Ghazni, who among the following reconstructed the Somnath temple?
102.x:
Most books and keys: Bhimdev (Bhima I). Strictly options (a) and (b) both name Bhima I; Kumarapala rebuilt the temple in stone later (PMF Ancient & Medieval 04 p.5).
Somnath was sacked in 1025 under Bhima I (Bhimadeva I), who rebuilt it after Mahmud left – books key 'Bhimdev'; 'Bhimraja-I' is the same king loosely named, and Kumarapala (not offered) later rebuilt it in stone.

102.s: Which of the following Chandela Kings was not defeated by Mahmud Ghaznavi –
102.x: Chandela Vidyadhara faced Mahmud (1019, 1022) and repulsed him – he was not defeated; Dhanga and Jayashakti never fought Mahmud as rulers.

102.s: Who among the following was the founder of Ghaznavid dynasty?
102.x:
Many guide books key Alptigin, who seized Ghazni in 962. Strictly the dynasty was founded by Sabuktigin in 977 (PMF; Britannica).
Sabuktigin (977-997) founded the Ghaznavid dynasty; Alptigin had only seized Ghazni (962) as a Samanid general, and Mahmud was Sabuktigin's son (some guide-book keys: Alptigin).

102.s: Who among the following issued silver coins with Sanskrit legend on one side:
102.x: Mahmud of Ghazni's silver coins carried Arabic on one side and a Sanskrit legend in Devanagari on the other.

102.s: Which among the following Indian ruler was not defeated by Mahmud Ghaznavi?
102.x: Vidyadhara, the Chandela who repulsed Mahmud (1019-22), was never defeated by him; Jayashakti (9th c.) lived before Mahmud and was never in contest, so the intended answer is Vidyadhar (same PYQ as UPPCS 1991).

102.s: What was the main motive of Mahmud Ghaznavi in context of invasion of India?
o: To make the country its colony.
102.x: Mahmud raided mainly to plunder temple wealth; he never tried to annex India beyond Punjab.

102.s: Who fought the Battle of Waihind (AD 1009)?
102.x: At Waihind (1008-09), near Peshawar, the Hindu Shahi Anandapala was defeated by Mahmud of Ghazni.

102.s:

Reason (R) : He wanted to establish permanent Muslim Empire in India.
Select the correct answer from the given codes :
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct
102.x: Mahmud invaded India 17 times (1000-1027) but for plunder, not to found a permanent empire – A is true, R is false.

102.x: Alptigin only seized Ghazni (962) under the Samanids; Sabuktigin (977-997) founded the dynasty; Mahmud made 17 raids (1000-1027); Anandapala (Hindu Shahi) fought Mahmud at Waihind (1008-09).

Match List-I (Raid of Mahmud of Ghazni) with List-II (Year):
List-I | List-II

b. Thanesar (Chakraswamin temple) | ii. 1025

102.x: Nagarkot – 1009; Thanesar – 1014; Mathura and Kanauj – 1018 (the Pratihara king submitted); Somnath – 1025-26.

102.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Mahmud raided Somnath in 1025 when the Solanki Bhima I ruled Gujarat.
2. Bhima I reconstructed the Somnath temple after Mahmud left.
3. The Chandela Vidyadhara was defeated by Mahmud in 1019.

102.x: Only two (1 and 2) are correct. 3 is wrong: Vidyadhara faced Mahmud in 1019 and 1022 and was not defeated – peace was made.

2. Mahmud's title Yamini-ud-Daulah was given by the Fatimid caliph.
3. Muhammad Ghori ended the Ghaznavid dynasty in 1186.
4. The Somnath Swabhiman Parv (January 2026) marks 1,000 years since Mahmud's attack on Somnath.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
102.x: Only three (1, 3 and 4) are correct. 2 is wrong: Yamini-ud-Daulah came from the Abbasid caliph (hence 'Yamini dynasty').

102.s: Who was the court historian of Mahmud of Ghazni –
102.x: Utbi (Kitab-ul-Yamini) was Mahmud's court historian; Firdausi was a poet, Hasan Nizami wrote under Aibak and Chand Bardai served Prithviraj.

102.s: Which one of the following statements about Alberuni is not correct?
o: His writing was influenced by India
He was an expert of trigonometry
102.x: Al-Biruni was a Sanskrit scholar and mathematician influenced by Indian learning, but he was not a secular author – he wrote as a Muslim scholar with no sympathy for the Somnath victims.

102.s: Farista, the author of Shah-nama was associated with the court of
102.x: The Shahnama was written by Firdausi (misspelt 'Farista' in the stem) at Mahmud Ghaznavi's court.

102.s: Al-Biruni came with Mahmud Ghaznavi in?
102.x: Al-Biruni came with Mahmud, whose raids were in 1000-1027 – the 11th century AD.

102.s: Who among the following has wrote Kitab-ul-Hind or Tahkik-e-Hind?
102.x: Kitab-ul-Hind (Tahqiq-i-Hind) was written by Al-Biruni; Hasan Nizami wrote Taj-ul-Maasir and Minhaj Tabaqat-i-Nasiri.

102.s: Who was the famous author of Kitab ul-Hind?
102.x: Al-Biruni wrote Kitab-ul-Hind; Hasan Nizami and Minhaj-us-Siraj wrote Taj-ul-Maasir and Tabaqat-i-Nasiri.

102.s: Al-Beruni came to India in –
102.x: Al-Biruni came with Mahmud of Ghazni (raids 1000-1027), i.e. in the 11th century AD.

102.s: The famous historian who visited India with Mahmud of Ghazni was –
102.x: Al-Biruni accompanied Mahmud to India; Ferishta, Afif and Ibn Battuta belong to later centuries.

102.s:
Match List-I (Work) with List-II (Author):
List-I | List-II
a. Kitab Patanjal | i. Al-Biruni
b. Kitab-ul-Yamini | ii. Baihaqi
c. Tarikh-i-Subuktigin | iii. Hasan Nizami

102.s:
Consider the following statements about Mahmud of Ghazni's court:
1. Firdausi, called the 'Homer of the East', wrote the Shahnama.
2. Unsuri was the poet laureate (Malik-ush-Shuara).
3. Al-Biruni's Kitab-ul-Hind was translated into English by H.G. Raverty.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
102.x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: Kitab-ul-Hind was translated into English by Edward Sachau.

o: Superior war technology of the Turks
102.x: The Turks won through superior military organisation – fast cavalry and mounted archers – against Prithviraj's larger, elephant-heavy army.

1. Genghis Khan
2. Mahmud Ghaznavi

102.s: Which slave of Muhammad Ghori conquered Bengal and Bihar –
102.x: Bakhtiyar Khalji, Ghori's slave-general, conquered Bihar and Bengal (1193-1203).

102.s: The slave of Muhammad Ghori who conquered Bengal and Bihar was?
102.x: Bakhtiyar Khalji conquered Bihar and Bengal (1193-1203); Aibak, Iltutmish and Yaldauz did not.

102.s: Nalanda Vihar was destroyed by :
102.x: Bakhtiyar Khalji sacked Nalanda, Vikramashila and Odantapuri during his Bihar conquest.

102.s:

2. He entered Nadiya in 1204 and drove Lakshmana Sena to East Bengal.
3. His Tibet expedition of 1205 was a success.

102.x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: his Tibet expedition of 1205 failed, and he was killed in 1206. He ruled from Lakhnauti.

106.x: Gujarat conquered by Ulugh Khan and Nusrat Khan (1299) → Mongol invasion under Ali Beg and Tartaq (1305, Amroha) → Malik Kafur plunders the Pandyas (1311) → Yadava kingdom annexed (Kafur, 1313): b, d, c, a.

106.s: What did Alauddin Khalji rename Chittor as?
106.x: After the conquest of Chittor in 1303, Alauddin Khalji renamed it Khizrabad after his son Prince Khizr Khan.
xs: Chittor was renamed **Khizrabad** after prince **Khizr Khan** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Alauddin took it in **1303** from **Rana Ratan Singh** of Mewar.
xa: **Rani Padmini's jauhar** is set at Chittor.
⚠ Prince **Khizr Khan** (set aside **1316**) ≠ Sayyid **Khizr Khan** (**1414-1421**).

106.s: What was the significance of Alauddin Khalji's raid on Devagiri in the history of the Delhi Sultanate?
o: The first expedition of the Tughlaqs into the south
The first Kakatiya invasion of Delhi
The first Turkish invasion of southern India
The first Mongol invasion of the Deccan
106.x: Alauddin Khalji's Devagiri raid of 1294–96 is described as the first Turkish invasion of the south.
106.tq: Use the FIRST/LAST marker to identify the historically defining event.
xs: Alauddin's Devagiri raid (**1294-96**) was **the first Turkish invasion of southern India** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It was made under **Jalaluddin**, before Alauddin's accession — not by the Tughlaqs or Mongols.
xa: He later murdered Jalaluddin at **Kara (1296)**.
Devagiri (Yadava **Ramachandra**) was attacked again by **Malik Kafur** in **1307-08**.

106.s:
Arrange the following conquests of Alauddin Khalji in chronological order:
1. Malwa
2. Gujarat
3. Chittor
4. Ranthambhore
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
106.x: Gujarat fell in 1299, Ranthambhore in 1301, Chittor in 1303 and Malwa in 1305.

106.s:
Match List-I (Kingdom conquered by Alauddin) with List-II (Ruler):
List-I | List-II
a. Gujarat | i. Rana Ratan Singh
b. Ranthambore | ii. Mahlak Deva
c. Chittor | iii. Hammir Deva
d. Malwa | iv. Rai Karan (Karnadeva II)
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
106.x: Gujarat (1299) – Vaghela Rai Karan; Ranthambore (1301) – Hammir Deva Chauhan; Chittor (1303) – Rana Ratan Singh; Malwa (1305) – Mahlak Deva.

106.s:
Consider the following statements about Alauddin Khalji's Gujarat campaign:
1. It took place in 1301.
2. It was led by Ulugh Khan and Nusrat Khan.
3. The Vaghela queen Kamala Devi was captured in it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
106.x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: Gujarat was conquered in 1299 – the first of Alauddin's conquests.

106.s:
Consider the following statements about Alauddin Khalji's conquests:
1. Nusrat Khan was killed during the first siege of Ranthambore.
2. Ain-ul-Mulk Multani conquered Malwa in 1305.
3. Shital Deva of Siwana was defeated during the campaigns in Rajputana.
4. The southern kingdoms were annexed and made provinces.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
106.x: Only three (1, 2 and 3) are correct. 4 is wrong: in the south the kings kept their thrones and paid tribute; only the north was annexed.

106.s: Who among the following was not a noble under Alauddin Khilji?
106.x: Alauddin's nobles included Ulugh Khan, Nusrat Khan, Zafar Khan, Ain-ul-Mulk Multani, Malik Kafur and Ghazi Malik. Munim Khan was a noble of Akbar, so he is the answer.

106.s: Ain-i-Mulk-Multani had not served under which among the following rulers?
106.x: Ain-ul-Mulk Multani was Alauddin's general (Malwa, 1305) and served later Sultans; Iltutmish died in 1236, long before, so Multani could not have served him.

106.s: Royal palace consisting of thousand pillars was constructed by the following ruler
106.x: The royal palace of a thousand pillars (Qasr-i-Hazar Sutun, at Siri) was built by Alauddin Khalji. The Thousand Pillar Temple at Hanamkonda is a Kakatiya temple (Rudradeva), not Ganapati Deva's palace. (Moved to the Khalji row.)

106.s: Who was the court poet of Alauddin Khalji?
106.x: Amir Khusrau was Alauddin's court poet.

106.s: Which title, meaning 'the Second Alexander', did Alauddin Khalji take?
106.x: Alauddin Khalji called himself Sikandar-i-Sani, the Second Alexander, and dreamt of world conquest.

106.s:
Match List-I (Name / post of Alauddin) with List-II (Meaning):
List-I | List-II
a. Ali Gurshasp | i. Army minister
b. Amir-i-Tuzuk | ii. The Second Alexander
c. Ariz-i-Mumalik | iii. Master of ceremonies
d. Sikandar-i-Sani | iv. His name before he became Sultan
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
106.x: Ali Gurshasp – his earlier name; Amir-i-Tuzuk – master of ceremonies and Ariz-i-Mumalik – army minister (posts under Jalaluddin); Sikandar-i-Sani – 'Second Alexander', on his coins.

106.s:
Consider the following statements about Alauddin Khalji's kingship:
1. He told Qazi Mughisuddin of Bayana that he acted in the interest of the state.
2. He revived the harsh, centralised rule of Balban, without religious sanction.
3. He dropped his plans of world conquest and a new religion on the advice of Kotwal Ala-ul-Mulk.
4. Barani separated the Shariat from the Zawabit, the state laws made by the ruler.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
106.x: All four are correct: he told Qazi Mughisuddin of Bayana he acted in the interest of the state, revived Balban's harsh centralised rule without religious sanction, dropped world conquest and a new religion on Kotwal Ala-ul-Mulk's advice, and Barani separated Shariat from Zawabit.

106.s:
Match the following columns I and II and choose the CORRECT answ Column I (Delhi Sultan)
A. Jalaluddin Khalji Column II (Period of rule)
1. 1451 -1489
B. Muhammad Tughluq
2. 1414-1421
3. 1324-1351
D. Bahlul Lodi
4. 1290 - 1296
C. Khizr Khan
106.src: APPSC 2023 Screening test (Online Mode) to the post of Deput
106.x: Jalaluddin Khalji 1290-96 (4), Muhammad bin Tughlaq 1325-51 (the option's 1324-1351, 3), Khizr Khan 1414-21 (2), Bahlol Lodi 1451-89 (1): A-4, B-3, C-2, D-1.

106.s: Who amongst the following General of Alauddin Khilji, ultimately became the first Sultan of Tughlaq Dynasty?
106.x: Ghazi Malik, Alauddin's general and governor of the Punjab, killed Khusrau Khan in 1320 and founded the Tughlaq dynasty as Ghiyasuddin Tughluq.

106.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
106.x: Bahlol Lodi ruled from 1451 to 1489, not 1491. The other three reign periods are correctly matched.
106.tq: Find the altered terminal year in an otherwise familiar reign period.
xs: **Bahlol Lodi — 1451–1491** is wrong — so option **(4)** is the answer.
Bahlol Lodi ruled **1451-1489**.
**Khizr Khan 1414-1421**, **Jalaluddin 1290-1296** and **Alauddin 1296-1316** are correct.
xa: **Muhammad bin Tughlaq**: **1325-1351** (some keys print **1324**).
⚠ Sayyid **Khizr Khan** ≠ Alauddin's son Khizr Khan.

106.s: During which period did the Sayyid Sultan Khizr Khan rule?
106.x: Khizr Khan (Sayyid) ruled 1414-1421; he is different from Alauddin's son Khizr Khan, set aside in 1316.

106.s:
Consider the following statements about the end of the Khaljis:
1. After Alauddin's death Malik Kafur set aside Khizr Khan and enthroned the minor Shihabuddin Umar.
2. Qutbuddin Mubarak Shah, the last Khalji, was murdered by Malik Kafur.
3. In 1320 Ghazi Malik killed Khusrau Khan and became Ghiyasuddin Tughluq.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
106.x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: Kafur himself was killed; Mubarak Shah was murdered by Khusrau Khan (Nasiruddin Khusrau Shah).

106.s: Padmini is associated with Ala-ud-Din’s conquest of Chittor. She was the wife of
106.x: In Jayasi's Padmavat (1540), Padmini was the wife of Rana Ratan Singh of Chittor, whom Alauddin defeated in 1303.

106.s:
Consider the following statements.

I. Muhammad Shah (1719-1748) was the first Mughal ruler to patronise Urdu.

II. Malik Muhammad Jayasi wrote the famous epic ‘Padmavat’ in Hindi.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
106.x: Jayasi wrote Padmavat (1540) in Awadhi, an early form of Hindi, so II is accepted; Muhammad Shah 'Rangila' (1719-48) is credited in books as the first Mughal to patronise Urdu, so I is accepted too.

106.s:
Consider the following statements about Chittor and the Padmini legend:
1. Alauddin took Chittor from Rana Ratan Singh in 1303.
2. Malik Muhammad Jayasi wrote Padmavat in Persian in 1540.
3. Padmavat was written more than two centuries after the conquest of Chittor.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
106.x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: Padmavat (1540) is in Awadhi (early Hindi), not Persian.

106.s: Where was Jalaluddin Khalji murdered by Alauddin?
106.x: Jalaluddin, who crowned himself at Kilokhari, was murdered at Kara by Alauddin in 1296.
xa: Before the murder Alauddin raided **Devagiri** (**1294-96**) — the **first Turkish invasion of the south**.
Jalaluddin was lenient to rebels like **Malik Chhajju**.

106.s:
Consider the following statements about Jalaluddin Khalji:
1. He crowned himself at Kilokhari in 1290 at about the age of 50.
2. He was lenient to rebels such as Malik Chhajju.
3. He married his daughter to Ulugh Khan, a descendant of Timur.
4. Mongol converts were settled in his reign as 'New Mussalmans'.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
106.x: Only two (2 and 4) are correct. 1 is wrong: he was about 70 when he crowned himself at Kilokhari. 3 is wrong: Ulugh Khan was a descendant of Chengiz Khan.

107.s: Why did Alauddin Khilji introduce a market policy of fixed prices for food grains?
o: For better return to the farmers
To ensure that consumers can directly purchase from farmers
To ensure that the market price is equal to the fair price
To ensure that soldiers can live comfortably with low salary
107.x: Alauddin's large standing army was paid low fixed cash salaries, so he fixed prices of daily goods so that soldiers could live comfortably on low pay. Farmers' returns and direct purchase were not the aim.

107.s: For whom did Alauddin Khilji introduced price control policy?
107.x: Price control was meant for the soldiers of the large standing army, who were paid low fixed salaries.

107.s:
Assertion (A): Alauddin Khalji introduced price control in Delhi.
Reason (R) : He wanted to pay lower wages to the artisans building his palaces in Delhi.
Select the correct answer from the code given below :
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not a correct
107.x: Alauddin did introduce price control in Delhi (A true), but to maintain a large army on low pay, not to pay lower wages to palace artisans (R false).

107.s: Which one of the following Kings of the medieval India began the ‘Public Distribution System’?
107.x: Alauddin Khalji's fixed prices, state granaries and rationing are called the first 'Public Distribution System' of medieval India.

107.s: The market control system was introduced by-
107.x: Market control and rationing were Alauddin Khalji's system, set up to support his large army; Balban, Jalaluddin and the Tughluqs had no such system.

107.s: Which post did Malik Kabool hold under Alauddin Khalji?
107.x: Malik Kabool was a Shahna-i-Mandi, superintendent of a market.

107.s:
Match List-I (Market of Alauddin Khalji) with List-II (Goods):
List-I | List-II
a. Mandi | i. Food grains
b. Sarai Adl | ii. Cloth, sugar, dry fruits, butter and oil
c. Third market | iii. Miscellaneous goods
d. Fourth market | iv. Horses, slaves and cattle
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
107.x: Alauddin set up four markets: Mandi – food grains; Sarai Adl – cloth, sugar, dry fruits, butter, oil; the third – horses, slaves, cattle; the fourth – miscellaneous goods.

107.s:
Match List-I (Official / department) with List-II (Role):
List-I | List-II
a. Shahna-i-Mandi | i. Recovery of revenue arrears from officials
b. Diwan-i-Riyasat | ii. Ran the whole market system
c. Munhiyan | iii. Secret spies sending daily reports
d. Diwan-i-Mustakhraj | iv. Superintendent of each market
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
107.x: Shahna-i-Mandi – superintendent of a market (e.g. Malik Kabool); Diwan-i-Riyasat – the whole market system, under the Naib-i-Riyasat; Munhiyan – secret spies; Diwan-i-Mustakhraj – recovery of arrears.

107.s:
Consider the following statements about Alauddin Khalji's market control:
1. Its plan aimed at fixed prices, sure supply, controlled distribution and the end of monopolies.
2. One of its aims was to pay lower wages to the palace artisans.
3. State granaries released grain in times of shortage.
4. Slave boys were used to make test purchases.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
107.x: Only three (1, 3 and 4) are correct. 2 is wrong: the aim was to let a large, low-paid standing army live on fixed low prices – not lower wages for palace artisans.

107.s:
Consider the following statement connected with Alauddin Khalji :
I. He collected revenue by measuring the cultivated land.
II. He enforced revenue measures in his entire empire.
III. He abolished the powers of provincial Governors.
Select the correct answer from the coding scheme given below :
107.x: I is true – Alauddin was the first Sultan to measure cultivated land. III is accepted in the key – he took revenue under direct state control and curbed the governors' (muqtis') independent powers. II is false – measurement was limited to Delhi and the Doab.

107.s: The term used for measurement of land in the Delhi Sultanate Period was
107.x: Masahat means measurement of land; Alauddin was the first Sultan to assess revenue on it (unit: biswa). Kismat-i-Ghalla and Ghalla-Bakhshi are crop-sharing; Ghazi is a title.

107.s: During the regime of which Sultan was the Khalisa land developed on a large scale?
107.x: Alauddin reclaimed milk, inam and waqf grants and brought much land under khalisa (crown land) to pay his army in cash.

107.s: At what share did Alauddin Khalji fix the state's demand of produce (kharaj)?
107.x: The state share was one-half (50%); he was also the first Sultan to measure land, using the biswa.
xa: New taxes: **ghari** (house) and **charai** (grazing); **jizya** continued.
Resumed **inam** and **waqf** grants enlarged the **khalisa**.

107.s:
Consider the following statements about Alauddin Khalji's revenue reforms:
1. The privileges of khuts and muqaddams were abolished.
2. Land measurement covered the whole empire.
3. Khalisa land was expanded by reclaiming milk, waqf and inam lands.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
107.x: Intermediaries lost their privileges and khalisa grew; measurement was limited to Delhi and nearby areas.

107.s:
Consider the following statements about Alauddin Khalji's revenue terms:
1. Ghari was a grazing tax on milch cattle.
2. Charai was a house tax.
3. Kismat-i-khuti, the headman's cess, was abolished.
4. Biswa was the unit of land measurement.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
107.x: Only two (3 and 4) are correct. 1 and 2 are interchanged: Ghari was the house tax and Charai the grazing tax on milch cattle.

107.s: Which Sultan had forbidden the nobles to hold banquets and festivities, and make marriage alliance without his permission?
107.x: Alauddin forbade nobles to hold social gatherings and festivities or to make marriage alliances without his permission, to stop conspiracies.

107.s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Alauddin Khalji forbade nobles to hold feasts or make marriage alliances without his permission.
Reason (R): Barani names the nobles' intermarriages and gatherings as one cause of revolts.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
107.x: Both are true and R explains A: the ordinance on feasts and marriage alliances was aimed at the gatherings and intermarriages that Barani saw as breeding revolt.

107.s:
Consider the following statements about Alauddin Khalji's ordinances:
1. A weak spy system was one of the causes of revolt he perceived, so he reorganised the spies.
2. He confiscated the nobles' property, religious grants and free lands.
3. He prohibited liquor, intoxicants and gambling.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
107.x: All three are correct: Barani lists the nobles' wealth, the weak spy system, drinking and the nobles' gatherings as causes, and an ordinance met each.

107.s: The attempt of Alauddin Khalji to control the market prices
107.x: The sources and the keys call Alauddin's market control highly successful: prices stayed fixed even in famine and the army was kept on low pay.

107.s: Alauddin Khalji’s reign is often called the ‘imperial period’ of the Delhi Sultanate mainly because it was marked by:
o: the replacement of the Sultanate by the Bahmani kingdom
the exclusive supremacy of the ulema over state policy
extensive conquests, strong centralisation and imperial ambitions
the abandonment of expansion and the growth of provincial independence
107.x: Alauddin’s extensive conquests, centralised administration, strong army and imperial ambitions led his reign to be described as the imperial period of the Sultanate.
107.tq: Infer the historical label from the cluster of policies and achievements.
xs: The reign shows **extensive conquests, strong centralisation and imperial ambitions** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Alauddin dreamed of being **Sikandar-i-Sani** and ran **harsh, centralised** rule.
The **ulema** were overridden, not supreme.
xa: Firsts: **state-run price control**, **rationing**, **land measurement** for revenue.
Kafur's campaigns reached **Madurai** (**1311**).

107.s:
Consider the following statements about the dynasties of the Delhi Sultanate:
1. Token currency, the transfer of the capital and canals are associated with the Tughlaqs.
2. Agra was founded by the Tughlaqs.
3. The Lodis were the first Afghan dynasty.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
107.x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: Agra was founded by the Lodis.

107.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Ziauddin Barani's Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi is the main source for Alauddin's market control.
2. Amir Khusrau's Khazain-ul-Futuh describes Alauddin's campaigns.
3. Alauddin's price controls were abolished by Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
107.x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: Qutbuddin Mubarak Shah (1316-20) abolished price control and restored the confiscated lands.

107.s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Alauddin Khalji's controls were enforced uniformly across the whole empire.
Reason (R): Espionage and repression under Alauddin bred discontent among merchants and peasants.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
107.x: A is false: the controls were largely confined to Delhi. R is true: espionage and repression bred discontent.

107.s: Which ruler is associated with the creation of the first standing army paid in cash, along with the systems of dagh and huliya?
107.x: Alauddin Khalji created the first standing army paid in cash and introduced dagh and huliya in military administration.
107.tq: Link the military reform, payment method and identifying administrative terms to one ruler.
xs: **Alauddin Khalji** created the first standing army paid in **cash**, with **dagh** and **huliya** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It was recruited by the **Ariz-i-Mumalik** (army minister).
xa: Ferishta puts its cavalry at about **4,75,000**.
Dagh = **branding of horses**; huliya = **descriptive roll** of soldiers.

107.s:
Consider the following statements about Alauddin Khalji's military reforms:
1. Dagh was the branding of horses and huliya (chehra) the descriptive roll of soldiers.
2. The Ariz-i-Mamalik headed revenue collection.
3. The Bahmani minister Mahmud Gawan later copied dagh and chehra.
4. The soldiers of the standing army were paid through iqtas.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
107.x: Only two (1 and 3) are correct. 2 is wrong: the Ariz-i-Mamalik handled army administration. 4 is wrong: the standing army was paid in cash from the treasury.

108.s: Public Works Department was primarily established by-
108.x: Firoz Shah Tughlaq set up the Public Works Department for his canals, towns and buildings – not Iltutmish, Balban or Alauddin.

108.s: The Sultan of Delhi who was very concerned about charity and alms and established a department called ‘Diwan-i-Khairat’ for it, was:
108.x: Firoz Tughlaq created the Diwan-i-Khairat for charity to orphans, widows and poor girls.

108.s: Which one of the following Sultans of Delhi introduced measures for improving the quality of fruits?
108.x: Firoz laid out about 1,200 gardens near Delhi and took measures to improve the quality of fruits; MBT, Sikandar Lodi and Sher Shah are not credited.

108.s: What was ‘Dar-ul-Shafa’ established by Firuz Tughluq?
108.x: Dar-ul-Shafa (Dar-ul-Shifa) was Firoz's free hospital – not an almshouse, library or guest house.

108.s: Who among the following Sultans of Delhi established an ‘Employment Exchange’ to help the unemployed?
108.x: Firoz Shah Tughlaq set up an employment bureau; kotwals listed the jobless.

108.s: What was ‘Dar-ul-Shafa’ established by Firuz Shah Tughlaq?
108.x: Dar-ul-Shafa was Firoz Shah's free hospital.

108.s: Public works department was for the first time established by
108.x: The Public Works Department was first set up by Firoz Shah Tughlaq.

108.s: Which of these Sultans set up a Department of Public Works to look after building programmes?
108.x: Firoz Tughlaq set up a Department of Public Works to look after his building programme.

108.s: Which of these Sultans set up a Department of Public Works to look after building programmes?
108.x: Firoz Tughlaq set up the Public Works Department; the other Sultans are not linked to it.

108.s: Which one of the following sultans provided employment to the unemployed?
108.x: Firoz Tughluq opened an employment office for the unemployed – not Alauddin, MBT or Sher Shah.

108.s:
Match List-I (Institution of Firoz Shah Tughlaq) with List-II (Function):
List-I | List-II
a. Diwan-i-Khairat | i. Pensions and grants to deserving persons
b. Diwan-i-Bandagan | ii. Charity
c. Dar-ul-Shifa | iii. Department of slaves
d. Diwan-i-Istihqaq | iv. Free hospital
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
108.x: Diwan-i-Khairat – charity (orphans, widows, marriages of poor girls); Diwan-i-Bandagan – slaves (about 1,80,000); Dar-ul-Shifa – free hospital; Diwan-i-Istihqaq – pensions and grants.

108.s:
Consider the following statements about Firoz Shah Tughlaq's welfare measures:
1. His kotwals listed the unemployed, who were given jobs by merit.
2. He laid out about 1,200 gardens and orchards near Delhi.
3. He retained mutilation (cutting of hands and feet) as a punishment.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
108.x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: Firoz banned mutilation.

108.s: Who was the first Sultan of Delhi to have levied ‘Haqh-i-sharab’ or irrigation tax?
108.x: Firoz Shah Tughlaq was the first to levy haqq-i-sharb, one-tenth of the produce on fields watered by state canals.

108.s: Who was the first Sultan of Delhi to have levied ‘Haqq-i-Sharb’ or irrigation tax ?
108.x: Firoz Tughlaq built state canals and charged haqq-i-sharb (one-tenth of the produce); the others did not levy it.

108.s: Who among the following translated 300 volumes Sanskrit books collected by Firuz Tughluq during the campaign of Nagarkot?
108.x: The Sanskrit works taken at Nagarkot (Jawalamukhi) were translated into Persian by Azizuddin Khan (Khalid Khani) as Dalail-i-Firoz Shahi; the others are Mughal-era names.

108.s: The city of Jaunpur was founded in the memory of
108.x: Firoz founded Jaunpur in memory of his cousin Muhammad bin Tughlaq, whose name was Jauna Khan.

108.s: Fatehabad district derives its name from the anonymous headquarters town founded by ……… in the 14th century, who named it after his son Fateh Khan.
108.x: Fatehabad was founded by Firoz Shah Tughlaq and named after his son Fateh Khan.

108.s: The Sultan of Delhi who is reputed to have built the biggest network of canals in India was
108.x: Firoz Shah Tughlaq built the largest canal network of the Delhi Sultans (Sutlej–Hansi, Yamuna–Hisar and others).

108.s: The Sultan of Delhi who is reputed to have built the biggest network of canals in India was :
108.x: Firuz Shah Tughluq is reputed for the biggest canal network; Ghiyasuddin dug the first canals but few.

108.s: The state-promoted canal irrigation system was initiated by:
108.x:
Most books and keys: Firoz Tughlaq. Strictly: Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq was the first Sultan to dig canals (NextGen Indian History 03 p.64).
Books and keys credit Firoz Tughlaq with state-promoted canal irrigation: he built the largest canal network and the first irrigation tax. Ghiyasuddin dug the first canals, which makes him the tempting option.

108.s: Which one of the following is NOT a town associated with Firoz Shah Tughlaq?
108.x: Firozabad, Fatehabad and Hisar Firoza were associated with Firoz Shah. Daulatabad was the renamed capital under Muhammad bin Tughlaq.
108.tq: Find the odd location by separating Firoz Shah's town-building from Muhammad bin Tughlaq's capital transfer.
xs: **Daulatabad** is not a Firoz town — so option **(1)** is the answer.
Daulatabad was **Devagiri**, renamed by **Muhammad bin Tughlaq** (**1327**).
Firoz founded **Firozabad** (Firoz Shah Kotla), **Fatehabad**, **Hisar Firoza** and **Jaunpur**.
xa: He laid about **1,200** fruit gardens around Delhi.
He moved **Ashokan pillars** from **Topra** and **Meerut** to Delhi.

108.s: From where were the Ashokan pillars brought to Delhi during the reign of Firoz Shah Tughlaq?
108.x: Firoz Shah transported Ashokan pillars from Topra in the Ambala region and from Meerut to Delhi.
108.tq: Test the pair of source locations and reject the nearby religious and inscriptional sites.
xs: The Ashokan pillars came from **Topra** (Ambala) **and Meerut** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Jwalamukhi** at **Nagarkot** is where he seized **Sanskrit texts**, not pillars.

111.s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): The Delhi Sultans named the Caliph in the khutba and on their coins.
Reason (R): The Caliph exercised real administrative control over the Delhi Sultanate.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
111.x: A is true, but R is false: the Sultans saw themselves as the Caliph's lieutenants only nominally; the Caliph had only moral authority.

111.s: In the context of the administration of Delhi Sultanate, 'Diwan-i-Arz' refers to which of the following departments ?
111.src: AP Grama Ward Sachivalayam Village Agriculture Assistant 202
111.x: Diwan-i-Arz was the military department under the Ariz-i-Mumalik (first made separate by Balban); finance was Diwan-i-Wizarat, correspondence Diwan-i-Insha, religious affairs Diwan-i-Risalat.

111.s: With reference to medieval Indian rulers, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: Alauddin Khalji first set up a separate Ariz’s
Balban introduced the branding system of horses in
Muhammad-Bin-Tughluq was succeeded by his uncle
Firuz Tughluq set up a separate department for slaves
111.x: Firuz Tughlaq set up a separate department for slaves (Diwan-i-Bandagan). Balban, not Alauddin, set up the Ariz department; Alauddin, not Balban, introduced branding of horses; MBT was succeeded by his cousin Firuz, not his uncle.

111.s: 'Diwan-i-Arj' department was associated with:
111.x: Diwan-i-Arz (printed 'Arj') was the army / defence department; royal correspondence was Diwan-i-Insha and finance Diwan-i-Wizarat.

111.s: Which one of the following dynasties saw the heyday of the Wizarat:
111.x: The wizarat reached its heyday under the Tughlaqs, above all under Firoz's wazir Khan-i-Jahan Maqbul.

111.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
111.x: Diwan-i-Bandagan (slaves) was set up by Firoz Tughlaq. Diwan-i-Mustakhraj was Alauddin's, Diwan-i-Kohi MBT's and Diwan-i-Arz Balban's.
