111.s: Who was 'Khareetadar'?
o: An officer who was trained in keeping accounts
111.x: The Khareetadar (kharitadar) was the officer who despatched royal decrees and letters.

111.s: Who among the following had established the Diwan-i-Arz department under Delhi Sultanate?
111.x: Diwan-i-Arz was set up as a separate military department under Balban (Ariz-i-Mumalik Imad-ul-Mulk); Alauddin enlarged the army but did not found the department.

111.s: In the Delhi Sultanate, the Naib was the official who:
o: Ranked next to the Sultan and in practice controlled all departments
Headed the news and intelligence department
111.x: The Naib ranked next to the Sultan and in practice controlled all departments.

111.s: What did the Diwan-i-Khairat of Firoz Tughlaq deal with?
111.x: Diwan-i-Khairat was Firoz's department of charity; Diwan-i-Bandagan dealt with slaves.

111.s:
Consider the following statements about Sultanate diwans:
1. Diwan-i-Insha was headed by the Dabir-i-Khas.
2. Diwan-i-Risalat under the Sadr-us-Sudur dealt with religious affairs.
3. Diwan-i-Kohi was set up by Firoz Tughlaq.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
111.x: Insha was under the Dabir-i-Khas and Risalat under the Sadr-us-Sudur; Diwan-i-Kohi was set up by MBT, not Firoz.

111.s: Which department of the Delhi Sultanate dealt with finance and revenue?
111.x: The Diwan-i-Wizarat, headed by the Wazir, handled finance and revenue.

111.s: Which of the following offices was Mughal and did not exist under the Delhi Sultans?
111.x: Mir Bakshi was a Mughal office; Shiqdar, Ariz-i-Mumalik and Muqti belonged to the Sultanate.

111.s:
Consider the following pairs (Diwan – Work – Founder):
1. Diwan-i-Mustakhraj – recovery of arrears of revenue – Alauddin Khalji
2. Diwan-i-Riyasat – commerce / market control – Alauddin Khalji
3. Diwan-i-Amir-i-Kohi – agriculture – Firoz Tughlaq
4. Diwan-i-Khairat – charity – Firoz Tughlaq
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
111.x: Pair 3 is wrong: the Diwan-i-Amir-i-Kohi (agriculture) was set up by Muhammad bin Tughlaq. Mustakhraj and Riyasat were Alauddin's; Khairat (with Bandagan and Istihqaq) was Firoz's.

111.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Official)
a. Barid-i-Mumalik
b. Wakil-i-Dar
c. Amir-i-Hajib
d. Qazi-ul-Quzat
List-II (Duty)
i. Royal household and court
ii. Chief Justice
iii. News and intelligence
iv. Master of ceremonies; petitions

111.x: Barid-i-Mumalik – news and intelligence; Wakil-i-Dar – royal household and court; Amir-i-Hajib – ceremonies and petitions; Qazi-ul-Quzat – Chief Justice.

111.s:
Consider the following statements about the central government of the Sultanate:
1. The Diwan-i-Insha, under the Dabir-i-Mumalik, handled royal correspondence and decrees.
2. The Naib ranked below the Wazir.
3. The Diwan-i-Risalat, under the Chief Sadr, dealt with religious affairs and grants to mosques and madrasas.
4. The office of Mir Bakshi existed under the Khaljis.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
111.x: Statements 2 and 4 are wrong: the Naib was the most powerful post after the Sultan, with the Wazir next; Mir Bakshi was a Mughal office, not a Khalji one.

111.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Diwan-i-Wizarat under the Wazir dealt with finance, revenue, accounts and iqta allotment.
2. In the Qutb Shahi administration the Mir Jumla commanded the army.
3. The wizarat reached its heyday under the Tughlaqs, with Firoz's wazir Khan-i-Jahan Maqbul.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
111.x: Statement 2 is wrong: under the Qutb Shahis the Mir Jumla handled finance; Ain-ul-Mulk headed the army.

111.s: During the period of Delhi Sultanate, who was the wazir of Iltutmish?
111.src: AP recruitment paper (header page missing in scan)
111.x: Nizam-ul-Mulk Muhammad Junaidi was Iltutmish's wazir; Ain-ul-Mulk Multani served Alauddin and MBT.

111.s: Name the group established by Iltutmish?
111.x: Iltutmish organised the Turkan-i-Chahalgani, the 'Forty' Turkish nobles.

111.s: Who broke the power of ‘Chahalgani nobles’ ?
111.x: Balban, himself one of the Forty, eliminated the power of the Turkan-i-Chahalgani that Iltutmish had created.

111.s: Who among the following sultans succeeded in finally breaking and destroying the power of Turkan-i- Chihalgani?
111.x: Balban, himself one of the Forty, eliminated the power of the Turkan-i-Chahalgani that Iltutmish had created.

111.s: Whose wazir was Khan-i-Jahan Maqbul, a Telugu Brahmin convert?
111.x: Khan-i-Jahan Maqbul was Firoz Tughlaq's wazir, under whom the wizarat reached its heyday.

111.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Alauddin Khalji — Kingship knows no kinship
Muhammad bin Tughlaq — Exclusion of non-Turks from high office
111.x: Muhammad bin Tughlaq followed rationalist absolutism and appointed non-Turks and low-born persons. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
111.tq: Look for the reversed policy statement, especially where a ruler's inclusionary policy is made exclusionary.
xs: **MBT – exclusion of non-Turks** is wrong: MBT **appointed non-Turks and low-born men** — option **(4)**.
The rest are correct: **Alauddin** – "kingship knows no kinship"; **Balban** – "blood and iron"; **Iltutmish** – created the **Turkan-i-Chahalgani** (the Forty).
xa: MBT's theory: **rationalist absolutism**.
MBT sought investiture from the Abbasid Caliph in **Egypt**.
MBT set up the **Diwan-i-Kohi** (agriculture).

111.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched with the policy concerning nobility?
o: Muhammad bin Tughluq — Promoted foreigners and low-born men
Alauddin Khalji — Crushed the Balbani and Jalali nobles
Lodi Sultans — Treated Afghan nobles as subordinate officials without tribal equality
111.x: Lodi rulers dealt with an Afghan tribal nobility that treated the Sultan as first among equals. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
111.tq: Detect the reversed description in a dynasty-wise comparison of nobility.
xs: **Lodis – nobles as subordinate officials** is wrong: the **Afghan tribal nobility** treated the Sultan as "**first among equals**" — option **(4)**.
The rest are correct: **Firoz** made iqtas **hereditary**; **MBT** promoted **foreigners and low-born men**; **Alauddin** crushed **Balbani and Jalali** nobles.
xa: Khalji revolution (**1290**) opened office to **non-Turks** and **Indian Muslims**.
Slave dynasty nobility = **Turkish monopoly**.

111.s: After Balban, the nobles set aside his nominee Kai Khusrau; whom did they raise to the throne?
111.x: The nobles set aside Kai Khusrau and raised Kaiqubad; Jalaluddin Khalji took power in 1290.

111.s:
Consider the following statements about the Sultanate nobility:
1. Muhammad bin Tughlaq kept foreigners and low-born men out of high office.
2. After Balban the nobles set aside his nominee Kai Khusrau and raised Kaiqubad.
3. The Khalji revolution of 1290 opened high office to non-Turks and Indian Muslims.
4. Under the Lodis the Sultan was 'first among equals' among the Afghan nobles.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
111.x: Statement 1 is wrong: MBT promoted foreigners and low-born men. The other three are correct.

b. Malik Kafur
c. Ain-ul-Mulk Multani

ii. Wazir of Firoz; a Telugu Brahmin convert
iii. Naib Malik of Alauddin
iv. Ariz under Balban, freed from the Wazir's financial control
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
111.x: Imad-ul-Mulk – Balban's Ariz; Malik Kafur – Alauddin's Naib Malik; Ain-ul-Mulk Multani – Malwa 1305; Khan-i-Jahan Maqbul – Firoz's wazir, a Telugu Brahmin convert from Warangal.

111.s: Government of medieval period was a composite structure. It was a fusion of :
111.x: Sultanate government was a composite of Perso-Arabic (title Sultan, caliph, court customs), Turko-Mongol (decimal army) and Indian elements.

111.s: Zawabits were concerned with :
111.x: Zawabit were state laws (royal regulations) framed by the Sultans to supplement the sharia.

111.s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Succession in the Delhi Sultanate followed the rule of primogeniture.
Reason (R): Iltutmish nominated his daughter as his successor.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
111.x: A is false: there was no fixed rule of succession (no primogeniture) – acceptance by nobles and ulema, or military strength, decided it. R is true: Iltutmish nominated his daughter (Razia).

111.s:
Consider the following statements about the Sultanate state:
1. Criminal law followed the sharia alone.
2. The Sultan was the commander-in-chief and the final court of appeal.
3. The organisation of the army in decimal units was a Perso-Arabic element of the government.
4. Hindus kept their personal laws, through panchayats.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
111.x: Statements 1 and 3 are wrong: criminal law followed the Sultan's rules, and the decimal army with mounted archers was the Turko-Mongol element (Perso-Arabic gave the title Sultan, sijda, paibos, Nauroz).

112.s: Fawazil in the Sultanate period meant
o: extra payment made to the nobles
revenue assigned in lieu of salary
excess amount paid to the exchequer by the iqtadars
illegal exactions extracted from the peasants
112.x: Fawazil was the surplus revenue an iqtadar had to send to the treasury after paying his troops and salary.

112.s: Which medieval king of India introduced the ‘Iqta system’?
112.x: In India the iqta system was started (as an institution) by Iltutmish; Balban and Alauddin only tightened control.

112.s: Which one of the following is NOT the characteristic of 'Iqta System'?
o: Iqta was a revenue collection system
Siyasatnama was the source of information for Iqta
Revenue from Iqta was directly deposited in Sultan's
Muqti was supported to maintain troops out of the
112.x: Iqta revenue was collected by the muqti, who paid his troops and kept his salary before sending the surplus; it was not deposited directly in the Sultan's treasury. The Siyasatnama describes the iqta.

112.s: Which among the following medieval ruler of India introduced Iqta system?
112.x: In India the iqta system was started (as an institution) by Iltutmish; Balban and Alauddin only tightened control.

112.s:
Consider the following statements.

I. In the revenue administration of Delhi Sultanate, the in-charge of revenue collection was known as ‘Amil’.

II. The Iqta system of Sultans of Delhi was an ancient indigenous institution.

III. The office of ‘Mir Bakshi’ came into existence during the reign of Khalji Sultans of Delhi.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
112.x: Only I: the amil was in charge of revenue collection in a pargana. The iqta was a foreign (Caliphate) institution, and the Mir Bakshi was a Mughal office.

112.s: Muhammad Ghori granted first Iqta in India to –
112.x: Muhammad Ghori gave the first iqta in India, Hansi, to Qutbuddin Aibak.

112.s:
Consider the following statements:
1.
Assertion (A): At first, the Turkish administration in India was essentially military.
2.
Reason (R): The country was parcelled out as 'Iqtas' among leading military leaders.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not a correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
112.x: Early Turkish administration was essentially military because the country was parcelled out as iqtas among military commanders who held them with troops – R explains A.

112.s: What was the holder of an iqta called in the Delhi Sultanate?
112.x: The iqta holder was the muqti (wali for a province); the amil collected revenue in a pargana and the patwari was the village accountant.

112.s: Which Sultanate system of revenue assignments financed the army by linking military obligations with the administration of territories?
112.x: The iqta system provided the financial basis for maintaining troops while connecting military service with the administration of assigned territories.
xa: The muqti **kept troops** and sent the **fawazil** to the centre.
The iqta is the ancestor of the Mughal **jagir/mansab** system.

112.s:
Consider the following statements about the iqta system:
1. Balban appointed khwajas (auditors) to check the muqtis.
2. Firoz Tughlaq made iqtas hereditary but abolished the jagir.
3. Alauddin Khalji enlarged the khalisa by taking back milk, idrarat and waqf lands.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
112.x: Statement 2 is wrong: Firoz relaxed control, made iqtas hereditary and revived the jagir (army efficiency fell). 1 and 3 are correct.

112.s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Until Firoz Tughlaq, muqtis were usually transferred every three or four years.
Reason (R): An iqta was an assignment of the revenue of a territory in lieu of salary, not ownership of the land.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
112.x: Both true and R explains A: because the iqta was only a revenue assignment in lieu of salary (not ownership), it could be transferred, and muqtis were rotated every 3-4 years until Firoz.

112.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The iqta is the ancestor of the Mughal jagir and mansab system.
2. The holder of an iqta was called the muqti or iqtadar.
3. Under Firoz Tughlaq the efficiency of the army rose because iqtas became hereditary.
How many of the above statements are correct?
112.x: Two are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: when Firoz relaxed control and made iqtas hereditary, army efficiency fell.

112.s: Which of the following Sultan appointed a special army to protect the boundaries of the empire?
112.x: Alauddin Khalji raised a huge standing army paid in cash to defend the frontier against the Mongols – the UPRO key; Balban's frontier policy (forts) was adopted and completed by Alauddin.

112.s: The largest standing army of the Sultanate, directly paid by the state was created by
112.x: Under Alauddin Khalji the standing army was the largest, recruited and paid in cash by the state.

112.s: Who among the following sultans of Delhi was the first to have paid to his soldiers in cash?
112.x: Alauddin Khalji was the first Sultan to pay his soldiers in cash from the treasury; Iltutmish and Balban paid through iqtas.

112.s: Which Sultan introduced large-scale cash payment to his standing army?
112.x: Alauddin Khalji paid his standing army in cash, whereas Iltutmish and Balban used iqtas and Firoz Tughlaq returned to assignment-based payment.
xa: Firoz also made iqtas **hereditary**.
Alauddin enlarged the **khalisa** to fund cash pay.

112.s: What was the main purpose of dagh and huliya?
o: Record the revenue of each iqta
Determine the hereditary rights of military officers
Prevent the presentation of substandard horses and substitute soldiers at muster
Classify villages according to agricultural production
112.x: Branding horses and maintaining descriptive rolls helped prevent soldiers from bringing inferior horses or sending proxies in their place during inspection.
112.tq: Infer the administrative purpose from the control mechanism.
xs: Dagh and huliya stopped **substandard horses** and **proxy soldiers** at the muster — option **(3)**.
**Dagh** = branding of horses; **huliya** = descriptive roll of each soldier.
xa: Introduced by **Alauddin Khalji**; dagh revived by **Sher Shah**.
The **Ariz's department** recruited, inspected and paid the army.

112.s: Which ruler later revived the practice of dagh?
112.x: Dagh was introduced by Alauddin Khalji and revived by Sher Shah.

112.s:
Consider the following statements about dagh and huliya:
1. Dagh was the branding of horses.
2. Huliya was the descriptive roll of soldiers.
3. Both were introduced by Balban.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
112.x: Dagh and huliya were branding of horses and descriptive roll; both were Alauddin Khalji's, not Balban's.

112.s:
Arrange the following Sultanate military ranks from the lowest to the highest:
1. Malik
2. Sar-i-khail
3. Khan
4. Amir
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
112.x: The decimal ranks run sar-i-khail (10 horsemen) → sipah-salar → amir → malik → khan (the highest, commanding 10 maliks): 2, 4, 1, 3.

112.s:
Consider the following statements about the Sultanate army:
1. Balban set up the Diwan-i-Arz under the Ariz-i-Mumalik to keep a large standing army against the Mongols.
2. Horses for the cavalry were mainly imported from Bengal.
3. The iron stirrup was among the Turkish military gains.
4. War elephants were the monopoly of the Sultan.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
112.x: Statement 2 is wrong: horses were imported from West Asia. The others are correct.

112.s: Supreme rural officials of land revenue in Sultanate period?
112.x: The chaudhari, above the village headmen, was the leading rural official of land revenue (pargana level) – IAS key; ravat and malik were not revenue posts and the patwari was only the accountant.

112.s: During the Delhi Sultanate, the designation 'Muqaddam or Chaudhari' was used for
o: More than one of the above
112.x: Muqaddam or Chaudhari denoted the village headman (BPSC key), not the accountant (patwari).

112.s: Who was the village accountant in the Delhi Sultanate?
112.x: The patwari was the village accountant; the muqaddam or chaudhari was the headman.

112.s: Which Sultan abolished the cess of the khuts, the hereditary rural landholders?
112.x: Alauddin Khalji abolished the khut's cess.

112.s: Which pair of unit and officer is INCORRECTLY matched?
112.x: The wali governed an iqta or wilayat; the village had the chaudhari or muqaddam and the patwari.

112.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Unit / post)
a. Shiq
b. Pargana revenue collection
c. Village headman
d. Village accountant
List-II (Officer)
i. Patwari
ii. Shiqdar
iii. Amil
iv. Muqaddam
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
112.x: Shiq – shiqdar; pargana – amil (revenue collection) and chaudhri; village headman – muqaddam / chaudhari; village accountant – patwari.

112.s:
Consider the following statements:

Reason (R): The pargana was the province of the Sultanate, governed by the muqti.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
112.x: A is true, but R is false: the province was the iqta under the muqti / wali; the pargana was a smaller unit under the amil and chaudhri.

112.s: Which system of transport was often used by the Delhi Sultanate to transport fruits of Khorasan to India?
112.x: Ibn Battuta says the foot-post (dawa), quicker than the horse-post (ulaq), was often used to carry the fruits of Khurasan, much desired in India.

112.s: In the Delhi Sultanate, what was the crown land whose revenue supported the court and royal household called?
112.x: Khalisa was crown land; iqta was assigned to officials in place of salary and inam was granted to religious men and institutions.
xa: **UPPSC 2025**: Sultanate territory broadly **Khalisa and Iqta**.
Bahmani khalisa **paid the central army**.
**Alauddin** enlarged the **khalisa**.

112.s: To whom were Madad-i-Mash revenue-free grants given?
112.x: Madad-i-Mash grants went to saints, religious institutions and mashaikhs; mansabdars were paid through jagirs or cash.
n: Madad-i-Mash was associated with saints. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 82-84]
Madad-i-Mash was associated with religious institutions. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 82-84]
Madad-i-Mash was associated with mashaikhs. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 82-84]
xa: **Maal** = land revenue under the **Mughals**.
**Inam** = land granted to religious leaders/institutions.
**Jagir** = revenue assignment to a **Mansabdar or Jagirdar**.

112.s: Into which categories was the territory of the Delhi Sultanate broadly divided?
112.x: Sultanate land was broadly khalisa (crown land) and iqta (revenue assignments); the jagir belongs to the Bahmani, Qutb Shahi and Mughal systems.
xa: Khalisa revenue went to the **royal treasury, court and household**.
The **Mughal jagir** was tied to **mansab** rank.

112.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Term)
a. Khalisa
b. Inam
c. Mahrousa
d. Madad-i-Mash
List-II (Meaning)
i. Protected town
ii. Mughal revenue-free grant to saints and religious institutions
iii. Crown land
iv. Grants to religious men
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
112.x: Khalisa – crown land for the court and household; inam – grants to religious men; mahrousa – protected town; madad-i-mash – Mughal revenue-free grant to saints, religious institutions, mashaikhs.

112.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Amaram – Vijayanagara
2. Mokasa – Mughals
3. Chauth – one-fourth
4. Sardeshmukhi – one-fifth
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
112.x: Two pairs are correct (amaram – Vijayanagara; chauth – one-fourth). Mokasa was the Marathas' (jagir was the Mughals'), and sardeshmukhi was one-tenth.

112.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Alauddin Khalji received daily market reports from barids and munhiyans.
2. The munhiyans were the open news-writers and the barids the secret spies.
3. The Kakatiya royal bodyguards were called Lenkas.
4. Sultanate territory was broadly divided into khalisa and iqta lands.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
112.x: Statement 2 is wrong: it is the other way round – barids were the news-writers and munhiyans the secret spies.

113.s: What is the name of the tax levied by Aurangzeb on Non-Muslim subjects of his kingdom?

113.x: Aurangzeb reimposed jizya, the tax on non-Muslims, in 1679; zakat and ushr were paid by Muslims and khums was the share of booty.

113.s: ' Khama ' is the state's financial resource from
o: Trade tax paid by Muslim merchants
State's share of 1 / 5th of the war booty
113.x: Khams (khums) was the state's one-fifth share of war booty.

113.s: Which of the following indicates taxes levied on the land product? i. Kharaj ii. Khums iii. Ushr iv. Muktai Select your answer from the following codes –
113.x: Kharaj and ushr were taxes on land produce (and the muqtai/land levy too); khums was the share of war booty, so only the code without it – i, iii and iv – fits.

113.s: ‘Sharb’ was a tax levied on:
113.x: Haq-i-sharb (sharb) was the irrigation tax, 10% of the yield, levied by Firuz Tughlaq.

113.s: Which Sultan of Delhi was the first to charge ‘Ghari’ or House-tax ?
113.x: Alauddin Khalji first levied ghari (house tax) and charai (grazing tax).

113.s: What was Abwab?
o: Tax on merchandise and custom duties.
Miscellaneous kinds of taxes like the house tax, grazing tax, irrigation tax etc.
113.x: Abwab were miscellaneous cesses outside the sharia – house tax, grazing tax, irrigation tax; zakat was a separate religious tax.

113.s: Which one of the following sets consists only of the four Sharia taxes retained by Firoz Tughlaq?
113.x: Firoz Tughlaq abolished the many illegal cesses and kept only the four Sharia taxes: kharaj, jizya, zakat and khams. The other sets include non-Sharia items such as ghari, charai, haq-i-sharb (cesses), taccavi (loans) and iqta or inam (land assignments).
113.tq: Separate the standard Sharia taxes from additional cesses, loans and land assignments.
xs: Firoz kept only the four sharia taxes: **kharaj, jizya, zakat and khams** — option **(3)**.
**Ghari, Charai, Haq-i-sharb** are cesses; **taccavi** is a loan; **iqta** and **inam** are land categories.
xa: Firoz **abolished many illegal cesses**.
He restored the **1/5** khams share.
He extended **jizya** to **Brahmins**.

113.s:
Consider the following statements about Sultanate taxes:
1. Zakat was about 2.5% of wealth.
2. Ushr was paid by non-Muslim cultivators.
3. Ghari and charai were sharia taxes.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
113.x: Zakat was about 2.5%; ushr was paid by Muslim landholders and ghari, charai were cesses, not sharia taxes.

113.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Tax)
a. Kharaj
b. Ushr
c. Jizya
d. Zakat
List-II (Nature and payer)
i. Religious tax of about 2.5% of wealth on Muslims
ii. Land tax of one-tenth on Muslim landholders
iii. Land tax on non-Muslim cultivators
iv. Poll tax on non-Muslims in place of military service
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
113.x: Kharaj – land tax (usually 1/3) on non-Muslim cultivators; ushr – 1/10 land tax on Muslim landholders; jizya – poll / protection tax on non-Muslims in place of military service; zakat – about 2.5% of wealth, Muslims only.

113.s:
Consider the following statements about Sultanate taxation:
1. Firoz Tughlaq kept only the sharia taxes kharaj, jizya, zakat and ushr.
2. Alauddin Khalji and Muhammad bin Tughlaq took four-fifths of the war booty.
3. Firoz Tughlaq restored the sharia share of one-fifth of booty to the state.
4. Charai, a grazing tax on milch cattle, was levied by Alauddin Khalji.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
113.x: Statement 1 is wrong: Firoz's four sharia taxes were kharaj, jizya, zakat and khams (not ushr). The other three are correct.

113.s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Khams was not a tax on land produce.
Reason (R): Khams was the state's one-fifth share of war booty and treasure-troves.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
113.x: Both true and R explains A: khams was the state's share of booty, so unlike kharaj and ushr it was not levied on land produce.

113.s:
Consider the following statements

A. Shamsudin Iltutmish was the first sultan of Delhi to issue regular currency and to declare Delhi as the capital of his empire

B. Shamsudin Iltutmish set up the Iqtadari system which means division of empire into Iqtas, which were assigned to the nobles and officers in lieu of salary

C. Shamsudin Iltutmish introduced the silver tanka and the copper Jital, two basic coins of sultanate period, with a standard weight of 175gm
Which of the above statement is/are correct?
113.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
113.x:
NextGen and this paper write '175 gm'. Strictly the tanka weighed 175 grains (about 11 g), so C is literally wrong; read as grains, all three are correct.
Intended key 'All of these': Iltutmish issued regular currency and made Delhi the capital (A), set up the iqtadari system (B) and introduced the silver tanka and copper jital (C).

113.s: Who introduced the silver tanka and the copper jital - the two basic coins of the Sultanate period ?
113.x: Iltutmish introduced the silver tanka and the copper jital, the two basic coins of the Sultanate.

113.s: Who introduced the silver tanka and the copper mi jital—the two basic coins of the Sultanate period?|| C)
113.x: Iltutmish introduced the silver tanka and the copper jital, the two basic coins of the Sultanate.

113.s: Coins-Tanka, Shashgani and Jital of Sultanate period was made of which of the following metals-
113.x: The tanka and shashgani were silver and the jital copper; no gold or zinc among them.

113.s:
Find out the two main currencies of the Sultanate period from the code given below.

I. Dam
II. Jital

III. Rupiya
IV. Tanka
Codes
113.x: The jital (copper) and tanka (silver) were the two main Sultanate coins; rupiya and dam belong to Sher Shah.

113.s: The term 'Delhiwal' in the medieval history is associated with
o: Coins that were minted in Delhi
Taxes collected on Agriculture by rulers
Export of Spices, textiles and Indigo from Delhi
113.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
113.x: Dehliwal (Delhiwal) was a coin minted at Delhi, current in the Sultanate period (also under the Rajput Chauhans and Tomaras), not a tax or an export.

113.s: Who issued the tanka and jital coins?
113.x: Iltutmish consolidated the Sultanate, issued the tanka and jital and completed the Qutub Minar.
n: Qutbuddin Aibak founded the Slave dynasty. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #82 · pp 162-165]
Qutbuddin Aibak began the construction of the Qutub Minar. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #82 · pp 162-165]
Iltutmish consolidated the Sultanate. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #82 · pp 162-165]
Iltutmish introduced the Tanka. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #82 · pp 162-165]
Iltutmish introduced the Jital. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #82 · pp 162-165]
Iltutmish completed the Qutub Minar. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #82 · pp 162-165]
Balban established a strong monarchy. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #82 · pp 162-165]
Alauddin Khalji introduced market reforms. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #82 · pp 162-165]
Alauddin Khalji introduced military reforms. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #82 · pp 162-165]
Alauddin Khalji undertook southern expeditions. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #82 · pp 162-165]
xa: Aibak also built the **Quwwat-ul-Islam** (**1206–1210**).
**Razia** (**1236–1240**) was the **first and only woman ruler**.
**Firoz Shah Tughluq** — **canals**, **public works**, **Ashokan pillars**.

113.s: Sher Shah's revenue system served as a model for the later:
113.x: Sher Shah's surveyed revenue system became the model for Todar Mal's bandobast.
113.tq: Match the earlier revenue system with the later administrative adaptation.
xs: **Sher Shah's** survey-based revenue was the model for **Todar Mal's bandobast** — option **(4)**.
Sher Shah took **1/4 to 1/3** of produce, **based on survey**.
The **canal** work was **Ghiyasuddin's** and **Firoz's**; the **karkhanas** were Firoz's; the iqta was organised by **Iltutmish**.
xa: Sultanate peasants paid **1/3**, sometimes **1/2**.
Sher Shah also set up the **dak chowki**.

113.s: Who issued the copper Bahloli coin?
113.x: The Bahloli was a copper coin of Bahlol Lodi.

113.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Coin)
a. Shashgani
b. Dinar
c. Token currency
d. Bahloli
List-II (Description)
i. Gold coin popular after the South Indian loot (Alauddin)
ii. Copper coin of Bahlol Lodi
iii. Silver coin worth 6 jitals (Tughlaqs)
iv. Copper / brass at par with silver (MBT)
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
113.x: Shashgani – silver, 6 jitals, Tughlaqs; dinar – gold, popular after the South Indian loot, Alauddin; token – copper/brass at par with silver, MBT (1329-30); Bahloli – copper, Bahlol Lodi.

113.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Iltutmish's silver tanka weighed 175 grains.
2. Muhammad bin Tughlaq's token currency failed through forgery.
3. 64 jitals made one tanka.
4. Sher Shah's revenue system was the model for Todar Mal's bandobast.
How many of the above statements are correct?
113.x: Three are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: 48 jitals made one tanka; 64 is the number of dams in Sher Shah's rupiya.

113.s: With reference to the economic history of medieval India, the term 'Araghatta' refers to
o: Land grants made to military officers
Waterwheel used in the irrigation of land
113.x: Araghatta was a water-wheel used to irrigate land – a wheel with pots on its rim worked by animals to lift water from wells.

113.s: The irrigation device called 'Araghatta' was
o: a water bag made of leather pulled over a pulley
a large wheel with earthen pots tied to the outer ends of its spokes
a larger earthen pot driven by bullocks
a large water bucket pulled up by rope directly by hand
113.x: Araghatta (ara = spokes, ghata = pot) was a large wheel with earthen pots tied to the outer ends of its spokes, turned by bullocks – not a leather bag (charas) or a hand-drawn bucket.

113.s: With reference to the economic history of medieval India, the term ‘Araghatta’ refers to –
o: Land grants made to military officers
Waterwheel used for the irrigation of land
113.x: Araghatta was a water-wheel used to irrigate land – a wheel with pots on its rim worked by animals to lift water from wells.

o: a water bag made of leather pulled over a pulley
a large wheel with earthen pots tied to the outer ends of
a larger earthen pot driven by bullocks
a large water bucket pulled up by rope directly by hand
113.x: Araghatta (ara = spokes, ghata = pot) was a large wheel with earthen pots tied to the outer ends of its spokes, turned by bullocks – not a leather bag (charas) or a hand-drawn bucket.

113.s: In 13th and 14th Century, Indian farmer did not cultivated .....
113.x: Wheat, barley and gram were grown; maize reached India only later, through the Portuguese.

113.s: What was the land tax of the Kakatiyas called?
113.x: The Kakatiya land tax was Ari; Maagani was irrigated land and Metta rain-fed land.

113.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq is regarded as the first canal-builder of the 14th century.
2. Muhammad bin Tughlaq laid out 1,200 orchards near Delhi.
3. Firoz Tughlaq built the most canals; the longest ran from the Yamuna to Hisar.
4. In Kakatiya land classification, Maagani meant dry land.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
113.x: Statements 2 and 4 are wrong: the 1,200 orchards were Firoz's (MBT is known for the Diwan-i-Kohi and taccavi), and Maagani was irrigated land – Metta was dry land.

113.s: Who was the first Sultan to provide relief to famine-affected people ?
113.src: AP Grama Ward Sachivalayam Category-III Ward Sanitation & En
113.x: Muhammad bin Tughlaq was the first Sultan to organise famine relief – taccavi (sondhar) loans to cultivators, relief camps and moving the court to Swargadwari during the Doab famine.

113.s: The Sultan who is said to have raised the land revenue to one-half of the produce was
113.x: Alauddin Khalji raised the land revenue (kharaj) to one-half of the produce.

113.s:
Consider the following statements.

I. Alauddin Khilji held religious discourse with Acharya Mahasena.

II. Alauddin Khilji and Muhammad bin Tughluq demanded one-sixth of the agricultural produce as revenue from the peasants.
Which of the statements(s) given above is/are correct?
113.x: Only I: Alauddin held discourses with the Jain Acharya Mahasena. Alauddin demanded one-half, and MBT raised it further in the Doab – not one-sixth.

113.s:
With reference to Sultan Alauddin Khilji, consider the following statements.

I. Alauddin Khilji fixed the prices of foodgrains.

II. Alauddin Khilji was the first Sultan, who paid his soldiers in cash.

III. During Alauddin Khilji’s rule, the share of the land revenue to be paid by the peasant was raised to half of the produce.
Which of these statements are correct?
113.x: All three: Alauddin fixed grain prices, paid soldiers in cash and raised land revenue to half the produce.

113.s: Who gave taccavi (sondhar) loans for agriculture?
113.x: MBT set up Diwan-i-Kohi and gave taccavi (sondhar) loans.

113.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Khalisa was the land assigned to army commanders.
2. Iqta was land revenue assigned to officials in place of salary.
3. Inam was land given as religious grants.
4. Alauddin's price-control markets show that military needs shaped economic policy.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
113.x: Statement 1 is wrong: khalisa was crown land. Iqta (in place of salary), inam (religious grants) and the military motive of Alauddin's markets are correct.

113.s: Which of the following cities was a Mughal imperial centre?
113.x: Agra was a Mughal imperial centre; Siri, Tughlaqabad and Jahanpanah were Sultanate cities of Alauddin, Ghiyasuddin and MBT.
n: Agra was a Mughal imperial centre. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #26-2 · pp 90-93]
Delhi was a Mughal imperial capital, especially under Shah Jahan. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #26-2 · pp 90-93]
Lahore was a Mughal political and architectural centre. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #26-2 · pp 90-93]
Allahabad was associated with Akbar's fort. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #26-2 · pp 90-93]
Allahabad was associated with Mughal administration. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #26-2 · pp 90-93]
Allahabad was also known as Prayagraj. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #26-2 · pp 90-93]
Delhi was a Mughal political centre. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #26-2 · pp 90-93]

113.s: Which one of the following was NOT founded by Firoz Shah Tughlaq?
113.x: Siri was founded by Alauddin Khalji. Firoz Shah Tughlaq founded Firozabad, Fatehabad, Hisar-Firoza and Jaunpur.
113.tq: Find the odd city-founder association within the same historical period.
xs: **Siri** was NOT founded by Firoz; it was **Alauddin Khalji's** — option **(4)**.
Firoz founded **Firozabad**, **Hisar Firoza**, **Fatehabad** and **Jaunpur**.
xa: **Tughlaqabad** = Ghiyasuddin; **Jahanpanah** = MBT.
**Agra (1504)** = Sikandar Lodi.

113.s: Which of the following pairs (town – founder) is INCORRECTLY matched?
113.x: Jahanpanah was founded by MBT; Alauddin built Siri.

113.s: Why was paper-making important for the Sultanate administration?
113.x: The availability of paper strengthened bureaucratic record-keeping in the Sultanate administration.
113.tq: Link a technological development to its administrative consequence.
xs: Paper-making **strengthened bureaucratic record-keeping** — option **(2)**.
It did not replace coinage: the **tanka** (silver) and **jital** (copper) remained the basic coins.
xa: Paper and the **Persian wheel** were lasting gains.
Other Turkish technologies: **glass-making**, **spinning wheel**, better **looms**.
Superior **mortar** for **arches and domes**.

113.s: Which statement regarding slaves during the Sultanate period is correct?
o: Slaves were employed only in agriculture and not traded
Ibn Battuta mentioned slave markets, and Firoz Tughlaq maintained a separate department for slaves
Slaves were absent from urban markets
Firoz Tughlaq abolished all forms of slavery
113.x: Ibn Battuta referred to slave markets, and Firoz Tughlaq maintained a separate department for slaves.
113.tq: Reject absolute statements and combine the two documented features of slavery.
xs: **Ibn Battuta** mentioned **slave markets**, and **Firoz** had a **separate department** for slaves — option **(2)**.
Firoz did not abolish slavery; slaves were traded in markets.
xa: Firoz's slave department = **Diwan-i-Bandagan**.
Firoz also ran about **36 karkhanas**.

113.s: Which social developments are associated with medieval Hindu society during the Sultanate period?
o: The disappearance of caste distinctions and purdah
The abolition of sati and caste by royal decree
The replacement of caste by iqta administration
The continuation of caste order and the spread of sati and purdah
113.x: Hindu society retained its caste order, while sati and purdah spread during this period.
113.tq: Identify the option that preserves both social features rather than reversing them.
xs: Hindu society kept its **caste order**, while **sati and purdah spread** — option **(4)**.
So caste did not disappear and sati was not abolished.
xa: **Nobles** held iqtas; **ulema** kept religious law.
**Peasants** bore the revenue burden.

113.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Commodity)
a. Horses and glassware
b. Silk and porcelain
c. Pepper (Ibn Battuta)
d. Diamonds (Amir Khusrau)
List-II (Source)
i. Malabar
ii. Warangal
iii. West Asia
iv. China
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
113.x: Horses, textiles, glassware from West Asia; silk and porcelain from China; Ibn Battuta notes Malabar pepper; Amir Khusrau says Warangal's wealth and diamonds drew the Delhi invasions.

113.s:
Consider the following statements about Sultanate trade and crafts:
1. The Multanis and Khurasanis handled overseas trade and finance.
2. Gujaratis, Marwaris and Bohras carried on mainly inland trade.
3. The Banjaras carried grain on camels.
4. Firoz Tughlaq ran about 36 royal karkhanas.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
113.x: Statement 3 is wrong: the Banjaras carried grain on oxen.

113.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Paper and the spinning wheel were among the Turkish gains.
2. Firoz Tughlaq took about 1,300 Sanskrit manuscripts from a temple at Mathura.
3. Leather, metal-work and carpet-weaving were crafts of the Sultanate period.
4. Agra was founded by Sikandar Lodi in 1504.
Which of the statements given above is/are NOT correct?
113.x: Only statement 2 is wrong: Firoz took the 1,300 Sanskrit manuscripts from the Jawalamukhi temple at Nagarkot, not Mathura.

113.s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): The khuts and muqaddams collected the peasants' revenue.
Reason (R): The ulema were the keepers of the religious law.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
113.x: Both are true (notes on society: khuts and muqaddams collected revenue; the ulema kept the religious law), but R does not explain A.

114.s: The historian Barani refused to consider the state in India under Delhi Sultans as truly Islamic because:
o: the majority of the population did not follow Islam
the Muslims theologists were often disregarded
the Sultan supplemented the Muslim law by framing his own regulations
religious freedom was accorded to non‑Muslims
114.x: Barani said the state was not truly Islamic because the Sultan supplemented the sharia with his own state laws (zawabit).

114.s: The historian Barani did not consider the state in India under Delhi Sultans as truly Islamic because :
o: The majority of the population did not follow Islam
The Muslim theologists were often disregarded
The Sultan supplemented the Muslim law by framing
The religious freedom was accorded to non-Muslims
114.x: Barani said the state was not truly Islamic because the Sultan supplemented the sharia with his own state laws (zawabit).

114.s: Who were called ‘Dastar-Bandan’?
114.x: The ulema were called Dastar-bandan (turban-wearers); the Sayyids were the Kulah-daran.

114.s:
Consider the following statements about Sultanate social groups:
1. The Ajlaf were lower-status Muslims.
2. The Kulah-daran were the ulema.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
114.x: The Ajlaf were lower-status Muslims; the Kulah-daran were the Sayyids, while the ulema were the Dastar-bandan.

114.s: Which officer of the Delhi Sultanate was in charge of religious grants and also acted as Chief Qazi?
114.x: The Sadr-us-Sudur handled religious grants and was also the Chief Qazi.

114.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Term)
a. Dastar-bandan
b. Kulah-daran
c. Ashraf
d. Ajlaf
List-II (Meaning)
i. Sayyids (pointed-cap wearers)
ii. Muslims of foreign descent
iii. Lower-status (Indian convert) Muslims
iv. Ulema (turban-wearers)
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
114.x: Dastar-bandan – ulema; kulah-daran – Sayyids; ashraf – Turks, Persians, Afghans of foreign descent; ajlaf – lower-status Indian convert Muslims.

114.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Barani set out his ideal of rule in the Fatawa-i-Jahandari.
2. The Qazi-ul-Quzat handled religious grants.
3. The Rais and Ranas were local Hindu chiefs who paid tribute and collected taxes.
4. Turks and Indian Muslims intermarried freely.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
114.x: Statements 2 and 4 are wrong: the Qazi-ul-Quzat was the chief judge (the Sadr-us-Sudur handled religious grants), and Turks, Persians, Afghans and Indian Muslims rarely intermarried.

114.s: Which Sultan of Delhi had levied ‘Jizya’ on Brahmins?
114.x: Firuz Tughlaq was the first to levy jizya on Brahmins, who had been exempt earlier.

114.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Muhammad bin Tughlaq — Leaned on Sufis against the ulema
Firoz Tughlaq — Followed the ulema’s advice
Sikandar Lodi — Tolerant ruler who gave non-Muslims important posts
114.x: Sikandar Lodi was orthodox; he destroyed temples at Mathura, broke the Jwalamukhi images at Nagarkot and imposed jizya. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
114.tq: Find the one reversed ruler–policy association.
xs: **Sikandar Lodi – tolerant ruler** is wrong: he was **orthodox** — option **(3)**.
He destroyed **Mathura** temples, broke the **Jwalamukhi** images at **Nagarkot** and imposed **jizya**.
The rest are correct: **MBT** leaned on Sufis; **Firoz** followed the ulema; **Iltutmish** gave non-Muslims posts.
xa: **Jalaluddin Khalji** = first Sultan benevolent to Hindus.
⚠ **Alauddin** = ulema shut out; **Firoz** = ulema followed.

114.s: Which Sultan leaned on the Sufis against the ulema and visited the Ajmer shrine?
114.x: Muhammad bin Tughlaq leaned on the Sufis against the ulema; Firoz, by contrast, followed the ulema.

114.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched (Sultan – religious approach)?
o: Alauddin Khalji – followed the counsel of the ulema
Jalaluddin Khalji – first Sultan benevolent to Hindus
Muhammad bin Tughlaq – leaned on the Sufis
114.x: Alauddin kept the ulema out of state affairs; it was Firoz Tughlaq who followed the ulema.

114.s: Which of the following was NOT exempt from jizya under the Sultans?
114.x: Women, children, the old and the disabled were exempt; jizya fell on other non-Muslims in place of military service.

114.s:
Consider the following statements about jizya under the Sultans:
1. Women, children and the old were exempt.
2. Sikandar Lodi imposed jizya.
3. Brahmins remained exempt throughout the Sultanate.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
114.x: Women, children and the old were exempt and Sikandar Lodi imposed jizya; Brahmins were exempt only at first, as Firoz extended jizya to them.

114.s:
Consider the following statements about the religious policy of the Sultans:
1. Jalaluddin Khalji was the first Sultan benevolent to Hindus.
2. In 1320 Hindu gods were worshipped in the palace under Qutbuddin Mubarak Shah.
3. Alauddin Khalji told Qazi Mughisuddin that he ordered whatever was good for the state.
4. Muhammad bin Tughlaq leaned on the Sufis against the ulema and visited the Ajmer shrine.
How many of the above statements are correct?
114.x: Three are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Hindu gods were worshipped in the palace in 1320 under Nasiruddin Khusrau Shah.

114.s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Women, children and the old were exempt from jizya.
Reason (R): The Qutb Shahis of Golconda imposed jizya on all non-Muslims.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
114.x: A is true (women, children, the old, the disabled and at first Brahmins were exempt), but R is false: the Qutb Shahis never imposed jizya.

114.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Sikandar Lodi destroyed the Mathura temples and broke the Nagarkot images.
2. Firoz Tughlaq respected the Abbasid Caliph of Baghdad.
3. Temple destruction often served political ends of royal legitimacy as well as religious ones.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
114.x: Statement 2 is wrong: Firoz respected the Egyptian Caliph. 1 and 3 are correct.

114.s: Which of the following Sultans had most number of slaves in his court?
114.x: Firuz Tughlaq had about 1,80,000 slaves and a separate department (Diwan-i-Bandagan) for them.

114.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about women in the Sultanate period?
o: Chand Bibi ruled the Delhi Sultanate
Jauhar was performed at Chittor in 1303
114.x: Chand Bibi defended Ahmadnagar and never ruled Delhi; Razia was the only woman ruler of Delhi.

114.s:
Consider the following statements about women in the Sultanate period:
1. Purdah spread among upper-class women of north India from the 13th century.
2. Jauhar was performed at Ranthambhor (1301) and Chittor (1303).
3. Sati in this period was recorded by Al-Biruni.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
114.x: Statement 3 is wrong: the traveller who recorded sati was Ibn Battuta.

114.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Woman)
a. Lal Ded
b. Chand Bibi
c. Rudrama Devi
d. Razia
List-II (Identity)
i. Only woman ruler of Delhi
ii. Kakatiya
iii. Woman saint of Kashmir
iv. Ahmadnagar
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
114.x: Lal Ded – Kashmiri woman saint; Chand Bibi – Ahmadnagar; Rudrama Devi – Kakatiya; Razia (1236-40) – the only woman ruler of Delhi.

114.s:
Consider the following statements about slavery:
1. Alauddin's third market dealt in horses, slaves and cattle.
2. Slavery in the Vijayanagara empire was called Perantallu.
3. Firoz Tughlaq had about 18,000 slaves.
4. Firoz Tughlaq created the Diwan-i-Bandagan.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
114.x: Statements 2 and 3 are wrong: Vijayanagara slavery was Benabaga (Perantallu were Reddi-period women deified after sati), and Firoz had about 1,80,000 slaves.

114.s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): The first dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate is called the 'Slave' or 'Mamluk' dynasty.
Reason (R): Aibak, Iltutmish and Balban had themselves been slaves (bandagan).
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
114.x: Both true and R explains A: the dynasty is called 'Slave' or 'Mamluk' because Aibak, Iltutmish and Balban had been slaves.

114.s:
Consider the following statements about theories of conversion in medieval India:
1. Political patronage, such as office and tax relief, was a partial factor.
2. Under the social liberation theory, caste-like ranks disappeared among converts.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
114.x: Political patronage was a partial factor; social liberation is also only partial because caste-like ranks survived among converts.

114.s: In which of the following did the Bhakti movement have its indigenous roots?
114.x: The Bhakti movement had indigenous roots in the Alvars and Nayanars; Islam only reinforced its egalitarian and anti-ritual tendencies.
xa: Islam shaped later Bhakti's **egalitarianism** (**Kabir, Nanak, Ravidas**).
Khanqahs and dargahs drew **Hindus and Muslims** alike.

114.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Arthashastra – Compared by Al-Biruni with the Sufi idea of divine love
Amritakund – Translated into Arabic and Persian
Al-Biruni – Parallel between the Sufi idea of the soul and Patanjali's Yoga Sutra
114.x: Al-Biruni compared the Sufi idea of divine love with the Gita, not the Arthashastra; the other pairs are correct.
xa: **Nizamuddin Auliya** was struck by **Nath-yogic** body theory.
Amritakund = a **Hatha-yoga** text.

114.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Raja Man Singh of Gwalior — Man Kautuhal
114.x: Dalail-i-Firozshahi was associated with Sanskrit texts translated during Firoz Tughlaq's reign, not with Baba Farid. Pir Bhodan, Raja Man Singh and Jayasi are correctly matched.
114.tq: Find the swapped author-work association among closely related cultural figures.
xs: **Baba Farid – Dalail-i-Firozshahi** is wrong: Baba Farid was a **Chishti Sufi** — option **(1)**.
The rest are correct: **Jayasi – Padmavat**; **Raja Man Singh of Gwalior – Man Kautuhal**; **Pir Bhodan – Sufi musician**.
xa: Other Chishtis: **Muinuddin**, **Nizamuddin Auliya**.
Padmavat uses **human love** as metaphor for **divine love**.

114.s: Which musical instrument is credited to Amir Khusrau?
114.x: Amir Khusrau is credited with the sitar and with qawwali.

114.s: Akkanna and Madanna, called the 'Andhra Sultans', belonged to which kingdom?
114.x: Akkanna and Madanna were the 'Andhra Sultans' of Qutb Shahi Golconda under Abul Hasan Tana Shah.

114.s:
Consider the following statements about theories of conversion:
1. The 'sword' theory of forced mass conversion is rejected as a colonial trope.
2. The Meenakshipuram conversion (February 1981) is cited as a case of social liberation.
3. Sufi influence with agrarian expansion was a major factor in Gujarat and the Deccan.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
114.x: Statement 3 is wrong: Sufi influence with agrarian expansion was a major factor in Bengal and Punjab.

114.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Person)
a. Al-Biruni
b. Sheikh Nuruddin
c. Malik Muhammad Jayasi
d. Amir Khusrau
List-II (Contribution)
i. Padmavat
ii. Compared Sufi divine love with the Bhagavad Gita
iii. Credited with the sitar and qawwali
iv. Founded the Rishi movement of Kashmir
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
114.x: Al-Biruni – Sufi love compared with the Gita; Sheikh Nuruddin – Kashmir's Rishi movement; Jayasi – Padmavat; Amir Khusrau – sitar and qawwali.

114.s:
Consider the following statements about syncretism:
1. The Amritakund, a hatha-yoga text, was put into Arabic and Persian.
2. The Chishtis spoke to the people in Hindavi.
3. Amir Khusrau wrote the Padmavat.
4. The Dalail-i-Firozshahi rendered Sanskrit texts in Persian under Firoz Tughlaq.
How many of the above statements are correct?
114.x: Three are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Padmavat is by Malik Muhammad Jayasi.

114.s:
Consider the following statements about the Deccan:
1. Gesu Daraz moved to Gulbarga under Firoz Shah Bahmani and wrote the Mirqat-ul-Ashyaq.
2. In Golconda the foreign Muslims were called Afaqis.
3. Ibrahim Qutb Shah granted villages to the Bhadrachalam temple.
4. Brahmins in Golconda held Mustajir (tax-farming) rights.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
114.x: Statement 3 is wrong: the Bhadrachalam grant was made by Abul Hasan Tana Shah.

115.s: The Horse-Shoe arch was first introduced in the -
115.x: The Alai Darwaza (1311) of Alauddin Khalji introduced the horse-shoe arch with a lotus-bud fringe, and has the first true dome. Balban's tomb has the first true arch, not the horse-shoe arch.

115.s: The first true arch in the Sultanate memorial could be seen in
115.x: Balban's tomb at Mehrauli shows the first true arch in India. The Alai Darwaza has the first true dome; Iltutmish's tomb and Quwwat-ul-Islam use corbelled (false) arches.

115.s: India’s first tomb constructed in the Indo-Islamic style was
115.x:
Most books and keys: Balban's tomb (first tomb in a true Indo-Islamic style, with the true arch). Strictly: the first Islamic tomb in India is Sultan Ghari (1231), built by Iltutmish for his son Nasiruddin Mahmud (app notes 1:115; ASI).
Balban's tomb (Mehrauli) is given as the first tomb in a purely Indo-Islamic style, being the first with a true arch. Humayun's tomb is Mughal; Aibak's tomb (Lahore) and Alauddin's tomb are not counted as the first.

115.s: Which among the following is ‘Octagonal tomb’?
115.x: Sikandar Lodi's tomb is octagonal (an arched verandah round the chamber) and has the first double dome. Balban's, Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq's and Firoz Shah's tombs are square.

115.s:
Match the following.
List I (Architectural Style)
List II (Associated Dynasty)

A. 'Lotus bud' fringe on the underside of the arch
1. Sharquis

B. Emergence of octagonal tomb
2. Vijayanagara

C. Use of Bodegoi in the pillar
3. Khiljis

D. Massive entrance gate with inclined walls
4. Tughluqs
Codes A B C D
115.x: Lotus-bud fringe on the arch = Khaljis (A-3, Alai Darwaza); octagonal tomb emerged under the Tughluqs (B-4, Khan-i-Jahan Tilangani); bodegai (bracket capital) = Vijayanagara (C-2); massive propylon gateways with inclined walls = Sharqis of Jaunpur (D-1, Atala Masjid). So 3 4 2 1.

115.s: For which of the following is the tomb of Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq at Tughlaqabad noted?
o: A double dome on an octagonal plan
Sloping walls and a marble dome
A horseshoe arch with lotus-bud fringe
115.x: Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq's tomb is noted for its sloping (battered) walls and marble dome.
xa: **Tughlaqabad** fort-city was built by **Ghiyasuddin Tughluq** — massive, rugged, built for security.
Tughlaq style is called the "**crisis period of architecture**" (Mongol threat, finances).
Qutb complex holds the **Tomb of Iltutmish**, not the Tughlaq tombs.

115.s: The domes and false arches of Tughlaq architecture show the influence of which styles?
115.x: Tughlaq domes and false arches show Syrian and Byzantine influence.
xa: The Tughlaq period is called the "**crisis period of architecture**".
Examples: **Tughlaqabad** fort-city and **Ghiyasuddin's tomb** (battered walls, **marble dome**).
First **octagonal** tomb (Khan-i-Jahan Tilangani's) also dates from the **Tughlaq** period.

115.s:
Consider the following statements about Indo-Islamic architecture:
1. The true arch is held in place by a keystone.
2. The Indian trabeate style was based on lintel, pillar and corbel.
3. Decoration moved towards human and animal figures.
4. Surkhi was brick dust used in lime mortar.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
115.x: Statement 3 is wrong: decoration moved away from human and animal figures to arabesque, geometry and Quranic calligraphy.

115.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Architectural first)
a. Earliest Indo-Islamic building
b. First Islamic tomb (strictly)
c. First octagonal tomb
d. First double dome
List-II (Building)
i. Sikandar Lodi's tomb
ii. Sultan Ghari (1231)
iii. Quwwat-ul-Islam, Delhi
iv. Khan-i-Jahan Tilangani's tomb
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
115.x: Earliest Indo-Islamic building – Quwwat-ul-Islam (Aibak, 1198); first Islamic tomb strictly – Sultan Ghari (1231); first octagonal tomb – Khan-i-Jahan Tilangani's; first double dome – Sikandar Lodi's tomb.

115.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Sultan Ghari (1231) was built by Iltutmish for his son Nasiruddin Mahmud.
2. The Lodis pioneered the double dome, which reached the Mughals through Akbar's tomb.
3. Balban's tomb has the first true arch.
4. The Alai Darwaza has the first true dome.
How many of the above statements are correct?
115.x: Three are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the double dome reached the Mughals through Humayun's Tomb.

115.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Feature)
a. Horse-shoe arch with lotus-bud fringe
b. Battered walls and Syrian/Byzantine-type false arches
c. Massive propylon gateway, no minarets
d. Bodegai (bracket capital) on pillars
List-II (Style)
i. Tughlaq
ii. Vijayanagara
iii. Sharqi (Jaunpur)
iv. Khalji
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
115.x: Lotus-bud fringed horse-shoe arch – Khalji (Alai Darwaza); battered walls and false arches – Tughlaq; propylon gateway without minarets – Sharqi (Atala Masjid); bodegai – Vijayanagara.

115.s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): The mihrab is the pulpit of a mosque.
Reason (R): A jali is a pierced stone screen.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
115.x: A is false: the mihrab is the prayer niche; the pulpit is the minbar. R is true: a jali is a pierced stone screen.

115.s: Which sultan built Alai Darwaza?
115.x: Alauddin Khalji built the Alai Darwaza (1311) as the southern gateway of the Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque.

115.s: Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque in Delhi was built by:
115.x: Qutbuddin Aibak built the Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque (completed 1198), the first mosque of the Turkish rulers in Delhi, from the material of 27 temples.

115.s: What is ‘Adhai Din ka Zhonpda’?
115.x: Adhai Din ka Jhonpra at Ajmer is a mosque built by Qutbuddin Aibak from temple material. It is not a temple, hut or tower.

115.s: Hauz-e-Sultani is a…
115.x: Hauz-i-Sultani (Hauz-i-Shamsi) at Mehrauli is a reservoir dug by Iltutmish; 'hauz' means a water tank.

115.s:
Match the following.
List I (Monuments)
List II (Builder)

A. Quwwat-ul-Islam
1. Alauddin Khilji

B. Hauz Khas in Delhi
2. Iltutmish

C. Adilabad Fort
3. Muhammad bin Tughluq

D. Jama Masjid in Budaun
4. Qutbuddin Aibak
Codes A B C D
115.x: Quwwat-ul-Islam – Aibak (A-4); Hauz Khas (Hauz-i-Alai) tank – Alauddin Khalji (B-1); Adilabad Fort – Muhammad bin Tughluq (C-3); Jama Masjid, Budaun – Iltutmish (D-2). So 4 1 3 2. Firoz Tughlaq only added the madrasa and his tomb at Hauz Khas.

115.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
115.x: Tughlaqabad was built by Ghiyasuddin Tughluq. The Qila-i-Kuhna Mosque is Sher Shah Suri's, the Moth Masjid dates from Sikandar Lodi's reign and the Kirti Stambha is Rana Kumbha's.
n: Qila-e-Kuhna Mosque was built by Sher Shah Suri. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #70 · pp 146-147]
Moth Masjid was built during the reign of Sikandar Lodi. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #70 · pp 146-147]
Tughluqabad was built by Ghiyasuddin Tughluq. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #70 · pp 146-147]
Kirti Stambha was built by Rana Kumbha. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #70 · pp 146-147]
xa: Qila-e-Kuhna is at **Purana Qila**, Delhi, built in **1541**.
**Tughlaqabad** was massive and rugged, built for security.
**Muhammad bin Tughlaq** built **Jahanpanah**.

115.s: Who built the city of Jahanpanah?
115.x: Jahanpanah and a fortress at Allahabad are associated with Muhammad bin Tughlaq; Siri Fort is Alauddin's and Firoz Shah Kotla is Firoz's.
xa: **Ghiyasuddin Tughluq** built the **Tughlaqabad** fort-city — massive, rugged, built for security.
Tughlaq style: **sloping (battered) walls**, pointed domes, false arches.

115.s:
Which of the following is the correct chronological order of these monuments?
1. Alai Darwaza
2. Qila-i-Kuhna Mosque
3. Sultan Garhi
4. Tughlaqabad Fort
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
115.x: Sultan Garhi (1231), Alai Darwaza (1311), Tughlaqabad (1320-25) and Qila-i-Kuhna Mosque (1541).

115.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Monument)
a. Red Palace (Kushk-i-Lal)
b. Jamat Khana Masjid, Nizamuddin dargah
c. Adilabad Fort
d. Kirti Stambha, Chittor
List-II (Builder)
i. Rana Kumbha
ii. Balban
iii. Khizr Khan (Alauddin's son)
iv. Muhammad bin Tughlaq
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
115.x: Kushk-i-Lal – Balban; Jamat Khana Masjid – Khizr Khan, Alauddin's son; Adilabad Fort – MBT; Kirti Stambha – Rana Kumbha.

115.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Firoz Shah Tughlaq added a madrasa and his own tomb at Hauz Khas, on Alauddin's tank.
2. The Qila-i-Kuhna Mosque (1541) in the Purana Qila was built by Humayun.
3. The Topra Ashokan pillar stands in Firoz Shah Kotla.
4. The Moth ki Masjid and Bara Gumbad belong to Sikandar Lodi's reign.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
115.x: Statement 2 is wrong: the Qila-i-Kuhna Mosque (1541) was built by Sher Shah Suri.

115.s: The Qutab Minar was named after: merican
115.x:
Most books and keys: named after Khwaja Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki. Some historians: named after its builder Qutbuddin Aibak (Wikipedia, citing ASI).
The Qutb Minar is commonly held to be named after the Sufi saint Khwaja Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki; it was begun by Qutbuddin Aibak and completed by Iltutmish. Iltutmish and Raziya are not its namesakes.

115.s: Who amongst the following sultans built the fifth storey of Qutub Minar?
115.x: Firoz Shah Tughlaq replaced the lightning-damaged top storey and added the fifth storey. Aibak built the first storey and Iltutmish the next three; Sikandar Lodi only repaired it.

115.s: Who among the following sultans built the fifth storey of Qutub Minar?
115.x: Firoz Shah Tughlaq replaced the lightning-damaged top storey and added the fifth storey. Aibak built the first storey and Iltutmish the next three; Sikandar Lodi only repaired it.

115.s:
Consider the following statements about the Qutb Minar:
1. Sikandar Lodi carried out repairs to it.
2. It is about 180 ft high.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
115.x: Sikandar Lodi, like Firoz Tughlaq, repaired the minar; it is about 238 ft (72.5 m) high, not 180 ft.

115.s:
Consider the following statements about the Qutb Minar:
1. Qutbuddin Aibak began it, building the first storey (c. 1199).
2. Iltutmish built the second to fourth storeys.
3. Sikandar Lodi added the fifth storey.
4. It is about 72.5 m high, with five tapering storeys.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
115.x: Statement 3 is wrong: Firoz Shah Tughlaq replaced the lightning-damaged top storey and added the fifth; Sikandar Lodi only repaired it.

115.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. 'Qutb Minar and its Monuments, Delhi' became a World Heritage Site in 1993.
2. The site includes Tughlaqabad.
3. The site includes Imam Zamin's tomb and the Alai Minar.
4. The king 'Chandra' of the Iron Pillar is identified with Samudragupta.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
115.x: Statements 2 and 4 are wrong: Tughlaqabad is not part of the site, and 'Chandra' of the Gupta-period Iron Pillar is Chandragupta II.

115.s: Which one of the following monuments has a dome which is said to be one of the largest in the world?
115.x: The Gol Gumbaz (Bijapur), tomb of Muhammad Adil Shah, has one of the largest domes in the world (second only to St Peter's, Rome) and a whispering gallery.

115.s: Which of the following sets consists entirely of monuments associated with Bengal architecture?
o: Mahmud Gawan Madrasa, Bidar Fort and Ashtur tombs
Atala Masjid, Chand Minar and Gol Gumbaz
Charminar, Adina Mosque and Jami Masjid of Mandu
Eklakhi tomb, Dakhil Darwaza and Chota Sona Masjid
115.x: The Eklakhi tomb, Dakhil Darwaza and Chota Sona Masjid are all Bengal monuments. Option A is Bahmani (Bidar), B mixes Jaunpur, Daulatabad and Bijapur, and C mixes Hyderabad, Bengal and Mandu (Malwa).
115.tq: Identify the complete regional cluster rather than matching only one monument.
xs: **Eklakhi tomb, Dakhil Darwaza and Chota Sona Masjid** are all **Bengal** monuments — option **(4)**.
Option (1) is **Bahmani** (Bidar); (2) mixes **Jaunpur**, Daulatabad and **Bijapur**; (3) mixes **Hyderabad**, Bengal and **Mandu**.
xa: Bengal style: **brick** building, **curved roofs**.
**Adina Mosque** and the **Pandua** mosques are the earliest Bengal examples.

115.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
115.x: The Adina Mosque is associated with Pandua in Bengal, not Gujarat. Gol Gumbaz is at Bijapur, Jami Masjid at Mandu and Chand Minar at Daulatabad.
115.tq: Check the region of each monument and locate the swapped regional association.
xs: **Adina Mosque — Gujarat** is wrong: the Adina Mosque is at **Pandua, Bengal** — option **(4)**.
Others are correct: **Chand Minar–Daulatabad**, **Gol Gumbaz–Bijapur**, **Jami Masjid–Mandu** (Malwa).
xa: **Gujarat** style: strong Hindu-Jain carving; **Jama Masjid, Ahmedabad**.
⚠ **Atala Masjid** = Jaunpur; **Adina Mosque** = Pandua (Bengal); **Gol Gumbaz** = Bijapur.

115.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Monument)
a. Adina Mosque
b. Atala Masjid
c. Jahaz Mahal
d. Chand Minar
List-II (Place)
i. Mandu
ii. Pandua
iii. Daulatabad
iv. Jaunpur
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
115.x: Adina Mosque – Pandua (Bengal); Atala Masjid – Jaunpur (Sharqi); Jahaz Mahal – Mandu (Malwa); Chand Minar – Daulatabad (Bahmani, 1435).

115.s:
Consider the following statements about provincial styles:
1. The Gujarat style shows strong Hindu-Jain carving.
2. The Gulbarga Jama Masjid has a fully covered courtyard and a large dome.
3. The Mahmud Gawan Madrasa is at Gulbarga.
4. Bengal buildings used brick, curved bamboo-type roofs and terracotta.
How many of the above statements are correct?
115.x: Three are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Mahmud Gawan Madrasa is at Bidar.

115.s: What is the name of the 16th century stepwell that the Archaeological Survey of India recently conserved in collaboration with the World Monuments Fund India?
o: More than one of the above
115.x: Rajon ki Baoli, Mehrauli (c. 1506, Daulat Khan Lodi, reign of Sikandar Lodi) was conserved by the ASI with the World Monuments Fund India (TCS Foundation funding) and reopened in May 2025. Agrasen ki Baoli and Chauki Bavdi were not this project.

115.s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Rajon ki Baoli at Mehrauli was built in the reign of Ibrahim Lodi.
Reason (R): Rajon ki Baoli was built around 1506 by Daulat Khan Lodi.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
115.x: A is false: the stepwell belongs to Sikandar Lodi's reign (Ibrahim ruled 1517-26). R is true: Daulat Khan Lodi built it about 1506.

115.s: Which of the following features is associated with Golconda Fort?
o: A fully covered courtyard and a Persian madrasa
An acoustic system and piped water supply
Curved brick roofs and a Bengal-style mosque plan
115.x: Golconda Fort is known for its remarkable acoustics and its provision of piped water.
115.tq: Identify the monument through its unusual functional features rather than its dynasty alone.
xs: **Golconda Fort** is known for its **acoustics** and **piped water** — option **(2)**.
A handclap at the gate is heard at **Bala Hisar**, nearly **1 km** away.
Covered courtyard = **Gulbarga**; curved brick roofs = **Bengal**; propylon = **Jaunpur**.
xa: **Qutb Shahi Tombs** at **Ibrahim Bagh** hold the **seven** rulers.
Golconda Jami Masjid gateway has fine **Nastaliq** calligraphy.

115.s: By which building are the minarets of the Charminar said to have been inspired?
115.x: The minarets of Sultan Quli's Juma Masjid at Golconda are said to have inspired the Charminar.

115.s:
Consider the following statements about Qutb Shahi Hyderabad and Golconda:
1. Hyderabad was founded in 1591, and the capital moved there from Golconda in 1592.
2. Hyderabad was planned on the model of Isfahan by Mir Momin Astarabadi.
3. The gateway of the Golconda Jami Masjid bears calligraphy in Naskh, and the verses round its mihrab are in Nastaliq.
4. The Qutb Shahi Tombs at Ibrahim Bagh hold seven rulers, with onion domes on square bases.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
115.x: Statement 3 is wrong: it is the other way round – the gateway is in Nastaliq and the verses round the mihrab are in Naskh.

115.s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): The Charminar marks the end of a plague.
Reason (R): Qutb Shahi architecture is an Indo-Saracenic blend of Persian and Hindu traditions.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
115.x: Both are true, but the style of Qutb Shahi buildings does not explain why the Charminar was built (to mark the end of a plague).

116.s: The first writer to use Urdu as the medium of poetic expression was:
116.x: Amir Khusrau is regarded as the first writer to use Hindavi/Rekhta, the early form of Urdu, for poetry. Ghalib, Zafar and Faiz came centuries later.

116.s: The first writer to use Urdu as the medium of poetic expression was:
116.x: Amir Khusrau is regarded as the first writer to use Hindavi/Rekhta, the early form of Urdu, for poetry. Ghalib, Zafar and Faiz came centuries later.

116.s: The savant of both languages “Hindi and Persian” was –
116.x: Amir Khusrau wrote in both Persian and Hindavi (Hindi), hence 'savant of both languages'. Akbar, Tansen and Bairam Khan are Mughal-era figures.

116.s: Father of new Persian poetry style “Sabak-i-Hindi or Hindustani style was :
116.x: Amir Khusrau created the Sabak-i-Hindi (Indian style) of Persian poetry. Barani was a historian, Afif and Isami chroniclers.

116.s: Who among the following was the first Persian poet to depict Indian environment in his poetry?
116.x: Amir Khusrau was the first Persian poet to depict the Indian environment, praising India's land, languages and people (Nuh Sipihr). Amir Hasan, Kalim and Faizi came after or were less known for this.

116.s: Amir Khusrau, the “Parrot of India,” was born at-
116.x: Amir Khusrau was born at Patiyali (1253), near Etah (now Kasganj district), Uttar Pradesh.

116.s: Who among the following is called the ‘Sadi of India’?
116.x: Amir Hasan Dehlavi (Sijzi), Khusrau's friend and compiler of Fawaid-ul-Fuad, is called the 'Sadi of India' for his ghazals. Khusrau is the 'Tuti-i-Hind'.

116.s: Which of the following is not associated with the Bhakti Movement?
116.x: Amir Khusrau was a Sufi poet (disciple of Nizamuddin Auliya), not a Bhakti saint. Vallabhacharya, Chaitanya and Guru Nanak belong to the Bhakti movement.

116.s: Who among the following is known as the ‘Father of Hindi Khari Boli?
116.x: Amir Khusrau is called the father of Khari Boli for his Hindavi riddles and verses. Jayasi wrote in Awadhi; Kabir and Rahim came later.

116.s: Amir Khusrau played a pioneer role in the development of
116.x: Amir Khusrau's Hindavi verses, riddles and mukris are the earliest Khari Boli, from which Hindi and Urdu grew. Braj, Awadhi and Bhojpuri developed separately.

116.s: Amir Khusrau was court poet of
116.x: Amir Khusrau was chiefly associated with the court of Alauddin Khalji, who gave him the title Tuti-i-Hind. He died in 1325 (Firoz and Ibrahim Lodi came later; Muhammad bin Tughluq's reign had barely begun).

116.s: Who among the following called himself the ‘parrot of India’?
116.x: Tuti-i-Hind (Parrot of India) was Amir Khusrau's title. Amir Hasan was 'Sadi of India'; Qutban and Usman were Sufi premakhyan poets.

116.s: Amir Khusrau was a –
116.x: Amir Khusrau was poet, historian (Khazain-ul-Futuh, Tughluqnama) and musician (qawwali, tarana, sitar tradition).

116.s: “Every pearl in the Royal crown is the crystallised drops of blood fallen from the tearful eyes of the poor peasants” … Who made this statement?
116.x: The line 'every pearl in the royal crown is the crystallised drop of blood fallen from the tearful eyes of the poor peasant' is attributed to Amir Khusrau. Al-Biruni, Ibn Battuta and Badauni are not credited with it.

116.s: Amir Khusrau was born in
116.x:
Patiyali was part of Etah district — now in Kasganj district, carved out of Etah in 2008 (kasganj.nic.in)
Khusrau was born at Patiyali, then in Etah district (now Kasganj district, UP). Agra, Barabanki and Etawah are wrong.

116.s: Who among the following witnessed the reign of Seven Sultans of Delhi?
116.x:
Most books and keys: Amir Khusrau (court poet of seven Sultans). Strictly, Nizamuddin Auliya (1238-1325) also lived under seven or more Sultans; PMF lists five Sultans Khusrau served.
Amir Khusrau (1253-1325) lived through and served the courts of about seven Delhi Sultans, from Balban's son to Ghiyasuddin Tughluq. Nizamuddin Auliya also lived through these reigns but kept away from all courts.

116.s: Who gave Amir Khusrau the title Tuti-i-Hind (Parrot of India)?
116.x: His patron Alauddin Khalji called him Tuti-i-Hind.
xa: He served about **seven Sultans**, from **Balban's** time to Ghiyasuddin Tughluq.
⚠ **Tutinama** (Nakhshabi) ≠ **Tuti-i-Hind** (Khusrau's title).
He founded **Sabaq-i-Hindi**, the Indian style of Persian poetry.

116.s: In which language did Amir Khusrau write riddles and poetry that later developed into Rekhta or Urdu?
116.x: Khusrau wrote riddles and poetry in Hindavi, which later developed into Rekhta or Urdu.
xa: Hindavi grew into **Urdu** in **camps and bazaars**.
He founded **Sabaq-i-Hindi**, the Indian style of Persian poetry.
Title **Tuti-i-Hind** (Parrot of India), from **Alauddin Khalji**.

116.s: Amir Khusrau is associated with the development of which style of Persian poetry?
116.x: Amir Khusrau is credited with founding the Indian style of Persian poetry known as Sabak-i-Hindi or the Hindustani style.
116.tq: Match the exact technical term rather than a geographically similar distractor.
xs: Amir Khusrau founded **Sabak-i-Hindi**, the Indian style of Persian poetry — option **(4)**.
Also spelt **Sabaq-i-Hindi**.
xa: He pioneered **Hindavi-Urdu** poetry (riddles + verse in Hindavi).
Disciple of **Nizamuddin Auliya** (Chishti).
**Poet laureate** under **Ghiyasuddin Tughluq**.

116.s: Amir Khusrau was given which of the following titles?
116.x: Amir Khusrau was called Tuti-i-Hind, the Parrot of India. Homer of the East refers to Firdausi, Andhra Bhoja to Krishnadevaraya and Kaviraja to Samudragupta.
116.tq: Link each literary title with its bearer.
n: Amir Khusrau was known as Tuti-i-Hind. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #45 · pp 112-113]
Firdausi was known as the Homer of the East. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #45 · pp 112-113]
Unsuri was a Persian poet. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #45 · pp 112-113]
Uzari was a Persian poet. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #45 · pp 112-113]
Hastimalla was associated with the Hoysala rulers. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #45 · pp 112-113]
Hastimalla was a Kannada poet. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #45 · pp 112-113]
Hastimalla was a Kannada playwright. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #45 · pp 112-113]
xs: **Amir Khusrau** was called **Tuti-i-Hind** (Parrot of India) — so option **(3)** is correct.
The title was given by his patron **Alauddin Khalji**.
xa: He became **poet laureate** under **Ghiyasuddin Tughluq**.
He was a **disciple of Nizamuddin Auliya** (Chishti).
⚠ **Tutinama** (**Nakhshabi**) ≠ **Tuti-i-Hind**.
He founded **Sabaq-i-Hindi**, the Indian style of Persian poetry.

116.s: Under which Sultan was Amir Khusrau the poet laureate?
116.x: Khusrau got the title Tuti-i-Hind from Alauddin but was poet laureate under Ghiyasuddin Tughluq.

116.s: Amir Khusrau was a disciple of which Chishti saint?
116.x: Amir Khusrau was a disciple of Nizamuddin Auliya.

116.s: What was the real name of Amir Khusrau?
116.x: Amir Khusrau's real name was Abul Hasan Yaminuddin Khusrau; he was born at Patiyali.

116.s:
Match the following authors with their works:
List I
List II
a. Al-Biruni
I. Tariqh-i-Firoz Shahi
b. Minhaj-us-Siraj
II. Tahqiq-i-Hind
c. Ziauddin Barani
III. The Rihla
d. Ibn Battuta
IV. Tabaqat-i-Nasiri
116.x: Al-Biruni – Tahqiq-i-Hind (II); Minhaj-us-Siraj – Tabaqat-i-Nasiri (IV); Barani – Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi (I); Ibn Battuta – Rihla (III). So a-II, b-IV, c-I, d-III.

116.s: 'Tarikh-i-Firuz Shahi' was written by
116.x: Shams Siraj Afif wrote a Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi on Firoz Tughlaq's reign (Barani wrote the other of the same name). Yahya Sirhindi wrote Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi, Minhaj the Tabaqat-i-Nasiri and Isami the Futuh-us-Salatin.

116.s: Who is the author of "Tarikh-i-Firujshahi"?
116.x:
Two options are right: both Barani and Shams Siraj Afif wrote a Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi. Most keys give Barani; Afif (option a) is equally correct strictly.
Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi is best known as Ziauddin Barani's history (to 1357); Shams Siraj Afif wrote a second work of the same title. Isami wrote Futuh-us-Salatin and Yazdi wrote Zafarnama (Timur), so the printed key 'Isami' is wrong.

116.s:
Consider the following text and arrange them in chronological order.

I. Fatwa-I – Jahandari

II. Prithviraj – Raso

III. Kitab-ul-hind

IV. Tabaqat-i-Nasiri
Select the correct answer from the codes given below.
116.x: Kitab-ul-Hind (c. 1030) → Prithviraj Raso (traditionally late 12th c.) → Tabaqat-i-Nasiri (c. 1260) → Fatawa-i-Jahandari (Barani, c. 1358). So III, II, IV, I.

116.s:
Consider the following text and arrange them in chronological order:
1. Fatawa-i-Jahandari
