120.x: All four are correct: Saluva Narasimha ended the Sangamas (1485); Vira Narasimha deposed Immadi Narasimha, the last Saluva (1505); Vira Narasimha was succeeded by his younger brother Krishnadevaraya (1509); and Krishnadevaraya by his half-brother Achyuta Raya (1529).

120.s: Annamayya the lyric writer was a contemporary to
120.x: Tallapaka Annamacharya (1408-1503) was a contemporary of Saluva Narasimha Raya; Harihara and Devaraya I and II ruled earlier.

120.s: Who was the founder of Saluva dynasty?
120.x: Saluva Narasimha of Chandragiri expelled Praudha Raya in 1485 and began the Saluva dynasty. Immadi Narasimha was the last Saluva, and Vira Narasimha founded the Tuluva dynasty.

120.s: Who was the contemporary of Vaggeyakara Annamayya?
120.x: Vaggeyakara Annamayya (Annamacharya, 1408-1503) was a contemporary of Saluva Narasimha Raya; Harihara, Devaraya I and Devaraya II ruled earlier.

120.s: When did the Saluva dynasty come to power?
120.x: The Saluva dynasty came to power in 1485, when Saluva Narasimha expelled Praudha Raya (first usurpation).

120.s: Who was the founder of the Saluva dynasty?
120.x: Saluva Narasimharaya founded the Saluva dynasty in 1485 by expelling Praudha Devaraya, the last Sangama. Krishnadevaraya and Rama Raya came later.

120.s: Which statement regarding the rulers preceding Saluva Narasimha is correct?
o: Praudha Raya was the general who seized the throne for Saluva Narasimha.
Virupaksha II was described as a drunkard, while Praudha Raya was considered worthless.
Virupaksha II founded the Saluva dynasty, while Praudha Raya ruled from Chandragiri.
Both rulers successfully repelled the Gajapati and Bahmani invasions.
120.x: Nuniz described Virupaksha II as a drunkard, while Praudha Raya was considered worthless; their weakness contributed to the crisis of the kingdom.
120.tq: Match the correct description with each of two neighbouring rulers.
xs: **Virupaksha II** was described (by **Nuniz**) as a **drunkard**, and **Praudha Raya** as **worthless** — option **(2)**.
The general who seized the throne for Saluva Narasimha was **Tuluva Narasa Nayaka**, not Praudha Raya.
Their weakness let **Gajapati** and **Bahmani** invasions eat into the kingdom — they did not repel them.
xa: Saluva Narasimha, lord of **Chandragiri**, took the throne in **1485** — the **first usurpation**.
Saluva rule (**1485-91**) moved the capital from **Kalyanapuram** to **Chandragiri**.
Praudha Raya was the **last Sangama ruler**.

120.s: Where did Vira Narasimha kill Immadi Narasimha, the last Saluva ruler, in 1505?
120.x: The second usurpation took place at Penugonda, where Vira Narasimha killed Immadi Narasimha and began the Tuluva dynasty.

120.s: Whom did Saluva Narasimha expel in the first usurpation of 1485?
120.x: Saluva Narasimha of Chandragiri expelled Praudha Raya in 1485, ending the Sangama dynasty.

120.s: In which year did the second usurpation, which began the Tuluva dynasty, take place?
120.x: The second usurpation was in 1505; the first (Saluva) was in 1485.

120.s: By what other name is the Battle of Talikota known?
120.x: Talikota (1565) is also called Rakshasi-Tangadi or Bannihatti.

120.s: From where did Saluva Narasimha bring Arab horses?
120.x: Saluva Narasimha brought Arab horses from Ormuz and introduced Samugaris (gunmen).
xa: Udayagiri was later retaken by **Krishnadevaraya** (**1513-14**) after an **18-month siege**.
Saluva capital: **Kalyanapuram** → **Chandragiri**.
Court poet: **Rajanatha Dindima** (**Saluvabhyudayam**).

120.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
120.x: Rajanatha Dindima, court poet of Saluva Narasimha, wrote Saluvabhyudayam. Gangadevi wrote Madhura Vijayam, not Saluvabhyudayam; Dhurjati wrote Sri Kalahasteeswara Mahatyam and Satakam, not Madhura Vijayam; Ramabhyudayamu is by Ayyalaraju Ramabhadrudu, while Tirumalamba wrote Varadambika Parinayam.
120.tq: Use a sure author–work pair to eliminate literary-name swaps.
xs: **Rajanatha Dindima — Saluvabhyudayam** is correct — option **(1)**; he was Saluva Narasimha's court poet.
**Dhurjati** wrote **Sri Kalahasteeswara Mahatyam** and **Satakam**, not Madhura Vijayam.
**Ramabhyudayamu** is by **Ayyalaraju Ramabhadrudu**; **Tirumalamba** wrote **Varadambika Parinayam**.
xa: Dhurjati was the **Shaiva** poet of **Kalahasti**, one of the **Ashtadiggajas**.
Ayyalaraju Ramabhadrudu's Ramabhyudayamu is the **Ramayana in Telugu**.
**Annamacharya** was Saluva Narasimha's contemporary.

120.s: Saluva Narasimha lost Udayagiri to which Gajapati ruler?
120.x: Saluva Narasimha lost Udayagiri to Gajapati Purushottama; Krishnadevaraya later won it back from Prataparudra.

120.s: To which place did Saluva Narasimha move his capital from Kalyanapuram?
120.x: Saluva Narasimha's capital shifted from Kalyanapuram to Chandragiri.

120.s: Who wrote Saluvabhyudayam, the work on Saluva Narasimha?
120.x: Rajanatha Dindima was Saluva Narasimha's court poet and wrote Saluvabhyudayam.

120.s: Annamacharya, who composed 32,000 kirtanas on Lord Venkateswara, was a contemporary of which Vijayanagara ruler?
120.x: Annamacharya (1408-1503) lived in the time of Saluva Narasimha (1485-91); he died before Krishnadevaraya was crowned in 1509.

120.s: Krishnadevaraya was crowned on 8 August of which year?
120.x: The Hampi inscription dates his coronation to 8 August 1509.

120.s: Who among the following is known as 'Yavana Rajya Sthapanacharya'?
120.x: Krishnadevaraya took the title Yavana Rajya Sthapanacharya for restoring the Bahmani Sultan Mahmud Shah to his throne; Deva Raya, Saluva Narasimha, Tuluva Narasa Nayaka and the others did not bear it.

120.s: Who had the title 'Yavana Rajya Sthapanacharya'?
120.x: Krishnadevaraya took the title Yavana Rajya Sthapanacharya for restoring the Bahmani Sultan Mahmud Shah to his throne; Deva Raya, Saluva Narasimha, Tuluva Narasa Nayaka and the others did not bear it.

120.s: Nagulapuram was built to commemorate Nagamamba. Who was Nagamamba?
120.x: Krishnadevaraya built Nagalapuram in memory of his mother Nagamamba (Nagala Devi).

120.s: Who built the city of Nagalapuram?
120.x: Sri Krishnadevaraya founded Nagalapuram, a suburb of Vijayanagara, in memory of his mother Nagala Devi; Bukka I, Devaraya I and Virupaksha did not.

120.s: Who among the following famous rulers founded a suburban township of Nagalapuram, near Vijayanagara, after his mother's name?
o: More than one of the above
120.x: The suburban township of Nagalapuram near Vijayanagara was founded by Krishnadevaraya after his mother Nagala Devi; Harihara and Bukka are wrong.

120.s: Who had the title 'Yavana Rajya Sthapanacharya'?
120.x: Krishnadevaraya took the title Yavana Rajya Sthapanacharya for restoring the Bahmani Sultan Mahmud Shah to his throne; Deva Raya, Saluva Narasimha, Tuluva Narasa Nayaka and the others did not bear it.

120.s: Who among these known as ‘Andhra Bhoj’?
120.x: Andhra Bhoja is a title of Krishnadevaraya, reflecting his literary patronage. Rajendra Chola, Harihara and Bukka did not bear it.

120.s: The king with the title of 'Yavanarajya Sthapanacharya'?
120.x: Krishnadevaraya took the title Yavana Rajya Sthapanacharya for restoring the Bahmani Sultan Mahmud Shah to his throne; Deva Raya, Saluva Narasimha, Tuluva Narasa Nayaka and the others did not bear it.

120.s: ____ founded a suburban township near Vijayanagara called Nagalapuram after his mother.
120.src: Social and Cultural History of A.P and Welfare Programmes 20
120.x: Krishnadevaraya founded Nagalapuram near Vijayanagara in honour of his mother Nagala Devi. The other options are not Vijayanagara kings.

120.s: ____ was conferred the title of - Establisher of Yavana (Greek or foreigners) Kingdom for helping Sultans.
120.src: Social and Cultural History of A.P and Welfare Programmes 20
120.x: Krishnadevaraya took the title Yavanarajya Sthapanacharya ('establisher of the Yavana kingdom') for restoring the Bahmani Sultan. Kulottunga and the Gonka rajas are earlier dynasties.

120.s: ___ was conferred the title of - Establisher of Yavana (Greek or foreigners) Kingdom for helping Sultans.
120.src: Social and Culture History & Welfare Programmes paper 2019
120.x: Krishnadevaraya took the title Yavanarajya Sthapanacharya ('establisher of the Yavana kingdom') for restoring the Bahmani Sultan. Kulottunga and the Gonka rajas are earlier dynasties.

120.s: Which one of the following was NOT a title of Krishnadevaraya?
120.x: Andhra Bhoja, Sahiti Samarangana Sarvabhauma and Kannada Rajya Rama Ramana were titles of Krishnadevaraya. Gajabetekara (elephant hunter) was the title of the Sangama ruler Devaraya II.

xa: **Yavana Rajya Sthapanacharya**: for restoring the Bahmani Sultan; celebrated in **Manucharitra**.
Others: **Gajapati Gajakuta Pakaveni**, **Dakshinapatha Swami**, **Mururaya Raganda**, **Paribhuta Suratrana**.

120.s: Which of the following is NOT a title associated with Krishnadevaraya?
120.x: Andhra Kavita Pitamaha was the title conferred on Allasani Peddana. The other three are titles of Krishnadevaraya.
120.tq: Separate the ruler's titles from an honorific belonging to his court poet.
xs: **Andhra Kavita Pitamaha** was not Krishnadevaraya's title — option **(2)**; it was conferred on **Allasani Peddana** (APPSC G2 **2019**).
**Mururaya Raganda**, **Sahiti Samarangana Sarvabhauma** and **Andhra Bhoja** are Krishnadevaraya's titles.
xa: The king himself fixed the **Gandapenderam** anklet on Peddana's foot.

Other royal titles: **Yavana Rajya Sthapanacharya**, **Kannada Rajya Rama Ramana**, **Dakshinapatha Swami**.

120.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
120.x: Nagalapuram was named after Krishnadevaraya's mother Nagalamba.
120.tq: Match a foundation name with its namesake, avoiding queen–mother confusion.
xs: **Nagalapuram — Nagalamba** is correct — option **(3)**; it is named after his mother.
**Hospet** is named after his queen **Tirumaladevi**, not Nagalamba.
**Gangadevi** was the author of Madhura Vijayam, not linked to Hospet.
xa: Hospet is also called **Tirumaladevipattana**.
⚠ **Nagalapuram** = mother; **Hospet** = queen.
Titles: **Andhra Bhoja**, **Sahiti Samarangana Sarvabhauma**.

120.s: After whom was Hospet, also called Tirumaladevipattana, named?
120.x: Krishnadevaraya named Hospet after his queen Tirumaladevi.

120.s: Who among the following had the title 'Gajabetekara'?
120.x: Gajabetekara is Devaraya II's title and is a common decoy among Krishnadevaraya's titles.

120.s: What do Krishnadevaraya's titles 'Andhra Bhoja' and 'Sahiti Samarangana Sarvabhauma' reflect?
120.x: Both titles honour Krishnadevaraya as a patron of letters, like King Bhoja.

120.s: Who was the Sultan of Bijapur who fought at Raichur during the reign of Krishnadevaraya?
120.x: In the battle of Raichur (1520) Krishnadevaraya defeated Ismail Adil Shah (Adil Khan) of Bijapur with Portuguese help. Ahmed Barid, Muhammad Shah I and Mujahid Shah are wrong.

120.s: Who was the Sultan of Bijapur who invaded Raichur during the reign of Sri Krishnadevaraya?
120.x: The battle of Raichur (1520) was fought between Krishnadevaraya and Ismail Adil Khan, Sultan of Bijapur; Krishnadevaraya won and took the Raichur Doab.

120.s: The great battle fought by Krishnadevaraya in 1520?
120.x: The great battle of 1520 was Krishnadevaraya's victory over Ismail Adil Shah near Raichur, which Telugu texts call the battle of Gobburu. Mudgal was Devaraya I's battle with Firoz Shah Bahmani, and Gulbarga was only taken later (1523).

120.s: With whom the king of Viyayanagara, Krishnadeva Raya fought the battle of Golconda?
120.x: The battle of Golconda was fought against Sultan Quli Qutb Shah of Golconda, who had seized forts while Krishnadevaraya was fighting the Gajapatis; he was finally defeated. Qutbuddin Aibak, Ismail Adil Shah and the Gajapati are wrong.

120.s: With whom did the king of Vijayanagara, Krishnadeva Raya fight the battle of Golconda?
120.x: The battle of Golconda was fought between Krishnadevaraya and Sultan Quli Qutb Shah, founder of the Qutb Shahi dynasty, who had taken forts such as Warangal and Kondaveedu while the Raya fought the Gajapatis; Quli was finally defeated.

120.s: The place where Krishnadevaraya planted the victory pillar?
120.x: Krishnadevaraya erected his victory pillar (jayastambha) at Potnuru near Simhachalam on returning from the Kalinga (eastern) campaign; Kondaveedu and Kondapalli were forts he captured.

120.s: Sri Krishna Devaraya erected a pillar of victory to commemorate his conquest of coastal Andhra at
120.x: To commemorate the conquest of coastal Andhra from the Gajapatis, Krishnadevaraya set up a victory pillar at Potnuru (Padmanabham, Visakhapatnam district). Udayagiri and Kondaveedu were forts taken; Nagarjunakonda is unrelated.

120.s: Which idol was taken by Krishnadevaraya after capturing Udayagiri fort?
120.x: After the 18-month siege of Udayagiri, Krishnadevaraya took the Balakrishna idol to Hampi and built the Krishna temple for it.

120.s: Which of the Kingdoms was defeated by Sri Krishnadevaraya and Coastal Andhra and Odisha were annexed from that Kingdom?
120.src: APPSC Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer (Sainik Welfare Service)
120.x: Krishnadevaraya defeated the Gajapati king Prataparudra of Odisha and took coastal Andhra up to Simhachalam. The Hoysalas, Chalukyas and Kakatiyas had long ended.

120.s: Which campaign resulted in the defeat of Yusuf Adil Khan?
120.x: During the Diwani or Kovilkonda campaign of 1509–10, the Bahmani jihad was crushed and Yusuf Adil Khan was killed.
120.tq: Match the military result with the correct campaign.
xs: **Yusuf Adil Khan** was killed in the **Diwani / Kovilkonda** campaign (**1509-10**) — option **(1)**; the Bahmani "jihad" was crushed.
**Udayagiri**, **Kondaveedu** and **Simhachalam** belong to the **Kalinga campaign (1513-1519)** against the Gajapatis.
xa: ⚠ **Yusuf Adil Khan** killed at Kovilkonda; **Ismail Adil Shah** routed at **Raichur (1520)**.
**Raichur Doab (1510)**: Raichur taken; freed **Sultan Mahmud Shah** from **Ali Barid**.
Ummattur / Sivasamudram (**1512-13**): **Gangaraja** defeated.

120.s: With which campaign of Krishnadevaraya is the title 'Yavanarajya Sthapanacharya' associated?
120.x: After taking Raichur and freeing Sultan Mahmud Shah from Ali Barid, Krishnadevaraya acquired the title Yavanarajya Sthapanacharya.
120.tq: Link an honorific title with the event that produced it.
xs: The title came from the **Raichur and Bidar** campaign (**1510**) — option **(4)**: he freed **Sultan Mahmud Shah** from **Ali Barid**.
**Ummattur** defeated **Gangaraja**; **Udayagiri** and the **Kalinga campaign** were against the Gajapatis.
xa: The title **Yavana Rajya Sthapanacharya** is celebrated in **Manucharitra**.
Other titles: **Andhra Bhoja**, **Sahiti Samarangana Sarvabhauma**, **Kannada Rajya Rama Ramana**, **Gajapati Gajakuta Pakaveni**.
Raichur was again won in **1520**, routing **Ismail Adil Shah** with **Portuguese** help.

120.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the Ummattur campaign?
o: Gangaraja was defeated and a new province was established at Srirangapatna.
Yusuf Adil Khan was killed and the Bahmani jihad was crushed.
The Balakrishna idol was brought to Hampi.
Victory pillars were erected at Potnuru and Simhachalam.
120.x: In the Ummattur or Sivasamudram campaign of 1512–13, Gangaraja was defeated and a new province was established at Srirangapatna.

xs: In the **Ummattur / Sivasamudram** campaign (**1512-13**), **Gangaraja was defeated** and a new province set up at **Srirangapatna** — option **(1)**.
**Yusuf Adil Khan** was killed at **Kovilkonda**; the **Balakrishna idol** came from **Udayagiri**; victory pillars stood at **Potnuru** and **Simhachalam**.

120.s: In which year did Krishnadevaraya take Gulbarga?
120.x: After routing Ismail Adil Shah at Raichur in 1520, he took Gulbarga in 1523.

120.s: Krishnadevaraya earned the title Yavanarajya Sthapanacharya by freeing which Sultan from Ali Barid?
120.x: In the Raichur-Bidar campaign of 1510 he restored the Bahmani Sultan Mahmud Shah, freeing him from Ali Barid.

120.s: In which year did Krishnadevaraya defeat Ismail Adil Shah of Bijapur in the Battle of Raichur?
120.x: In the Battle of Raichur (1520) Krishnadevaraya routed Ismail Adil Shah with Portuguese help; Gulbarga followed in 1523.

120.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Yusuf Adil Khan was killed in Krishnadevaraya's Kovilkonda campaign.

120.x: Yusuf Adil Khan fell in the Kovilkonda (Diwani) campaign of 1509-10 and Ismail Adil Shah was routed at Raichur in 1520, so both are correct.

120.s: After a siege of how long did Udayagiri fall during Krishnadevaraya's Kalinga campaign?
120.x: Udayagiri fell after an 18-month siege in the Kalinga campaign of 1513-1519.
xa: Aim: win back **Tirandhra** and **Telangana** from **Prataparudra Gajapati**.
Telangana forts taken: **Devarakonda, Nalgonda, Kambhamettu, Jallipalli and Warangal**.
Victory pillars: **Potnuru** and **Simhachalam**.

120.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Ummattur — Balakrishna idol taken to Hampi
120.x: After the conquest of Kondaveedu, Krishnadevaraya performed Talapurusha Danam at Amaravati. The other pairs associate results with the wrong campaigns.
120.tq: Start from the sure campaign–event pair and eliminate swapped results.
xs: **Kondaveedu — Talapurusha Danam at Amaravati** is correct — option **(1)**.
**Udayagiri** = **Balakrishna idol** to Hampi; the **Potnuru** pillar marked the conquest of coastal Andhra.
**Srirangapatna** province came from **Ummattur**, not Raichur.
xa: Kondaveedu was taken with **Saluva Timmarusu's** help, who split **Veerabhadra Gajapati's** army.
At **Kondapalli and Bejawada**, **Praharajeshwara** and Prataparudra's forces were beaten.
PYQ **2025**: pillar marking the conquest of coastal Andhra = **Potnuru**.

120.s: Where did Krishnadevaraya set up his victory pillars?
120.x: Victory pillars were erected at Potnuru and Simhachalam after the Kalinga campaign. The pillar at Potnuru marked the conquest of coastal Andhra.

xs: Victory pillars stood at **Potnuru and Simhachalam** — option **(3)**.
PYQ **2025**: the pillar marking the conquest of coastal Andhra = **Potnuru**.
**Amaravati** saw **Talapurusha Danam**; **Mangalagiri** got a land grant; **Udayagiri** and **Kondaveedu** were forts taken.
xa: **Simhachalam**: a **diamond necklace** to **Varaha Narasimha**.

AP angle: **Udayagiri, Kondaveedu, Kondapalli** forts of the campaign lie in AP.

120.s: Whose daughter did Krishnadevaraya marry after the Kalinga campaign?
120.x: Prataparudra Gajapati gave his daughter to Krishnadevaraya, and lands north of the Krishna went back to the Gajapati.
xa: Her name: **Annapurnadevi** (some notes) vs **Bhadradevi (Tukka / Jaganmohini)**.

Aim: win back **Tirandhra** and **Telangana**.

120.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Simhachalam — diamond necklace to Varaha Narasimha
Potnuru — pillar marking the conquest of coastal Andhra

**Simhachalam** (diamond necklace) and **Potnuru** (coastal Andhra pillar) are correctly matched.

120.s: Which coastal places were known for salt, with salt pans at one of them being taxed?

**Potnuru** and **Simhachalam** were victory-pillar sites; **Kondaveedu** and **Kondapalli** were forts.

120.s: Who wrote the book 'Varadambika Parinayam'?

(I) Gangamba

120.s: Who is the author of Jaimini Bharatham?
120.x: Jaimini Bharatam was written by Pillalamarri Pina Veerabhadrudu, a contemporary of Saluva Narasimha. Gona Budda Reddy wrote the Ranganatha Ramayanam; Jaimini Maharshi is the sage of the original story.

o: The marriage of Achyutaraya and Varadambika

120.s: Who of the following rulers of medieval India gave permission to the Portuguese to build a fort at Bhatkal?
120.x: Krishnadevaraya, friendly with the Portuguese governor Albuquerque, allowed them to build a fort at Bhatkal (1510) in return for horses and help against Bijapur. Narasimha Saluva, Muhammad Shah III and Yusuf Adil Shah did not.

120.x: Krishnadevaraya, friendly with the Portuguese governor Albuquerque, allowed them to build a fort at Bhatkal (1510) in return for horses and help against Bijapur. Narasimha Saluva, Muhammad Shah III and Yusuf Adil Shah did not.

120.s: Who among the ruler of Vijayanagar maintained friendly relations with Albuquerque, the Portuguese Governor and granted him permission to build fort at Bhatkal?
120.x: Krishnadevaraya kept friendly relations with Albuquerque and allowed the Portuguese a fort at Bhatkal (1510). Vira Narasimha's Portuguese contact was Almeida.

120.s: Who among the following, gave a vivid description of the House of victory of Krishnadevaraya?
120.src: APPSC Group-II (Mains) Paper-II Social History & Constitutio
120.x: The Portuguese Domingo Paes gave the vivid eyewitness description of Krishnadevaraya's House of Victory (Bhuvana Vijayam / Mahanavami Dibba) and of the city.

120.s: Who made peace after Sadasiva and Rama Raya defeated Governor Martin de Souza for damaging temples?

xs: **Joao de Castro** made peace — option **(4)**.

**Almeida** allied with **Vira Narasimha**; **Albuquerque** took Goa in **1510**; **Duarte Barbosa** visited Krishnadevaraya's court.
xa: **Aliya Rama Raya**, Krishnadevaraya's son-in-law of the **Aravidu** family, made **Sadasiva** a figurehead.

120.s: Vira Narasimha entered into an alliance with which Portuguese Viceroy for securing horses and military training?
120.x: Vira Narasimha allied with Viceroy Francisco de Almeida for horses and military training.

xs: **Vira Narasimha** allied with Viceroy **Francisco de Almeida** for **horses** and **military training** — option **(2)**.
**Albuquerque** was backed by **Krishnadevaraya** in taking **Goa (1510)**; **Joao de Castro** made peace with Sadasiva/Rama Raya; **Duarte Barbosa** was a visitor.
xa: ⚠ **Almeida** = Vira Narasimha; **Albuquerque** = Krishnadevaraya.
In return for Goa, the Portuguese supplied **horses** and were allowed a fort at **Bhatkal**.
Portuguese help counted at **Raichur (1520)**.

120.s: Where did Krishnadevaraya permit the Portuguese to build a fort for their support to Albuquerque in capturing Goa?
120.x: Krishnadevaraya received horses and military training and allowed the Portuguese a fort at Bhatkal.
xa: Goa was captured by **Albuquerque** from **Bijapur** in **1510**, through envoy **Luis**.
Bhatkal had earlier been taken by **Saluva Narasimha**.

120.s: Which Portuguese governor captured Goa from Bijapur in 1510 with Krishnadevaraya's backing?
120.x: Through his envoy Luis, Krishnadevaraya backed Albuquerque's capture of Goa from Bijapur in 1510.

120.s: Which foreign traveller, besides Domingo Paes, is associated with a visit to Krishnadevaraya’s court?

xs: **Domingo Paes** described the king's **looks** and the **city's beauty** — option **(1)**.

Rayasam secretaries named: **Kondamarasu**, **Ayyamarasu**.
In the village, the **Reddi** was head and collector of revenue.

121.s: Which matters did the Athavane department deal with in Vijayanagara administration?
121.x: Athavane was the revenue department; Kandachara was military and Bhandara the treasury.

121.s: Which of the following pairs (department – function) is correctly matched?
121.x: Bhandara was the treasury; Athavane was revenue, Kandachara military and Dharmasana judicial.

121.s: What was the chief minister heading the pradhanis in Vijayanagara called?
121.x: The Mahapradhani headed the pradhanis (e.g. Saluva Timmarusu); the Dalavayi was commander-in-chief.

121.s: According to the Rayavachakam, how many departments were there in the Vijayanagara administration?
121.x: The Rayavachakam records nine departments, each headed by a Samprati.

121.s: Who headed the Kandachara department of the Vijayanagara administration?
121.x: Kandachara was the military department; it was headed by the Senapati or Dalavayi, the commander-in-chief.

121.s:
Match the following:
List-I (Department)
a. Kandachara
b. Athavane
c. Bhandara
d. Dharmasana
List-II (Function)
1. Treasury
2. Military
3. Justice
4. Revenue
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
121.x: Kandachara dealt with military affairs, Athavane with revenue, Bhandara was the treasury and Dharmasana the judicial department.

121.s: Which one of the following responsibilities was not entrusted to the Polygar by the Nayaka rulers of South India?
o: Building centers for health and education
121.src: Social and Cultural History of A.P and Welfare Programmes 20
121.x: Polygars administered their palaiyams, collected taxes and kept law and order with their troops; building health and education centres was not their duty.

121.s: The Vijayanagar Empire adopted the innovative political system of amara-nayaka system. Which one of the following option is incorrect about the statement?
o: They were wise men who advised the rulers.
They collected taxes on behalf of the rulers.
Their contingents helped the kings with fighting forces.
121.src: Social and Cultural History of A.P and Welfare Programmes 20
121.x: Amara-nayakas were military commanders who collected taxes from their amaram lands and kept contingents for the king; they were not wise men advising the ruler, so (a) is incorrect.

121.s: What was the administrative unit of the Vijayanagara Empire?
121.x: The question means the administrative system of the empire: the Amaranayaka (Amara-Nayankara) system, in which military governors (Nayakas) held amarams for salary and army expenses.

121.s: The Nayakas in the Vijayanagar empire were
o: Priests of large and powerful temples.
121.x: Nayakas (amaranayakas) were military chiefs who held and administered territories (amarams) in lieu of salary - not ministers, priests or ordinary cavalry.

121.s: Who were polygars of South India?
121.x: Polygars (Palegars) were amara-nayakas who administered territories and owed military service - territorial administrative and military governors; they were only forerunners of the zamindars.

121.s:
Consider the following statements about Vijayanagar Empire.

I. Vijaynagar was noted for its markets dealing in spices, textiles and precious stones.

II. Krishnadeva Raya’s rule was characterised by the strain within the imperial structure.

III. The amara-nayakas were military commanders who were given territories to be governed by the Rayas.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?
121.x: I and III: Vijayanagara's markets dealt in spices, textiles and precious stones, and the amara-nayakas were military commanders given territories by the Rayas. II is wrong – Krishnadeva Raya's reign was one of expansion and consolidation; strain came after him (NCERT).

121.s: What was the land assigned by the Vijayanagara king to military chiefs in lieu of cash salaries called?
121.x: Amaram was land granted to military chiefs, who were known as Amaranayakas, Nayaks, Palaiyagars or Poligars. The grant substituted for direct cash payment to the chiefs.
121.tq: Use the exact administrative term rather than a similar land-revenue term.
xs: Land granted to military chiefs instead of cash salaries was the **Amaram** — option **(2)**.
Holders were **Amaranayakas / Nayakas / Poligars** (also Palaiyagars), titled **Mahamandaleshwara**.
**Manyam** = tax-free lands of the **Ayagars**; **Jagir** belongs to the **Mughal** mansabdari.
xa: They paid a fixed **annual tribute (kist / kappam)**.
Krishnadevaraya had about **200 nayankaras** (Nuniz).
**Amara gramalu** collected **Durgadayam** for the army.

121.s: What title did the Vijayanagara amaranayakas hold?
121.x: Amaranayakas held the title Mahamandaleshwara and had more autonomy than the Durgadannayakas.
xa: They paid **kist / kappam** and attended the **Mahanavami** court.
The Vijayanagara amara-nayankara **evolved from the Kakatiya** system (CDX).

121.s: At which festival did Vijayanagara amaranayakas attend court with gifts?
121.x: Amaranayakas paid tribute, kept troops, horses and elephants, and attended court at Mahanavami with gifts.
xa: Local duties: keep order, maintain **forts**, fund **temples** and **irrigation**.
⚠ Kakatiya **75/77** nayakas vs Vijayanagara about **200**.
After **1565** they grew into **independent Nayaka states** (Madurai, Tanjore, Keladi).

121.s: What was the tribute paid by the Vijayanagara amaranayakas to the king called?
121.x: Amaranayakas paid tribute called Kappam and kept troops, horses and elephants for the king.

121.s: What was the principal political outcome of the Vijayanagara Amara-Nayankara system after 1565?
o: The replacement of Nayakas by hereditary village accountants
The conversion of all amarams into Mughal jagirs
The complete abolition of regional chieftaincies
The emergence of semi-independent and later independent Nayaka states such as Madurai, Tanjore and Keladi
121.x: After 1565, semi-independent Nayaka kingdoms emerged and some became independent, including those of Madurai, Tanjore and Keladi.
121.tq: Test the result of the system through its named regional examples.
xs: After **1565**, **semi-independent** and then **independent Nayaka states** arose — **Madurai, Tanjore, Keladi** — option **(4)**.
The Nayankara gave a huge army **cheaply** but bred kingdoms that **broke away after Talikota**.
xa: Amara-nayakas also became **Palegars (Poligars)**, forerunners of the **zamindars**.
The Mughal mansabdari, by contrast, was **non-hereditary** and centrally controlled.

121.s: Which of the following pairs (system – characteristic) is correctly matched?
o: Vijayanagara Amara-Nayankara – Amaram fiefs and about 200 Nayakas
Vijayanagara Amara-Nayankara – Numerical zat and sawar ranks
Mughal Mansabdari – Mandalams and forts held by 75 or 77 Nayakas
Kakatiya Nayankara – Amaram fiefs and about 200 Nayakas
121.x: The Vijayanagara system involved amaram fiefs and about 200 Nayakas. The Kakatiya system had 75 or 77 Nayakas holding mandalams and forts, and Mughal mansabdars held zat and sawar ranks.
xa: Kakatiya origin: **Prataparudra II** (APPSC **2025** key).
Vijayanagara nayakas included **Shudra** chiefs.

121.s: Who is identified as the originator of the Kakatiya Nayankara system?
121.x: Prataparudra II is identified as the originator of the Kakatiya Nayankara system. The Vijayanagara Amara-Nayankara system grew out of the Kakatiya system.
121.tq: Use the originator–system association and avoid substituting a later ruler.
xs: The Kakatiya Nayankara originated with **Prataparudra II** — option **(3)** (APPSC **2025** key).
**Akbar** is linked to the Mughal **mansabdari**; the Vijayanagara system **grew out of** the Kakatiya one (CDX).
xa: Kakatiya nayakas held **a fort and a quarter of the land** and paid a fixed sum.
⚠ Kakatiya **75/77** vs Vijayanagara about **200**.

121.s: About how many nayakas held amarams under the Vijayanagara amara-nayankara system?
121.x: Vijayanagara had about 200 nayakas, against the Kakatiyas' 75 or 77.

121.s: The Kakatiya nayankara system had how many nayakas?
121.x: The Kakatiya system had 75 or 77 nayakas holding mandalams and forts; Vijayanagara had about 200.

121.s: From whom did the Palegars or Poligars primarily originate?
121.x: The Amara-nayakas became the Palegars or Poligars when central authority weakened after the Battle of Talikota.
121.tq: Trace the origin of the later institution to its Vijayanagara military-administrative predecessor.
xs: The Palegars (Poligars) grew out of the **Amara-nayakas** — option **(3)**.
After **Talikota (1565)** weakened central authority, they became **hereditary** local rulers.
xa: They were **forerunners of the zamindars**.
In **Rayalaseema** they were suppressed by **Thomas Munro** with **Campbell**.
⚠ **Ayagars** were village functionaries; **Parupatyagars** were Nadu revenue officials.

121.s: The Palegars (Poligars), who became hereditary local rulers after Talikota, are regarded as the forerunners of whom?
121.x: The Palegars are regarded as forerunners of the zamindars; Ryotwari was introduced by Munro after suppressing them.
xa: Palegars arose from the **Amara-nayakas**.
Rayalaseema (the **Ceded Districts**) had a dense network of fortified poligar chiefs.

121.s: Which system did Thomas Munro introduce after suppressing the poligars of Rayalaseema?
121.x: Munro, with military officer Campbell, suppressed the poligars and then brought in the Ryotwari system.
xa: Poligars grew from **amara-nayakas** after **Talikota (1565)**.
**Uyyalawada Narasimha Reddy**, Kurnool polygar, looted the **Koilkuntla** treasury.
**Kurnool Nawabs** were deposed in **1839**.

121.s: Which British officer, assisted by Campbell, crushed the Palegars of Rayalaseema?
121.x: Thomas Munro, with his officer Campbell, crushed the Palegars and then introduced the Ryotwari system.

121.s: What was the chief characteristics of financial system of Vijayanagara Empire?
121.x: Land revenue - usually 1/6 of the produce, more on fertile land - was the mainstay of Vijayanagara finance.

121.s: The Vijayanagar King who totally withdrew the marriage tax was:
121.x:
Most books and keys (Rocket, NextGen previous papers, APPSC G1 2010): Krishnadevaraya. Some keys and the old notes: Sadasiva Raya.
The king who totally withdrew the marriage tax is Krishnadevaraya (it was first remitted under Saluva Narasimha). The Sadasiva-period (Rama Raya) inscriptions record the remission of the barbers' tax, not the marriage tax. (Printed key Sadasivaraya.)

121.s: What is "Meruka" a tax on?
121.x: Meruka was a tax on the sale and purchase of goods; Mera was the Ayagars' harvest share, and Magani/Metta were land classes.

121.s: Vijayanagara king who completely abolished marriage tax?
121.x:
Most books and keys (Rocket, NextGen previous papers): Krishnadevaraya. Some keys and the old notes: Sadasiva Raya.
Krishnadevaraya totally withdrew the marriage tax (Kalyana Kanike); Sadasivaraya's regent Rama Raya remitted the barbers' (Mangali) tax.

121.s:
Match the following taxes:
List I

a. Navidadere

b. Melivamsam

c. Manevana

d. Tudimeya
List II

I. Tax on Marriage

II. Tax on Barbers

III. Tax on Ploughs

IV. Tax Houses
121.x: Navidadere = barbers' tax (II), Melivamsam = plough tax (III), Manevana = house tax (IV), Tudimeya = marriage tax (I): a-II, b-III, c-IV, d-I - the only option with Navidadere-barbers and Manevana-houses.

121.s:
Regarding the taxation system of Krishna Devaraya, the ruler of Vijayanagar, consider the following statements:

A. The tax rate on land was fixed depending on the quality of the land.

B. Private owners of workshops paid an industries tax.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
121.x: Both are correct: Krishnadevaraya's land tax varied with the quality of land, and private owners of workshops paid an industries tax (UPSC 2016 key: both). (Moved: Vijayanagara administration and revenue, book 1 row 121.)

121.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Mera was the share of the harvest given to the Ayagars.
2. Meruka was a tax on sale and purchase.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
121.x: Mera was the Ayagars' harvest share and Meruka was the sale and purchase tax, so both statements are correct.

121.s: Which of the following pairs relating to land classification is correctly matched?
121.x: Bagayati denoted garden land. Nanja was wet land, Punja was dry land and Banjara was waste land.
121.tq: Use elimination through the land-classification terms.
xs: **Bagayati — garden land** is correct — option **(3)**.
**Nanja** = wet; **Punja** = dry; **Banjara** = waste — so options 1, 2 and 4 are wrong.
xa: Andhra terms: **Neerarambamu (Magani)** = irrigated, paid in grain; **Kaadarambamu (Metta)** = dry, paid in cash.
Tax rates depended on the **quality of land**.

121.s: What did Neerarambamu or Magani denote in the Andhra terminology of Vijayanagara revenue administration?
o: Garden land assessed through market tolls
121.x: Neerarambamu, also called Magani, was irrigated land and was generally taxed in grain at higher rates.
121.tq: Distinguish the two closely related Andhra land-assessment terms.
xs: **Neerarambamu (Magani)** = **irrigated land**, taxed in **grain** at a higher rate — option **(3)**.
Dry land, **Kaadarambamu (Metta)**, was taxed in **cash** at a lower rate.
xa: Andhra shares: **Sangoru (1/2)**, **Mungoru (1/3)**.
Water tax: **Neeruganti**.

121.s: How were the rights to collect market or santhalu taxes generally given in the Vijayanagara Empire?
o: Assigned permanently to village assemblies without payment
121.x: The right to collect market taxes was auctioned to Sunkandarlu.
121.tq: Identify the agency associated with the collection right rather than the tax itself.
xs: The right to collect market (**santhalu**) taxes was **auctioned to Sunkandarlu** — option **(4)**.
The **Dalavayi** was the army C-in-C, not a toll collector.
xa: Customs and excise came under the **Sunka vyavahara** department.
**Adikasu** was the tax on shops; **Meruka** on sale and purchase.
Land tax remained the **main source** of revenue.

121.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Putrodaya kanuka — Sale and purchase of goods
121.x: Putrodaya kanuka was a tax on the birth of a son. Sale and purchase of goods was taxed through Meruka.
121.tq: Find the wrongly matched tax and object.
xs: **Putrodaya kanuka — Sale and purchase** is wrong — option **(1)**; it was a tax on the **birth of a son**.
Sale and purchase was taxed by **Meruka**.
**Kalyana kanika** = weddings; **Illari pannu** = houses; **Kondaju** = barbers — all correct.
xa: **Sadashiva Raya** abolished the barbers' tax **Kondaju**.
The **marriage tax** was abolished empire-wide by **Krishnadevaraya**, after **Saluva Narasimha** lifted it in some areas.

121.s: Which of the following statements regarding Siddhaya is correct?
o: It was exclusively a military title of the commander-in-chief.
It denoted a fixed levy, with varieties connected with occupations such as cotton ginning and toddy tapping.
It was the name of the royal treasury.
It referred only to a tax on sale and purchase of goods.
121.x: Siddhaya meant a fixed levy. Pinje Siddhayam was connected with cotton ginners, Eidipi Siddhayam with toddy tappers and Jati Siddhayam with castes or professions.
121.tq: Identify the general term from its occupational applications.
xs: **Siddhaya** was a **fixed levy**, with occupational forms — option **(2)**.
**Pinje Siddhayam** = cotton ginners; **Eidipi Siddhayam** = toddy tappers; **Jati Siddhayam** = castes/professions.
The treasury was **Bhandara**; tax on sale and purchase was **Meruka**.
xa: Under the **Kakatiyas**, Siddhaya was an extraordinary **war-time tax**.
**Kanika / Kanuka** = levy or present, e.g. **Kalyana kanika**.

121.s: On whom was the Vijayanagara tax Navidadere levied?
121.x: Navidadere (Kondaju) was the barbers' tax; Maneyanna was the house tax.

121.s: On what was the Vijayanagara tax Maneyanna (Illari Pannu) levied?
121.x: Maneyanna was the house tax.

121.s: What was the usual share of produce collected as land revenue in Vijayanagara?
121.x: The usual share was 1/6; fertile land paid 1/4 or 1/3.

121.s: Which Vijayanagara tax was levied on the birth of a son?
121.x: Putrodaya Kanuka was levied on the birth of a son; Kalyana Kanika was the wedding tax.

121.s: Which Vijayanagara ruler totally withdrew (abolished) the marriage tax?
121.x:
Most books and keys (Rocket, NextGen previous papers, APPSC G1 2010): Krishnadevaraya. Some keys and the old notes: Sadasiva Raya.
Krishnadevaraya totally withdrew the marriage tax (first remitted under Saluva Narasimha); the Sadasiva-period (Rama Raya) inscriptions record the remission of the barbers' tax. (Old key Sadasiva Raya.)

121.s: Which tax of the Vijayanagara period was levied on sale and purchase?
121.x: Meruka was the tax on sale and purchase; Mera was the Ayagars' harvest share and Merulu the Talari's grain gifts.

121.s: What were the land-tax documents of the Vijayanagara period called?
121.x: Land-tax documents of the Vijayanagara period were called Adhuvanatantram.

121.s: Which Vijayanagara ruler first remitted the marriage tax?
121.x: Saluva Narasimha first remitted the marriage tax; Krishnadevaraya later withdrew it totally.

121.s: During the ancient and medieval days, Pradvivaka was an adviser to the king in:
121.x: The Pradvivaka was the king's adviser in the judiciary, interpreting legal texts; not military, revenue or espionage.

121.s: Which of the following scriptures was considered authoritative in the administration of justice during the Vijayanagara period?
121.x: Parasara Madhaviyam, Madhavacharya's commentary on the Parashara Smriti, was the authoritative law book of Vijayanagara; Amuktamalyada and the Arthashastra are statecraft works.

121.s: Police rights were sometimes sold in the Vijayanagara Empire. What was this called?
121.x: Under Padikaval, police rights were sold to individuals; Athavana was revenue and Kandachara the military department.

121.s: In ancient medieval times Pradvivaka was the advisor to the king in this department?
121.x: The Pradvivaka was the chief judicial adviser to the king, interpreting Dharmashastra; not revenue, espionage or military.

121.s: Through which work did the Vijayanagara judicial system follow the Yajnavalkya and Parashara Smritis?
121.x: The Yajnavalkya and Parashara Smritis were followed through Madhavacharya’s Parashara Madhaviyam.
121.tq: Match the legal texts with the specific work through which they were applied.
xs: The **Yajnavalkya and Parashara Smritis** were followed via Madhavacharya's **Parashara Madhaviyam** — option **(1)**.
**Amuktamalyada** is Krishnadevaraya's poem; **Dhanodbhava** = civil case; **Rayavachakam** is a chronicle of departments.
xa: Courts: **Pratishtita** (fixed), **Apratishtita** (mobile), **Mudrita** (royal appointee), **Shastrita** (king himself).
Cases: **Himsodbhava** (criminal), **Dhanodbhava** (civil).

121.s: What did Himsodbhava and Dhanodbhava respectively refer to in the Vijayanagara judicial system?
121.x: Himsodbhava referred to criminal cases, whereas Dhanodbhava referred to civil cases.
121.tq: Separate the two similar judicial terms by matching each with its case category.
xs: **Himsodbhava** = **criminal** case; **Dhanodbhava** = **civil** case — option **(1)**.
Option **(3)** reverses them.
xa: Court types: **Pratishtita** (fixed), **Apratishtita** (mobile).
Punishments: **death for treason**, mutilation for theft.

121.s: What was the punishment for theft in the Vijayanagara period?
121.x: Theft was punished by mutilation and treason by death; Brahmins received life imprisonment instead of death.
xa: **Divine ordeals** were used as proof (**Conti**).
Cases: **Himsodbhava** (criminal) and **Dhanodbhava** (civil).
Police: **Talari** (village), **Kavali Daru** (Sthala), **Peta Kavalidaru** (towns).

121.s: Who policed the village under the Vijayanagara Kavali system?
121.x: The Talari policed the village, the Peta Kavalidaru the towns and the Kavali Daru the Sthala.
xa: The Talari had **no salary** and collected **Merulu** at harvest.
Police watched communities suspected of receiving stolen goods, e.g. the **Panchanam**.

121.s: What punishment did a Brahmin guilty of a crime punishable by death receive in the Vijayanagara period?
121.x: Brahmins got life imprisonment instead of death.

121.s: Who policed the Sthala level under the Kavali system?
121.x: Talari policed the village, Kavali Daru the sthala and Peta Kavalidaru the towns.

121.s:
Consider the following statements about the Vijayanagara Kavali system:
1. The Talari policed the village.
2. The Kavali Daru policed the towns.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
121.x: The Talari policed the village; towns were policed by the Peta Kavalidaru, while the Kavali Daru worked at the sthala level.

121.s: Who was the Pradvivaka in the Vijayanagara administration?
o: A judge who advised the king and explained legal texts
The head of the village police
The officer in charge of the treasury
The commander of the hill forts
121.x: The Pradvivaka was the judge and adviser who helped the king in justice and explained the legal texts.

121.s: While appointing 'Brahmins' as 'Karanams', Harihara I of the Vijayanagara Empire followed the appointment system of which of the following dynasties?
121.src: APPSC Junior Assistant in Dr. NTR University of Health Scien
121.x: Harihara I appointed Brahmins as village Karanams on the Kakatiya pattern - the Sangama brothers had served the Kakatiya state, and Vijayanagara village administration (Ayagars, Karanam) continued the Kakatiya system.

121.s: Who was the repair and maintenance officer of forts in the Vijayanagara Empire?
121.x: The Parupatyagar, the king's officer of the nadu/sima, collected revenue and repaired and maintained forts. Gowda was a village/sthala head and Dandanayaka a commander.

121.s: The biggest administrative unit in the Vijayanagara Empire was
121.x: The Rajya or Mandala (province) was the largest unit, above Nadu, Sthala and Grama; Kottam and Kurram were smaller Chola-era units.

121.s: What was the village headman called in the Vijayanagara Empire?
121.src: APPSC Junior Assistants (Dr. NTR University of Health Scienc
121.x:
Key: Gowda (Gauda). In Andhra the same village head was the Reddi, which is also printed (NextGen p.29).
The village headman of the Vijayanagara empire is keyed as Gowda (Gauda), the Karnataka name of the Andhra Reddi; Chowdhary and Parupatyadar are wrong.

121.s: Who headed a Nadu or Seema in Vijayanagara provincial administration?
121.x: A Nadu was under the Nadagauda and Parupatyagar; a Rajya under a prince or Durgadhipati, a Sthala under the Reddi/Gauda/Sthalakaranam and a village under the Ayagars.
xa: Sangama princes as governors were titled **Odeyar/Vodeyar**; the office was the **Chavadi**.
About **17 rajyams** existed under **Achyutaraya**, e.g. **Udayagiri, Chandragiri, Kondaveedu**.
**Kavalgar** kept order at the Sthala level.

121.s: Which of the following statements about Vijayanagara provincial governors is correct?
o: They could not keep their own armies
They held office for life without transfer
121.x: Governors could mint coins, levy taxes and keep armies, but they were frequently transferred.

121.s: What title did the Sangama princes who governed Vijayanagara provinces hold?
121.x: Princes governing a Rajya or Mandala under the Sangamas were titled Odeyar.

121.s: Before 1485, Saluva Narasimha was the governor of which Andhra rajya?
121.x: Saluva Narasimha governed Chandragiri before 1485; it later became a capital.

121.s: Which Andhra rajya became the new headquarters of Tirumala after Talikota?
121.x: After Talikota, Penukonda became Tirumala's new headquarters.

121.s: About how many rajyams were there under Achyutaraya?
121.x: There were about 17 rajyams under Achyutaraya.

121.s: Which officer of the nadu (sima) collected revenue and maintained forts in the Vijayanagara empire?
121.x: The Parupatyagar was the nadu/sima officer who collected revenue and maintained the forts.

121.s: Which was the most important Andhra rajya of the Vijayanagara empire, covering the Paka and Muliki districts (Nellore, Kadapa)?
121.x: Udayagiri was the most important Andhra rajya and was governed by royal princes under the first dynasty.

121.s: How many Ayagars traditionally ran each village under the Ayagar system?
121.x: Each village was administered by 12 hereditary Ayagars. They included officials, artisans and service providers.
121.tq: Test the fixed numerical composition of the village institution.
xs: Each village had **12 hereditary Ayagars (Ayagandlu)** — option **(3)** (APPSC **2012**).
They included officials (**Karanam, Reddi, Talari, Purohita**) and artisans/servants.
xa: Artisans: **Kamsali** (goldsmith), **Kummari** (potter), **Vadrangi** (carpenter), **Kase** (mason), **Kammari** (blacksmith).
Servants: **Chakali** (washerman), **Mangali** (barber), **Madiga**.
Ayagar and Nayankara tenure both continued **Kakatiya** practice.

121.s: How were the Ayagars generally paid?
o: A fixed share of customs duties alone
Tax-free Manyam lands and a share of the harvest called Mera
Regular cash salaries from the royal treasury only
121.x: Ayagars received tax-free Manyam lands, also called Mirasi, Bhattu Vrutti or Jatikattu Manyalu, along with a share of the harvest called Mera. They were not paid regular cash salaries.
121.tq: Distinguish in-kind and land-based village remuneration from cash salary and Mughal jagir payment.
xs: Ayagars got **tax-free Manyam lands** and a **share of the harvest called Mera** — option **(2)**.
They drew **no cash salary**; **zat** ranks and transferable jagirs are Mughal.
xa: Manyam types: **Mirasi / Bhattuvritti / Jatikattu** manyams.
**Jodi** was a nominal tax on Ayagar and manya lands.
⚠ **Mera** = Ayagar harvest share; **Merulu** = Talari's grain gifts.

121.s: Which of the following pairs (Ayagar – function) is correctly matched?
121.x: The Talari was the village watchman. The Karanam was the accountant, the Reddi the village head and the Purohita the priest.
xa: Karanam kept village accounts, land and crop registers, and **temple accounts**.
Reddi was also collector of revenue; under the **Kakatiyas**, the village judge.
**Begari** supervised forced labour (**vetti**).

121.s: Who was the 'Kase' among the village artisans of the Vijayanagara period?
121.x: Kase was the mason or house-builder; Vadrangi was the carpenter, Kummari the potter and Chakali the washerman.
xa: **Kammari** = blacksmith; **Mangali** = barber.
There were **12 Ayagars** per village.

121.s: Who collected the grain gifts called 'Merulu' in Vijayanagara villages?
121.x: The Talari (watchman) collected Merulu; Mera was the Ayagars' harvest share.

121.s: Which village officer kept the accounts and land and crop registers in Vijayanagara villages?
121.x: The Karanam kept accounts, land and crop registers and temple accounts; the Reddi was the village head.

121.s: Who supervised forced labour (vetti) in a Vijayanagara village?
121.x: The Begari supervised vetti (forced labour).

121.s: What was the village head called Reddi in Andhra known as in Karnataka?
121.x: The Reddi was the village head and revenue collector of Andhra; in Karnataka he was the Gauda.

121.s: What was the practice adopted by the Vijayanagar Kings to protect the inhabitants within a fortified area from starvation due to sieges by enemy armies?
o: Large granaries were built within the fortified area to store grains
Secret pathways were maintained to transport groceries into fortified areas
Large agricultural tracts were incorporated within the fortified area
The forts were built on hills to prevent siege by the enemy
121.x: Vijayanagara enclosed large agricultural tracts within its fortifications so the city could feed itself during a siege - NCERT notes this was unlike the usual practice of building granaries.

121.s: The Vijayanagara king, though supreme head of state, was expected to act within Dharma and in consultation with whom?
121.x: The king was supreme head, commander and fountain of justice, but acted within Dharma and with ministerial counsel.
xa: Burton Stein called Vijayanagara a **"segmentary state"**; Nilakanta Sastri a **"military administration"**.
The PM was the **Mahapradhana/Mahapradhani** (e.g. **Saluva Timmarusu**), heading the **pradhanis**.
As supreme judge the king sat in the **Dharmasana**.

121.s: Which historian characterised the Vijayanagara empire as a 'segmentary state'?
121.x: Burton Stein called it a segmentary state, whereas Nilakanta Sastri described it as a military administration.
xa: The Nayankara gave a huge army cheaply but bred **Nayaka kingdoms** that broke away after **Talikota**.
The king was supreme head but bound by **Dharma** and ministers' counsel.

121.s: Which historian described the Vijayanagara state as a 'military administration'?
121.x: Nilakanta Sastri called it a military administration; Burton Stein called it a segmentary state.

121.s: What does Krishnadevaraya's Amuktamalyada advise the king to do regarding foreign merchants?
o: Treat them generously and encourage imports
Confine them to a single port
Bar them from the horse trade
121.x: Amuktamalyada advises improving harbours, encouraging imports and treating foreign merchants generously.
xa: It also says **Brahmins** should command forts.
It advises building **tanks and irrigation**.

121.s: What does Krishnadevaraya's Amuktamalyada advise the king to do regarding forest tribes?
o: Win them over rather than merely crush them
121.x: Amuktamalyada combines devotion with statecraft and advises winning over forest tribes rather than merely crushing them.
xa: "Political matters are discussed" in it (APPSC G2 **2003**).
Revenue maxim: the **bulk of revenue should go to the army**.

121.s: According to Amuktamalyada, to whom should the bulk of the king's revenue go?
121.x: Amuktamalyada advises that the bulk of revenue go to the army.

121.s: According to Amuktamalyada, who should command the forts?
121.x: Krishnadevaraya's maxim was that Brahmins should command forts.

121.s: Which of the following is correctly stated regarding the contents of Amuktamalyada?
o: It refers to Krishnadevaraya’s campaigns and gives political advice, but does not trace a genealogy from Bukka.
It is exclusively a manual on fort construction.
It records the genealogy of the dynasty from Bukka but not Krishnadevaraya’s campaigns.
It contains no discussion of kingship or administration.
121.x: Amuktamalyada contains political maxims on rajaniti, kingship and administration and refers to Krishnadevaraya’s campaigns, but it gives no genealogy from Bukka to Krishnadevaraya (APPSC G2 2003).
121.tq: Discriminate between the work’s dynastic genealogy and the campaigns it does not record.

121.s: Who headed the Siddha (standing) army of Vijayanagara?
121.x: The standing army was under the Dalavayi; Durga Dannayakas commanded forts.
xa: Nuniz put the standing army at about **50,000**.
The other wing: **Amara-nayaka levies** — **600,000** under Achyutaraya (Nuniz).

121.s: Who was the first Vijayanagara king to use cannon?
121.x: Bukka I was the first Vijayanagara king to use cannon; firearms were associated with Turkish and Portuguese experts.
xa: ⚠ First cannon = **Bukka I**; **Samugaris** (gunmen) = **Saluva Narasimha**.
Cavalry was **decisive**.

121.s: Through which ports did Vijayanagara mainly import Arabian and Persian horses?
121.x: Horses came via the west-coast ports Goa, Honnavar and Bhatkal; Portuguese and Arab merchants ran the trade.
xa: Krishnadevaraya had **24,000 horses**.
Amuktamalyada urges importing **horses, elephants and gems**.

121.s: Who introduced the Samugaris, or gunmen, into the Vijayanagara military system?
121.x: Saluva Narasimha introduced the Samugaris, or gunmen. Bukka I is associated with the first use of cannon by a Vijayanagara king.
121.tq: Separate the closely related military innovations of Bukka I and Saluva Narasimha.
xs: **Saluva Narasimha** introduced the **Samugaris** (gunmen) — option **(2)**.
**Bukka I** was the first to use **cannon**; **Devaraya II** and **Rama Raya** recruited **Muslim** troops.
xa: Firearms came with **Turkish** and **Portuguese** experts.
Horses came via **Goa, Honnavar, Bhatkal**.

121.s: What were the four types of forts in the Vijayanagara period?
121.x: The four types of forts were Giri (hill), Sthala (land), Jala (water) and Vana (forest) forts.
xa: Forts were under **Durga Dannayakas**.
Krishnadevaraya advised making **Brahmins** fort commanders.
The **Amara gramalu** collected **Durgadayam** for the army.

121.s: How often was the Siddha (standing) army of Vijayanagara paid?
121.x: The standing army was paid every four months.

121.s: Under whom were the forts placed in the Vijayanagara period?
121.x: The four kinds of forts were under Durga Dannayakas.

122.x: Both Nicolo Conti and Fernao Nuniz recorded Sati in Vijayanagara; Barbosa and Paes also mention it.

122.s: Which traveller recorded that women in Vijayanagara served as wrestlers, accountants, astrologers and even judges?
122.x: The Portuguese Fernao Nuniz (with Paes) recorded women working as wrestlers, accountants, astrologers, palanquin bearers and even judges.

122.s: Who wrote the Matla-us-Sadain?
122.x: The Persian envoy Abdur Razzaq described Vijayanagara under Devaraya II in his Matla-us-Sadain.

122.s: In which work did Abdur Razzaq record his visit to Vijayanagara?
122.x: Abdur Razzaq wrote the Matla-us-Sadain; Journey Beyond Three Seas is Nikitin's work.

122.s: Which foreign traveller wrote a dynastic history of Vijayanagara, including its foundation legend?
122.x: Fernao Nuniz, a Portuguese horse dealer, wrote on the dynasty's history and foundation legend.

122.s: According to Fernao Nuniz, how many amara troops did the Vijayanagara nayakas maintain?
122.x: Nuniz put the amara troops at 600,000; Conti put the army at 90,000.

122.s: Which traveller recorded that 250 buffaloes and 400 goats were sacrificed on the last day of Mahanavami?
122.x: Domingo Paes recorded the Mahanavami sacrifices.

122.s: Which inscription contains the 12 Sutras to be followed during the construction of Tataka?
122.x: The Porumamilla inscription (Kadapa, 1369, Prince Bhaskara) lays down the 12 rules for building a tank. Tummalagudem, Korlagallu, Bitragunta, Bodhan, Palampet and Pakhala are other records.

122.s: The rules to be followed in the construction of Tataka are mentioned in?
122.x: The Porumamilla inscription (Kadapa, 1369, Prince Bhaskara) lays down the 12 rules for building a tank. Tummalagudem, Korlagallu, Bitragunta, Bodhan, Palampet and Pakhala are other records.

122.s: Which of the following inscriptions describes the 12 rules to be observed while undertaking tank D) construction?
122.x: The Porumamilla inscription (Kadapa, 1369, Prince Bhaskara) lays down the 12 rules for building a tank. Tummalagudem, Korlagallu, Bitragunta, Bodhan, Palampet and Pakhala are other records.

122.s: Narasambudhi Tatakam was built during which period?
122.x: The Narasambudhi tank was built by Saluva Narasimha, so it belongs to the Vijayanagara period, not to the Kakatiyas, Yadavas, Hoysalas, Velamas or Reddis.

122.s: Narasambudhi Tatakam (pond) belongs to which period?
122.x: The Narasambudhi tank was built by Saluva Narasimha, so it belongs to the Vijayanagara period, not to the Kakatiyas, Yadavas, Hoysalas, Velamas or Reddis.

122.s: The Vijayanagara kings are credited with achieving agricultural development by which initiatives?
o: By reducing the tax on cultivated land
By providing market facilities for agricultural produce
By purchasing food grains for their army
By constructing ponds, dams and wells
122.x: Vijayanagara kings built tanks, dams, canals and wells for irrigation; tank-building was one of the seven meritorious acts.

122.s: The crop known to people of Vijayanagara Empire is:
122.x: Coconut is native to the Indian coasts and was grown in Vijayanagara times; groundnut, tobacco and red chilli are American crops brought later by the Portuguese. (Moved: Vijayanagara economy.)

122.s: Whose help did Vijayanagaradhisas take in the construction of dams?
122.x: Nuniz records that a Portuguese engineer helped Krishnadevaraya build the great tank (dam) near the capital, so the Vijayanagara kings took Portuguese help. (Moved to Vijayanagara.)

122.s: Which of the following irrigation works is correctly matched with its ruler?
o: Bukka I — Siruveru tank near Penukonda
122.x: Bukka I is associated with the Siruveru tank near Penukonda. Narasambudhi was associated with Saluva Narasimha, while the Toragallu and Kambham works belonged to Krishnadevaraya.
122.tq: Use the ruler–irrigation work association and reject swapped patrons.
xs: **Bukka I — Siruveru tank near Penukonda** is correct — option **(1)**.
**Toragallu dam** and **Kambham tank** belong to **Krishnadevaraya**; **Narasambudhi tank** (Anantapur) to **Saluva Narasimha**.
xa: Krishnadevaraya also built the **Nagalapuram tank** with **Portuguese engineers**.
The **Anantasagaram** tank (**1369**) dates to **Bukka I's** time.
⚠ **Penukonda** = Siruveru tank; **Penugonda** (West Godavari) = Vasavi Kanyaka Parameswari.

122.s: Who issued the Porumamilla inscription, which lays down 12 rules (Dwadasa Sutras) for building a tank?
122.x: The Porumamilla inscription, with its 12 rules (Dwadasa Sutras) for building a tank, was issued by Bhaskara (Bhaskara Bhavadura), son of Bukka I and prince of Udayagiri. It records the Anantasagaram tank (1369) in Kadapa; it was not issued by Krishnadevaraya.

122.s: What was the temple treasury kept by the Karanam called in the Vijayanagara period?
122.x: The temple treasury was the Sri Bhandara, kept by the Karanam; Devadaya villages were temple endowments.
xa: **Samayas** (merchant guilds) met in **temple mandapas**.
The **Sadasivakona** inscriptions (**1554 CE**) show **Kaanika** diverted from **Gudimallam** lands to a new temple.

122.s: Where did the merchant guilds (Samayas) of the Vijayanagara period usually meet?
122.x: The Samayas, led by the Ayyavali guild, met in temple mandapas, not royal palaces.
xa: Industries: **textiles (Kalamkari), silk, zari, diamonds, metalwork**.
Traders included **Settis**, **Komatis** and **Balijas**.

122.s: What was the main revenue of the Vijayanagara state?
122.x: Land tax was the main revenue source.

122.s: Who built the Siruveru tank near Penukonda?
122.x: Bukka I built the Siruveru tank; Saluva Narasimha built Narasambudhi.

122.s: Which inscription lays down twelve rules (Dwadasa Sutras) for building a tank?
122.x: The Porumamilla inscription of Bhaskara Bhavadura (1369) lays down the twelve rules for tank building.

122.s: In which present-day district is Porumamilla, whose inscription records the Anantasagaram tank, located?
122.x: Porumamilla, site of the 1369 inscription on the Anantasagaram tank, is in Kadapa district.

122.s: Who built the Narasambudhi tank in Anantapur?
122.x: Saluva Narasimha built the Narasambudhi tank; Bukka I built the Siruveru tank.

122.s: Which tank did Krishnadevaraya build with the help of Portuguese engineers?
122.x: Krishnadevaraya built the Nagalapuram tank with Portuguese engineers, besides the Toragallu dam and Kambham tank.

122.s: Tank-building was counted among the Saptasantanas. What were the Saptasantanas?
122.x: The Saptasantanas were the seven meritorious acts, and tank-building was one of them.

122.s: What were 'Devadaya' in the Vijayanagara period?
122.x: Devadaya were temple villages or endowments; Sri Bhandara was the temple treasury.

122.s: What profession did the 'Balanjalu' take up in Vijayanagara society?
122.x: The Balanjalu (Balijas, Veerabalijas), like the Ayyavalu, were a trading community, so business. They were not weavers, herders or barbers.

122.s: Who were the Vipravinodulu during the Vijayanagara period?
o: A caste of Shudras who depended only on Brahmins for their sustenance
Shudras performing their arts to entertain Brahmins
Brahmin jugglers who entertained only Brahmins in their homes
Brahmin scholars skilled in all arts
122.x: Vipravinodins were Brahmin jugglers who gave indoor entertainment to Brahmins only, so they were a sect of Brahmins. They were not Shudras, weavers, Kshatriyas or Vaisyas.

122.s: Who were Vipravinodulu during the Vijayanagara period?
o: They are a caste of Shudras who depend only on Brahmins for their sustenance.
Shudras performing their arts to entertain Brahmins.
Brahmin jugglers who entertain only Brahmins in their homes.
Brahmin scholars skilled in all arts.
122.x: Vipravinodins were Brahmin jugglers who gave indoor entertainment to Brahmins only, so they were a sect of Brahmins. They were not Shudras, weavers, Kshatriyas or Vaisyas.

122.s: Who were Vipra-Vinodins of the Vijayanagaraperiod?
o: Sudras, who exhibited the arts only for the entertainment of brahmins
Brahmin scholars, well versed in all arts
Brahmin jugglers, who provided in-door entertainment to brahmins only
Non-brahmin jugglers. who depended on brahmins for their livelihood
122.x: Vipravinodins were Brahmin jugglers who gave indoor entertainment to Brahmins only, so they were a sect of Brahmins. They were not Shudras, weavers, Kshatriyas or Vaisyas.

122.s: During Vijayanagar rule Vipravinodins were a sect of
122.x: Vipravinodins were Brahmin jugglers who gave indoor entertainment to Brahmins only, so they were a sect of Brahmins. They were not Shudras, weavers, Kshatriyas or Vaisyas.

122.s: During the Vijayanagara period, the 'Vipra Vinodinis' were part of?
122.x: Vipravinodins were Brahmin jugglers who gave indoor entertainment to Brahmins only, so they were a sect of Brahmins. They were not Shudras, weavers, Kshatriyas or Vaisyas.
