122.x: Vipravinodins were Brahmin jugglers who gave indoor entertainment to Brahmins only, so they were a sect of Brahmins. They were not Shudras, weavers, Kshatriyas or Vaisyas.

122.s: Which of the following pairs (group – occupation) is correctly matched?
122.x: The Kaikkolars were weavers, like the Padmasalis. Vira Panchalas were artisans and Settis were traders.
xa: Weaving groups: **Padmasali, Jandra, Kuruba**, called **Kaikkolar**.
CDX's **Panchanam** community had **74** sub-sects (inscription of **Devaraya I**).
Traders included **Arya** (vegetarian) and **Kalinga** Vaishyas.

122.s: Vijayanagara society is described as having four varnas and about how many castes?
122.x: Society had four varnas and about eighteen castes; Brahmins included Vaidikas and Niyogis and many Sudras became amaranayakas.
xa: **Vipravinodins** were Brahmin jugglers who entertained only Brahmins.
Traders: **Settis (Chettis)**, **Komatis**, **Balijas**.

122.s: Who were the Vira Panchalas in Vijayanagara society?
122.x: The Vira Panchalas worked in gold, iron, brass, wood and stone.

122.s: Who were the Niyogis in Vijayanagara society?
122.x: Niyogis were Brahmin officials; Vaidikas were priests.

122.s: Which of the following groups of Vijayanagara society were traders?
122.x: Settis, Komatis and Balijas were the trading groups; Vira Panchalas were artisans, Kaikkolars weavers and Vaidikas/Niyogis Brahmins.

122.s: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Valangai and Idangai divisions in Vijayanagara society?
o: Valangai consisted exclusively of Brahmins, whereas Idangai consisted of royal officials
Valangai consisted mainly of agricultural and trading groups, whereas Idangai consisted mainly of artisans and some traders
Valangai consisted mainly of artisans, whereas Idangai consisted exclusively of priests
Both Valangai and Idangai consisted only of agricultural communities
122.x: Valangai or right-hand groups were mainly agricultural and trading communities. Idangai or left-hand groups were mainly artisans, including Panchala smiths, along with some traders.
122.tq: Use the reversed-comparison trap by separating the occupations associated with the two groups.
xs: **Valangai** (right-hand) = mainly **agricultural and trading** groups; **Idangai** (left-hand) = mainly **artisans and some traders** — option **(2)**.
Idangai included the **Panchala** smiths.
xa: The division began in **Chola** times and continued under Vijayanagara.
They clashed over **precedence and honours** — processions and insignia.

122.s: The Valangai and Idangai caste groupings of the Vijayanagara period had their origin in which earlier period?
122.x: The right-hand and left-hand groupings began during Chola times and continued under the Vijayanagara Empire.
122.tq: Test chronological continuity by linking the institution with its earlier origin.
xs: The Valangai–Idangai division began in **Chola times** — option **(2)** and continued under **Vijayanagara**.
It is not of Mughal, Maurya or Satavahana origin.
xa: Valangai (right-hand) = agricultural and trading groups.
Idangai (left-hand) = artisans, incl. **Panchala** smiths, plus some traders.
Clashes were over **precedence and honours**.

122.s: Which groups mainly made up the Idangai (left-hand) division of Vijayanagara society?
122.x: Idangai were mainly artisans (including Panchala smiths); Valangai were agricultural and trading groups.

122.s: Kudirai Chettis was a local community of merchants engaged in the import of horses from Arabia and Central Asia during the ____.
122.src: APPSC Junior Assistant in Dr. NTR University of Health Scien
122.x: NCERT (Themes II) names the kudirai chettis, local horse merchants, as the middlemen in the Vijayanagara horse trade from Arabia and Central Asia. The Cholas, the Delhi Sultanate and the Mughals are not linked to them.

122.s: Vajrakarur is famous for
122.x: Vajrakarur in Anantapur district is known for diamonds (kimberlite pipes), worked since Vijayanagara times. It is not a textile, gold or copper centre.

122.s: Which was a prominent import from the West during the Sangama clan?
122.x: Horses from Arabia and Persia were the chief import for the cavalry, ahead of pearls, silk and precious stones; Kalamkari cloth was the chief export.

122.s: Which among the following was the single biggest item of import to the Vijayanagara Empire?
122.x: Horses from Arabia and Persia were the chief import for the cavalry, ahead of pearls, silk and precious stones; Kalamkari cloth was the chief export.

122.s: Which of the following groups consists entirely of east-coast ports associated with the Vijayanagara period?
122.x: Pulicat, Mylapore, Motupalli and Machilipatnam were east-coast ports. The other groups contain west-coast ports.
122.tq: Classify every item geographically and choose the homogeneous group.
xs: **Pulicat, Mylapore, Motupalli, Machilipatnam** are all **east coast** ports — option **(2)**.
**Honnavar, Bhatkal, Goa, Mangalore, Calicut** are **west coast** ports.
xa: **Pulicat** traded with **Pegu, Malacca, Sumatra**.
**Machilipatnam** port revival (**8 Aug 2026**) recalls its medieval trade role.
**Devaraya I** took **Motupalli** from **Kondaveedu**.

122.s: What was the chief export of the Vijayanagara empire?
122.x: Kalamkari was the chief export; horses were the chief import and Chinese silk was also imported.

122.s: Where were the diamonds mined in Kurnool and Anantapur polished in the Vijayanagara period?
122.x: Diamonds were polished at Vajrakarur; Gutti and Rayadurg supplied silk and Venkatagiri zari.
xa: Textile centres: **Tadipatri, Adoni, Gutti** (Kalamkari).
**Vajrakarur diamonds** are an AP-angle favourite.

122.s: Of which industry were Tadipatri, Adoni and Gutti Vijayanagara centres?
122.x: Tadipatri, Adoni and Gutti were textile centres; Vajrakarur was known for diamonds.

122.s: Which of the following was a west-coast port of the Vijayanagara period?
122.x: Bhatkal was on the west coast; Pulicat, Motupalli and Machilipatnam were east-coast ports.

122.s: For what was Venkatagiri known in the Vijayanagara period?
122.x: Venkatagiri was known for zari; Gutti and Rayadurg for silk.

122.s: The Motupalli Dharma Sasanam (1416) is linked with which ruler, who took Motupalli?
122.x: Devaraya I took Motupalli; the Motupalli Dharma Sasanam dates to 1416.

122.s: With what was Vajrakarur associated in the Vijayanagara period?
122.x: Vajrakarur is associated with diamonds; Pulicat, Motupalli and Machilipatnam were important Andhra ports.
xa: AP hooks: Andhra ports, **Vajrakarur** diamonds, **Porumamilla** (Kadapa) tank rules.
Pulicat traded with **Pegu, Malacca, Sumatra**.

122.s: What was the chief import of the Vijayanagara empire?
122.x: Horses were the chief import; Kalamkari was the chief export and diamonds and sugar were also exported.

122.s: Which places were centres of silk production in the Vijayanagara period?
122.x: Gutti and Rayadurg were silk centres; Vajrakarur polished diamonds.

122.s: Who was the tutelary deity of Vijayanagara?
122.x: Virupaksha of Hampi, a form of Shiva, was the family and tutelary deity of the Vijayanagara kings. 'Lord Shiva' is too general; Durga and Krishna are wrong.

122.s: Who was the tutelary deity of Vijayanagara?
122.x: Virupaksha of Hampi, a form of Shiva, was the family and tutelary deity of the Vijayanagara kings. 'Lord Shiva' is too general; Durga and Krishna are wrong.

122.s: Which festival was celebrated in a great manner by the rulers of Vijayanagara every year?
122.x: The Mahanavami (Dasara) was the great annual royal festival, held on the Mahanavami Dibba and described by Paes and Abdur Razzaq. Ramanavami, Janmashtami and Deepavali were not the state festival.

122.s: Which Vijayanagara ruler of the Aravidu dynasty allowed a church to be established at Chandragiri and protected the Jesuit mission?
122.x: Venkatapati Raya II allowed a church at Chandragiri and extended protection to the Jesuit mission.
122.tq: Use the ruler–religious-policy association and avoid swapping rulers of different dynasties.
xs: **Venkatapati Raya II** (Aravidu) allowed a **church at Chandragiri** and protected the **Jesuit mission** — option **(1)**.
**Devaraya II** built a **mosque**; **Achyutaraya** was crowned at **Tirumala**; **Saluva Narasimha** saw **Tirupati** rise.
xa: From **Venkatapati II** onward, **Venkateswara** replaced **Virupaksha** as main deity.
**Chevvappa Nayaka** let the Portuguese build a church in **Thanjavur**.

122.s: From the reign of which ruler did Venkateswara replace Virupaksha as the main deity?
122.x: From Venkatapati II onward, Venkateswara replaced Virupaksha as the main deity.
122.tq: Locate the religious change at the correct point in the dynastic sequence.
xs: From **Venkatapati II** onward, **Venkateswara** replaced **Virupaksha** — option **(3)**.
**Bukka I** reconciled Jains and Vaishnavas; **Devaraya II** built a mosque; **Achyutaraya** was crowned at Tirumala.
xa: Venkatapati Raya II also allowed a **church at Chandragiri**.
**Tirupati** rose under **Saluva Narasimha**.

122.s: Which of the following groups consists entirely of Shaiva centres?
122.x: Srisailam, Tripurantakam and Srikalahasti were Shaiva centres. Kanchi, Mangalagiri and Pushpagiri and Tirupati, Ahobilam and Kadiri were Vaishnava centres, and the last group is mixed.
xa: **Draksharama** and **Amaravati** followed **Smarta Shaivism**.
⚠ **Penugonda** (West Godavari) = Vasavi Kanyaka Parameswari; **Penukonda** = Siruveru tank.

122.s: Who built the Mahanavami or Dasara Dibba at Vijayanagara?
122.x: The Mahanavami Dibba, on which the Dasara celebrations were held, was built by Krishnadevaraya.
122.tq: Avoid the ruler-swapping trap by associating the monument with its builder.
xs: The **Mahanavami (Dasara) Dibba** was built by **Krishnadevaraya** — option **(2)**.
Mahanavami was the festival of the **royal capital**.
xa: **Nayakas** brought their tribute; the **financial year** began with it.
**Burton Stein** compared it to an **Ashvamedha**.
It was described by **Paes** and **Abdur Razzaq**.

122.s: Who was the family deity of the Sangama dynasty?
122.x: The Shaivite Sangamas had Virupaksha as family deity; their family guru was Kalamukha Kriya Shakti.
xa: **Saluva, Tuluva, Aravidu** were **Vaishnavas**.
⚠ Sangama = Shaiva (**Virupaksha**); Saluva-Tuluva-Aravidu = Vaishnava (**Venkateswara**).

122.s: For temples of which deity were Ahobilam and Kadiri known?
122.x: Ahobilam and Kadiri had Narasimha temples; Tirupati rose under Saluva Narasimha.
xa: Vaishnava centres: **Tirupati, Kanchi, Mangalagiri, Pushpagiri**.
From **Venkatapati II**, **Venkateswara** became the main deity.

122.s: From where did Narahari Tirtha spread the Dvaita philosophy?
122.x: Narahari Tirtha spread Dvaita from Srikurmam, not Sringeri.
xa: **Veerappa Nayaka** admitted Portuguese missionaries to **Madurai**.
**Barbosa** recorded **religious freedom** for all creeds.

122.s: Who was the guru of the Sangama rulers?
122.x: The Shaiva Sangamas had Kalamukha Kriya Shakti as guru and Virupaksha as family deity.

122.s: Which Vijayanagara ruler enlisted Muslims in the army and built a mosque?
122.x: Devaraya II enlisted Muslims in the army with jagirs and built a mosque.

122.s: Under which ruler did Tirupati rise to prominence?
122.x: Tirupati rose under Saluva Narasimha, as the later dynasties were Vaishnava.

122.s:
Consider the following statements about Christian missions under Vijayanagara:
1. Venkatapati Raya II allowed a church at Chandragiri.
2. Venkatapati Raya II belonged to the Tuluva dynasty.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
122.x: Venkatapati Raya II allowed the Chandragiri church and protected the Jesuit mission, but he was an Aravidu ruler.

122.s: Which place in West Godavari was the main seat of Vasavi Kanyaka Parameswari, the goddess of the Arya Vysyas?
122.x: Penugonda in West Godavari is the seat of Vasavi Kanyaka Parameswari; Penukonda in Anantapur was the later Vijayanagara capital.

122.s: In which work of Krishnadevaraya does Vasantotsava, the spring festival, appear?
122.x: Vasantotsava appears in Jambavati Parinayam; Paes and Abdur Razzaq described the Mahanavami.
xa: Other festivals: **Shivaratri, Deepavali, Rathotsavam, Eruvaka Punnami**.
**Palnati Veeracharitra** mentions **Tholu Bommalata**.

122.s: To which ritual did Burton Stein compare the Vijayanagara Mahanavami festival?
122.x: Stein compared the Mahanavami to an Ashvamedha; nayakas brought tribute and the financial year began with it.
xa: Venue: **Mahanavami (Dasara) Dibba**, built by **Krishnadevaraya**.
Paes recorded **250 buffaloes and 400 goats** sacrificed on the last day.

122.s: With which festival did the Vijayanagara financial year begin?
122.x: The financial year began with Mahanavami, when the nayakas brought tribute.

122.s: Which is not correct regarding the Vijayanagara period?
o: The practice of sati sahagamana prevailed
There was an exchange of dowries
122.x: Sati, polygamy and dowry were all prevalent and child marriages were common, so 'child marriages were unknown' is the wrong statement.

122.s: Which was the most popular form of marriage in the Vijayanagara Empire?
122.x: The app notes give Brahma vivaha, in which the father gives his daughter to a suitable groom, as the most popular form in Vijayanagara society. Daiva, Gandharva and Prajapatya were less common.

122.s: Which one of the following statements about devadasis in Vijayanagara society is correct?
o: They were military officers appointed as amaranayakas.
They were exclusively palace slaves without religious functions.
They were temple dancers trained in music and dance and could be land-owning and respected.
They were Brahmin officials known as Niyogis.
122.x: Devadasis were temple dancers trained in music and dance; many were land-owning and socially respected. Domingo Paes described them.
122.tq: Apply the social description to distinguish devadasis from administrative and military groups.
xs: **Devadasis** were **temple dancers trained in music and dance**, often **land-owning and respected** — option **(3)**.
**Niyogis** were Brahmin officials; **Amaranayakas** were military chiefs.
xa: Temple dance was the forerunner of **Bharatanatyam**.
**Domingo Paes** described the devadasis.

122.s: Which social practice did the term 'Benabaga' denote in Vijayanagara society?
122.x: “Benabaga” is used in connection with the existence of slavery in Vijayanagara society.
122.tq: Identify the exact meaning of a specialised historical term.
xs: **"Benabaga"** meant **slavery** — option **(3)**.
**Dowry** = **Varashulkam**; trial by ordeal was recorded by **Conti**.
xa: **Conti** also recorded slavery.
**Kanyashulkam** = bride price.

122.s: What did 'Varashulkam' mean in Vijayanagara society?
122.x: Varashulkam was dowry, while Kanyashulkam was bride price.
xa: Prostitution was state-taxed: each woman paid **12,000 panams** a year.
**Polygamy** existed in royal families.

122.s: Which of the following was generally NOT practised among women in Vijayanagara society?
122.x: Strict purdah was not generally practised; women served as bodyguards and wrestlers, and both kanyasulkam and dowry existed.
xa: Respectable women attended the **Mahanavami** (Paes).
Women in such roles were noted by **Nuniz** and **Paes**.

122.s: Which of the following women are specifically mentioned as learned women of the Vijayanagara period?
122.x: Gangadevi and Tirumalamba are identified as learned women of the Vijayanagara period.
122.tq: Recall the exact pair of personalities rather than substituting famous women from other periods.
xs: **Gangadevi** and **Tirumalamba** are the learned women named — option **(1)**.
Gangadevi wrote **Madhura Vijayam**; Tirumalamba wrote **Varadambika Parinayam**.
xa: **Timmakka** wrote **Subhadra Kalyanam**; **Ramabhadramba** is also listed.
Women could even serve as **judges** and **accountants**.
122.fixed: Molla was a 16th-c. Vijayanagara-era poetess, so option 2 was also defensible

122.s:
Consider the following statements about social terms of the Vijayanagara period:
1. Kanyashulkam meant bride price.
2. Varashulkam meant slavery.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
122.x: Kanyashulkam was bride price; Varashulkam meant dowry, and Benabaga meant slavery.

122.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about women in Vijayanagara society?
o: Women served as bodyguards and wrestlers
122.x: There was no strict purdah; the other three statements are correct.

122.s: Which form of marriage was the most popular in Vijayanagara society?
122.x: Brahma vivaha, in which the father gives his daughter to a suitable groom, was the most popular form.

122.s: Which source states that the annual income of Sadashivaraya of the Vijayanagara period was 12 crore hons?
122.x: The Nizam Shahi chronicle Burhan-i-Maasir put Sadasiva Raya's annual income at 12 crore huns. Abdur Razzaq wrote a century earlier; Futuh-us-Salatin is Isami's Delhi chronicle; Sewell was a modern historian.

122.s:
Match the following.
List I (Coins)
List II (Region)

A. Pagoda

123.x: The Lepakshi Veerabhadra temple stands on Kurma Shailam hill near Hindupur.

123.s: To whom are the three shrines of the Lepakshi temple complex dedicated?
123.x: Lepakshi has shrines of Shiva, Veerabhadra and Vishnu, each with a mukha mandapa.

123.s: Where is the largest monolithic Nandi in India?
123.x: Lepakshi's monolithic Nandi is the largest in India (APPSC G2 2017).

123.s: Which temple is famous for its 'hanging pillar'?
123.x: The hanging pillar is at Lepakshi (APPSC 2019).

123.s: The serpent over the Naga linga at Lepakshi has how many hoods?
123.x: The Naga linga is a linga under a seven-hooded serpent, carved from a single boulder.

123.s:
Consider the following statements about the Lepakshi temple:
1. It lies in Sri Sathya Sai district.
2. Its builders were governors of Chandragiri.
3. It was built c. 1530-40 under Achyutaraya.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
123.x: Lepakshi is in Sri Sathya Sai district and was built c. 1530-40 under Achyutaraya; its builders Virupanna and Veeranna were governors of Penukonda.

123.s: Near which town is the Lepakshi temple located?
123.x: The Lepakshi Veerabhadra temple stands on Kurma Shailam hill near Hindupur, Sri Sathya Sai district.

123.s: By what other name is the Veerabhadra temple at Lepakshi known?
123.x: The Lepakshi Veerabhadra temple is also called the Papanaseswara temple.

123.s: Where was the state launch of Yogandhra-2026 held on 8 June 2026?
123.x: The state launch of Yogandhra-2026 was held at Lepakshi on 8 June 2026.

123.s: Themes from which works are depicted on the ceilings of the Lepakshi temple?
123.x: The ceilings show Ramayana and Mahabharata themes, while the walls carry Shiva subjects such as Parvati Parinayamu and Tripurasura Samharam.
xa: APPSC **2019**: Lepakshi is famous for **"pictorial inscriptions"**.
The murals are the **peak of the Vijayanagara school**.

123.s: Which place is famous for 'pictorial inscriptions' in the Vijayanagara style?
123.x: Lepakshi, with the finest Vijayanagara-school murals, is famous for 'pictorial inscriptions'. Tadipatri is known for its gopurams, Ahobilam for Narasimha temples and Chandragiri for its fort.
xa: Exam angle: **"stone bull / hanging pillar / frescoes"** → Lepakshi.
Yogandhra-**2026** was launched at Lepakshi (**8 Jun 2026**).

123.s: What do the murals at the Virupaksha temple at Hampi depict?
o: The campaigns of the Aravidu rulers
The life of Buddha and Jataka stories
123.x: The Hampi Virupaksha temple murals include the Dashavatara and Girijakalyana themes.
123.tq: Use the theme–temple association instead of relying only on the site name.
xs: Hampi Virupaksha murals show the **Dashavatara** and **Girijakalyana** — option **(2)**.
They are not limited to the Ramayana, and do not show Aravidu campaigns or Buddhist themes.
xa: **Kanchi** murals are in the **Kamakshi** and **Varadaraja** temples.
**Lepakshi** shows **Parvati Parinayamu** — the Shiva-Parvati wedding.

123.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Vijayanagara mural painting?
o: Mineral pigments such as ochre, green, black and white were used
The figures lacked movement and were rigidly proportioned
The paintings were executed on lime plaster
Bold dark outlines and flat colours were characteristic
123.x: Vijayanagara murals had elongated figures and energetic movement, so the claim that they lacked movement is false.

123.s: Who wrote A Survey of Painting in the Deccan, identified as a key source for the study of Vijayanagara painting?
123.x: Stella Kramrisch wrote A Survey of Painting in the Deccan.
123.tq: Test the author–work association directly, a common literature and art-history pattern.
xs: **Stella Kramrisch** wrote **A Survey of Painting in the Deccan** — option **(3)**.
**Percy Brown** described Vijayanagara architecture as the **"matured state of the Dravidian tradition"**.
xa: The peak of the Vijayanagara school: **Lepakshi** murals.
Technique: **mineral pigments** on **lime plaster**.

123.s: Where are the wall murals of Parvati Parinayamu and Tripurasura Samharam found?
123.x: Lepakshi's walls show Shiva themes such as Parvati Parinayamu and Tripurasura Samharam.

123.s: The remains of the Vijayanagar empire can be found in
123.x: The ruins of the Vijayanagara capital are at Hampi on the Tungabhadra (UNESCO 1986). Bijapur, Golconda and Ahmadnagar were sultanate capitals; Baroda was the Gaekwads'.

123.s: The archaeologists have found that fortification under Vijayanagara Empire was very well planned. The agricultural fields were incorporated within the fortified areas. Which one of the following is the correct reason for such planning?
o: The fields could be irrigated under all conditions.
To have food supply even if invader block the area for several months
The rulers found it easy to keep an account of land revenue
The granaries were under the control of the rulers.
123.src: Social and Cultural History of A.P and Welfare Programmes 20
123.x: NCERT notes that the walls enclosed fields and gardens so the city could feed itself if besieged for months. Irrigation, revenue accounts and royal granaries were not the reason.

123.s: Why did the Vijayanagara rulers build a massive number of temples in honour of many gods and cults? Choose the correct option.
o: To legitimise their authority through association with divinities in the shrines.
To announce to general public that they were religious and good rulers.
To encourage the people to have high moral values.
To take a stand against any anti-social activity.
123.src: Social and Culture History & Welfare Programmes paper 2019
123.x: NCERT explains temple building as a way for rulers to claim authority by association with the deities; the kings ruled on behalf of Virupaksha.

123.s: What was known as the 'Athens of Vijayanagara'?
o: Present Bangalore, Kolar and Chittoor districts
Valley areas around the Virupaksha temple
123.x: The app notes (from the source book) give the valley around the Virupaksha temple at Hampi as the 'Athens of Vijayanagara'. The other regions are provinces of the empire, not this cultural centre.

123.s: Ruins of which of the following represent the old capital of Vijayanagara?
123.x: The ruins of the Vijayanagara capital are at Hampi on the Tungabhadra (UNESCO 1986). Bijapur, Golconda and Ahmadnagar were sultanate capitals; Baroda was the Gaekwads'.

123.s: The remains of Vijayanagara empire are found in -:
123.x: The ruins of the Vijayanagara capital are at Hampi on the Tungabhadra (UNESCO 1986). Bijapur, Golconda and Ahmadnagar were sultanate capitals; Baroda was the Gaekwads'.

123.s: The capital of Vijaynagar Empire was situated on the bank of which river?
123.x: Hampi, the capital, is on the southern bank of the Tungabhadra. The Narmada, Godavari and Bhima are elsewhere.

123.s: The ruins of the ancient city of Hampi- capital of Vijayanagara is located in which present day Indian state?
123.x: Hampi lies in Vijayanagara district of Karnataka. Haryana, Bihar and Telangana are wrong.

123.s: Many grand temples, such as the Veerabhadra Temple at Lepakshi, were built by rulers of contemporary Andhra Pradesh. What was a major factor that made such constructions possible?
o: Possessing sufficient financial assets, they sourced raw materials from faraway places.
The geography of the Deccan Plateau provided easy access to raw materials like stone locally
Every temple was built only after winning wars with neighboring kingdoms
Many Shiva temples were entirely made from stone sourced from Mount Kailash
123.src: APPSC Assistant Tribal Welfare Officer in A.P. Tribal Welfar
123.x: The Deccan plateau's granite gave builders easy local access to stone. Distant sourcing, wars or stone from Kailash were not the factor.

123.s: In which year was the 'Group of Monuments at Hampi' inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
123.x: The Group of Monuments at Hampi became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1986.
123.tq: Test the year directly with closely spaced numerical distractors.
xs: The **Group of Monuments at Hampi** became a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** in **1986** — option **(3)**.
Its temples include **Virupaksha**, **Vittala** and **Hazara Rama**; the other years are distractors.
xa: The **Vittala stone chariot** is on the reverse of the **₹50 note** (Mahatma Gandhi (New) series).
Virupaksha is the **first and largest** temple of Hampi.

123.s: Which Hampi monument appears on the reverse of the Rs 50 note (Mahatma Gandhi New series)?
123.x: The Vittala stone chariot is on the reverse of the Rs 50 note.

123.s: Around which Hampi temple did the area called the 'Athens of Vijayanagara' lie?
123.x: The area around the Virupaksha temple, the first and largest temple of Hampi, was called the 'Athens of Vijayanagara'.

123.s: In which present-day district of Karnataka is Hampi located?
123.x: Hampi, on the southern bank of the Tungabhadra, is in Vijayanagara district of Karnataka.

123.s: According to Domingo Paes, why did the walls of Vijayanagara enclose fields and gardens?
o: To separate the royal centre from temples
123.x: Paes noted that the walls enclosed agricultural tracts so the city could withstand sieges.

123.s:
Consider the following statements in respect of 'Yaganti Temple'

a. Yaganti is located in the Kurnool District in the state of Andhra Pradesh.

b. The three famous caves situated around the temple are the Agastya Cave, the Venkateswara Cave and the Veera Brahmam Cave.

c. The Nandi (Bullock, Lord Shiva's) idol in front of the temple is continuously increasing its size.
Which of the above statements are incorrect?
123.src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
123.at: None of the above (all three statements are correct)
123.x:
Yaganti was in Kurnool district — now Nandyal district (formed 4 April 2022) (nandyal.ap.gov.in)
All three statements are commonly accepted: Yaganti (Uma Maheswara temple) has the Agastya, Venkateswara and Veera Brahmam caves and a Nandi said to be growing. The temple was in Kurnool district (now Nandyal district).

123.s: Who built the Ekambaranatha temple in Kanchipuram?
123.x: The temple is of Pallava origin, but its great southern Rajagopuram and mandapas were built by Krishnadevaraya in 1509, the builder the question expects. 'Pallava Nandivarman' is not credited with it; the Gangai nayakas and Sriranga III are not builders.

123.s: After the bifurcation of Andhra Pradesh, Badrachalam Sri Rama temple has become part of Telangana which is the official temple for the celebration of 'Sri Ramanavami' for Andhra Pradesh. Where is this temple located?
123.src: APPSC General Studies & Mental Ability (Common Paper: Hostel
123.x: The Kodandarama temple at Ontimitta (Vontimitta), Kadapa district, became AP's official Sri Rama Navami venue after Bhadrachalam went to Telangana.

123.s: 'Chintala Venkata Ramana Temple' is in this place
123.x: The Chintala Venkataramana temple is at Tadipatri (Anantapur), built by the Pemmasani Nayakas. Lepakshi, Penugonda and Chandragiri are wrong.

123.s: According to art critics, the gopurams of which temple in Andhra are more beautiful than the Vithalalaya gopurams of Hampi?
123.x: Art critics rate the gopurams of the Tadipatri temples above those of Hampi's Vitthala temple. Ahobilam, Srisailam and Lepakshi are known for other features.

123.s: According to art critics, the gopurams of which temple in Andhra are more beautiful than the Vittala Temple gopurams of Hampi?
123.x: Art critics rate the gopurams of the Tadipatri temples above those of Hampi's Vitthala temple. Ahobilam, Srisailam and Lepakshi are known for other features.

123.s: According to art critics, the gopuras of which temple in Andhra excel in their beauty over those of Hampi Vithalalaya?
123.x: Art critics rate the gopurams of the Tadipatri temples above those of Hampi's Vitthala temple. Ahobilam, Srisailam and Lepakshi are known for other features.

123.s: Where is 'Chintala Venkataramana Temple' located?
123.x: The Chintala Venkataramana temple is at Tadipatri (Anantapur), built by the Pemmasani Nayakas. Lepakshi, Penugonda and Chandragiri are wrong.

123.s: Tadipatri, a centre of the Vijayanagara style, lies in which district?
123.x: Tadipatri is in Anantapur; Lepakshi is in Sri Sathya Sai district.
xa: **Percy Brown** called it the **"matured state of the Dravidian tradition"**, blending **Chola, Hoysala, Pandya and Chalukya** styles.
It spread in Andhra through courts at **Kondavidu, Udayagiri, Chandragiri, Vinukonda**.
New feature: **secular buildings inside temple premises**.

123.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Largest monolithic Nandi in India — Lepakshi
Gopurams surpassing those of Hampi Vittala temple — Chandragiri
123.x: The gopurams said by art critics to surpass those of Hampi's Vittala temple are at Tadipatri, not Chandragiri. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
123.tq: Find the single wrong site association among familiar monument features.
xs: **Gopurams surpassing Hampi's Vittala temple — Chandragiri** is wrongly matched — so option **(4)** is the answer.
Art critics say the gopurams of **Tadipatri** surpass those of the **Vittala** temple (APPSC G2 **2019**).
**Musical pillars** and the **stone chariot** belong to the **Vittala** temple, Hampi — correct.
The **largest monolithic Nandi** and the **hanging pillar** are both at **Lepakshi** — correct.
xa: Tadipatri's two temples: **Chintala Venkataramana** (Vishnu) and **Bugga Ramalingeswara** (Shiva), in **Anantapur**.
The Vittala Ranga mandapa has **56** musical pillars that give notes when tapped.
**Chandragiri fort and Raja Mahal** were an Aravidu capital under **Venkatapati Raya II**.
**Lepakshi** also has the finest Vijayanagara-school **murals** ("pictorial inscriptions").

123.s: With whom is the mukha mandapam of the Mallikarjuna Temple at Srisailam associated?
123.x: Harihara II is associated with the mukha mandapam at Srisailam; Saluva Narasimha began the Vijayanagara patronage of Tirupati.
xa: ⚠ **Mukha mandapam** = Harihara II; **prakaram** = Shanti Lingayya; **Kalyana mandapam** = Krishnadevaraya.
**Kadiri** was an early centre of the **Narasimha** cult.

123.s: At which place are the temples credited to the Pemmasani Nayakas?
123.x: The Pemmasani Nayakas are credited with the Tadipatri temples, not Tirupati.
xa: Aravidu feudatory **Anantaraju** built the **steps to Tirumala** and the **Govindaraja** temple.
Krishnadevaraya added the Tirumala **Kalyana mandapam** and bronze statues of himself with his queens.

123.s: In which year did the gali gopuram at Srikalahasti collapse?
123.x: Krishnadevaraya renovated Srikalahasti; its gali gopuram collapsed in 2010.
xa: Srikalahasti's presiding deity: the **Vayu linga**.
**Kadiri** was an early centre of the **Narasimha** cult.

123.s: Which temple is noted for four entrance gates facing the four directions?
123.x: Among these, Srisailam is noted for its four entrance gates facing the four directions.
123.tq: Use the architectural exception clue and distinguish it from other Andhra temple sites.
xs: The temple noted for **four entrance gates facing the four directions** is at **Srisailam** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Tadipatri** is noted for gopurams that surpass Hampi's **Vittala** gopurams.
**Ahobilam** has the **Upper and Lower Narasimha** temples; **Lepakshi** has the **hanging pillar**.
xa: Srisailam (**Mallikarjuna**): **Mukha mandapam** by **Harihara II**.
Srisailam's sculptured **prakaram** was built by **Shanti Lingayya** in Krishnadevaraya's time.
⚠ Mukha mandapam = **Harihara II**; prakaram = **Shanti Lingayya**; Tirumala Kalyana mandapam = **Krishnadevaraya**.

123.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Chintala Venkataramana and Bugga Ramalingeswara — Tadipatri
Upper and Lower Narasimha Temples — Kadiri
123.x: The Chintala Venkataramana and Bugga Ramalingeswara temples are at Tadipatri. The Upper and Lower Narasimha temples are at Ahobilam (not Kadiri), Mallikarjuna is the deity of Srisailam (not Tirupati), and Venkateswara is the deity of Tirupati (not Ahobilam).
123.tq: Use location-based elimination among closely related Andhra temples.
xs: **Chintala Venkataramana** and **Bugga Ramalingeswara** are at **Tadipatri** — option **(1)**.
**Upper and Lower Narasimha** temples are at **Ahobilam**; **Mallikarjuna** is at **Srisailam**; **Venkateswara** at **Tirupati**.
xa: Art critics rate Tadipatri gopurams **above the Vittala gopurams** of Hampi (APPSC **2019**).
Tadipatri also has **Ubattu Shilpalu** (high relief) and a painting of **Vatapatra Shayi**.

123.s: Who is the presiding deity of the Ahobilam temples?
123.x: Ahobilam's Upper and Lower temples are dedicated to Narasimha.

123.s: The Srikalahasti temple enshrines which linga?
123.x: Srikalahasti is the Vayu linga shrine.

123.s: Who built the Chintala Venkataramana temple at Tadipatri?
123.x: Pemmasani Timmanayudu built it in the mid-16th century.

123.s: Kadiri, an early centre of the Narasimha cult, has a temple of which deity?
123.x: Kadiri's temple is dedicated to Narasimha.

123.s: Where are the high-relief sculpture (Ubattu Shilpalu) and the painting of Vatapatra Shayi found?
123.x: Tadipatri has Ubattu Shilpalu and the painting of Vatapatra Shayi.

123.s: Where is the Bugga Ramalingeswara temple located?
123.x: Bugga Ramalingeswara is at Tadipatri, credited to the Pemmasani Nayakas.

123.s: In which district is the Ontimitta Kodandarama temple located?
123.x: The Vijayanagara-era Kodandarama temple of Ontimitta is in Kadapa district.

123.s: Which temple is the venue of Andhra Pradesh's official Sri Rama Navami celebrations?
123.x: Ontimitta Kodandarama temple, linked with Pothana, is the venue of AP's official Sri Rama Navami; Bhadrachalam is now in Telangana.

123.s: In March 2026, inscriptions of Achyutaraya (1534 CE) were found on a 50-ft monolithic pillar of which temple?
123.x: The 1534 CE inscriptions were found on the 50-ft monolithic pillar of the Somapalayam Chennakesava temple in Annamayya district.

123.s: With whom was the sculptured prakaram at Srisailam associated?
o: Shanti Lingayya during the time of Krishnadevaraya
123.x: Shanti Lingayya constructed the sculptured prakaram at Srisailam during the reign of Krishnadevaraya.
123.tq: Avoid the ruler–builder swap by identifying both the individual and the period.
xs: The Srisailam sculptured **prakaram** was built by **Shanti Lingayya**, in **Krishnadevaraya's** time — option **(4)**.
**Harihara II** built the **Mukha mandapam**; **Anantaraju** built the **steps to Tirumala**.
xa: Srisailam: **four entrance gates** facing the four directions.
Its deity: **Mallikarjuna (Shiva)**.

123.s: With whom are the steps to Tirumala and the Govindaraja temple associated?
123.x: They were associated with Anantaraju; Krishnadevaraya added the Kalyana mandapam, outer prakara and bronze statues.
xa: The queens installed idols at **Tirumala**.
Tirupati developed from **Saluva Narasimha**, expanded by Krishnadevaraya and the **Aravidus**.

123.s: To whom are the Tirumala Kalyana mandapam and the bronze statues of the king with Chinnadevi and Tirumaladevi credited?
123.x: Krishnadevaraya added these at Tirumala; Harihara II built the Srisailam mukha mandapam.

123.s:
Consider the following statements about Vijayanagara additions at Srisailam and Tirupati:
1. The Srisailam mukha mandapam is credited to Harihara II.
2. The sculptured prakaram at Srisailam is credited to Shanti Lingayya.
3. The steps to Tirumala are credited to Krishnadevaraya.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
123.x: The mukha mandapam is Harihara II's and the prakaram Shanti Lingayya's; the steps to Tirumala are credited to the Aravidu feudatory Anantaraju.

123.s: The Indo-Saracenic style of architecture is depicted in one of the buildings of Vijayanagaram rulers. Name the Building?
123.src: APPSC Asst. BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Mains Paper-II 2017
123.x: The Lotus Mahal at Hampi, built by Krishnadevaraya 'in Indo-Arabic style', shows the Indo-Islamic (Indo-Saracenic) arches and domes. The Vitthala and Hazara Rama temples are Dravidian; Mahamandapa is a temple hall.

123.s: Who got the monumental Rayagopurams in front of the temples at Hampi, Tiruvannamalai, Chidambaram, Sri Rangam, Tirupati etc constructed?
123.x: Krishnadevaraya built the Raya gopurams at Hampi, Tiruvannamalai, Chidambaram, Srirangam, Tirupati and Kalahasti. Vidyaranya was a sage, Harihara the founder, Rajaraja a Chola.

123.s: Building 'Kalyana Mandapas' was a notable feature in the temple construction in the kingdom of
123.x: Kalyana mandapas for the divine marriage are a hallmark of Vijayanagara temples, with Raya gopurams. Chalukya, Chandela and Rashtrakuta temples do not have them.

123.s: Author of "Sangita Suryodayam"?
123.x: Sangita Suryodayam was written by Bandaru Lakshminarayana, court musician of Krishnadevaraya. Krishnadevaraya, Rama Raya and Ramabhadramba wrote other works.

123.s: Which musical instrument gained prominence during the Vijayanagara Empire?
123.x: The veena was the chief instrument of Vijayanagara court music - treatises such as Sangita Suryodaya and the Carnatic tradition of Vidyaranya's Sangita Sara centre on it. Mridangam, tambura and cymbals were accompaniments.

123.s: What was the 'kalyana mandapa' in Vijayanagara temple architecture?
o: Hall of composite pillars with yalis
123.x: The kalyana mandapa was the marriage hall; the Raya gopuram was the towering gateway and the Amman shrine the goddess's shrine.
xa: Example of an Amman shrine: **Hazara Rama**.
Krishnadevaraya built the Tirumala **Kalyana mandapam**.

123.s: Which statement regarding Vijayanagara secular architecture is correct?
o: The period introduced secular buildings inside temple premises.
The period used only wooden structures for royal buildings.
The period excluded all Indo-Islamic architectural influence.
Secular structures were confined exclusively to forts outside temple areas.
123.x: The Vijayanagara period introduced secular buildings within temple premises, while also showing Indo-Islamic influence in structures such as the Lotus Mahal and Huzur Daftar.
123.tq: Reject absolute exclusions and identify the precise architectural development.
xs: The period introduced **secular buildings inside temple premises** — option **(1)**.
Secular buildings show **Indo-Islamic** (Lotus Mahal) and **Indo-Persian** (Huzur Daftar) influence, so option 3 is wrong.
xa: Pillared corridors were also added to older temples.
**Chandragiri Raja Mahal** blends **Hindu** and **Indo-Saracenic** elements.

123.s: What is the towering gateway that dwarfs the central shrine in Vijayanagara architecture called?
123.x: The Raya gopuram is the towering gateway that dwarfs the central shrine.

123.s: What is a separate goddess shrine in a Vijayanagara temple complex, as at Hazara Rama, called?
123.x: The Amman shrine is the separate goddess shrine, seen at the Hazara Rama temple.

123.s: What are the thousand-pillared halls with carved composite pillars in Vijayanagara temples called?
123.x: Sahasra Stambha Mandapas are thousand-pillared halls with carved composite pillars.

123.s: Who described Vijayanagara architecture as the 'matured state of the Dravidian tradition'?
123.x: Percy Brown called it the matured state of the Dravidian tradition; Kramrisch surveyed Deccan painting.

123.s:
Consider the following statements about the Vijayanagara style:
1. Secular buildings were raised inside temple premises.
2. Pillared corridors were added to older temples.
3. The Ekapaadam was a Chola-type single pillar.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
123.x: Secular buildings in temple premises and added pillared corridors were new; the Ekapaadam was a Hoysala-type pillar.

123.s: With which ruler are the Mahanavami Dibba and the Lotus (Padma) Mahal at Hampi associated?
123.x: Krishnadevaraya's building at Hampi included the Ugra Narasimha, Hanuman statue, monolithic Ganesha, Mahanavami Dibba and Lotus Mahal.
xa: He added Virupaksha's central hall and **eastern gopuram (1510)**.
He installed the **Bala Krishna** idol from **Udayagiri**.

123.s: By what other names is the Lotus Mahal at Hampi known?
123.x: The Lotus Mahal is also called Chitrangi or Padma Mahal.
123.tq: Discriminate between alternative names of closely related Hampi structures.
xs: The **Lotus Mahal** is also called **Chitrangi** (Chitrangana) or **Padma Mahal** — option **(3)**.
**Maharani Snanavatika** = Queen's Bath; **Huzur Daftar** = **Diwan Khana**; **Mahanavami Dibba** = **Dasara Dibba**.
xa: It is lotus-shaped with domes in **Indo-Islamic (Indo-Arabic)** style.
The **Elephant stables** and **Queen's Bath** stand nearby in the zenana area.

123.s: What was the Huzur Daftar, or Diwan Khana, at Vijayanagara?
o: Stepped tank in the royal enclosure
Council chamber in Indo-Persian style with 40 pillars
Temple hall for divine marriage with 56 musical pillars
Royal bath with a lotus-shaped dome
123.x: Huzur Daftar or Diwan Khana was a council chamber in Indo-Persian style and had 40 pillars.
123.tq: Use the building–function–style–number combination to eliminate partial matches.
xs: The **Huzur Daftar (Diwan Khana)** was a **council chamber** in **Indo-Persian** style with **40 pillars** — option **(2)**.
**56 musical pillars** belong to the **Vittala** temple; the **lotus-shaped** domed building is the **Lotus Mahal**.
xa: The stepped tank is a symmetrical stone tank in the royal enclosure.
⚠ Lotus Mahal = **Indo-Islamic**; Huzur Daftar = **Indo-Persian**.

123.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Lotus Mahal — Lotus-shaped structure with domes and Indo-Islamic influence
Huzur Daftar — Stepped tank in the royal enclosure
Queen's Bath — Council chamber with 40 pillars

126.s: ____ was the adventurous ruler of Vijayanagara who followed the policy of playing one Sultan against another which eventually led to their joining hands with each other.
126.src: Social and Cultural History of A.P and Welfare Programmes 20
126.x: Aliya Rama Raya, regent of Sadasiva, played one Deccan Sultan against another until they united against him at Talikota in 1565.

126.s: Who was the king of Vijayanagara during the Rakshasa Tangadi (Tallikota) battle of 1565?
126.x: Sadasiva Raya was the king at Talikota (1565); Aliya Rama Raya was only his regent, and Tirumala Raya founded the Aravidu line afterwards.

126.s: ............ The Vijayanagara Empire came to an end in the Battle of Talikota.
126.x: Vijayanagara's power ended at Talikota (Rakshasa Tangadi) in 1565.

126.s: Son-in-law of Krishnadevaraya?
126.x: Aliya ('son-in-law') Rama Raya was Krishnadevaraya's son-in-law and the regent who led Vijayanagara at Talikota (1565). Achyuta Raya was Krishnadevaraya's half-brother.

126.s: In which year did the Talikota war take place?
126.x: The Battle of Talikota was fought in January 1565 (23 January in most books).

126.s: The Battle of Talikota was fought in –
126.x: Talikota was fought in 1565; 1526 is the First Battle of Panipat and 1576 Haldighati.

126.s: The Battle of Talikota was fought between
o: Vijayanagara and combined forces of Bijapur, Ahmadnagar and Golconda.
126.x: Vijayanagara fought the combined forces of Bijapur, Ahmadnagar and Golconda (with Bidar). The Bahmani kingdom had already broken up, so option 2 is wrong.

126.s: In January 1565, the Battle of Talikota was fought between-
o: The Vijayanagara Empire and the Deccani Sultanates
The Mughal Empire and the Vijayanagara Empire
The Marathas and the Deccani Sultanates
The Bahmani Sultanate and the Vijayanagara Empire
126.x: Talikota (January 1565) was fought between Vijayanagara and the Deccan Sultanates (Bijapur, Ahmadnagar, Golconda, Bidar) – not the Mughals, Marathas or the Bahmanis.

126.s: The famous battle held in 1565 is –
126.x: The famous battle of 1565 is Talikota; Panipat I was 1526, Khanwa 1527 and Panipat II 1556.

126.s: Who fought the Battle of Rakshashi-Thangadi (Talikota, 1565 A.D.) which ended the glory of the Vijayanagar empire?
o: Ramaraya and the Imadshahis of Berar
The Adilshahis of Bijapur and Ramaraya
Veeranarasimha and the Nizamshahis of Ahmednagar
Ramaraya and Nizam Shah of Ahmednagar
126.x: The NextGen Rocket Sheet records Rakshasi-Tangadi as fought 'between Adil Shahis of Bijapur and Ramaraya'. Berar's Imad Shahis stayed out, Veeranarasimha belongs to 1505, and the Nizam Shah of Ahmadnagar was only one of four allied sultans (he beheaded Rama Raya).

126.s: Vijayanagara Empire was destroyed in Tallikota war of ________.
126.x: Vijayanagara was defeated at Tallikota in 1565 and Hampi was sacked.

126.s: In 1565 the Vijayanagar empire fell as a result of the war
126.x: The Vijayanagara empire's power was broken at the Battle of Tallikota (Rakshasi-Tangadi), 1565, by the Deccan Sultans; the capital then moved to Penugonda.

126.s: In the year 1565 the battle of Tallikota was fought between them?
o: The kings of Vijayanagara and the Sultanate of Golconda
Vijayanagar kings and Kondaveeti Reddy kings
Deccan Sultans and Kondaveeti Reddy Kings
126.x: Tallikota (1565) was fought between Vijayanagara under Rama Raya and the combined Deccan Sultans (Bijapur, Ahmadnagar, Golconda, Bidar) – not Golconda alone and not the Kondaveedu Reddis, who had gone long before.

126.s: Which dynasty ruled Berar, the Deccan Sultanate that stayed out of the alliance against Vijayanagara at Talikota?
126.x: Berar was ruled by the Imad Shahis and stayed out; Bijapur, Ahmadnagar, Golconda and Bidar formed the alliance.
xa: **Ibrahim Qutb Shah** of Golconda organised the alliance.
Vijayanagara faced the **Deccan Sultanates**, not the Bahmani kingdom (G1 **2018**).

126.s: From which Sultanate was Jagadeva Rao, whose shelter by Rama Raya helped provoke the Deccan coalition, a rebel?
126.x: Rama Raya sheltered Jagadeva Rao, a rebel from Golconda, one of the causes of the coalition.
xa: Marriage links: **Bibi Jamal** married Ibrahim; **Chand Bibi** married Ali Adil.
**Ferishta** also alleges religious insults.
Rama Raya **sacked Ahmadnagar** in **1557-63**.

126.s: Which region did Rama Raya acquire in 1546-47 by backing Ahmadnagar against Bijapur and Bidar?
126.x: In 1546-47 Rama Raya supported Ahmadnagar against Bijapur and Bidar and took the Raichur doab.
xa: This **divide-and-rule** diplomacy is listed as a cause that **united the Sultans** against him.
Rama Raya had earlier served under **Golconda** and the **Bahmanis**.
He also sheltered **Jagadeva Rao**, a rebel from Golconda.

126.s: Who was the key organiser of the Deccan Sultanates' alliance that fought at Talikota (1565)?
126.x: Ibrahim Qutb Shah of Golconda was the key organiser of the coalition.
xa: **Robert Sewell** called it **Talikota**; **Fr. Heras** and **Nilakanta Sastri** called it **Rakshasi-Tangadi**.
Date: **23 January 1565**; some notes give **26 January**.
**Ali Adil Shah** ruled **Bijapur**; **Ali Barid Shah** ruled **Bidar**.
⚠ **Berar** (Imad Shahi) stayed out of the battle.

126.s: Which statement about the aftermath of Talikota is correct?
o: Sewell held that the capital suffered no destruction.
The sack is universally held to have wiped out Vijayanagara culture.
Tirumala wrote the account of the sack in 1570.
Sewell called the sacked city a 'graveyard', a view that may be exaggerated.
126.x: Sewell used the expression 'graveyard' for the sacked capital, though that assessment may be exaggerated.
xa: Sewell wrote **A Forgotten Empire** (**1900**).
**Caesar Frederick** gave an eyewitness account in **1567**.
Nayaka courts later spread **Raya gopurams** and **kalyana mandapas** across Andhra.

126.s: Which of the following pairs (Sultanate – Ruler at Talikota) is correctly matched?
126.x: Bijapur was ruled by Ali Adil Shah. Ahmadnagar was under Hussain Nizam Shah, Golconda under Ibrahim Qutb Shah and Bidar under Ali Barid Shah.
xa: **Ibrahim Qutb Shah** was the key organiser of the alliance.
**Hussain Nizam Shah** beheaded Rama Raya.
**Berar** (Imad Shahi) stayed out.

126.s: Who among the following was married to Chand Bibi among the marriage alliances before Talikota?
126.x: Chand Bibi married Ali Adil Shah, while Bibi Jamal married Ibrahim Qutb Shah.
xa: Rama Raya sheltered **Jagadeva Rao**, a rebel from Golconda.
In **1546-47** he took the **Raichur doab**.

126.s: For how long was Hampi looted after the Battle of Talikota?
126.x: Hampi was looted for about six months; the damage was severe but not total.
xa: Sewell's **"graveyard"** account may exaggerate.
Golconda gained **Kondavidu and Machilipatnam** + coastal tracts.
Sadashiva and Tirumala fled to **Penukonda**.

126.s: Which historian named the Battle of 1565 'Rakshasi-Tangadi'?
126.x: Heras called it Rakshasi-Tangadi; Sewell used Talikota and Sherwani used Bannihatti.

126.s: Who beheaded Aliya Rama Raya at the Battle of Talikota?
126.x: Hussain Nizam Shah of Ahmadnagar beheaded Rama Raya; Ibrahim Qutb Shah was the alliance's main organiser.

126.s:
Consider the following statements about Aliya Rama Raya:
1. He ruled as regent of Sadasiva Raya.
2. Between 1557 and 1563 he backed Bijapur and razed Ahmadnagar.
3. He gave shelter to Jagadeva Rao, a rebel of Golconda.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
126.x: All three are correct: Rama Raya was Sadasiva's regent, razed Ahmadnagar with Bijapur in 1557-63 and sheltered Jagadeva Rao.

126.s: Who called the Vijayanagara capital after Talikota a 'graveyard'?
126.x: Robert Sewell called the city a 'graveyard', a view that may be exaggerated.

126.s: In which year was the Battle of Talikota (Rakshasi-Tangadi) fought?
126.x: The Battle of Talikota was fought on 23 January 1565 between Vijayanagara and the Deccan Sultanates.

126.s: Aliya Rama Raya, the regent at the time of Talikota, was the son-in-law of which ruler?
126.x: Aliya ('son-in-law') Rama Raya was the son-in-law of Krishnadevaraya.

126.s: Where did Sadasiva and Tirumala flee after the defeat at Talikota?
126.x: They fled to Penukonda; Chandragiri became a capital later, under Venkata II.
xa: Capital order: **Penukonda (1570) → Chandragiri → Vellore (1600)**.
After **1565**, the empire's centre moved into AP.
**Sriranga Raya I** later lost **Kondaveedu** to Ibrahim Qutb Shah.

126.s: The Aravidu Dynasty ruled from which one of the following place?
126.src: Social and Cultural History of A.P and Welfare Programmes 20
126.x: After Talikota the Aravidu dynasty ruled from Penukonda (later Chandragiri and Vellore); Bijapur, Golconda and Ahmadnagar were the capitals of the Sultanates that defeated Vijayanagara.

126.s: Which became the second capital of the Vijayanagara Empire after 1565 AD?
126.x: After Talikota (1565) Sadasiva and Tirumala moved to Penukonda, which became the second capital (later Chandragiri and Vellore).

126.s: What was the capital of Vijayanagara after the Battle of Tallikota?
126.x: After Tallikota Tirumala Raya moved to Penugonda and founded the Aravidu dynasty there. Chandragiri became the capital later, under Venkatapati II.

126.s: Which became the second capital of the Vijayanagara Empire after 1565 AD?
126.x: After Talikota and the sack of Hampi, Penukonda became the capital; Chandragiri and Vellore followed later.

126.s: Capital of Araveeti dynasty?
126.x: The Araviti (Aravidu) dynasty's capital was Penukonda, where Tirumala Raya founded it.

126.s: The Vijayanagara ruler who permitted Jesuits to build churches at Nellore and Chandragiri was
126.x: Venkatapati Raya II (1585-1614) let the Jesuits build churches at Nellore and Chandragiri; the Jesuit mission reached his court at Chandragiri in 1598.

126.s: Which Vijayanagara rulers allowed the Jesuits to build churches in Nellore and Chandragiri?
126.x: Venkatapati Raya II allowed the Jesuits to build churches at Nellore and Chandragiri – not Devaraya II, Tirumala Raya I or Sadasiva Raya.

126.s: When Raja Wodeyar founded the kingdom of Mysore, who was the ruler of the Vijayanagar Empire?
126.x: Raja Wodeyar took Srirangapatna in 1610 and founded the Mysore kingdom in the reign of Venkata II (1585-1614).

126.s: When Raja Wodeyar founded the Kingdom of Mysore, who was the ruler of the Vijayanagara Empire?
126.x: Raja Wodeyar founded the Mysore kingdom (Srirangapatna, 1610) under Venkata II; Sadasiva and Tirumala ruled before 1572.

126.s: Vijayanagara kingdom completely disappeared with this battle
126.x: After Talikota (1565) the Aravidus survived at Penugonda and Chandragiri; the civil-war Battle of Toppur (Topuru, 1616) broke up what was left, after which the empire disintegrated completely. Penugonda and Chandragiri were capitals, not the decisive battles.

126.s: In order of succession, which ruling dynasty of Vijayanagara was the Aravidu dynasty?
126.x: The Aravidu dynasty was the fourth dynasty of Vijayanagara and ruled from 1570 to 1680 with seven rulers.
xa: Some notes date the empire's end to **1646**.
Founder **Tirumala** shifted the capital to **Penukonda** in **1570**.
Greatest ruler: **Venkatapati Raya II** (**1585-1614**).

126.s: Who founded the Aravidu dynasty and was crowned at Penukonda in 1570?
126.x: Tirumala Raya founded the Aravidu dynasty and was crowned at Penukonda in 1570.
126.tq: Match the founder with his accession place and year.
xs: **Tirumala Raya** founded the Aravidu dynasty and was crowned at **Penukonda** in **1570** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Sriranga Raya I** (**1572-85**) succeeded him; **Venkatapati Raya II** (**1585-1614**) was the greatest.
**Ramadeva** (**1616-30**) fought the **Battle of Toppur**.
xa: Tirumala was crowned at the age of **90**.
He wrote a commentary on the **Gita Govinda**; **Vasucharitra** was dedicated to him.
⚠ **Tirumala Raya** = Aravidu founder; **Tirumala Nayaka** = Madurai.

126.s:
Consider the following statements about the Battle of Toppur:

xs: Only statement **1** is correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: **Toppur (1616)** is called the **"second Talikota"**.
Statement 2 is wrong: **Jagga Raya** was killed at Toppur; **Mir Jumla** later defeated **Sriranga III** at **Vandavasi (1642)**.
xa: Toppur was won by **Velugoti Yachama Nayaka** and **Raghunatha of Tanjore**.
It was fought in **Ramadeva**'s reign (**1616-30**).
Jagga Raya had killed **Sriranga II** (**1614**).

126.s:
Consider the following statements about Sriranga Raya III:
1. He was the last ruler of the Aravidu dynasty.
2. He was defeated at Vandavasi (1642) by Ibrahim Qutb Shah.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
126.x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: he was defeated at Vandavasi by Mir Jumla of Golconda. So 1 only (A).
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: **Sriranga Raya III** (**1643-80**) was the **last** Aravidu ruler.
Statement 2 is wrong: he was defeated at **Vandavasi (1642)** by **Mir Jumla** of Golconda, not Ibrahim Qutb Shah.
xa: He later held **Penukonda** as a chieftain; his death in **1680** ended the empire.
Mir Jumla also melted temple idols into cannon at **Gandikota** (**1657**).
**Ibrahim Qutb Shah** organised the Talikota alliance.

126.s: Which Vijayanagara ruler was called the 'Second Andhra Bhoja'?
126.x: Venkatapati Raya II was called the 'Second Andhra Bhoja' (and 'Second Krishnadevaraya').

126.s: Which pair of leaders won the Battle of Toppur in 1616?
o: Velugoti Yachama Nayaka and Raghunatha of Tanjore
Mir Jumla and Sriranga Raya III
Damarla Venkatadri Nayaka and Veerappa Nayaka

xs: **Velugoti Yachama Nayaka** and **Raghunatha of Tanjore** won **Toppur (1616)** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Jagga Raya** was killed there; it is called the **"second Talikota"**.
**Mir Jumla** defeated **Sriranga III** at **Vandavasi (1642)**, a different battle.
xa: Toppur came in **Ramadeva**'s reign (**1616-30**).
Jagga Raya had killed **Sriranga II** in **1614**.
**Tanjore** was founded by **Sevappa Nayaka**.

126.s: The Aravidu dynasty of Vijayanagara derived its name from which place?
126.x: The dynasty was named after Araviti, also called Aravidu, a village in Kurnool district.

xs: The Aravidu dynasty is named after **Araviti (Aravidu) village, Kurnool district** — so option **(2)** is correct.

**Gandikota** is where **Mir Jumla** melted temple idols into cannon (**1657**).

126.s: Which Aravidu ruler lost Kondaveedu to Ibrahim Qutb Shah?
126.x: Sriranga I (1572-85), eldest son of Tirumala, lost Kondaveedu to Ibrahim Qutb Shah.

126.x: Sriranga II was killed by Jagga Raya, who was himself killed at Toppur in 1616.

126.s: To which place did the Aravidu rulers move their capital in 1600?
126.x: The capitals shifted Hampi, Penukonda (1570), Chandragiri (Venkata II) and Vellore (1600).

Sher Shah minted **pure** gold and silver coins.
He restored the **Grand Trunk Road** (Sadak-e-Azam) from **Sonargaon** to the **Indus**.

128.s: Of which metal was Sher Shah's rupiya, weighing about 178 grains, made?
128.x: The rupiya was a silver coin of about 178 grains; the dam was copper and the mohur gold.

128.x: The mohur was gold, the rupiya silver and the dam copper.

128.s:
Consider the following statements about Sher Shah's sarais:
1. They served as dak-chowkis for relaying news and mail.
2. Market towns grew around them.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
128.x: Both are correct: sarais served as dak-chowkis with horses, and market towns grew around them.

128.x: The sarais served as dak-chowkis; market towns also grew around them.
xa: Dak-chowkis were post stations relaying news and mail, with **horses**.
The **Grand Trunk Road** ran from **Sonargaon** to the **Indus**.

128.s: Which route did Sher Shah's Sadak-e-Azam (Grand Trunk Road) cover?
128.x: The Sadak-e-Azam ran from Sonargaon in Bengal to the Indus; Agra-Burhanpur and Lahore-Multan were other Sur roads.

128.s: Besides the Sadak-e-Azam, which of the following roads was built by Sher Shah?
128.x: Sher Shah also built the Agra-Burhanpur, Agra-Jodhpur-Chittor and Lahore-Multan roads, with sarais at intervals.

128.s: Who among the following built or restored the Sadak-e-Azam, later known as the Grand Trunk Road?
128.x: Sher Shah built or restored the Sadak-e-Azam (Grand Trunk Road) and set up sarais along it.

128.s: Where is Mausoleum of Sher Shah ?
128.x: Sher Shah's mausoleum, an octagonal tomb in the middle of a tank, stands at Sasaram (Rohtas, Bihar).

128.s: Sher Shah was buried at –
128.x: Sher Shah died at Kalinjar in 1545 but was buried at Sasaram in Bihar, his father's jagir, where his tomb stands.

128.s: Where is Sher Shah's tomb located?
128.x: Sher Shah's tomb is at Sasaram in Rohtas district, Bihar - not Maner, Sitamarhi or Pavapuri.

128.s:
Which of the following monuments were built by Emperor Shershah?
1. Sasaram Tomb
2. Qila-e-Kuhna Mosque
3. Tomb of Sikandar
4. Jama Masjid
128.x: Sher Shah built his own tomb at Sasaram (completed by Islam Shah) and the Qila-i-Kuhna Mosque in Purana Qila (1541). The tomb at Sikandra is Akbar's and the Delhi Jama Masjid is Shah Jahan's: 1 and 2.

128.s: Who amongst the following got ‘Purana Quila’ of Delhi built in the present form?
128.x: Humayun began the citadel (Dinpanah), but the Purana Qila in its present form was built by Sher Shah Suri.

128.s: Who built the mosque "Qila-E-Kuhna" inside Purana Qila of Delhi
128.x: The Qila-i-Kuhna Mosque inside Purana Qila was built by Sher Shah in 1541, as was the Sher Mandal.

128.s: Which one of the following monument was constructed by Sher Shah?
128.x: Sher Shah built the Qila-i-Kuhna Mosque in Delhi (1541). Atala Masjid is Sharqi, Bara Sona Masjid is of the Bengal Sultans and Quwwat-ul-Islam is Aibak's.

128.s: Building of ‘Purana Qila’ in Delhi was constructed by
128.x: The Purana Qila was begun by Humayun as Dinpanah, but its present form is Sher Shah's work; Firuz Tughlaq, Ibrahim Lodi and Babur did not build it.

128.s: Which one of the following is a monument constructed by Sher Shah?
128.x: Qila-i-Kuhna Mosque in the Purana Qila, Delhi, was built by Sher Shah in 1541; the other three are pre-Mughal buildings of other rulers.

128.s: Building of ‘’Purana Qila’’ was constructed in Delhi by–
128.x: The Purana Qila, begun by Humayun, was given its present form by Sher Shah, who also built the Qila-i-Kuhna Mosque and Sher Mandal inside it.

128.s: Who is the author of the Humayun-nama?
128.x: The Humayun-nama was written by Humayun's sister Gulbadan Begum. Hamida Banu Begum was Humayun's wife and Akbar's mother; Abul Fazl wrote the Akbarnama; Babur wrote the Tuzuk-i-Baburi.
xs: The **Humayun-nama** was written by Humayun's sister **Gulbadan Begum** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Hamida Banu Begum** was Humayun's wife and **Akbar's** mother.
**Babur** wrote the **Tuzuk-i-Baburi**.
xa: Akbar was born at **Amarkot** (**1542**).
Humayun died in **January 1556** at the **Sher Mandal** library, **Purana Qila**.

128.s: In which year did Sher Shah build the Qila-e-Kuhna Mosque inside Purana Qila?
128.x: The Qila-e-Kuhna Mosque dates to 1541, after Chausa (1539) and before Sher Shah's death at Kalinjar (1545).
n: Sher Shah Suri invaded Kalinjar in 1531. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 137-138]
Humayun first invaded Chunar in 1532. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 137-138]
Humayun annexed Raisina Fort in 1535. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 137-138]
Sher Shah built the Qila-e-Kuhna Mosque inside Purana Qila in 1541. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 137-138]
Purana Qila is associated with Sher Shah Suri. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 137-138]

128.s: For what is Sher Shah's tomb at Sasaram notable?
o: a four-domed marble mausoleum in Agra
an octagonal tomb set in a tank
a circular tomb built inside the Purana Qila
128.x: The tomb at Sasaram is an octagonal monument surrounded by water in a tank.
128.tq: Use the distinctive architectural feature to distinguish the monument from other Sur structures.
xs: **Sher Shah's tomb** at **Sasaram** (Bihar) is an **octagonal tomb in a tank** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Rohtas fort** is in present-day **Pakistan**; the **Purana Qila** is in **Delhi**.
xa: Sher Shah rebuilt the **Purana Qila** (Dinpanah), begun by **Humayun**.
He built the **Qila-i-Kuhna mosque** inside it.
**Humayun's Tomb** is the first **garden tomb**, with a **double dome**.

128.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Purana Qila – Qila-e-Kuhna Mosque built inside it by Sher Shah
Kalinjar Fort – Sher Khan submitted to Humayun after its siege
Chunar Fort – Sher Shah died during its siege in 1545
Bhatkal Fort – Sher Khan submitted to Humayun after its siege
128.x: Sher Shah built the Qila-e-Kuhna Mosque inside Purana Qila. Sher Khan submitted after the siege of Chunar, Sher Shah died besieging Kalinjar, and Krishnadeva Raya let the Portuguese build at Bhatkal.
n: Chunar Fort is associated with Humayun. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 137-138]
Chunar Fort is associated with Sher Khan. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 137-138]
Kalinjar Fort is associated with Sher Shah Suri. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 137-138]
Raisina Fort is associated with Humayun. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 137-138]
Bhatkal Fort is associated with Krishnadeva Raya. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 137-138]
xa: Humayun first invaded **Chunar** in **1532**.
Sher Shah built the Qila-e-Kuhna Mosque in **1541**.
Purana Qila (**Dinpanah**) was begun by **Humayun** and rebuilt by **Sher Shah**.

128.s: Near which place is Rohtas Fort, begun by Sher Shah in 1541, located?
128.x: Rohtas Fort near Jhelum, Pakistan, was begun by Sher Shah in 1541 under Todar Mal.

128.s: Who built Humayun's Tomb in Delhi?
128.x: Bega Begum (Haji Begum) built Humayun's Tomb; Gulbadan Begum wrote the Humayun-nama.

128.s: Who was the architect of Humayun's Tomb?
128.x: Mirak Mirza Ghiyas designed Humayun's Tomb, built 1565-72.

128.s: Where is Balban's Tomb, with the first true arch in India, located?
128.x: Balban's Tomb is at Mehrauli, Delhi; Sasaram has Sher Shah's octagonal tomb.
xa: Balban's Tomb is the first in India in a **purely Indo-Islamic style**, with the **first true arch**.
Sher Shah's octagonal tomb in a tank at Sasaram was **completed** by **Islam Shah**.
Humayun's Tomb uses **red sandstone + white marble**.

128.s: Who began the citadel of Purana Qila (Dinpanah) in Delhi, which was later given its present form by Sher Shah?
128.x: Humayun began the Dinpanah citadel; Sher Shah gave the Purana Qila its present form.

128.s: Who completed Sher Shah's tomb at Sasaram?
128.x: Sher Shah began his octagonal tomb at Sasaram; his son Islam Shah completed it.

128.s: Under whose supervision was the Rohtas Fort near Jhelum begun by Sher Shah in 1541?
128.x: Rohtas Fort was begun in 1541 under Todar Mal, who later served Akbar.

128.s: Who built the tomb of Sikandar Lodi in Delhi?
128.x: Sikandar Lodi's tomb in Delhi was built by his son Ibrahim Lodi.

128.s: In which year was Humayun's Tomb in Delhi declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
128.x: Humayun's Tomb became a UNESCO site in 1993; Rohtas Fort followed in 1997.

128.s: In which year was Sher Shah's Rohtas Fort inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
128.x: Rohtas Fort near Jhelum, Pakistan, became a UNESCO site in 1997.

128.s: From which place were Jayata and Kumpa associated who impressed Shershah with their valour?
128.x: Jaita and Kumpa were the generals of Maldeo Rathore of Marwar who fought Sher Shah at Samel (1544) with great valour.

128.s: Which of the following rulers at first assumed the title of ‘Hazrat-e-Ala’ and afterwards ‘Sultan’?
128.x: Sher Khan took the title Hazrat-e-Ala after defeating Nusrat Shah of Bengal, and became Sher Shah (Sultan) after Chausa (1539).

128.s: With which medieval ruler following statement is associated “I would have lost the empire just for a handful of millet’?
128.x: Sher Shah said it after the battle of Samel (1544), where Maldeo's generals Jaita and Kumpa nearly beat him: he had almost lost Hindustan for a handful of bajra (millet).

128.s:
Which among the following titles were assumed by the Sher Shah Suri?

I. Hazrat-e-Alam

II. Sultan

III. Zille-e-Ilahi

IV. Raiyat-e-Ala
Codes
128.x: Sher Shah took the titles Hazrat-e-Ala and then Sultan (Sher Shah) - I and II. Zill-e-Ilahi and Raiyat-e-Ala were not his titles.

128.s: With which medieval ruler would you associate the statement ‘I would have lost the empire just for a handful of millet’ ?
128.x: Sher Shah made the remark after the hard-won battle of Samel (1544) against Maldeo's Rajputs led by Jaita and Kumpa.

128.s: Death of Sher Shah Suri occurred in :-
128.x: Sher Shah died on 22 May 1545 during the siege of Kalinjar fort, wounded by a gunpowder explosion; he was buried at Sasaram.

128.s: From where did Fareed, who later on became Sher Shah Suri, get his education :
128.x: Farid (later Sher Shah) studied Arabic and Persian at Jaunpur, then called the 'Siraj-i-Hind'.

128.x: Sher Shah's last expedition was against Kalinjar (Kalanjar), where he died in May 1545 in a gunpowder accident.

128.s:
With reference to Sher Shah Suri, which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. He was the architect of a brilliant administrative system.
2. However his qualities as a ruler were not more remarkable than his victories on the field of battle.
Select the correct answer from the code given below :
128.x: Sher Shah was the architect of a brilliant administrative system (1 true), and his qualities as a ruler were MORE remarkable than his victories, so 2 is false.

128.s: From whom did Farid receive the title 'Sher Khan' for slaying a tiger?
128.x: The title 'Sher Khan' was given by Bahar Khan of Bihar, not Babur.
xa: He studied at **Jaunpur** and managed his father's jagir from **1511**.
⚠ **"Sher Shah"** was assumed after **Chausa (1539)**.

128.s: From whom did Sher Shah take the fort of Raisen?
128.x: Raisen was taken from Puran Mal.
xa: At **Samel (1544)** Sher Shah fought **Maldeo of Marwar**.
He died in **1545** in a gunpowder explosion during the siege of **Kalinjar**.
⚠ Title **"Sher Khan"** came from **Bahar Khan**; **"Sher Shah"** was assumed after **Chausa (1539)**.

128.s: At which battle did Sher Shah fight Maldeo Rathore of Marwar?
128.x: Sher Shah fought Maldeo Rathore at Samel (Giri-Sumel) in 1544, where Jaita and Kumpa fought bravely.

128.s: Whose generals were Jaita and Kumpa?
128.x: Jaita and Kumpa were Maldeo's generals at the hard-fought battle of Samel (1544).
xa: Samel is also called **Sammel / Giri-Sumel**.
**Bahadur Shah** of Gujarat let the **Portuguese** fortify **Diu** (**1535**).
Sher Shah's other conquests: **Malwa** and **Raisen** (Puran Mal).

128.s: What was the original name of Sher Shah Suri?
128.x: Sher Shah was born Farid (Farid Khan); Jalal Khan was his son Islam Shah.

128.s: Sher Shah's father was an Afghan jagirdar of which place?
128.x: Farid was the son of an Afghan jagirdar of Sasaram, of the Sur tribe.

128.s: Which city, where young Farid (Sher Shah) studied, was called 'Siraj-i-Hind'?
128.x: Farid studied at Jaunpur, known as Siraj-i-Hind.

128.s:
Consider the following statements regarding administration during Sher Shah Suri?

I. He divided his empire into Sarkars, which in turn was divided into Pargana.

II. He administered Sarkar and Paragana directly without using any other officials.
Which among the following statement(s) is/are correct?
128.x: Sher Shah divided the empire into 47 sarkars, each split into parganas (I is correct), but ran them through officers such as the chief shiqdar, chief munsif, shiqdar, amin and fotedar, so II is wrong.

128.s:
Consider the following statements on Sher Shah's land revenue administration:
I. Land was classified into three categories on the basis of produce from the land.
II. Land was measured according to a uniform system.
III. 1/4 of the produce was collected as tax.
Which of the above statements are correct?
128.x: Sher Shah measured land by a uniform system (gaz-i-Sikandari) and classified it into three categories (good, middling, bad) by produce, so I and II are correct. The state's share was one-third, not one-fourth, so III is wrong.

128.s: Which medieval ruler introduced the system of “patta” and “qabuliyat” to help the peasants?
128.x: Sher Shah gave each peasant a patta (title deed stating the state's share) and took a qabuliyat (deed of acceptance) from him.

128.s: Kabuliyat and Patta was introduced by
128.x: Patta (title deed) and qabuliyat (deed of acceptance) were introduced by Sher Shah, not by Shivaji, Jahangir or Aurangzeb.

128.s: Kabuliyat and Patta as instruments of settlement were introduced by
128.x: Sher Shah introduced patta and qabuliyat as instruments of direct state-peasant settlement; Ghiyasuddin Mahmud Shah, Bahlul Lodi and Humayun did not.

128.s: The rate of land tax levied by Shershah was
128.x: Sher Shah fixed the state's share at one-third of the average produce, after measuring the land and classing it into three grades.

128.s: What was the role of the Fotedar in a Sur-era pargana?
128.x: The Fotedar was the pargana treasurer; Karkuns were the Hindi and Persian writers.
xa: The pargana also had an **Amin** (munsif).
Sarkar level: **Chief Shiqdar** (law and order) and **Chief Munsif** (revenue/civil).

128.s: In Sher Shah's army, what did 'dagh' mean?
128.x: Dagh was the branding of horses; chehra/huliya was the descriptive roll of soldiers.
xa: Both measures were aimed **against fraud**.
**Hindus** held high army posts.

128.s: What did Sher Shah's administration do to stop officers from building local interests?
o: Gave officers their posts for life
Appointed officers in their home areas
128.x: Officers were frequently transferred so that they did not build local interests.
xa: **dagh** = horse branding; **chehra/huliya** = descriptive roll of soldiers — both against fraud.
Sarkar level: **Chief Shiqdar** (law and order) and **Chief Munsif** (revenue/civil).
Pargana: **Shiqdar**, **Amin**, treasurer (**fotedar**) and **Hindi and Persian writers** (karkuns).

128.s: In Sur administration, what did the Chief Shiqdar (shiqdar-i-shiqdaran) of a sarkar look after?
128.x: The Chief Shiqdar handled law and order; the Chief Munsif was the sarkar revenue/civil officer.
xa: Pargana officers: **Shiqdar**, **Amin** (munsif), **fotedar**, **Hindi and Persian writers** (karkuns).
Officers were **frequently transferred**.

128.s: Which statement about policing under the Sur administration is correct?
o: Public morals were regulated only by village accountants.
Local headmen were made responsible for detecting crime.
Crime detection was entrusted exclusively to the central army.
The Sur rulers had no organised espionage system.
128.x: Local headmen were held responsible for detecting crime. The system also included censors of public morals and an efficient espionage network.
128.tq: Test the responsible authority and reject the exclusive or negative claims.
xs: **Local headmen** were made responsible for **detecting crime** — so option **(2)** is correct.
There were **censors of public morals** and an efficient **espionage** system — so options (1) and (4) are wrong.
xa: Justice was **uniform** and **harsh**.
Sarkar law and order lay with the **Chief Shiqdar**.
Officers were **frequently transferred**.

128.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with Sher Shah's revenue administration?
o: Qanungo — command of the royal cavalry
128.x: The amin (munsif) of the pargana made the revenue assessment. The shiqdar kept law and order, and the qanungo and patwari kept revenue and local records; none of them prepared manuscripts, commanded the cavalry or minted coins.
128.tq: Use the 'who would do this job?' method to identify the official function.

128.s: In Sur administration, what did the Chief Munsif (munsif-i-munsifan) of a sarkar deal with?
128.x: The Chief Munsif handled revenue and civil matters; the Chief Shiqdar looked after law and order.

128.s: In Sher Shah's army, what did 'chehra' (huliya) mean?
128.x: Chehra or huliya was the descriptive roll of soldiers; dagh was horse branding. Both checked fraud.

128.s: In a Sur-era pargana, who were the Karkuns?
o: Writers keeping records in Hindi and Persian
128.x: Karkuns were writers who kept records in Hindi and Persian.

128.s: Which measure did Sher Shah's land survey use to measure land uniformly?
128.x: Land was measured with the sikandari gaz and the jarib, and classified into good, middling and bad.
xa: State share: **one-third** of average produce, paid in **cash or grain**.
⚠ APPSC-G1 **2024** key: "one-fourth" is false.
**Patta** = title deed given to the cultivator; **Qabuliyat** = deed of acceptance signed by the peasant.
The system became the model for **Todar Mal's Bandobast**.

128.s: In Sher Shah's revenue system, what was the Qabuliyat?
o: the title deed given to the peasant stating his revenue dues
the deed of agreement signed by the peasant accepting the revenue demand
the fee paid to the surveyor
the fee paid to the revenue collector
128.x: The Qabuliyat was the peasant's deed of acceptance of the revenue demand, signed by him. The Patta was the title deed given to the cultivator. Jaribana was the surveyor's fee and muhasilana the collector's fee.
128.tq: Patta given to peasant; Qabuliyat signed by peasant
xs: The **Qabuliyat** was the peasant's **deed of agreement** accepting the revenue demand, **signed by him** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The **Patta** was the **title deed** given to the cultivator.
**Jaribana** = surveyor's fee; **Muhasilana** = collector's fee.
xa: ⚠ **Patta** = given by the state; **Qabuliyat** = signed by the peasant.
Assessment was by the **Amin**, with shiqdar, qanungo and patwari.

128.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the revenue systems of Sher Shah and Akbar-Todar Mal?
o: Sher Shah classified land into three categories.
Akbar-Todar Mal used four land classes: polaj, parauti, chachar and banjar.
Akbar-Todar Mal retained the one-third share but used ten-year averages.
Sher Shah fixed the state's share at one-fourth of average produce.
128.x: Sher Shah's rate was one-third of average produce, not one-fourth; the other three statements are correct.
xa: Sher Shah's classes: **good, middling, bad**.
His system was the model for **Todar Mal's Bandobast**.
⚠ APPSC-G1 **2024**: "one-fourth" for Sher Shah's share is false.

128.s: Under Sher Shah, to whom was the 'jaribana' fee paid?
128.x: Jaribana was the surveyor's fee; muhasilana was the collector's fee.

128.s: What was the state's share of land revenue under Sher Shah?
128.x: The state share was one-third of average produce; the system became the model for Todar Mal's Bandobast.
xa: ⚠ Some notes say "one-fourth to one-third".
Some notes call Sher Shah the first to introduce a **ryotwari**-type system.

128.s: Under Sher Shah, what was the 'muhasilana'?
o: The fee paid to the revenue collector
The fee paid to the surveyor
The title deed given to the cultivator
The deed of acceptance signed by the peasant
128.x: Muhasilana was the collector's fee; jaribana was the surveyor's fee.

128.s: Hem Chandra Vikramaditya is famous in Indian history as –
128.x: Hem Chandra Vikramaditya is Hemu, Adil Shah Sur's Hindu general and prime minister, defeated at Panipat II (1556).

128.x: Sher Shah was succeeded by his second son Jalal Khan as Islam Shah (1545-53).

128.x: Hemu (Hem Chandra Vikramaditya) was the Hindu army chief and Prime Minister of Muhammad Adil Shah.

128.x: Islam Shah was Sher Shah's second son and ruled from 1545 to 1553.

129.s: The first Indian ruler to organise Haj Pilgrimage from the state exchequer was
129.x: Akbar was the first Indian ruler to send Haj caravans at state expense (from 1576, under a Mir Haj); Alauddin, Firuz Tughlaq and Aurangzeb did not start it.

the room in which the nobles belonging to different religions gathered to discuss religious affairs
