129.s: ‘Din-i-Ilahi’ of Akbar was not a success because
o: after Akbar, it was not patronised.
the Muslims did not accept other religious practices.
it was not suitably projected to the masses.
129.x: Din-i-Ilahi failed for all three reasons: not patronised after Akbar, rejected by orthodox Muslims and never projected to the masses.

129.s: In which of the following years Akbar built Ibadatkhana?
129.x: Akbar built the Ibadat Khana in 1575 and opened it to all religions in 1578.

129.s: Among the following which Mughal Emperor introduced the policy of Sulh-i-Kul?
129.x: Sulh-i-Kul was Akbar's policy; the other three were not Mughal emperors.

129.s:
Causes of Akbar’s popularity were

I. Mansabdari customs

II. Religious policy

III. Land revenue system

IV. Social reforms
Select the correct answer by using codes given below.
129.x: Mansabdari, liberal religious policy, the Dahsala revenue system and social reforms all made Akbar popular.

129.s: The Mahzar or an attested statement signed by the seven leading Ulemas was issued by
129.x: The Mahzar (1579), drafted by Shaikh Mubarak and signed by leading Ulemas, made Akbar the supreme arbiter in religious disputes.

129.s: Which historian said ‘’Din-i-Ilahi’’ is a religion ?
129.x: None of these: Abul Fazl, Badauni and Nizamuddin did not call Din-i-Ilahi a religion - it was Mohsin Fani (Dabistan-i-Mazahib).

129.s: What among the following is/are true about the priests who were sent to Akbar's court to resolve his curiosities toward Christianity in 1595 by Goa Church Authorities? (i) This was the third mission of Goa Church Authorities which was sent to Akbar's court. (ii) This session met Akbar in Lahore. (iii)Antonio Monserrate was included in this mission.
129.x: The 1595 mission (Jerome Xavier, Pinheiro, Bento de Goes) was the third and met Akbar at Lahore; Monserrate came with the first mission (1580): (i) and (ii).

129.s: Who among the following was conferred with the title of 'Jagat Guru' by Akbar?
129.x: Akbar honoured the Jain monk Hiravijaya Suri with the title Jagat Guru; Jinachandra Suri got 'Yuga Pradhan'.

129.s: Who was the renowned Jain Acharya, to be greatly honoured by Akbar?
129.x: Hiravijaya Suri was the Jain acharya most honoured by Akbar ('Jagat Guru').

129.s:
Arrange the following events of Akbar’s regime in their chronological order :
1. Abolition of Jizya
2. Construction of Ibadat Khana
3. Signing of Mahzar
4. Foundation of Din-i-Ilahi
Select the correct answer from the codes given below :
129.x: Jizya abolished 1564, Ibadat Khana 1575, Mahzar 1579, Din-i-Ilahi 1582: 1, 2, 3, 4.

129.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
129.x: Ushr was the land tax on Muslims. Zakat was the alms tax on Muslims, khums one-fifth of war booty and jizya the tax on non-Muslims.
xa: Jizya: abolished by Akbar (**1564**), reimposed by Aurangzeb (**1679**).
Pilgrim tax: abolished by Akbar in **1563**.

129.s: Which one of the following pairs regarding Akbar's religious measures is correctly matched?
129.x: The pilgrimage tax was abolished in 1563 and jizya was abolished in 1564 according to the commonly used chronology. Some accounts place both abolitions in 1564.
129.tq: Use the numerical comparison and distinguish two closely dated measures.
xs: **Pilgrimage tax — 1563; Jizya — 1564** — so option **(3)** is correct.
⚠ Some older notes give **1564** for both.
xa: **Aurangzeb** reimposed jizya in **1679**.
**Shah Jahan** abolished the pilgrim tax at **Banaras and Allahabad** after **Kavindracharya**'s deputation.

129.s: Who drafted the Mahzar of 1579, which made Akbar supreme arbiter in religious disputes?
129.x: The Mahzar was drafted by Shaikh Mubarak.
xa: It is also called the so-called **Infallibility Decree**.
**Din-i-Ilahi** followed in **1582**.

129.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Sikandar Lodi abolished the tax on grains and several grain levies.
Zain-ul-Abidin of Kashmir abolished cow slaughter.
Akbar abolished the tax on grains and several grain levies.
Alauddin Khalji abolished the privileges of Khutt, Mukaddam and Chaudhary.
129.x: Option C is incorrect: Sikandar Lodi, not Akbar, abolished the tax on grains. Zain-ul-Abidin banned cow slaughter, and Alauddin Khalji ended the privileges of the Khuts, Muqaddams and Chaudharis.
129.tq: Link each reform to its ruler.
n: Sikandar Lodi abolished the tax on grains, also described as several grain levies. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #84 · pp 166-167]
Zain-ul-Abidin of Kashmir abolished cow slaughter. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #84 · pp 166-167]
Alauddin Khalji abolished the privileges of the Khutt. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #84 · pp 166-167]
Alauddin Khalji abolished the privileges of the Mukaddam. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #84 · pp 166-167]
Alauddin Khalji abolished the privileges of the Chaudhary. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #84 · pp 166-167]
xs: The incorrect statement: **Akbar abolished the tax on grains** — option **(3)**.
The **tax on grains** (several grain levies) was abolished by **Sikandar Lodi**.
**Zain-ul-Abidin** of Kashmir abolished **jizya** and **cow slaughter**; **Alauddin Khalji** abolished the privileges of **Khutt, Mukaddam, Chaudhary**.
xa: **Akbar** abolished **jizya** and the **pilgrimage tax**.
**Shah Jahan** abolished **Sijda**.
**Aurangzeb** reimposed jizya in **1679**.

129.s: In which year did Akbar build the Ibadat Khana at Fatehpur Sikri?
129.x: The Ibadat Khana was built in 1575; 1582 is the year of Din-i-Ilahi.
xa: **1579**: the **Mahzar** made Akbar supreme arbiter.
Guiding principle: **Sulh-i-Kul**.

129.s: Which one of the following represents the central meaning of Sulh-i-Kul?
o: Compulsory conversion to a single faith
129.x: Sulh-i-Kul means universal peace or peace with all and served as a guiding principle of Akbar's policy.
129.tq: Discriminate the exact meaning of a Persian administrative-religious term.
xs: **Sulh-i-Kul** means **"peace with all"** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It was the **guiding principle** of Akbar's religious policy.
**Din-i-Ilahi** was **never forced** on anyone, so compulsory conversion is wrong.
xa: Measures: abolition of **jizya** (**1564**) and **pilgrimage tax** (**1563**), **Ibadat Khana**, **Mahzar**.
Shaikh Ahmad **Sirhindi** attacked Sulh-i-kul and Din-i-Ilahi.
Akbar's coins showed **Rama and Sita** with the legend **'Rama-Siya'**.

129.s: With the death of which emperor did Din-i-Ilahi, joined by only a handful of people, lapse?
129.x: Din-i-Ilahi lapsed with Akbar and did not continue as a major institution.
xa: Proclaimed **1582**; features: one God, greeting **"Allah-hu-Akbar"**, avoiding meat, reverence for **sun and fire**.
Members included **Abul Fazl**, **Faizi** and **Shaikh Mubarak**; **Birbal** was the only Hindu.
It was never forced on anyone.

129.s: In Islamic taxation, what did 'Khums' mean?
129.x: Khums was one-fifth of war booty; Ushr was land tax, Zakat alms tax and Haqq-e-Sharb irrigation tax.

129.s: In which year did Akbar abolish the pilgrimage tax?
129.x: The pilgrimage tax was abolished in 1563 and jizya in 1564.

129.s: Which ruler abolished the grain tax?
129.x: The grain tax was ended by Sikandar Lodi, not Akbar.

129.s: In which year was Akbar's Ibadat Khana opened to Hindus, Jains, Christians and Zoroastrians?
129.x: Built in 1575 for Muslim divines, the Ibadat Khana was opened to all faiths in 1578.

129.s: Akbar issued coins with figures of Rama and Sita bearing which Devanagari legend?
129.x: Akbar's Rama-Sita coins carry the Devanagari legend 'Rama-Siya'.

129.s: Which Mughal emperor ended the pilgrim tax at Banaras and Allahabad at the request of Kavindracharya?
129.x: Shah Jahan ended the pilgrim tax at Banaras and Allahabad after Kavindracharya and the Banaras pandits asked.

129.s: In medieval Islamic taxation, what was 'Haqq-e-Sharb'?
129.x: Haqq-e-Sharb was the irrigation tax; zakat was alms tax and ushr land tax on Muslims.

129.s: Which of the following was NOT a feature associated with Din-i-Ilahi?
o: Reverence for the sun and fire
129.x: Din-i-Ilahi included belief in one God, reverence for the sun and fire, and avoidance of meat-eating. It was never forcibly imposed on anyone.
129.tq: Reject the extreme compulsory feature that contradicts the voluntary character of the order.
xs: **Compulsory conversion of all subjects** was not a feature — Din-i-Ilahi was **never forced on anyone** — so option **(1)** is the answer.
Its features included **one God**, **reverence for sun and fire** and **avoiding meat**.
xa: Other features: greeting **"Allah-hu-Akbar"**, readiness to sacrifice wealth, high character.
Proclaimed in **1582**.
Orthodox critics: **Badauni** and Naqshbandi **Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi**.

129.s: Why did Din-i-Ilahi not become a mass religion?
o: Was confined to the Rajput nobility
Was abolished by Akbar soon after its launch
Was never forced on anyone and drew only a small circle
Was banned by the ulema in 1579
129.x: Its voluntary nature and small membership explain why Din-i-Ilahi never became a mass religion.
xa: Debate: new religion or a **discipleship order**?
**Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi** (**Mujaddid Alf-i-Sani**) attacked it and propounded **Wahdat-ul-Shuhud**.
The **Naqshbandi** order, founded by **Baha-ud-din Naqshband**, came to India with **Babur**.

129.s: By what title was Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi known?
129.x: Sirhindi was Mujaddid Alf-i-Sani and propounded Wahdat-ul-Shuhud.
xa: **Wahdat-ul-Wujud** was the stand of the **Qadiri** order; **Dara Shikoh** followed it.
Sirhindi attacked Akbar's **Sulh-i-kul** and **Din-i-Ilahi**.
The **Naqshbandi** order was founded by **Baha-ud-din Naqshband** and came to India with **Babur**.

129.s: Who among the following criticised Din-i-Ilahi and Sulh-i-Kul from an orthodox Islamic standpoint?
129.x: Badauni and the Naqshbandi scholar Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi criticised Akbar's religious innovations, including Din-i-Ilahi and Sulh-i-Kul.
129.tq: Match the criticism with the correct orthodox scholars rather than with supporters or foreign visitors.
xs: Orthodox criticism of Akbar's religious innovations came from **Badauni** and the Naqshbandi **Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Sirhindi** (**Mujaddid Alf-i-Sani**) attacked Akbar's **Sulh-i-kul** and **Din-i-Ilahi**.
**Faizi** and **Abul Fazl** were members of Din-i-Ilahi; **Abul Fazl** was its chief exponent.
**Hiravijaya Suri** and **Jinachandra Suri** were Jain monks honoured by Akbar; **Acquaviva** and **Jerome Xavier** led Jesuit missions from Goa.
xa: **Naqshbandi** order: founded by **Baha-ud-din Naqshband**; came to India with **Babur**; stressed strict **Sharia**.
Sirhindi propounded **Wahdat-ul-Shuhud** (Unity of Appearance) against **Wahdat-ul-Wujud**.
**Badauni** wrote the **Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh**.
Din-i-Ilahi (**1582**) had about **18** members; **Birbal** was the only Hindu disciple.

129.s: Din-i-Ilahi had about how many members?
129.x: Din-i-Ilahi was a small voluntary circle of about 18 members.

129.s: Who is regarded as the chief exponent ('prophet') of Din-i-Ilahi?
129.x: Abul Fazl was its chief exponent; Badauni and Ahmad Sirhindi were its orthodox critics.

129.s: To which Sufi order did Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi, known as Mujaddid Alf-i-Sani, belong?
129.x: Ahmad Sirhindi was a Naqshbandi, the most orthodox order, and criticised Akbar's religious ideas.

129.s: Who among the following called Din-i-Ilahi a religion in his Dabistan-i-Mazahib?
129.x: Mohsin Fani, a contemporary of Jahangir, called it a religion in the Dabistan-i-Mazahib.

129.s: Who led the first Jesuit mission to Akbar's court (1580)?
129.x: The first Jesuit mission from Goa in 1580 was led by Rudolf Acquaviva and Antonio Monserrate; Jerome Xavier led the third mission in 1595.
xa: The second mission came in **1591**.
The missions came from **Goa**.

129.s: Under whose leadership was the third Jesuit mission to Akbar's court in 1595 conducted?
129.x: The third Jesuit mission, sent in 1595, was under Jerome Xavier.
129.tq: Distinguish the leader of the later mission from those of the first mission.
xs: The **third** Jesuit mission (**1595**) was led by **Jerome Xavier** (CGPSC **2022**) — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Rudolf Acquaviva** and **Antonio Monserrate** led the **first** (**1580**).
**Dastur Meherji Rana** was a **Parsi** leader.
xa: The second mission came in **1591**.
The Ibadat Khana was opened to **Christians** among others.

129.s: With the growth of which city is Akbar's grant of land to Guru Ram Das associated?
129.x: Land granted to Guru Ram Das became associated with the growth of Amritsar.
129.tq: Link the religious leader with the place connected to the grant.
xs: Akbar's land grant to **Guru Ram Das** is where **Amritsar** grew — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Fatehpur Sikri** housed the **Ibadat Khana**.
xa: **Guru Arjan Dev** built the **Golden Temple (Harmandir)** at Amritsar.
Guru Arjan Dev was **executed by Jahangir (1606)**.
Akbar also gave land to Parsi **Dastur Meherji Rana**.

129.s: On which Jain scholar did Akbar confer the title 'Yuga Pradhan'?
129.x: Jinachandra Suri was called Yuga Pradhan; Hiravijaya Suri received the title Jagat Guru.

129.s: Which Parsi priest received a land grant from Akbar?
129.x: Dastur Meherji Rana, a Parsi, received a land grant; Xavier and Acquaviva were Jesuits.

129.s: In which year did the second Jesuit mission from Goa reach Akbar's court?
129.x: The Jesuit missions came in 1580, 1591 and 1595; 1591 was the second.

129.s: Who was the only Hindu member of Din-i-Ilahi?
129.x: Birbal was the only Hindu member of Din-i-Ilahi. The circle of members was small, numbering about 18 according to the cited account.
129.tq: Distinguish the sole Hindu member from other prominent Hindu officials at Akbar's court.
xs: **Birbal** was the **only Hindu** disciple of Din-i-Ilahi — so option **(3)** is correct.
The circle was small — about **18** members.
xa: Other members: **Abul Fazl, Faizi and Shaikh Mubarak**.
Birbal (Mahesh Das) was killed in **1586** fighting the **Yusufzai**.
**Man Singh** and **Todar Mal** are not listed as members.

129.s: In which year did Aurangzeb reimpose jizya?
129.x: Aurangzeb reimposed jizya in 1679 and banned festivals such as Navroz.
xa: The reversal is cited among the **causes of decline**.
Akbar had abolished jizya in **1564**.
⚠ Aurangzeb still had the **highest number of Hindu nobles** in absolute terms.

129.s: Which of the following about Akbar's religious measures is NOT correct?
o: The Ibadat Khana was built in 1575.
The Mahzar preceded the construction of the Ibadat Khana.
129.x: The Mahzar (1579) came after the Ibadat Khana (1575); the order is jizya abolished 1564, Ibadat Khana 1575, Mahzar 1579, Din-i-Ilahi 1582.

129.s: The first Jesuit Mission is associated with which year?
129.x: The first Jesuit mission reached Akbar in 1580; 1800 is the Serampore Mission and 1942 the Cripps Mission.
n: The Jesuit First Mission took place in 1580. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #117 · pp 212-213]
The Serampore Mission took place in 1800. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #117 · pp 212-213]
The Cripps Mission took place in 1942. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #117 · pp 212-213]

129.s: Who among the following was personally killed by Akbar?
129.x: Akbar personally killed Adham Khan, Maham Anaga's son, in 1562 for murdering the minister Atagh Khan.

129.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Bairam Khan:
1. Akbar gave the title of Khan-i-Khanan to Bairam Khan.
2. This title was not conferred upon Bairam Khan at the time of his appointment as wazir of the empire.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
129.x: Akbar made Bairam Khan his Wakil and gave him the title Khan-i-Khanan at that very time, so 1 is correct and 2 (not conferred at appointment) is wrong.

129.s: In which of the following place Akbar was enthroned on getting the information of Humayun’s death?
129.x: On news of Humayun's death, Bairam Khan enthroned Akbar in a garden at Kalanaur (Gurdaspur, Punjab) on 14 February 1556.

129.s: At the time of his coronation at Kalanaur the age Lat par The of Akbar was:
129.x:
Most books and keys: fourteen. Strictly, born 15 Oct 1542 and crowned 14 Feb 1556, he was 13 years 4 months (Rocket: 'age <14').
Akbar was crowned at Kalanaur in February 1556 at about fourteen (NextGen: 'only fourteen years old'), so 'fourteen' is the intended answer; fifteen, eighteen and twenty are wrong.

129.s: Akbar ruled under the protection of Bairam Khan from
129.x: Bairam Khan was Akbar's regent from 1556 to 1560, when Akbar dismissed him; 1560-64 was the petticoat government.

129.s:
Consider the following statements:
1.
Assertion (A): Emperor Akbar marched towards Afghanistan in 1581 with a huge army.
2.
Reason (R): He was on his way to reclaim his ancestral country of Ferghana in Central Asia. Options:
o: Both A and R are individually true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are individually true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
129.x: Akbar did march to Kabul in 1581, but to crush his half-brother Mirza Hakim, who backed the Bengal-Bihar rebels - not to reclaim Ferghana. A true, R false.

129.s: Akbar merged Bengal and Bihar in his empire :
129.x: Akbar defeated Daud Khan Karrani and annexed Bihar and Bengal in 1576 (conquest 1574-76).

129.s: Akbar merged Bengal and Bihar in his empire in
129.x: Bengal (with Bihar) was annexed in 1576 after Daud Khan Karrani's defeat, making Akbar master of Hindustan.

129.s: Which one of the following territories was outside the boundaries of the Mughal Empire during the reign of Akbar?
129.x: Khandesh (1601), Kabul (1581) and Kashmir (1586) were in Akbar's empire; Bijapur was annexed only by Aurangzeb (1686).

129.s: Who among the following Indian rulers was a contemporary of Akbar?
129.x: Rani Durgavati of Gondwana resisted Akbar in 1564; Ahilya Bai, Martanda Varma and Sawai Jai Singh lived in the 18th century.

129.s: Yousuf Shah Chak, the last Muslim ruler of Kashmir valley, who was exiled to Bihar by the Mughal Emperor Akbar, was buried in
129.x: Yusuf Shah Chak, exiled to Bihar after Akbar annexed Kashmir (1586), died there and was buried at Biswak in Nalanda district.

Match
List I with

Codes:
129.x:
UPSC key: I-E, II-D, III-C, IV-B. Strictly, Shivaji died in 1680, not 1686 (Satish Chandra).
1556 - accession of Akbar (E), 1600 - charter to the East India Company (D), 1739 - Nadir Shah takes Delhi (B); only option b fits, pairing 1686 with Shivaji's death (C). Haldighati was 1576.

129.s: Which of the following is an incorrect sequence of Mughal rulers?
129.x: The Mughal order is Babur, Humayun, Akbar, Jahangir, Shah Jahan, Aurangzeb; 'Akbar, Shah Jahan, Jahangir' reverses the last two.

129.s: During whose reign did the Mughal empire become a political fact and a factor in the life of India, influencing her ever since?
129.x: Under Akbar's long reign (1556-1605) the Mughal empire was consolidated by conquest, mansabdari and Rajput policy and became a lasting political fact in India.

129.s: In which year was Akbar crowned at Kalanaur?
129.x: Akbar was crowned at Kalanaur in 1556 after Humayun died in January that year.

129.s: Where was Bairam Khan, Akbar's regent (1556-60), going when he was killed in 1561?
129.x: Dismissed in 1560, Bairam Khan was killed on the way to Mecca in 1561.
xa: Bairam Khan enthroned Akbar at **Kalanaur**.
His son **Abdur Rahim Khan-i-Khanan** translated the **Baburnama** into Persian.
129.fixed: y1afd9cc98a2 key: statement that title was NOT given at wazir appointment is wrong, so statement 3 is correct

129.s: Whose dominance does the expression 'petticoat government' in Akbar's early reign refer to?
o: Ruqaiya Sultan Begum and Man Singh I
Hamida Banu Begum and Salima Sultan Begum
Maham Anaga and her son Adham Khan
129.x: The term refers to the period from 1560 to 1564 when Maham Anaga and her son Adham Khan exercised considerable influence.
129.tq: Match the political expression with the persons and period it denotes.
xs: **Petticoat government** (**1560-64**) was the dominance of **Maham Anaga** and her son **Adham Khan** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It followed **Bairam Khan's regency** (**1556-60**).
xa: Bairam Khan was dismissed in **1560** and killed in **1561**.
**Man Singh I** was a Kachhwaha general; **Todar Mal** was the revenue minister.
Akbar married the daughter of **Raja Bharmal of Amber** in **1562**.

129.s: Against whom did Akbar's forces fight the Second Battle of Panipat (5 November 1556), which ended Afghan power?
129.x: At Panipat II (1556) Hemu was hit in the eye by an arrow and captured, ending Afghan power. Daud Khan Karrani opposed Akbar in Bengal (1576), Baz Bahadur in Malwa (1561), and Ibrahim Lodi lost the First Battle of Panipat (1526) to Babur.
129.tq: Panipat II = 1556 = Hemu (arrow in the eye).
xs: At **Panipat II (5 Nov 1556)**, Akbar's forces fought **Hemu** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Hemu was **hit in the eye by an arrow** and captured; **Afghan power ended**.
**Daud Khan Karrani** opposed Akbar in **Bengal** (**1576**); **Baz Bahadur** in **Malwa** (**1561**).
xa: Akbar was then **14**, under **Bairam Khan**.
Malwa (**1561**) was Akbar's first listed conquest.

129.s: On which date was Akbar enthroned?
129.x: Akbar was enthroned at Kalanaur on February 14, 1556, after Humayun's death. The 1658 and 1659 dates are Aurangzeb's two coronations.
129.tq: Match each coronation date with its ruler.
xs: Akbar was enthroned on **February 14, 1556** — option **(3)**.
He was crowned at **Kalanaur** in **Gurdaspur, Punjab**, by **Bairam Khan**.
**July 21, 1658** and **June 5, 1659** are **Aurangzeb's** two coronations.
xa: **Bairam Khan's regency**: **1556-60**; dismissed **1560**, killed on the way to Mecca **1561**.
**Petticoat government** (**1560-64**): **Maham Anaga** and **Adham Khan**.
Akbar gave Bairam Khan the title **"Khan-i-Khanan"**.

129.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Iltutmish declared himself Sultan at Delhi.
Aurangzeb’s first coronation took place at Kalanaur.
Akbar was enthroned at Kalanaur, Gurdaspur, Punjab.
129.x: Option C is incorrect: Aurangzeb's first coronation was at Delhi, not Kalanaur; Kalanaur is where Akbar was enthroned. Iltutmish at Delhi, Shivaji at Raigarh and Akbar at Kalanaur are right.
129.tq: Match each coronation with its place.
xs: The incorrect statement: **Aurangzeb's first coronation** was **not at Kalanaur** — option **(3)**.
His first coronation was on **July 21, 1658** in **Delhi**.
**Kalanaur** (Gurdaspur, Punjab) is where **Akbar** was enthroned.
**Iltutmish** declared himself Sultan at **Delhi**; **Shivaji** was crowned at **Raigarh** — both true.
xa: Aurangzeb's second coronation was on **June 5, 1659**.
**Bairam Khan** was associated with Akbar's accession.
**Rajaraja-I** acceded in **985**, beginning the Chola golden era.

129.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Shivaji – Worshipped at Buddha's birthplace, Lumbini
Akbar – Under 14 years of age at coronation
Ashoka – Succession backed by Turkish nobles
129.x: Akbar was only 13 when crowned. Turkish nobles backed Iltutmish, Shivaji was crowned at Raigarh and Ashoka worshipped at Lumbini.
n: Turkish nobles supported or approved Iltutmish’s succession after Qutbuddin Aibak. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 73-74]
Akbar was under 14 years of age at his coronation. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 73-74]
Shivaji was coronated at Raigarh. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 73-74]
Ashoka worshipped Buddha’s birthplace at Lumbini. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 73-74]
xa: Ashoka visited Lumbini in the **twentieth year** after coronation, exempted it from **Bali tax** and cut land revenue to **one-eighth**.
Iltutmish acceded in **1211**; Akbar on **February 14, 1556** at **Kalanaur**.
⚠ Sources differ: some notes say Akbar was aged **14**.

129.s: For murdering whom did Akbar personally kill Adham Khan in 1562?
129.x: Adham Khan, son of Maham Anaga, was killed by Akbar in 1562 for murdering Atagh Khan.

129.s: Where was Akbar born in 1542?
129.x: Akbar was born on 15 October 1542 at Amarkot; Kalanaur is where he was crowned in 1556.

129.s: On which date did Aurangzeb's first coronation take place at Delhi?
129.x: Aurangzeb was first crowned at Delhi on 21 July 1658, before Deorai; his second coronation was on 5 June 1659 after Khajwa and Deorai.
n: Aurangzeb’s first coronation took place on July 21, 1658. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 73-74]
Aurangzeb’s first coronation took place in Delhi. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 73-74]
Aurangzeb was coronated twice. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 73-74]
Aurangzeb’s second coronation took place on June 5, 1659. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 73-74]

**Batai** = crop-sharing; **Kankut** = estimation of the standing crop.

130.s:
Consider the following statements about the mansabdari system:
1. It was introduced by Akbar.
2. The Dagh system of horse branding dates from 1573-74.
3. Du-aspa sih-aspa was first granted to Mahabat Khan by Akbar.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
130.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; du-aspa sih-aspa was introduced by Jahangir, not Akbar.

130.s: Under Akbar's Karori experiment (1574), how much revenue was each circle meant to yield?
130.x: Each circle was to yield one crore dams, hence the name 'karori'.
xa: **Raja Todar Mal** was **Diwan** of the empire and one of the **Navratnas**; he had served **Sher Shah**.
**Gaz-i-Ilahi** = unit of length, about **82 cm**.
The **jarib** used **bamboo pieces joined with iron rings** instead of hemp rope.

130.s: What did the mansabdari and zabti-dahsala systems together give the Mughal state?
o: A salaried, transferable nobility and predictable cash revenue
A hereditary nobility and tribute from autonomous chiefs
Religious endowments in place of military service
Revenue in kind collected directly from every village
130.x: Mansabdari and zabti-dahsala together provided a salaried, transferable nobility and a predictable stream of cash revenue.
xa: ⚠ Mughal mansabdars combined **civil-military** roles; the British **ICS** was purely civil with a fixed salary.
Dahsala (**1580**) fixed cash revenue on the average of the **last ten years**.
State share: **one-third**, paid in **dam**.

130.s: In which year was Akbar's Karori experiment introduced?
130.x: The Karori experiment was in 1574; the Dahsala followed in 1580.

130.s: Under the Karori experiment, what were the officers in charge of the revenue circles called?
130.x: Each circle yielding one crore dams was under an officer called a karori.

130.s: Upon whose earlier survey-based system did Todar Mal's revenue arrangements build?
130.x: Todar Mal had earlier served Sher Shah and built upon Sher Shah's survey-based system.

130.s: Of what was the improved jarib made, which avoided shrinking or stretching in land measurement?
o: Bamboo pieces joined with iron rings
130.x: The jarib was made of bamboo pieces joined with iron rings, which avoided the shrinkage or stretching of hemp rope.
xa: The **Gaz-i-Ilahi** was the unit of length, about **82 cm**.
⚠ Some notes call the **gaz** itself a bamboo rod.
Measurement underpinned **Zabti**: land measured and cash rates fixed per crop per **bigha**.

130.s: Todar Mal held which office in the Mughal Empire?
130.x: Todar Mal served as the Diwan, or finance minister, of the empire and was also counted among the Navratnas.
130.tq: Use the office–portfolio association while avoiding neighbouring central offices.
xs: **Raja Todar Mal** was the **Diwan (finance minister)** of the empire — so option **(1)** is correct.
He was also one of Akbar's **Navratnas** and designed the **dahsala** system.
xa: He had earlier served **Sher Shah** and built on his survey-based system.
Before dahsala, the **Karori experiment (1574)** put circles yielding **one crore dams** under **karoris**.
Under dahsala, the state share was **one-third** of average produce, paid in cash (**dam**).

130.s: Which of the following about the state share under Todar Mal's revenue arrangement is NOT correct?
o: It was one-third of the average produce.
It was normally paid in cash called dam.
Payment in kind was allowed in some areas.
It was paid in cash called jital.
130.x: The state share was paid in cash called dam, not jital, though payment in kind was allowed in some areas.

130.s: About how long was the Gaz-i-Ilahi, Akbar's unit of length?
130.x: The Gaz-i-Ilahi was about 82 cm.

130.s: Who was the first to be given the proper status of Diwan by Akbar, with Todar Mal as his assistant?
130.x: Akbar first gave the proper status of Diwan to Muzaffar Khan Turbati; Todar Mal and Khwaja Shah Mansur came later.

130.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Zabti — Crop-sharing between the state and peasant
Batai — Rough assessment based on past revenue records
Kankut — Yield estimated on the standing crop
Nasaq — Land measured and cash rates fixed per crop
130.x: Kankut involved estimating the yield on the standing crop. Zabti involved measurement and cash rates, Batai involved crop-sharing, and Nasaq relied on past revenue records.
130.tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate swapped meanings.
xs: **Kankut — yield estimated on the standing crop** is correctly matched — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Zabti** = land measured and cash rates fixed per crop; **Batai** = crop-sharing.
**Nasaq** = rough assessment from **past revenue records**, without fresh measurement.
xa: Kankut was used where **measurement was not practical**.
**Nasaq** was used mainly in **Bengal**.
⚠ **Batai** = crop-sharing; **Kankut** = standing-crop estimate; **Nasaq** = past records.

130.s: In which region was the Nasaq method of revenue assessment mainly used under the Mughals?
130.x: Nasaq was used mainly in Bengal; Batai in Thatta, Kabul and Kashmir, Zabti in the core provinces, plough-based assessment in parts of the Deccan.
xa: **Kankut** estimated the yield on the **standing crop** where measurement was impractical.
**Zabti** fixed cash rates per crop per **bigha** after measuring land.
**Batai** is also called **Ghalla-bakhshi**.

130.s: In which year was Akbar's Dahsala system introduced?
130.x: Dahsala, based on ten-year average produce and prices commuted into cash, came in 1580; 1574 was the Karori experiment.
xa: Dahsala is also called **Ain-i-Dahsala**; it was the APPSC-G2 **2017** answer.
**Bandobast** system = **Dahsala** (JPSC **2013** key).
State share: **one-third** of average produce, paid in **dam**.

130.s: The Dahsala was based on the average produce and prices of which years?
130.x: The Dahsala (1580) used the average of the last ten years, 1571-1580.

130.s: Where was Batai (Ghalla-bakhshi) mainly used under the Mughals?
130.x: Crop-sharing (batai) was used in Thatta, Kabul and Kashmir; Nasaq was mainly in Bengal and Zabti in the core provinces.

130.s: Under Akbar's Zabti system, what were the 'dasturs'?
o: Cash revenue rates per crop per bigha
Revenue circles yielding one crore dams
130.x: Under zabti, land was measured and dasturs fixed cash rates per crop per bigha.

130.s: In parts of the Deccan, on what basis was land revenue fixed under the plough method?
o: An estimate of the standing crop
130.x: In parts of the Deccan revenue was assessed by the number of ploughs.

130.s: During the reign of Akbar, the role of an official called Amalguzar was
o: to be in-charge of law and order.
to make an assessment and collection of land revenue.
to be in-charge of imperial household.
130.x: The Amalguzar was the sarkar-level revenue officer who assessed and collected land revenue and extended cultivation.

130.s: In Mughal administrative vocabulary ‘Maal’ represents–
130.x: In Mughal usage 'maal' meant land revenue, the state's main income.

130.s: ‘Madad-i-Mash’ indicates in Mughal administration –
o: Revenue free land granted to learned persons
130.x: Madad-i-maash was a revenue-free land grant to learned and pious persons and the needy.

130.s: In the Mughal administration ‘Madad- i-Mash’ indicates
o: revenue free land given to learned persons
130.x: Madad-i-maash was a revenue-free grant to scholars, holy men and the needy - not a tax or an army pension.

130.s: In medieval Deccan, Deshmukh was a village official, wh responsible to-
o: Collect land revenue from the peasants and to deposit it in the State treasury
Maintain law and order in the village
130.x: The Deshmukh, a hereditary Deccan officer over a pargana, collected land revenue from the peasants and deposited it in the state treasury.

130.s:
Match the following revenue officials during the reign of Akbar with their duties:
List I
List II
a. Amalguzar
I. Kept records of the revenue payable by the villages
b. Karkuns
II. Revenue Collector in-charge of a District
c. Qanungo
III. Accountant
d. Bitikchi
IV. Prepared the seasonal crop statistics
130.x: Amalguzar - district revenue collector (II), Karkuns - crop statistics (IV), Qanungo - village revenue records (I), Bitikchi - accountant (III): a-II, b-IV, c-I, d-III; only option b has the amalguzar right.

130.s: What was Mughal crown land, whose revenue went straight to the imperial treasury, called?
130.x: Crown land was khalisa; suyurghal and madad-i-maash were charitable revenue-free grants.
xa: **Khalisa** revenue went straight to the imperial treasury; cash (**naqd**) salaries were paid from it.
A **jagir** was a right to collect revenue in lieu of salary — not ownership.
Khalisa expanded in Golconda under **Abdullah** and **Tana Shah**.

130.s: What did a jagir represent under the Mughal system?
o: A direct cash payment from the khalisa treasury
The right to collect revenue in lieu of salary, without ownership
A permanent revenue-free grant to scholars
130.x: A jagir was an assignment of the right to collect revenue in lieu of salary; it did not confer ownership of the land.
130.tq: Apply the distinction between revenue-collection rights and ownership.
xs: A **jagir** was the **right to collect revenue in lieu of salary**, not ownership — so option **(3)** is correct.
Direct cash salaries came from **khalisa** revenue (**naqd**); revenue-free grants to scholars were **madad-i-maash**.
xa: Mansabdars held **non-hereditary**, combined civil-military ranks **paid by jagir**.
⚠ British **ICS** = purely civil, fixed salary from the treasury.
**Suyurghal** = another name for charitable revenue-free grants.

130.s: What were Mughal revenue-free grants to scholars, holy men and the needy called?
130.x: Madad-i-maash (also suyurghal) was a charitable revenue-free grant; Khalisa was crown land.

130.s: What was the principal source of income of the Mughal state?
130.x: Maal, the land revenue, was the main income of the Mughal state.

130.s: What did the term 'Suyurghal' mean in the Mughal period?
130.x: Suyurghal, like madad-i-maash, was a revenue-free grant to scholars, holy men and the needy.

130.s: Under the Qutb Shahis of Golconda, the state generally took what share of the produce?
130.x: Golconda generally took one-third of the produce, not one-half.

130.s: Which Mughal official kept the land and revenue records of a pargana?
130.x: The qanungo kept pargana land and revenue records; the potdar was a treasurer.

130.s: What was the Potdar in Mughal revenue administration?
130.x: The potdar was the treasurer; the patwari was the village accountant and the amalguzar the sarkar revenue collector.

130.s: In Mughal revenue administration, what was the duty of the Bitikchi?
o: Collecting the revenue of the sarkar
Keeping records on land and produce
Maintaining law and order in towns
130.x: The bitikchi kept records on land and produce; the amalguzar collected revenue and the potdar was treasurer.

130.s: Who was the revenue collector of a Mughal sarkar, also charged with extending cultivation?
130.x: The amalguzar collected sarkar revenue and tried to extend cultivation.

130.s: From about which period do the dual ranks of Zat and Sawar in Akbar's mansabdari date?
130.x: Zat and Sawar dual ranks came about 1595-96; 1573-74 was the Dagh system.

130.s: Who introduced the du-aspa sih-aspa system?
130.x: Du-aspa sih-aspa was Jahangir's measure, first for Mahabat Khan; Zat-Sawar was Akbar's.

130.s: Which of the following pairs (Land assignment – Rulers) is NOT correctly matched?
