141.s: After the Third Anglo-Maratha War, where was Baji Rao II pensioned?
141.x: Baji Rao II was pensioned at Bithur near Kanpur; a small Satara state was created for a descendant of Shivaji.
xa: Baji Rao II's territory was **annexed**.
**1818 = extinction of the Peshwaship** — after Salbai (status quo) and Bassein (subordination).

141.s: To which war does the Battle of Assaye (1803), in which Arthur Wellesley defeated Scindia and Bhonsle, belong?
141.x: Assaye (23 September 1803) was fought in the Second Anglo-Maratha War (1803-05).

142.s: What is the meaning of 'pasuras'?
o: Singing of the hymns on Vishnu
142.x: Pasurams (pasuras) are the Tamil hymns of the Alvars in praise of Vishnu, collected in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham; Nayanar hymns on Shiva form the Tevaram.

142.s: The Bhakti movement was started by –
142.x: The Bhakti movement began in the Tamil South with the Vaishnava Alvars (and the Shaiva Nayanars) in the 6th-9th centuries; Surdas and Tulsidas came almost a thousand years later, and the Sufis were Muslim mystics.

142.s: Who was/were the 10th century composers of the Nalayira Divya Prabandham?
142.x: The Nalayira Divya Prabandham is the 4,000-hymn Vaishnava canon of the Alvars, compiled by Nathamuni in the 10th century. Appar and Sambandar were Nayanars, whose hymns are in the Tevaram.

142.s: Who was/were the 10th century composer(s) of the Naalayira Divya Prabandham?
142.x: The Naalayira Divya Prabandham is the hymn collection of the Alvars, compiled by Nathamuni in the 10th century; Nayanars like Appar and Sambandar sang the Shaiva Tevaram.

142.s: Who were the first Vaishnavite devotees in South India?
142.x: The Alvars (12 Vaishnava saints, 6th-9th c.) were the first Vaishnava devotees of South India. The Nayanars were Shaiva; the Virashaivas came later in Karnataka.

142.s: Who were the first Vaishnavite devotees in South India?
142.x: The Alvars (12 Vaishnava saints, 6th-9th c.) were the first Vaishnava devotees of South India. The Nayanars were Shaiva; the Virashaivas came later in Karnataka.

142.s: The earlier Vaishnava Bhakti Saints from the South were
142.x: The earlier Vaishnava Bhakti saints of the South were the Alvars; the Nayanars and Virashaivas were Shaiva.

142.s: Who were Nayanars?
142.x: The Nayanars were the 63 Tamil devotees of Shiva, i.e. Shaivas; the Vaishnava devotees were the Alvars.

142.s: Who were the ‘Nayanars’?
142.x: The Nayanars were the 63 devotees of Shiva, i.e. Shaivites; the Alvars were the Vaishnavites.

142.s: Divya Prabandhas are authored by
142.x: The Divya Prabandham (Nalayira Divya Prabandham) is the canon of hymns of the 12 Alvars, the Tamil Vaishnava saints. Haridasas were later Kannada Vaishnava singers.

142.s: Who among the following was not an ‘Alvar Saint’?
142.x: Poigai, Pudam (Bhutam) and Thirumangai were Alvars; 'Tirugyan' (Tirugnana Sambandar) was a Shaiva Nayanar, not an Alvar.

142.s: The collection of the writings of the Saivite saints is considered as Fifth Veda. What is the name of the above collection?
142.x: The Tirumurai, the 12-volume Tamil Shaiva canon of the Nayanars, is called the 'Fifth Veda'. Tolkappiyam is a grammar; Silappadikaram and Manimekalai are Sangam-age epics.

142.s: Vaishnavism was propagated by Alvar saints of Tamil Nadu. Who was the only female Sadhvi among the Alvar saints?
142.x: Andal was the only woman among the 12 Alvars. Nammalvar, Poigai and Thirumangai were male Alvars.

142.s: From which social groups did the Alvars and Nayanars, who challenged Brahmanical dominance, come?
142.x: The Alvars and Nayanars came from different castes, high and low, and challenged Brahmanical dominance.
xa: ⚠ **Alvars = 12** (Vishnu); **Nayanars = 63** (Shiva).
Women saints include **Andal** and **Karaikkal Ammaiyar**.

142.s: How many Nayanars (Shiva devotees) were there?
142.x: There were sixty-three Nayanars, devotees of Shiva, and twelve Alvars, devotees of Vishnu.
xa: Alvar hymns: **Nalayira Divya Prabandham** (**4,000** hymns).
Nayanar lives: **Periya Puranam** by **Sekkizhar**.

142.s: Who compiled the Nalayira Divya Prabandham, the "Tamil Veda" of 4,000 Alvar hymns?
142.x: The Nalayira Divya Prabandham contains 4,000 Alvar hymns and was compiled by Nathamuni.
xa: ⚠ "Tamil Veda" = **Nalayira Divya Prabandham**; "Fifth Veda" = **Tirumurai**.
**Alvars = 12** Vishnu devotees.

142.s: Who composed the Tiruvasagam?
142.x: The Tiruvasagam is by Manikkavachakar; Sekkizhar wrote the Periya Puranam.
xa: Tevaram = the first seven books of the **Tirumurai**.
Periya Puranam was written under **Kulottunga II** on the **63 Nayanars**.

142.s: Who compiled the Tirumurai, the 12-book Shaiva canon called the "Fifth Veda"?
142.x: Nambi Andar Nambi compiled the 12 books of the Tirumurai; Sekkizhar's Periya Puranam is its 12th book.
xa: Sekkizhar wrote it under **Kulottunga II**.
⚠ "Tamil Veda" is the Alvars' **Nalayira Divya Prabandham**.

142.s: Who is regarded as the foremost Alvar, author of the Tiruvaymoli?
142.x: Nammalvar is the foremost Alvar; his Tiruvaymoli has 1,102 verses.

142.s: Karaikkal Ammaiyar was one of the women saints among which group?
142.x: Karaikkal Ammaiyar was one of three women among the 63 Nayanars, and the only female Nayanar whose poems survive.

142.s: Who wrote the Periya Puranam, the lives of the 63 Nayanars?
142.x: Sekkizhar wrote the Periya Puranam under Kulottunga II; it is the 12th book of the Tirumurai.

142.s: Whose hymns does the Tevaram contain?
142.x: The Tevaram holds the hymns of the Nayanars Appar, Sambandar and Sundarar; Poigai, Bhoothath and Pey were the first three Alvars.

142.s: Which deity did the Nayanars of the Tamil region worship?
142.x: The 63 Nayanars were devotees of Shiva, while the 12 Alvars were devotees of Vishnu.

142.s: How many Alvars were there, by tradition?
142.x: By tradition there were 12 Alvars (Vishnu devotees); the Nayanars were 63.

142.s: Who was the only woman among the Alvars?
142.x: Andal was the only female Alvar; Karaikkal Ammaiyar was a woman Nayanar.

142.s: Who were the first three Alvars?
142.x: Poigai, Bhoothath and Pey are the first three Alvars; Appar, Sambandar and Sundarar were Nayanars.

142.s: Which of the following groups is known as the Samayacharyas of the Nayanar tradition?
o: Nathamuni, Ramanuja, Vedanta Desika and Andal
Basavanna, Allama Prabhu, Akkamahadevi and Channabasava
142.x: Appar, Sambandar, Sundarar and Manikkavachakar are the four Samayacharyas.

142.s: Under which Chola king did Sekkizhar write the Periya Puranam?
142.x: Sekkizhar wrote the Periya Puranam, the 12th Tirumurai, under Kulottunga II.

142.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
142.x: The Tirumurai is a 12-volume Tamil Shaiva canon compiled between the 7th and 12th centuries and called the Fifth Veda; Alvar hymns were in Tamil.
xa: The hymns became part of **temple ritual**.
Period of the Alvars and Nayanars: c. **6th-9th centuries**.

142.s: What is the traditional number of Alvars and Nayanars respectively?
142.x: There are traditionally 12 Alvars (Vaishnava, devotees of Vishnu) and 63 Nayanars (Shaiva, devotees of Shiva). '63 and 12' reverses them, and the other two options give both groups the same number.
xs: **12 Alvars** and **63 Nayanars** — option **(2)**.
Alvars were **Vaishnava** (Vishnu); Nayanars **Shaiva** (Shiva) (UPPSC **2014**, MPPSC **2022**).
Option 1 reverses the numbers.
xa: **Rajaraja I** consecrated bronzes of all **63 Nayanmars** at Chidambaram.
**Andal** = only female Alvar.

142.s: Which of the following was a Nayanar saint?
142.x: Appar, Sambandar, Sundarar and Manikkavachakar are notable Nayanars; Nammalvar, Andal and Tirumangai were Alvars.
xa: Nayanar canon: **Tevaram**, the earliest part of the **Tirumurai**.
⚠ Alvars = **12** = Vishnu; Nayanars = **63** = Shiva.

142.s: Where did Rajaraja I consecrate bronzes of all 63 Nayanmars?
142.x: Rajaraja I consecrated the bronzes at Chidambaram; Parantaka I had installed statues of Appar, Sambandar and Sundarar.
xa: Chola temples: **Thanjavur**, **Gangaikondacholapuram**, **Chidambaram**.
Chola patronage was a key **spread factor** for bhakti.

142.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
142.x: Karaikkal Ammaiyar was a Shaiva woman saint associated with the Nayanars. Andal, not Karaikkal Ammaiyar, was the only female Alvar.
142.tq: Find the single swapped sect and identify the confusable woman saint.
xs: Pair **(2)** is NOT correct: **Karaikkal Ammaiyar** was a **Nayanar** (Shaiva) saint, not an Alvar.
**Andal** was the **only female Alvar**.
**Appar — Nayanar**, **Tirumangai Alvar** and **Nammalvar — Alvar** are correct.
xa: **Periyalvar** is also an Alvar.
Karaikkal Ammaiyar was known for **extreme asceticism**.

142.s: What is the canon of the Alvar hymns known as?
142.x: The Alvar hymns form the Nalayira Divya Prabandham; Tevaram and Tirumurai are Nayanar (Shaiva) collections.

142.s:
Consider the following statements about the Alvars and Nayanars:
1. The Alvars were Vaishnavas, traditionally 12 in number.
2. The Nayanars were Shaivas, traditionally 63 in number.
3. Their hymns were composed in Sanskrit.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
142.x: Alvars (12) worshipped Vishnu and Nayanars (63) Shiva; their hymns were in Tamil, not Sanskrit.

142.s: Karaikkal Ammaiyar, known for extreme asceticism, belonged to which group of saints?
142.x: Karaikkal Ammaiyar was a Nayanar; Andal was the only female Alvar.

142.s: The Tirumurai, the Tamil Shaiva canon, consists of how many volumes?
142.x: The Tirumurai has 12 volumes, of which the Tevaram is the earliest and most sacred part.

142.s: Which is the earliest and most sacred part of the Tirumurai, the canon of the Nayanars?
142.x: Tevaram is the earliest and most sacred part of the Tirumurai, the Tamil Shaiva canon of the Nayanars.

142.s: Who had composed the ‘Gita Govinda’?
142.x: The Gita Govinda was composed by Jayadeva in the 12th century, at the court of Lakshmana Sena of Bengal; Dhoyi and Govardhanacharya were fellow poets of that court.

142.s: Vaishnavism in Kamrupa was popularised by
142.x: Vaishnavism in Kamarupa (Assam) was popularised by Shankaradeva, founder of the Ekasarana Dharma; Chaitanya worked in Bengal and Odisha.

142.s: Identify the wrong matching of poets and their languages in the 18th century:
142.x: Tayumanavar wrote Tamil sittar poetry, Waris Shah Punjabi (Heer Ranjha) and Kunchan Nambiar Malayalam, but Dayaram was a Gujarati lyricist, not Marathi.

142.s: Prem Vatika, poems on the life of Krishna, was composed by:
142.x: Prem Vatika, poems on Radha-Krishna love, was composed by Raskhan (Sayyid Ibrahim), a Muslim devotee of Krishna. Surdas wrote the Sur Sagar, Bihari the Satsai and Kabir the Bijak.

142.s: Prem Vatika, poems on the life of Krishna, was composed by :
142.x: Prem Vatika, poems on Radha-Krishna love, was composed by Raskhan (Sayyid Ibrahim), a Muslim devotee of Krishna. Surdas wrote the Sur Sagar, Bihari the Satsai and Kabir the Bijak.

142.s: Which among the following given pairs is not correctly matched?
142.x: Raskhan's works are Prem Vatika and Sujan Raskhan; Rasikpriya is by Keshavdas, so 'Raskhan - Rasikpriya' is the wrong pair. Nabhadas wrote the Bhaktmal, Dhruvdas the Bhakt Namavali and Usman the Chitravali.

142.s: Which one of the following wrote the famous ‘Ram Chandrika’ and ‘Rasik-Priya’?
142.x: Keshavdas (Keshav) of Orchha, the Riti poet, wrote Ramchandrika and Rasikpriya. Raskhan wrote Prem Vatika; Matiram and Senapati were other Riti poets.

142.s: Who among the following introduced Vaishnavism in Assam and Cooch Behar?
142.x: Shankaradeva introduced (Ekasarana) Vaishnavism in Assam and Cooch Behar; Chaitanya, Madhva and Vallabha worked elsewhere.

142.s: Vaishnavism in Kamarupa was popularised by –
142.x: Vaishnavism in Kamarupa (Assam) was popularised by Shankaradeva, founder of the Ekasarana sect devoted to Krishna, opposed to ritual and idolatry.

142.s: Famous medieval saint Shankaradeva belonged to –
142.x: Shankaradeva belonged to the Vaishnava cult: his Ekasarana Dharma centred on devotion to Krishna (Vishnu).

142.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
142.x: Raskhan wrote Prem Vatika; Mirabai sang of Krishna, Dadu Dayal founded the Dadu Panth and the Alvars were devotees of Vishnu.
n: Mirabai is associated with Krishna Bhakti. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 132-134]
Raskhan was a devotee of Krishna. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 132-134]
Raskhan is associated with Prem Vatika. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 132-134]
Dadu Dayal is associated with the Dadu Panth. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 132-134]
Alvars are associated with Vishnu. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 132-134]
Alvars are associated with Vaishnavism. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 132-134]
xa: Alvars numbered **12**; the Shaiva **Nayanars** numbered **63**.
Dadu Dayal (Rajasthan) founded the Dadu Panth in the **Kabir** tradition.
**Ravidas** was **Mirabai**'s guru.

142.s: In which region did Shankaradeva, founder of the Ekasarana Dharma, spread Bhakti?
142.x: Shankaradeva preached Ekasarana Dharma in Assam; Chaitanya worked in Bengal.

142.s: Who is the author of the Gita Govinda?
142.x: The Gita Govinda was written by Jayadeva (12th c.).

142.s: Shankaradeva's Ekasarana sect worshipped which single deity?
142.x: Shankaradeva's Ekasarana sect worshipped one deity, Krishna, and opposed rituals and idolatry.

142.s: The socio-religious movement led by Saint Ramanuja, which emphasized devotion to Lord Vishnu and advocated for social equality, had a significant impact on Andhra society. What was this movement called?
142.src: APPSC 2022 Various Non Gazetted Posts Limited Recruitment
142.x: A movement of devotion to Vishnu that preached social equality is the Bhakti movement, which Ramanuja carried into Andhra. Arya Samaj (19th c.) and Lingayatism (Shaiva) are different movements.

142.s: Which one of the following gives equal importance to Jnana, Karma and Bhakti as a means of liberation?
142.x: The Bhagavad Gita accepts jnana, karma and bhakti as valid paths to liberation (Chapter 12 is Bhakti Yoga). Advaita privileges knowledge, Vishishtadvaita devotion, and Mimamsa ritual action.

142.s: The Bhakti culture was reborn in India during-
142.x: Bhakti was reborn and reached its zenith in the 15th-16th centuries, when Kabir, Nanak, Surdas, Tulsidas and Mirabai spread it in the north; its first phase was in the Tamil South from the 6th century.

142.s: A common feature of all Bhakti Saints was that they –
o: Composed their verses in the language understood by
Rejected the authority of the priestly class
Encouraged women to go to the temples
142.x: What all Bhakti saints shared was composing in the language of the people (Hindi, Marathi, Bengali, Kannada and so on). Not all rejected priests, and Saguna saints kept idol worship, so the other options do not hold for all.

142.s: The number of forms of bhakti in the Bhagvata cult is–
142.x: The Bhagavata cult recognises navadha (ninefold) bhakti: shravana, kirtana, smarana, padasevana, archana, vandana, dasya, sakhya and atmanivedana.

142.s: What does the root 'bhaj', from which the word 'bhakti' is derived, mean?
142.x: The word bhakti is derived from the root bhaj, meaning to share or participate.
xs: **Bhaj** means **to share or participate** — option **(3)**.
Bhakti derives from this root.
xa: The **Bhagavata Purana** first put bhakti at the **centre of religion**.
It lists **ninefold (navadha) bhakti**: shravana, kirtana, smarana, padasevana, archana, vandana, dasya, sakhya, atmanivedana.

142.s: Which text put bhakti at the centre of religion and described a ninefold bhakti?
142.x: The Bhagavata Purana put bhakti at the centre; its ninefold bhakti includes kirtana, smarana and atmanivedana.
xa: Dating: some notes say the **6th c.**; most scholars **c. 9th-10th c.**
Other roots of bhakti: the **Upanishads** and the **Bhagavad Gita**.

142.s: Which of the following is NOT regarded as a root of the Bhakti movement?
142.x: The Upanishads, Bhagavad Gita and Bhagavata Purana are identified as roots of the Bhakti movement; the Arthashastra is not.
xa: **Gita Chapter 12 = Bhakti Yoga**.
Both streams drew on the **Upanishadic doctrine of Advaita**.

142.s: Which one of the following sequences represents the beginning of the Bhakti movement and its later spread most accurately?
o: Tamil region in the sixth–ninth centuries, followed by spread to northern India by the fifteenth century
Northern India in the fifteenth century, followed by spread to Tamil Nadu in the eighteenth century
Bengal in the ninth century, followed by spread to Tamil Nadu in the twelfth century
Rajasthan in the sixth century, followed by spread to Tamil Nadu in the fifteenth century
142.x: The movement first developed in the Tamil region through the Alvars and Nayanars during the sixth–ninth centuries and reached the northern belt by the fifteenth century. Its overall span is described as the sixth to the eighteenth century.
142.tq: Use the first regional centre and the later northern expansion to establish sequence.
xs: Bhakti began in the **Tamil region (6th-9th c.)** and reached **northern India by the 15th c.** — option **(1)**.
It started with the **Alvars and Nayanars**.
xa: Overall span: **6th to 18th c.**
**Ramananda** brought it to the north.

142.s: The Bhakti movement arose partly because ordinary people found which paths difficult?
142.x: The paths of knowledge (gyana) and action (karma) were considered difficult for ordinary people, alongside reaction against ritualism, priestly dominance and caste.
xa: Core beliefs: **monotheism**, **guru essential**, **salvation through devotion**.
Limit: it only **moderated** caste rigidity.

142.s: The Bhakti movement challenged caste hierarchy by placing devotion above which of the following?
142.x: The Bhakti saints placed devotion above birth and status, and that is how they challenged caste hierarchy.
n: The Bhakti Movement emphasized devotion over birth and status. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 80-82]
The Bhakti Movement challenged caste hierarchy. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 80-82]
xa: **Guru Nanak**'s **Guru Ka Langar** = common dining without caste discrimination.
**Alvars and Nayanars** came from **all castes, high and low**.
Limit: it only **moderated** caste rigidity to an extent.

142.s: To whom do modern scholars trace the indigenous roots of the Bhakti movement?
142.x: Modern scholars emphasise the movement's indigenous Alvar–Nayanar roots and see Islam as influencing mainly its later egalitarianism.
xa: Bhakti began in the **Tamil region (6th-9th c.)**.
It brought **Hindus and Muslims closer**, but lasting unity was not achieved.

142.s: Which chapter of the Bhagavad Gita is the Bhakti Yoga?
142.x: Gita Chapter 12 is Bhakti Yoga; it holds both Saguna and Nirguna valid.

142.s: The common goal of life of both Buddha and Mirabai was
o: The World is Full of Sorrow
142.x: Both the Buddha and Mirabai saw the world as full of sorrow and renounced worldly life; ahimsa was not Mirabai's central goal and Nirvana is a Buddhist idea only. The question is loosely framed; this is the answer books and quiz keys give.

142.s: Which of the following (Poetess-Compositions) is not correctly matched?
o: Son Kumari – Poem of Swarn Beli
142.x: Daya Bai wrote Vinay Malika, Sahajobai Sahaj Prakash and Son Kumari the Swarn Beli poems; Ganesh Dev Leela is not Gangabai's work, so that pair is wrong.

142.s: Women Saint Daya Bai was a disciple of –
142.x: Women saint Daya Bai was a disciple of Saint Charandas, founder of the Charandasi Sampradaya; she wrote the Dayabodh.

142.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
142.x: Kabir was a weaver. Dhanna was a Jat cultivator, Sena was a barber and Raidas was a shoemaker.
142.tq: Use the occupation-based social identities to detect the swapped identity.
xs: Pair **(1)** is NOT correct: **Kabir** was a **weaver**, not a Rajput prince.
**Raidas** = shoemaker; **Sena** = barber; **Dhanna** = Jat cultivator — all disciples of **Ramananda**.
xa: Kabir was raised by Muslim weavers **Niru and Nima**.
Ravidas was **Mirabai**'s guru.

142.s: Who is regarded as the first medieval reformer to denounce caste outright?
142.x: Ramananda is described as the first medieval reformer to denounce caste outright and he admitted disciples from all castes.
142.tq: Recall the reformer linked with the strongest anti-caste position.
xs: **Ramananda** was the **first medieval reformer to denounce caste outright** — option **(3)**.
He **admitted disciples of all castes** and brought bhakti to the **north**.
xa: His disciples: **Kabir** (weaver), **Raidas** (shoemaker), **Dhanna** (Jat cultivator), **Sena** (barber).
⚠ **Ramanuja → Ramananda → Kabir / Ravidas → Mirabai**.

142.s: The Bhakti movement weakened caste bondage and brought which two communities closer?
142.x: The movement brought Hindus and Muslims closer and weakened caste bondage, though it did not abolish caste or achieve lasting unity.

142.s: Who was the guru of Mirabai?
142.x: Ravidas was Mirabai's guru.
xa: **Charandas — Daya Bai** (RPSC **2018**).
Ramananda's disciples: **Kabir, Raidas, Dhanna, Sena**.

142.s: Who set up the Chapakudu, common dining for all castes?
142.x: Palnati Brahmanayudu set up the Chapakudu and treated the Mala devotee Kannama Dasu as his son.
xa: **Palnadu** = **Veeravaishnavism** + the Chapakudu.
Vemana wrote in **Telugu**.

142.s: Who was the guru of Kabir, Raidas, Dhanna and Sena?
142.x: Ramananda admitted disciples of all castes: Kabir, Raidas, Dhanna and Sena.

142.s: Who was the guru of Surdas?
142.x: Surdas was a disciple of Vallabhacharya.

142.s: Which one of the following Guru - Disciple pairs is NOT correctly matched?
142.x: Ravidas was the guru of Mirabai; Surdas was Vallabhacharya's disciple.

142.s: Who was the guru of the woman saint Daya Bai?
142.x: Daya Bai, author of Dayabodh, was a disciple of Charandas.

142.s: What was the background of Pipa, a disciple of Ramananda?
142.x: Pipa was a Rajput ruler of Gagron; Kabir was a weaver, Raidas a shoemaker and Dhanna a Jat cultivator.

142.s: Which one of the following groups consists entirely of Nirguna saints?
o: Surdas, Guru Nanak, Chaitanya and Dadu Dayal
Kabir, Guru Nanak, Dadu Dayal and Ravidas
142.x: Kabir, Guru Nanak, Dadu Dayal and Ravidas are associated with the Nirguna stream, which worships a formless God.
142.tq: Classify each saint by the stream with which he is associated.
xs: **Kabir, Guru Nanak, Dadu Dayal and Ravidas** are all **Nirguna** saints — option **(2)**.
**Surdas, Chaitanya, Tulsidas, Mirabai** are **Saguna** saints.
xa: Kabir as Nirguna was asked in **APPSC GS 2024**.
⚠ **Ramamargi** = Tulsidas; **Krishnamargi** = Surdas, Mirabai, Chaitanya.

142.s: Tulsidas belonged to which branch of the Saguna Vaishnava stream?
142.x: Saguna Vaishnavas split into Ramamargis and Krishnamargis; Tulsidas, a devotee of Rama, was a Ramamargi.
xa: **Vallabha** was also a Krishnamargi.
⚠ **Ramcharitmanas** = Awadhi; **Sur Sagar** = Braj.

142.s: Who founded the Dadu Panth in Rajasthan, in the tradition of Kabir?
142.x: Dadu Dayal founded the Dadu Panth in Rajasthan in Kabir's tradition; Kabir himself did not found it.

142.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Chaitanya Mahaprabhu was associated with Krishna Bhakti and Vaishnavism.
Raskhan was a devotee of Rama.
Dadu Dayal was associated with the Dadu Panth.
Kabir was associated with Nirguna Bhakti.
142.x: Option B is incorrect: Raskhan was a Muslim poet devoted to Krishna, not Rama, and wrote Prem Vatika. Chaitanya, Dadu Dayal and Kabir are correctly described.
142.tq: Check the deity linked with each saint.
n: Chaitanya Mahaprabhu is associated with Krishna Bhakti. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 132-134]
Chaitanya Mahaprabhu is associated with Vaishnavism. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 132-134]
Raskhan was a devotee of Krishna. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 132-134]
Dadu Dayal is associated with the Dadu Panth. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 132-134]
Kabir is associated with Nirguna Bhakti. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 132-134]
xs: The incorrect statement: **Raskhan** was a devotee of **Rama** — option **(2)**.
**Raskhan** was a **devotee of Krishna** and wrote **Prem Vatika**.
**Chaitanya** — **Krishna Bhakti**, Vaishnavism; **Dadu Dayal** — **Dadu Panth**; **Kabir** — **Nirguna Bhakti** — all true.
xa: **Tulsidas** = **Rama Bhakti** (Ramcharitmanas); **Mirabai** = **Krishna Bhakti**.
**Ramanuja** propounded **Vishishtadvaita**.
**Alvars** = Vishnu; **Nayanars** = Shiva.

142.s: Both the Nirguna and Saguna streams drew upon which Upanishadic doctrine?
142.x: Both Nirguna and Saguna traditions drew on the Upanishadic doctrine of Advaita; the movement was essentially monotheistic.
xa: **Shankaracharya** (b. **788**, Kaladi) was the Advaita forerunner.
**Gita Chapter 12** holds both Saguna and Nirguna **valid**.

142.s: Which one of the following groups represents the NIRGUNA tradition of Bhakti?
142.x: Kabir, Guru Nanak and Guru Ravidas are associated with the Nirguna tradition, which emphasises devotion to the formless divine.
142.tq: Separate the two doctrinal groups by identifying the members of the Nirguna tradition.
xs: **Kabir, Nanak and Ravidas** are **Nirguna** saints — option **(3)**.
**Tulsidas, Surdas, Mirabai, Chaitanya** are **Saguna** saints.
xa: Kabir as Nirguna was asked in APPSC-GS **2024**.
Ravidas was a contemporary of **Kabir**.

142.s: Which of the following saints belongs to the Saguna tradition of Bhakti?
142.x: Tulsidas worshipped God with form (Saguna); Kabir, Nanak and Ravidas were Nirguna saints.

142.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: North India — Surdas — Sur Sagar in Braj
Punjab — Guru Nanak — Punjabi in Gurmukhi
142.x: Palkuriki Somanatha is associated with Telugu in Andhra, including the Basava Puranam. Marathi is associated with saints such as Namdev, Eknath and Tukaram.
142.tq: Check the region–language pairing before checking the saint or work.
xs: Pair **(3)** is NOT correct: **Palkuriki Somanatha** wrote in **Telugu**, not Marathi.
His work is the **Basava Puranam**.
**Surdas — Sur Sagar in Braj**, **Guru Nanak — Punjabi (Gurmukhi)**, **Namdev — Marathi** are correct.
xa: Palkuriki Somanatha helped bring **Veerashaivism** to Andhra.
Other Marathi saints: **Eknath**, **Tukaram**, **Narhari**.

142.s: Who wrote the Basava Puranam in Telugu?
142.x: Palkuriki Somanatha wrote the Basava Puranam.

142.s: Akkamahadevi was a 12th-century woman saint of which region?
142.x: Akkamahadevi was a 12th-century woman saint of Karnataka.
xa: Other women saints: **Mirabai**, **Daya Bai**.
**Andal** = the only female Alvar.

142.s: Veerashaivism reached Andhra through Palkuriki Somanatha and whom?
142.x: Veerashaivism reached Andhra through Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya and Palkuriki Somanatha.
xa: **Palnadu**: **Veeravaishnavism** + the Chapakudu.
**Panditaradhya** is also among the **Panchacharyas**.

142.s: Under which Kalachuri king was Basavanna head of the treasury at Kalyana?
142.x: Basavanna served Kalachuri king Bijjala at Kalyana and set up the Anubhava Mantapa.

142.s: In which language were the vachanas of the Virashaiva saints composed?
142.x: Vachanas are short Kannada devotional sayings, signed Kudalasangamadeva by Basavanna.

142.s: Who presided over the Anubhava Mantapa, the assembly of sharanas?
142.x: Allama Prabhu presided over the Anubhava Mantapa set up by Basavanna.

142.s: Who led the Virashaiva (Lingayat) movement in Karnataka?
142.x: Basavanna, treasury head at Kalyana under Bijjala, led the Virashaiva movement with his Kannada vachanas.

142.s: With which signature (ankita) were Basavanna's vachanas signed?
142.x: Basavanna's vachanas are signed Kudalasangamadeva.

142.s: Where was Basavanna born?
142.x: Basavanna is linked to Bagewadi, Shankaracharya to Kaladi, Ramanuja to Sriperumbudur and Chaitanya to Nabadwip.
n: Adi Shankaracharya was born in Kaladi. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #80 · pp 159-160]
Ramanujacharya was born in Sriperumbudur. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #80 · pp 159-160]
Basavanna was born in Bagewadi. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #80 · pp 159-160]
Chaitanya Mahaprabhu was born in Nabadwip. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #80 · pp 159-160]
xa: **Kabir** — **Varanasi**; **Guru Nanak** — **Talwandi**.
**Ramananda** — **Prayag**; **Tulsidas** — **Rajapur**.
**Mirabai** — **Kudki**; **Surdas** — **Sihi**.

142.s: In which part of India did the Nathpanthis, Siddhas and Yogis mainly make devotional religion popular?
142.x: They made devotional religion popular in Northern India; their practices included hatha yoga, meditation and renunciation.
xa: Leading figures: **Gorakhnath**, **Matsyendranath**.
They used the **vernacular** and influenced **Kabir's nirguna idiom**.

142.s: Gorakhnath and Matsyendranath were leading figures of which group?
142.x: Gorakhnath and Matsyendranath were leading figures of the Nathpanthis, Siddhas and Yogis, who criticised caste, ritualism and orthodox religion.
xa: Practices: **hatha yoga, meditation, renunciation**.
They popularised devotion in **Northern India** (BPSC **2023**).

142.s: What did the Nathpanthis, Siddhas and Yogis mainly practise?
142.x: They practised hatha yoga, meditation and renunciation and criticised ritualism and caste.

142.s: Who discovered the manuscript of the Charyapada, the songs of the Buddhist Siddhacharyas, in the royal library of Nepal?
142.x: Haraprasad Shastri found the Charyapada palm-leaf manuscript in the Nepal royal court library in 1907.

143.s:
Consider the following statements.

I. ‘Bijak’ is a composition of the teaching of Saint Dadu Dayal.

II. The philosophy of Pushti Marg was propounded by Madhvacharya.
Which of the statements(s) given above is/are correct?
143.x: Both statements are wrong: the Bijak is the sacred book of Kabir's followers, not of Dadu Dayal, and Pushtimarg was propounded by Vallabhacharya, not Madhvacharya (who founded Dvaita).

143.s: Which among the following female Bhakti Saint wrote commentaries on Vedantasutra in Sanskrit?
143.x: Of the options only Vallabhacharya wrote a Sanskrit commentary on the Vedanta (Brahma) Sutra, the Anubhashya. Lalleshwari (Lal Ded) composed Kashmiri vakhs, Tulsidas wrote in Awadhi, and Ramananda left no accepted Brahma Sutra commentary; the word "female" in this version of the stem is an error, as no woman saint among the options wrote such a commentary.

143.s: Choose the correct pair of the following:
143.x: Ramanujacharya – Vishishtadvaita is the correct pair. Vallabhacharya taught Shuddhadvaita (not Jainism), Shankaracharya Advaita (not Vaishnavism) and Madhvacharya Dvaita (not Advaita).

143.s: Which of the following statements regarding the Bhakti Movement is not correct?
o: Nimbarka propounded the philosophy of Dvaitadvaita
143.x: Madhvacharya propounded Dvaita, a Saguna Vaishnava devotion, not Nirguna bhakti, so that statement is wrong. Vallabha founded Pushtimarg, Nimbarka taught Dvaitadvaita and Ramananda Rama bhakti.

143.s: Who among the following is not related to the Philosophy of Vedanta?
143.x: Abhinavagupta was a Kashmir Shaiva philosopher, not a Vedantin; Shankaracharya, Ramanuja and Madhva were the great Vedanta teachers.

143.s: “Shuddha Advaitvad” was propounded by –
143.x: Shuddhadvaita (pure non-dualism) was propounded by Vallabhacharya, who developed the views of Vishnuswami; Madhva taught Dvaita and Ramanuja Vishishtadvaita.

143.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched? Bhakti Saint Philosophy
143.x: Ramanuja propounded Vishishtadvaita (qualified non-dualism). Kevaladvaita/Advaita belongs to Shankara, not Ramananda or Chaitanya (Achintya Bhedabheda), and Avadhuta is not Shankara's philosophy.

143.s: Who propagated pushtimarga, a religion of grace?
143.x: Pushtimarga, the 'path of grace' centred on child Krishna (Shrinathji), was founded by Vallabhacharya; Chaitanya founded Gaudiya Vaishnavism and Vyasaraya was a Dvaita scholar.

143.s: Who propagated Pushtimarga, a religion of grace? for
143.x: Pushtimarga, the 'path of grace' centred on child Krishna (Shrinathji), was founded by Vallabhacharya; Chaitanya founded Gaudiya Vaishnavism and Vyasaraya was a Dvaita scholar.

143.s: The followers of Ramanuja are known as-
143.x: The followers of Ramanuja, the Sri Vaishnavas, are Vaishnavas (devotees of Vishnu-Narayana).

143.s: Which Philosophy propagated by Shri Raghavendra Swami?
143.x: Raghavendra Swami of Mantralayam was a saint of Madhvacharya's Dvaita (dualist) school, not of Advaita or Shivadvaita.

143.s: Who founded Dvaitadvaita (Bhedabheda)?
143.x: Nimbarka founded Dvaitadvaita; Madhva founded Dvaita and Ramanuja Vishishtadvaita.

143.s: Which philosophy is associated with Chaitanya?
143.x: Chaitanya's school is Achintya Bhedabheda (Gaudiya Vaishnavism).

143.s: Who founded the Dvaita school of philosophy?
143.x: Madhvacharya founded Dvaita (dualism); Ramanuja founded Vishishtadvaita and Nimbarka Dvaitadvaita.

143.s: Who propounded Vishishtadvaita (qualified non-dualism)?
143.x: Vishishtadvaita was founded by Ramanuja in the 11th century.

143.s:
Match the following:
List-I (School)
A. Advaita
B. Vishishtadvaita
C. Dvaita
D. Shuddhadvaita
List-II (Founder)
1. Madhvacharya
2. Vallabhacharya
3. Shankaracharya
4. Ramanuja
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
143.x: Advaita - Shankara; Vishishtadvaita - Ramanuja; Dvaita - Madhva; Shuddhadvaita - Vallabha.

143.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
143.x: Dvaitadvaita was founded by Nimbarka. Vallabhacharya founded Shuddhadvaita or Pushtimarga.
143.tq: Distinguish closely named philosophical schools by their founders.
xs: Pair **(1)** is NOT correct: **Dvaitadvaita** belongs to **Nimbarka**, not Vallabhacharya.
**Vallabhacharya** taught **Shuddhadvaita** (pure non-dualism).
**Madhva — Dvaita**, **Ramanuja — Vishishtadvaita**, **Shankara — Advaita** are correct.
xa: ⚠ Advaita = Shankara; Vishishtadvaita = Ramanuja; Dvaita = Madhva; Dvaitadvaita = Nimbarka; Shuddhadvaita = Vallabha.
Shankara = Advaita was asked in **APPSC-G1 2012**.

143.s: Which one of the following statements about Madhvacharya is correct?
o: He centred his teaching on devotion to Radha-Krishna.
He taught that God and souls are eternally distinct.
He identified his philosophy with pure non-dualism.
He propounded Nirguna devotion as the central path.
143.x: Madhvacharya’s Dvaita philosophy maintains that God, identified with Vishnu, and individual souls are eternally distinct. His devotional emphasis is Saguna bhakti.
143.tq: Catch the reversed or swapped teaching associated with a confusable acharya.
xs: **Madhvacharya** taught that **God and souls are eternally distinct** — option **(2)**.
This is **Dvaita** (dualism), with **Saguna** devotion to **Vishnu**.
**Radha-Krishna** = Nimbarka; **pure non-dualism** = Vallabha; ⚠ "Madhva propounded **Nirguna** bhakti" is wrong (RPSC **2024**).
xa: His centre: **Udupi** Krishna Matha.
Disciple **Narahari Tirtha** spread Dvaita in Andhra-Kalinga from **Srikurmam**.

143.s: Which of the following correctly describes Vallabhacharya's teaching?
o: Dvaita, with exclusive emphasis on ritual sacrifice
Shuddhadvaita, with Pushtimarg and Vatsalya bhakti
Vishishtadvaita, with rejection of Krishna worship
Advaita, with salvation through knowledge alone
143.x: Vallabhacharya taught Shuddhadvaita or pure non-dualism. He advocated Pushtimarg, the path of grace, Vatsalya bhakti towards child Krishna and householder life for devotees.
143.tq: Combine school, path and devotional emphasis to identify the precise option.
xs: Vallabhacharya taught **Shuddhadvaita**, with **Pushtimarg** and **Vatsalya bhakti** — option **(2)**.
Pushtimarg = "**path of grace**"; vatsalya bhakti to **child Krishna**; **householder life** for devotees.
xa: He set up **84** Pushtimarg centres.
Pushtimarga = Vallabhacharya (APPSC-G1 **2018**).

143.s: Which acharya's tradition worshipped child Krishna along with Radha-Krishna?
143.x: Vallabha worshipped child Krishna and Radha-Krishna; Ramananda worshipped Rama, Chaitanya Krishna and Nimbarka Radha-Krishna.
xa: Chaitanya founded **Gaudiya Vaishnavism**.
Nimbarka's centre: **Brindavan**.

143.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?

Acharya — Teaching emphasis
o: Vallabhacharya — Rejection of householder life for devotees
Ramanuja — Salvation through intense devotion to Vishnu
Madhvacharya — God and souls are identical
Nimbarka — Exclusive emphasis on Vedic ritual
143.x: Ramanuja taught that salvation is attained through intense devotion or prapatti to Vishnu. Madhva upheld the eternal distinction between God and souls, while Vallabha accepted householder life for devotees.
143.tq: Use the teaching-emphasis comparison and reject reversed philosophical positions.
xs: **Ramanuja — salvation through intense devotion (prapatti) to Vishnu** — option **(2)**.
**Vallabha** accepted **householder life** for devotees; **Madhva** held God and souls **eternally distinct**.
xa: For Ramanuja the best means of salvation is **devotion**, not Vedas, logic or meditation (UPSC **2022**).
**Nimbarka** emphasised devotion to **Radha-Krishna**.

143.s:
Consider the following statements about Madhvacharya:
1. He founded Dvaita (dualism).
2. He preached Nirguna bhakti.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
143.x: Madhva founded Dvaita and taught Saguna bhakti, not Nirguna.

143.s: Who taught salvation through prapatti (intense devotion) to Vishnu?
143.x: Ramanuja taught salvation through prapatti to Vishnu, in reaction against Advaita.

143.s: Vallabhacharya developed the views of which earlier teacher?
143.x: Vallabha's Shuddhadvaita developed the views of Vishnuswami.

143.s: With whom is Gaudiya Vaishnavism associated?
143.x: Gaudiya Vaishnavism was associated with Chaitanya; Pushtimarga with Vallabhacharya and Sri Vaishnava with Ramanuja.
xa: **Brahma (Madhva) Sampradaya** = Madhvacharya.
**Nimbarka (Sanaka) Sampradaya** = Nimbarka.

143.s: By what other name is Pushtimarga, the "path of grace", known?
143.x: Pushtimarga is the Vallabha Sampradaya; Vallabhacharya set up 84 Pushtimarg centres.
xa: Pushtimarga ("a religion of grace") = Vallabhacharya (APPSC-G1 **2018**).
"**Shashti Margam**" in some notes is a misprint for Pushti Margam.

143.s: Who wrote the Vedanta Parijata Saurabha?
143.x: Nimbarka wrote Vedanta Parijata Saurabha; Vallabhacharya wrote Anubhashya, Subodhini and Vedanta Rahasyam.
xa: **Sri Bhashya** = Ramanuja.
**Tattva Teeka**, **Nyaya Siddhanjanam** = Vedanta Desika.

143.s: Who founded the Brahma Sampradaya?
143.x: The Brahma (Madhva) Sampradaya was founded by Madhvacharya.

143.s: Who wrote the Sri Bhashya on the Brahma Sutras?
143.x: Sri Bhashya is Ramanuja's work; Anubhashya is by Vallabhacharya.

143.s: Who wrote the Anubhashya and Subodhini?
143.x: Anubhashya, Subodhini and Vedanta Rahasyam are works of Vallabhacharya.

143.s: How many Pushtimarg centres did Vallabhacharya set up?
143.x: Vallabhacharya set up 84 Pushtimarg centres.

143.s: Which philosophy did Ramanuja preach?
143.x: Ramanuja preached Vishishtadvaita and stressed the worship of Narayana and Lakshmi.
xa: He is the **first true exponent** of Bhakti; centre **Srirangam**.
The **Statue of Equality** at Hyderabad honours him.
⚠ Ramanuja = **Vishishtadvaita**; Basavanna = **Shakti Vishishtadvaita**.

143.s: Which philosophy did Nimbarka preach?
143.x: Nimbarka preached Dvaitadvaita; Ramanuja preached Vishishtadvaita and Madhva Dvaita.
xa: Shankara (Kaladi, **AD 788-820**) = **forerunner** of the Bhakti cult.
**Vedanta Desika** led Vishishtadvaita in that era.

143.s: Which philosophy did Shankaracharya preach?
143.x: Shankaracharya taught Advaita (non-dualism); Madhva taught Dvaita and Ramanuja Vishishtadvaita.

143.s: Who among the following was the first Bhakti saint to use Hindi for the propagation of his message?
143.x: Ramananda is regarded as the first Bhakti saint to preach in Hindi (the vernacular) instead of Sanskrit; Kabir, Dadu and Tulsidas came after him and in his line.

143.s: Who among the following was the first Bhakti Saint to use Hindi for the propagation of his message?
143.x: Ramananda is regarded as the first Bhakti saint to preach in Hindi (the vernacular) instead of Sanskrit; Kabir, Dadu and Tulsidas came after him and in his line.

143.s: The famous medieval Saint Ramananda was born at
143.x: By tradition Ramananda was born at Prayag (1299) in a Kanyakubja Brahmin family and later made Varanasi his centre (NextGen gives Varanasi as his birthplace). Lucknow and Kanpur have no link with him.

143.s: Who among the following Saints of the medieval Age India was born in Prayag?
143.x: By tradition Ramananda was born at Prayag (1299) in a Kanyakubja Brahmin family and later made Varanasi his centre (NextGen gives Varanasi as his birthplace). Raidas was born in Varanasi, Tulsidas at Rajapur and Kumbhandas near Mathura.

143.s: Kabir was disciple of –
143.x: Kabir was the foremost of Ramananda's twelve disciples; Ramanuja lived centuries earlier, Chaitanya was in Bengal and Tukaram in 17th-century Maharashtra.

143.s: ‘Let no man ask a man’s sect or caste’ whose dictum was this?”
143.x: 'Let no man ask a man's sect or caste' (jati-panti puchhe nahin koi) is Ramananda's dictum; his disciples came from all castes and creeds.

143.s: Who of the following leaders of the Bhakthi movement was greatly influenced by Islam?
143.x: Of the options, Ramananda (Ramanadhan) preached monotheism and the equality of all castes and took disciples like Kabir; this is the reading of him as influenced by Islam. Ramanuja and the Nayanars lived before Islam had any such influence, and Chaitanya's Krishna bhakti came from the Bhagavata tradition.

143.s: Who was Ramananda's principal object of devotion?
143.x: Ramananda worshipped Rama; child Krishna was the focus of Vallabha.
xa: Ramananda **replaced Vishnu worship with devotion to Rama**.
**Chaitanya**'s deity: **Krishna**.

143.s: Where was Ramananda born, by tradition?
143.x: Ramananda was born at Prayag and made Varanasi his centre.

143.s: Which disciple of Ramananda was a barber by background?
143.x: Sena was a barber; Kabir was a weaver, Raidas a shoemaker and Dhanna a Jat cultivator.
xa: Other disciples: **Padmavati** (woman), **Pipa** (Rajput ruler).
Ramananda's dictum: "**Let no man ask a man's sect or caste.**"

143.s: Which one of the following statements correctly describes Ramananda’s social teaching?
o: He restricted Rama worship to Kanyakubja Brahmins.
He upheld Brahmin supremacy as essential to devotion.
He accepted caste but rejected Vaishnavism.
He rejected caste distinctions and Brahmin supremacy.
143.x: Ramananda rejected caste and Brahmin supremacy. His dictum was “Let no man ask a man’s sect or caste,” and he is regarded as the first medieval reformer to denounce caste outright.
143.tq: Test the reformer’s central social message against extreme and reversed alternatives.
xs: **Ramananda rejected caste and Brahmin supremacy** — option **(4)**.
His saying: "**Let no man ask a man's sect or caste.**"
xa: He was the **first medieval reformer to denounce caste outright**.
Disciples included **Padmavati** (a woman) and **Pipa** (a Rajput ruler).

143.s: How many disciples did Ramananda have, by tradition?
143.x: Ramananda had 12 disciples, Kabir being one of them.

143.s: Who was the woman disciple of Ramananda?
143.x: Padmavati was Ramananda's woman disciple.

143.s: Yatis in Vaishnav tradition have to wear this
143.x: Sri Vaishnava ascetics (yatis) of Ramanuja's order carry the tridanda (triple staff), unlike the single staff of Advaita monks.

143.s: Who made the Paancharatra Agama popular?
143.x: Ramanujacharya, following Yamunacharya, defended the Pancharatra Agama as Vedic and made it the basis of Sri Vaishnava temple worship; Madhva, Nimbarka and Ramadasu did not.

143.s: On the occasion of 1000th birthday of which saint did Prime Minister Narendra Modi recently release a Stamp?
143.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Fisheries in A.P. Fisheries Serv
143.x: On 1 May 2017 PM Modi released a commemorative stamp on the 1000th birth anniversary of Sri Ramanujacharya (born 1017 at Sriperumbudur).

143.s: Which is the birth place of Ramanuja?
143.x: Ramanuja was born at Sriperumbudur in Tamil Nadu. Kaladi was Shankara's birthplace, Udupi Madhva's centre and Basava Kalyani Basavanna's.

143.s: Shriperumbudur is a birth place of
143.x: Sriperumbudur in Tamil Nadu is the birthplace of Ramanujacharya; Shankara was born at Kaladi and Basavanna at Bagewadi.

143.s: The world's second tallest statue in the sitting pose of Ramanuja was inaugurated by the Prime Minister of India at Hyderabad recently. Which one of the following statements correctly represents the teachings of Ramanuja
o: The best means of salvation was devotion.
Vedas are eternal, self-existent and wholly authoritative.
Logical arguments were essential means for the highest bliss.
Salvation was to be obtained through meditation.
143.x: Ramanuja taught that the best means of salvation is devotion (bhakti, prapatti) to Vishnu. That the Vedas are eternal and self-existent is a Mimamsa view; logic and meditation are other paths.

143.s: In opposition to which philosophy did the Bhakti acharyas give Bhakti a philosophical base?
143.x: The acharyas provided a philosophical basis for Bhakti against Advaita and helped open temple worship to lower groups.
xa: **Ramananda** admitted disciples like **Kabir, Raidas, Sena, Dhanna**.
Ramanuja taught any eager student without the customary long wait.

143.s: Who is regarded as the first true exponent of Bhakti?
143.x: Shankara was the forerunner (knowledge); Ramanuja was the first true exponent of Bhakti (devotion).

143.s: Vedanta Desika is associated with which sub-sect of Sri Vaishnavism?
143.x: Sri Vaishnavism split into Vadakalai, associated with Vedanta Desika, and Tengalai; both remained Vishishtadvaita.
xa: ⚠ Trap: calling Tengalai "**Dvaita-influenced**" is wrong.
Vedanta Desika spread Vadakalai in Andhra in the **14th c.**

143.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Sri Vaishnava split?
o: Vadakalai was led by Vedanta Desika
Both Vadakalai and Tengalai were Vishishtadvaita
143.x: Tengalai was not Dvaita-influenced; both branches remained Vishishtadvaita.

143.s: Who among the following was born at Sriperumbudur?
143.x: Sriperumbudur was the birthplace of Ramanuja; Shankaracharya is linked to Kaladi and Madhva to Udupi.
xa: Nimbarka's school: **Dvaitadvaita**; deity **Radha-Krishna**.
Kaladi lies in **Malabar, Kerala**.

143.s: Which was the main centre of Ramanuja?
143.x: Ramanuja, born at Sriperumbudur, had his main centre at Srirangam.

143.s: In Andhra, Sri Vaishnavism was patronised by the Palnati Haihayas and which other dynasty?
143.x: The Velanati Cholas and the Palnati Haihayas patronised Sri Vaishnavism in Andhra.
xa: It inspired **Brahmanayudu's Veera Vaishnava** movement in Palnadu.
It gave **Panchamas temple entry**.

143.s: Whom does the Statue of Equality at Hyderabad commemorate?
143.x: The Statue of Equality at Hyderabad commemorates Ramanuja and his message of spiritual and social equality.
143.tq: Use the monument–person association rather than confusing neighbouring Bhakti teachers.
xs: The **Statue of Equality** at Hyderabad honours **Ramanuja** — option **(4)**.
It is the world's **second-tallest sitting statue**, inaugurated by the PM (UPSC **2022**).
xa: Ramanuja gave **Panchamas temple entry**.
He taught any eager student **without the customary long wait**.

143.s: Ramanuja is credited with installing which deity at Tirupati?
143.x: Ramanuja is credited with ordering temple worship at Tirumala and installing Govindaraja at Tirupati.

143.s: Ramanuja is held to be an incarnation of whom?
143.x: Ramanuja, called Ilaya Azhwar, is held to be an incarnation of Adisesha/Lakshmana.

143.s: Which movement of Palnati Brahmanaidu in Andhra was inspired by Ramanuja's Vishishtadvaita?
143.x: Ramanuja's Vishishtadvaita inspired Palnati Brahmanaidu's Veera Vaishnava movement, with its common dining (Chapakudu).

143.s: To which group did Ramanuja give temple entry?
143.x: Ramanuja gave the Panchamas temple entry.

143.s: By which name is Ramanuja also called?
143.x: Ramanuja is called Ilaya Azhwar and held to be an incarnation of Adisesha.

143.s: Who was the Guru of Sankaracharya?
143.x: Adi Shankaracharya's guru was Govinda Bhagavatpada, himself a disciple of Gaudapada. Padmapada was Shankara's own disciple; Kumarila Bhatta was a Mimamsa scholar.

143.s: Who was the founder of Advaita Philosophy?

145.x: Veerabhadra Vijayam was Bammera Potana's first work, written at the request of his guru Ivaturi Somanaradhya; it is not by Srinatha, Tikkana or Errapragada.

145.s: According to some opinions, Vontimitta is the birthplace of?
145.x: Most accounts make Bammera (Jangaon dt.) Potana's birthplace, but one tradition places it at Vontimitta in Kadapa district.

145.s: In the opinion of some, Ottimitta is whose birthplace?
145.x: Ottimitta (Kadapa) is held by some to be the birthplace of Bammera Pothana, author of the Andhra Mahabhagavatam. (Moved to the Bhakti in Andhra row.)

145.s: Who wrote the Bhogini Dandakam, the first Telugu Dandakam?
145.x: The first Telugu Dandakam was Potana's Bhogini Dandakam.
xa: **Bhogini Dandakam** is about **Sarvajna Singabhupala** and **Bhogini**.
Other FIRSTs: **Sri Venkateswara Satakam** (Annamacharya) = first Telugu **Shringara Satakam**; **Vrushadhipa Satakam** = first full-featured satakam.
**Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya** = originator of the **Sataka form** in Telugu.

145.s: Veerabhadra Vijayam, written at the request of Ivaturi Somanaradhya, is regarded as the first work of which poet?
145.x: The cited accounts regard Veerabhadra Vijayam as Potana's first work, written at the request of his guru Ivaturi Somanaradhya.
xa: Potana's other works: **Andhra Maha Bhagavatamu**, **Bhogini Dandakam**, **Narayana Satakam** (lost).
Potana's title: **Sahaja Panditudu**.

145.s: To whom did Potana dedicate his Andhra Maha Bhagavatamu?
145.x: The Andhra Maha Bhagavatamu, the Telugu Bhagavata Purana, was offered to Lord Rama; Potana wrote eight of its twelve skandhas.
xa: Other skandhas: **Bopparaju Gangana** (5th), **Erchuri Singana** (6th), **Veligandala Narayana** (11th-12th).
**C.P. Brown** printed Andhra Maha Bhagavatamu in **1840**.
Potana vowed **never to dedicate his work to a human king**.

145.s: Which one of the following pairs of titles is associated with Bammera Potana?
145.x: Potana was known by the titles Sahaja Panditudu and Nigarva Chudamani.
145.tq: Use exact title-pair recognition to eliminate titles belonging to other poets.
xs: Potana's titles were **Sahaja Panditudu** and **Nigarva Chudamani** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Andhra Kavita Pitamaha** is **Allasani Peddana's** title; **Padakavita Pitamaha** is **Annamacharya's**.
**Kavibrahma** is **Tikkana's** title.
xa: Potana (c. **1450-1510**) was a native of **Bammera** (Janagama district, Telangana).
He was a contemporary of **Srinatha** (Kavi Sarvabhauma); some notes make him Srinatha's brother-in-law.
Other titles: **Nannaya** = Adikavi; **Errapragada** = Prabandha Parameswara.

145.s: Bammera Potana refused to dedicate his work to which ruler?
145.x: Potana vowed never to dedicate his work to a human king, refused Sarvajna Singabhupala of Rachakonda and offered the Bhagavatam to Sri Rama.

145.s: Of the 12 skandhas of the Andhra Maha Bhagavatamu, how many did Potana write?
145.x: Potana wrote 8 of the 12 skandhas; others such as Bopparaju Gangana and Erchuri Singana completed the rest.

145.s: In which year did C.P. Brown print Potana's Andhra Maha Bhagavatamu?
145.x: C.P. Brown printed the Bhagavatamu in 1840; his Verses of Vemana came out in 1829.

145.s: Which place in Kadapa district is held by one tradition to be the birthplace of Bammera Potana?
145.x: Most place Potana at Bammera, but one tradition says he was born at Vontimitta (Ontimitta) in Kadapa.

145.s: Bammera, in present Janagama district of Telangana, is the native place of which poet?
145.x: Bammera Potana, author of the Andhra Maha Bhagavatamu, takes his name from his native village Bammera.

145.s: Who was the guru of Bammera Potana, at whose request he wrote Veerabhadra Vijayam?
145.x: Potana wrote his first work, Veerabhadra Vijayam, at the request of his guru Ivaturi Somanaradhya.

145.s: Who among the following was NOT a co-author of the Andhra Maha Bhagavatamu besides Potana?
145.x: Bopparaju Gangana (5th skandha), Erchuri Singana (6th) and Veligandala Narayana (11th-12th) completed the skandhas Potana did not write; Nachana Somana was not one of them.

145.s: Who wrote the 5th skandha of the Andhra Maha Bhagavatamu?
145.x: Bopparaju Gangana wrote the 5th skandha; Erchuri Singana wrote the 6th and Veligandala Narayana the 11th-12th.

145.s: First Telugu poetess who wrote Ramayana
145.x: Atukuri Molla (16th century, potter family of Gopavaram) was the first Telugu poetess to write the Ramayana (Molla Ramayanam). Timmakka wrote Subhadra Kalyanam.

145.s: ' Madhura Vijayam ' was composed by:
145.x: Madhura Vijayam (Veera Kamparaya Charitam), a Sanskrit poem, was written by Gangadevi, wife of the Sangama prince Kumara Kampana, on his conquest of Madurai.

145.s: Identify the wrong match. (Author) (Literary Work)
145.x: Gangadevi wrote Madhura Vijayam, not Marichi Parinayam, which is by Mohanangi, Krishnadevaraya's daughter. Molla–Ramayanam, Timmakka–Subhadra Kalyanam and Tirumalamba–Varadambika Parinayam are correct.

145.s: What does Madhura Vijayam, also known as Veera Kamparaya Charitam, describe?
o: The conquest of Madurai by Kumara Kampana
The marriage of Achyuta Deva Raya and Varadambika
The legends of Rama in Telugu
The life of Venkateswara at Tirumala
145.x: Gangadevi's Sanskrit work Madhura Vijayam describes her husband Kumara Kampana's conquest of Madurai.
145.tq: Link the literary work to its historical subject rather than merely its author.
xs: **Madhura Vijayam** describes the **conquest of Madurai by Kumara Kampana** — option **(1)** is correct.
It was written in **Sanskrit** by **Gangadevi**, a **Sangama princess**, about her husband.
The marriage of Achyuta Deva Raya is **Varadambika Parinayam** (Oduva Tirumalamba).
xa: ⚠ PYQ (APPSC-G2 2023 and 2025): wrong match = **Gangadevi — Marichi Parinayam**.
**Molla Ramayanam** gives Rama's story in simple, elegant **Telugu**.

145.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Gatha Saptasati was authored by Hala.
Madhura Vijayam was authored by Gangadevi.
145.x: Option C is incorrect: Amuktamalyada was written by Krishnadevaraya; Tirumalamba wrote Varadambika Parinayam. Hala wrote Gatha Saptasati, Gangadevi Madhura Vijayam and Ketana Vignanesvaram.
145.tq: Match each work with its author.
n: Gatha Saptasati was written by Hala. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 9-11]
Vignanesvaram was written by Ketana. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 9-11]
Madhura Vijayam was written by Gangadevi. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 9-11]
Amuktamalyada was written by Krishnadevaraya. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 9-11]
xs: The incorrect statement: **Amuktamalyada** was authored by **Tirumalamba** — option **(3)**.
**Amuktamalyada** was written by **Krishnadevaraya**; **Allasani Peddana** was his court poet.
**Tirumalamba** wrote **Varadambika Parinayam**.
**Gangadevi** wrote **Madhura Vijayam** — option 2 is correct.
xa: Madhura Vijayam is in **Sanskrit**: Kumara Kampana's conquest of **Madurai**.
⚠ PYQ (APPSC-G2 **2023** and **2025**): wrong match = **Gangadevi - Marichi Parinayam**.
**Molla** = first Telugu woman poet to translate the Ramayana; **Timmakka** = first woman poet of the Andhra region.

145.s: Atukuri Molla, author of Molla Ramayanam, belonged to which community?
145.x: Molla came from the potter community and was the first Telugu woman to translate the Ramayana.

145.s: Which of the following was written by Tallapaka Timmakka?
145.x: Timmakka wrote Subhadra Kalyanam; Molla wrote Molla Ramayanam and Vengamamba Venkatachala Mahatyamu.
xa: ⚠ **Trap:** the **2025** answer key marked **Molla-Ramayanam** instead, but the explanation confirms Molla-Ramayanam is correct.
**Gangadevi** was a **Sangama princess**; husband **Kumara Kampana**.

145.s: Who wrote Amuktamalyada?
145.x: Amuktamalyada is by Krishnadevaraya, not Tirumalamba; Allasani Peddana was his court poet.

145.s: Who was the first Telugu woman to translate the Ramayana?
145.x: Atukuri Molla, of the potter community, wrote Molla Ramayanam, the first Ramayana translated by a Telugu woman.

145.s: Who is the author of Marichi Parinayam?
145.x: Marichi Parinayam was written by Mohanangi, the daughter of Krishnadevaraya, not by Gangadevi.

145.s: Mohanangi, author of Marichi Parinayam, was the daughter of which ruler?
145.x: Mohanangi, who wrote Marichi Parinayam, was Krishnadevaraya's daughter.

145.s: Whose marriage is described in Varadambika Parinayam by Oduva Tirumalamba?
145.x: Oduva Tirumalamba's Sanskrit work Varadambika Parinayam describes the marriage of Achyuta Deva Raya and Varadambika.

145.s: Who wrote the Sanskrit work Raghunathabhyudayam?
145.x: Raghunathabhyudayam is a Sanskrit work of the woman poet Ramabhadramba.

145.s: Who wrote a treatise predicting many bad consequences and unexpected events that will happen in Kali Yuga? What is the name of that book?
145.x: Potuluri Veerabrahmendra Swamy's Kalagnanam foretells the evils and unexpected events of the Kali Yuga. Vemana's satakam is satire, not prophecy.

145.s: Vemana's verses are mostly composed in which metre and commonly end with which refrain?
145.x: Vemana mainly used the Ataveladi metre, and his verses commonly conclude with the refrain “Vishwadabhirama Vinura Vema.”
145.tq: Pair the distinctive metre with its recurring refrain rather than recognising either in isolation.
xs: Vemana mostly used the **Ataveladi** metre with the refrain **"Vishwadabhirama Vinura Vema"** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Dvipada** is the metre of works like **Basava Puranam** and **Annamacharya Charitra**, not Vemana's verses.
xa: His verses are short, **satakam-style**, in **colloquial Telugu**.
**Dating disputed:** **17th c.** vs **14th-15th c.** — learn both.

145.s: Which one of the following was the social message of Veerabrahmendra Swamy?
o: He condemned caste differences and accepted disciples across castes and faiths.
He rejected vernacular literature in favour of Sanskrit.
He supported ritual hierarchy as the basis of social order.
He defended caste distinctions and restricted discipleship to one community.
145.x: Veerabrahmendra Swamy strongly condemned caste differences and accepted disciples from different castes and faiths, including Siddaiah, a Muslim.
145.tq: Apply the reformer’s stated social principles to a concrete description.
xs: Veerabrahmendra Swamy **condemned caste differences** and **accepted disciples across castes and faiths** — option **(1)** is correct.
His disciple **Siddaiah** was a **Muslim**, so options (3) and (4) are the opposite of his message.
xa: His prophecies are in **Kalagnanam**.
He is paired with **Vemana** as Andhra's anti-caste voices.

145.s: For what is Vemana's poetry chiefly known?
o: criticism of caste, superstition and empty ritual
145.x: Vemana criticised superstition, empty ritual, idol worship and hypocrisy and advocated humanism and equality.
xa: **C.P. Brown** edited and translated his verses as **Verses of Vemana** (**1829**).
Vemana is paired with **Potuluri Veerabrahmam** as Andhra's **anti-caste voices**.

145.s: Who translated Vemana's verses into English as 'Verses of Vemana' (1829)?
145.x: C.P. Brown collected, edited and translated Vemana's verses, published in 1829.
xa: Refrain: **"Vishwadabhirama Vinura Vema"**.
⚠ C.P. Brown dates: Verses of Vemana **1829**; Andhra Maha Bhagavatamu **1840**.

145.s: What are the prophecies of Potuluri Veerabrahmendra Swamy known as?
145.x: Veerabrahmendra Swamy's work is Kalagnanam, a book of prophecies.

145.s: To which community did Siddaiah, a famous disciple of Veerabrahmendra Swamy, belong?
145.x: Veerabrahmendra Swamy condemned caste and had disciples of all faiths, including Siddaiah, a Muslim.

145.s:
Assertion (A): The Bhakti traditions did not uniformly uphold Brahmanical dominance.
Reason (R): Alvars, Nayanars and Basava, and in Andhra Vemana and Potuluri Veerabrahmam, criticised caste distinctions.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
145.x: These saints criticised caste and some promoted common dining of all castes, so the traditions challenged rather than upheld Brahmanical dominance.
xa: **Women saints**: **Andal**, **Karaikkal Ammaiyar**, **Akka Mahadevi**, **Atukuri Molla**.
Spread factors: **Chola patronage** and the **"little-great tradition"** fusion (Jagannath at Puri).

145.s: Which literary forms helped spread Bhakti ideas among common people in Andhra?
145.x: The satakam and dwipada forms helped communicate Bhakti ideas to common people in Telugu-speaking regions.
145.tq: Identify the regional literary forms associated with popular religious communication.
xs: The **Satakam and dwipada** forms spread bhakti to common people — option **(2)** is correct.
**Vachanas** are Kannada prose-poems and **Tevaram** is the Tamil Shaiva canon — not Andhra's forms.
xa: **Desi kavita**: simple native metres (**dwipada, ragada, manjari, kanda**) vs the Sanskritised **Marga** style.
**Palkuriki Somanatha** wrote **Basava Puranam** in simple Telugu **Dwipada** metre.

145.s:
Consider the following statements about the spread of Bhakti among common people:
1. Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and Malayalam replaced Sanskrit as its vehicles.
2. Persian and Arabic were its main vehicles in South India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
145.x: Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and Malayalam carried Bhakti ideas to common people instead of Sanskrit; Persian and Arabic were not its vehicles.

146.s: From the given pairs identify the incorrect pair –
146.x: 'Auliya' is a title (Friends of God, e.g. Nizamuddin Auliya), not a Sufi order, so 'Auliya–Madhya Pradesh' is the incorrect pair. Chishti–Delhi and Doab, Suhrawardi–Sindh and Firdausi–Bihar are correct (Firdausi is not part of the Chishti order).

146.s:
Assertion (A): The sponsor and the most prominent figure of the Chisti order of Sufis in India is Khwaja Moinuddin Chisti.
Reason (R): The Chisti order takes its name from a village, Chisti, in Ajmer. In the context of the above two statements, which one of the following is correct?
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not a correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
146.x: A is true: Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti is the founder and most prominent Chishti in India. R is false: the order takes its name from Chisht, a town near Herat in Afghanistan, not a village in Ajmer.

146.s: In June, 2012 a fierce fire damaged the sacred site of Dastagir Sahib in Srinagar. Who among the following is known as Dastgir Sahib?
146.x: Dastgir Sahib is Shaikh Abdul Qadir Jilani, founder of the Qadiri order, called Pir Dastagir; his Srinagar shrine was damaged by fire in 2012.

146.s: Which of the following Sufis regarded Krishna among the Auliyas :
146.x: Shah Muhammad Ghaus of Gwalior, the Shattari saint who studied yogic texts, counted Krishna among the Auliya. Shah Waliullah and Shah Abdul Aziz were orthodox reformers, and Khwaja Mir Dard a Naqshbandi poet.

146.s: Who was the founder of Chishtia Branch of Sufism?
146.x:
Most books and keys: Khwaja Abu (Ahmad) Abdal. Strictly: Abu Ishaq Shami first settled at Chisht and began the line; Abu Ahmad Abdal was his disciple and successor (old app notes 1:146 sub 5).
The Chishti order began at Chisht (Afghanistan) with Abu Ishaq Shami and his disciple Khwaja Abu Ahmad Abdal, whom the keys name as founder; Moinuddin Chishti brought it to India.

146.s:
Given below are two statements, one labelled as
Assertion (A) and the other labelled as
Reason (R).
Assertion (A) : The sponsor and the most prominent figure of the Chishti order of Sufis in India is Khwaja Muinuddin Chishti.
Reason (R) : The Chishti order takes its name from a village Chishti in Ajmer. In the context of the above two statements, which one of the following is correct?
o: Both (A) and (R) is individually true, and (R) is the
Both (A) and (R) is individually true, but (R) is not
146.x: A is true: Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti is the founder and most prominent Chishti in India. R is false: the order takes its name from Chisht, a town near Herat in Afghanistan, not a village in Ajmer.

146.s: The “Chishtia SufiOrder” in India was established by-
146.x: The Chishti order was established in India by Khwaja Muinuddin Chishti, who came in 1192 and settled at Ajmer. Ahmad Sirhindi was Naqshbandi and Bahauddin Zakariya Suhrawardi.

146.s: The spread of which of the following Sufisect was mostly limited to Sindh, Multan and Punjab?
146.x: The Suhrawardi order, established in India by Bahauddin Zakariya at Multan, was largely confined to Sindh, Multan and Punjab.

146.s: Who among the following does not belong to the Chishti order?
146.x: Shaikh Abdul Qadir Jilani founded the Qadiri order; Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki, Moinuddin and Nizamuddin Auliya were Chishtis.

146.s: Which one of the following was not a Chishti Sufi Saint?
146.x: Bahauddin Zakariya was the Suhrawardi saint of Multan; Moinuddin, Baba Farid and Nizamuddin Auliya were Chishtis.

146.s: Who was the founder of Chishti Branch of Sufism?
146.x:
Most books and keys: Khwaja Abu (Ahmad) Abdal. Strictly: Abu Ishaq Shami first settled at Chisht and began the line; Abu Ahmad Abdal was his disciple and successor (old app notes 1:146 sub 5).
The Chishti order began at Chisht (Afghanistan) with Abu Ishaq Shami and his disciple Khwaja Abu Ahmad Abdal, whom the keys name as founder; Moinuddin Chishti brought it to India.

146.s: Sheikh Bahauddin Zakariya belonged to which sect?
146.x: Shaikh Bahauddin Zakariya established the Suhrawardi silsila in India, with his khanqah at Multan; he was not Chishti, Rishi or Firdausi.

146.s: The idea of ‘Farr-i-Izadi’, on which the Mughal kingship was based, was first developed by which one of the following Sufi saints?
146.x: Abul Fazl based Mughal kingship on farr-i-izadi (divine light), an idea first developed by the Iranian Sufi Shihabuddin Suhrawardi (d. 1191). Nizamuddin Auliya avoided courts.

146.s: Bihar was the centre of which among the following Sufi order?
146.x: The Firdausi order, led by Sharfuddin Yahya Maneri, was centred in Bihar.

146.s: The most orthodox Sufiorder was –
146.x:
Official JPSC key: Suhrawardi. Verified fact: the Naqshbandi was the most orthodox order (NextGen IH Part 5 p.10; Singhania App.2).
The Naqshbandi order insisted on rigid Sharia, opposed sama and Akbar's liberal policy, and is the most orthodox order (official JPSC key: Suhrawardi).

146.s: Shaikh Bahauddin Zakaria belonged to which sect?
146.x: Shaikh Bahauddin Zakariya established the Suhrawardi silsila in India, with his khanqah at Multan; he was not Chishti, Rishi or Firdausi.

146.s: Which of the following order of Sufism was against music :
146.x: The Naqshbandi order was the most orthodox and opposed sama (music) and tomb visits; the Chishtis encouraged sama and the Suhrawardis also practised it.

146.s: Which of the following Silsilas of Sufism was against music?
146.x: The Naqshbandi order was the most orthodox and opposed sama (music) and tomb visits; the Chishtis encouraged sama and the Suhrawardis also practised it.

146.s: Point out from the following Sufis, who is from the Chishti Sufi Silsilah.
146.x: Saiyid Muhammad Gesudaraz of Gulbarga was a Chishti; Bahauddin Naqshband and Shah Waliullah were Naqshbandis and Bahauddin Zakariya a Suhrawardi.

146.s:
Match the Sufi Saints with their sects.

a. Sheik-Bahavuddin Jakariya - i. Suhrawardi

b. Hajarat-Fariddin-Masud - ii. Chisti

c. Shaniya Math Ulla - iii. Khadiri

d. Hajarat Tawvibilam - iv. Nakshabandi
146.x: Bahauddin Zakariya – Suhrawardi, Fariduddin Masud (Baba Farid) – Chishti, Shah Niamatullah – Qadiri and Khwaja Baqi Billah – Naqshbandi, giving a-(i), b-(ii), c-(iii), d-(iv).

146.s: Dara Shikoh was a follower of which Sufi order?
146.x: Dara Shikoh followed the Qadiri order, associated with Abdul Qadir Jilani.
xa: The Naqshbandi order came to India with **Babur** and stressed strict **Sharia**.
**Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi** (**Mujaddid Alf-i-Sani**), a Naqshbandi, criticised **Sulh-i-kul** and **Din-i-Ilahi**.
Later Naqshbandi scholars: **Shah Waliullah** and **Shah Abdul Aziz**.

146.s: Shahabuddin was associated with which Sufi order?
146.x: Shahabuddin belonged to the Suhrawardi order, which Bahauddin Zakariya brought to Multan. The Chishti, Naqshbandi and Qadiri orders were led by other saints.
146.tq: Link the saint to his Sufi order.
n: Muinuddin Chishti belonged to the Chishti order. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 132-134]
Ahmad Sirhindi belonged to the Naqshbandi order. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 132-134]
Dara Shukoh belonged to the Qadiri order. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 132-134]
Shahabuddin belonged to the Suhrawardi order. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 132-134]
Shahabuddin is associated with Suhrawardiya. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 132-134]
xs: **Shahabuddin** belonged to the **Suhrawardi order** (Suhrawardiya) — option **(2)**.
**Ahmad Sirhindi** belonged to the **Naqshbandi** order.
**Dara Shukoh** belonged to the **Qadiri** order.
xa: Naqshbandi founder: **Baha-ud-din Naqshband**; came to India with **Babur**; strict **Sharia**.
Qadiri founder: **Abdul Qadir Jilani**; stood for **Wahdat-ul-Wujud**.
Sirhindi (**Mujaddid Alf-i-Sani**) propounded **Wahdat-ul-Shuhud** and attacked **Din-i-Ilahi**.

146.s: Who founded the Naqshbandi Sufi order?
146.x: The Naqshbandi order was founded by Baha-ud-din Naqshband in the 14th century and came to India with Babur.

146.s: Who founded the Qadiri Sufi order?
146.x: The Qadiri order was founded by Abdul Qadir Jilani; Dara Shikoh followed it.

146.s: Who brought the Suhrawardi Sufi order to Multan?
146.x: The Suhrawardi order of Shahabuddin was brought to Multan by Bahauddin Zakariya.

146.s: Which Sufi order was strictly orthodox and opposed Akbar's Sulh-i-Kul?
146.x: The Naqshbandis opposed Sulh-i-Kul; the Chishtis kept aloof from the court, the Suhrawardis accepted royal service and the Shattaris absorbed yogic practices.
xa: ⚠ Chishti (aloof, sama) vs Suhrawardi (close to court) = **most-asked contrast**; Naqshbandi = the **orthodox pole**.
Naqshbandis also opposed **Shia influence**.

146.s: With whom did the Naqshbandi order originate in Central Asia?
146.x: The order began with Bahauddin Naqshband; in India it was associated with Khwaja Baqi Billah and Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi.
xa: Naqshbandis were the **most orthodox** (JPSC 2016); **opposed sama** and visits to saints' tombs.
Sirhindi was **imprisoned by Jahangir**.

146.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Muhammad Ghaus of Gwalior — Shattari order
146.x: Abdul Qadir Jilani founded the Qadiri order; he was not a Chishti saint. Shah Abdullah Shattari, Muhammad Ghaus and Sharafuddin Yahya Maneri are correctly associated with the orders shown.
146.tq: The wrong-founder trap distinguishes Abdul Qadir Jilani from the Chishti order.
xs: **Abdul Qadir Jilani — Chishti** is wrong — option **(1)** is the answer; he **founded the Qadiri order** (RPSC 2016).
**Shah Abdullah Shattari** founded the **Shattari** order; **Muhammad Ghaus of Gwalior** was Shattari.
**Sharafuddin Yahya Maneri** belongs to the **Firdausi** order of **Bihar**.
xa: Chishti founder at Chisht (Herat): **Khwaja Abu Ishaq Shami**; in India **Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti**.
**Mahdawi** order = **Syed Muhammad of Jaunpur**.

146.s: Regarding the Naqshbandi order, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: Bahauddin Zakariya established its main khanqah at Multan.
Bahauddin Naqshband himself established the order in India during Akbar's reign.
Moinuddin Chishti brought the order to India with Muhammad Ghori.
Khwaja Baqi Billah brought the order to India in the late sixteenth century.
146.x: Bahauddin Naqshband was the Central Asian founder and was revered by Babur, but he did not come to India. Khwaja Baqi Billah brought the Naqshbandi order to India in the late sixteenth century.
146.tq: Separate the original founder outside India from the person who introduced the order in India.
xs: **Khwaja Baqi Billah** brought the Naqshbandi order to India in the **late 16th c.** — option **(4)** is correct.
⚠ **Bahauddin Naqshband** founded it in Central Asia but **never came to India**.

146.s: In the Sufi scheme of ten stages (maqamat), which are the first and the last stages respectively?
146.x: The ten maqamat begin with Tauba (repentance) and end with Riza (submission), passing through Wara, Zuhd, Faqr, Sabr, Shukr, Khauf, Raja and Tawakkul. Zuhd, Faqr, Sabr and Shukr are intermediate stages, and 'Riza and Tauba' reverses the order.

**Zuhd, Faqr, Sabr, Shukr** are intermediate stages; option (4) reverses the order.
xa: The **10 stages**: Tauba → **Wara, Zuhd, Faqr, Sabr, Shukr, Khauf, Raja, Tawakkul** → Riza.

146.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Wahdat-ul-Wujud — Unity of Being; Haq and Khalq are one
Wahdat-ush-Shuhud — Creator and creation are identical
Wahdat-ush-Shuhud — Doctrine associated with Ibn Arabi

147.x: The verses of Baba Farid (Fariduddin Ganj-i-Shakar) are included in the Adi Granth (Guru Granth Sahib); the other saints have no compositions in it.

147.s: The thought of which of the following Sufisaint has been incorporated in the religious book incorporated in the religious book ‘Adi Granth’ of the Sikhs?
147.x: The verses of Baba Farid (Fariduddin Ganj-i-Shakar) are included in the Adi Granth (Guru Granth Sahib); the other saints have no compositions in it.

147.s: The book 'Fawaid ul Fawad' is the record of the conversations of Shaikh Nizamuddin Auliya, it was compiled by :
147.x: Fawaid-ul-Fuad, the record of Nizamuddin Auliya's conversations, was compiled by Amir Hasan Sijzi, not Amir Khusrau, Barani or Hasan Nizami.

147.s: Who among the following has been imprisoned by Jahangir?
147.x: Jahangir imprisoned Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi in Gwalior Fort for his orthodox stand and claims.

147.s: Ahmad Sirhindi criticised Akbar’s Sulh-i-Kul and was subsequently imprisoned by which Mughal ruler?
147.x: Ahmad Sirhindi criticised Akbar’s Sulh-i-Kul and was imprisoned during the reign of Jahangir.
147.tq: Separate the ruler whose policy was criticised from the ruler who ordered the imprisonment.
xs: **Ahmad Sirhindi** criticised Akbar's **Sulh-i-Kul** and was **imprisoned by Jahangir** — option **(2)** is correct.
As a strictly orthodox **Naqshbandi**, he opposed Sulh-i-Kul and **Shia influence**.
xa: Sirhindi's title: **Mujaddid Alf-i-Sani**.
He propounded **Wahdat-ush-Shuhud** against Wahdat-ul-Wujud.
His works: **Maktubat-i-Imam Rabbani** (letters), **Radd-i-Khawafiq** (anti-Shia tract).

147.s: What is ‘Maktubat-i-Imam Rabbani’?
o: An anti-Shia tract by Abdul Haqq Dehlavi
A tazkira written by Mir Khwurd Kirmani
147.x: ‘Maktubat-i-Imam Rabbani’ consists of the letters of Ahmad Sirhindi.
xs: **Maktubat-i-Imam Rabbani** = **letters of Ahmad Sirhindi** — option **(3)** is correct.
The anti-Shia tract is Sirhindi's **Radd-i-Khawafiq**; the tazkira by **Mir Khwurd Kirmani** is **Siyar-ul-Auliya**.
xa: ⚠ **maktubat** = letters; **malfuzat** = conversations; **tazkiras** = biographies.
Sirhindi = **Mujaddid Alf-i-Sani**, a **Naqshbandi**.

147.s: Who compiled Fawaid-ul-Fuad, the malfuzat of Nizamuddin Auliya?
147.x: Amir Hasan Sijzi compiled Fawaid-ul-Fuad; Mir Khwurd Kirmani wrote Siyar-ul-Auliya.

147.s: Who wrote Siyar-ul-Auliya, a tazkira of Chishti saints?
147.x: Siyar-ul-Auliya is a tazkira by Mir Khwurd Kirmani.

147.s: Who wrote Radd-i-Rawafiz, an anti-Shia tract?
147.x: Radd-i-Rawafiz is Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi's anti-Shia tract; Ali Hujwiri wrote Kashf-ul-Mahjub and Amir Hasan Sijzi compiled Fawaid-ul-Fuad.

147.s: Who wrote Radd-i-Rawafiz, an anti-Shia tract?
147.x: Radd-i-Rawafiz is Ahmad Sirhindi's anti-Shia tract.

147.s: Who compiled the Fawaid-ul-Fuad?
147.x: Fawaid-ul-Fuad, the conversations of Nizamuddin Auliya, was compiled by Amir Hasan Sijzi, not Amir Khusrau.

He propounded **Wahdat-ush-Shuhud** vs Wahdat-ul-Wujud.

147.x: Sirhindi criticised Sulh-i-kul and Din-i-Ilahi and opposed sama and visits to saints' tombs.

Comparative: **Nizamuddin** (Chishti, sama, aloof) vs **Sirhindi** (Naqshbandi, orthodox, political critic).
