xs: Gidugu led the **vyavaharika** movement against the **Sanskritised grandhika** style — option **(2)**.
Granthika = Sanskritised classical Telugu with **archaic grammar**, claimed as the only "pure" literary medium.
xa: Vyavaharika = spoken Telugu (also **Gramya / Janapada bhasha**).
His ally in literature: **Gurajada Apparao**.
Outcome: the **Andhra Mahasabha** endorsed colloquial Telugu for literature, education and administration.

195.s: Along with Gurajada Apparao, who led the Vyavaharika (spoken Telugu) movement?
195.x: Gidugu and Gurajada led the Vyavaharika cause to narrow the gap between written and spoken Telugu, while orthodox pandits backed Granthika.
xa: Opponents: **Kokkonda Venkataratnam**, **Jayanti Ramaiah Pantulu** (Andhra Sahitya Parishad).
Supporters: **Tapi Dharma Rao**, **Navya Sahitya Parishat**.

195.s: In April 1913, Madras University set up a Telugu Composition Committee to fix the style of Telugu for which course?
195.x: The ten-member Telugu Composition Committee of April 1913 was to fix the style of Telugu composition for the Intermediate course.

195.s: Who wrote a Minute of Dissent (1914) favouring the spoken dialect in the Madras University controversy?
195.x: Gurajada's Minute of Dissent backed the spoken dialect; the majority, incl. Vedam Venkataraya Sastri, kept the literary dialect.

195.s: Who wrote 'A Defence of Literary Telugu' (1913)?
195.x: Jayanti Ramayya Pantulu wrote it and urged the University not to back the 'new school'.

195.s: Which title did Gidugu Ramamurthy receive in 1934?
195.x: Gidugu received the Kaisar-e-Hind in 1934; he was also Rao Saheb.

195.s: Where was the meeting held after which the Vyavaharika Bhashodyama Samstha was formed in 1910?
195.x: The Samstha was formed in 1910 after a meeting at Visakhapatnam.

195.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with the side taken in the Telugu language controversy?
195.x: Jayanti Ramaiah Pantulu and Kokkonda backed granthika; Gidugu, Gurajada and Tapi Dharma Rao backed vyavaharika.

195.s: Where did Gidugu Ramamurthy work as a Telugu teacher?
195.x: Gidugu Ramamurthy, born at Ponduru in 1863, was a Telugu teacher at Parlakimidi.

195.s: In the Madras University Telugu composition controversy, which style did the Sub-Committee majority led by Vedam Venkataraya Sastri retain?
195.x: The majority kept the literary (classical) dialect; Gurajada wrote a Minute of Dissent (1914) for the spoken dialect.

195.s: Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Chowdary's song 'Veeragandhamu techinaramu' is associated with which movement?
195.x: The song 'Veeragandhamu techinaramu' is associated with the Civil Disobedience Movement.
195.tq: Link a literary work with the correct phase of the national movement.
xs: Tripuraneni's song "**Veeragandhamu techinaramu**" is linked to the **Civil Disobedience Movement** — option **(1)** (PYQ **2012**).
The notes link the song to no other movement.
xa: Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Chowdary = **Kavi Raju**, a **rationalist poet**.
⚠ **Kavi Raju** (Tripuraneni) vs **Andhra Ratna** (Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya).

195.s: Where was the first Andhra Social Reform Conference organized in 1908?
195.src: Social and Cultural History of A.P and Welfare Programmes 20
195.x: The first Andhra Social Reform Conference (1908) is keyed to Masulipatnam as printed; no library source or web page checked confirms it.

195.s: Where was the earliest women's Association established in 1902 under leadership of Kotikalapudi Seethamma
195.src: APPSC Asst. BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Mains Paper-II 2017
195.x: The first women's association (1902) under Kotikalapudi Seethamma, Veeresalingam's follower, was at Rajahmundry.

195.s: Where was the first women's association founded in 1902 under the leadership of Kotikalapudi Seethamma?
195.src: APPSC Assistant Social Welfare, Assistant BC Welfare & Assis
195.x: Kotikalapudi Seethamma led the first women's association at Rajahmundry in 1902.

195.s: In which year was the American Baptist Mission established in Andhra?
195.x:
Most books and keys (NextGen, Rocket): 1866. Some keys (APPSC G2 Mains 2017 printed key): 1867.
NextGen and Rocket date the American Baptist Mission in Andhra to 1866, the year Clough's Ongole church began functioning; 1867 is the printed key.

195.s: In which year American Baptist Mission was established in Andhra
195.x: The American Baptist Mission was established in Andhra in 1866 (Ongole, Clough).

195.s: Which social reformer and poet of the 19th-century founded Ram Mohan School in 1909 and provided free education for children from depressed communities in Andhra Pradesh?
195.src: APPSC 2022 Various Non Gazetted Posts Limited Recruitment
195.x: Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham founded Ram Mohan School (1909) for children of depressed communities.

195.s: Which of these districts in Andhra was first Telugu speaking region to start social reform movement?
195.src: APPSC Deputy Educational Officer Screening Test (General Stu
195.x: East Godavari (Rajahmundry, Kandukuri Veeresalingam) was the first Telugu region of the social reform movement.

195.s: In the context of the Andhra renaissance, which place is identified as its centre?
195.x: Rajahmundry is identified as the place associated with the first renaissance in Andhra.
195.tq: Separate the Andhra-specific first from the later Brahmo Samaj centres and dates.
xs: **Rajahmundry** is the Andhra renaissance centre — so option **(2)** is correct.
The earliest Andhra **Prarthana Samaj** came up there in **1878** under **Veeresalingam** (APPSC **2019**).
xa: Andhra "**Trinity of the Brahma Samaj**": **Veeresalingam**, **Raghupati Venkataratnam Naidu**, **Desiraju Peda Bapaiah**.
First Andhra Brahmo: **Mannava Buchayya Pantulu**.

195.s: The earliest phase of Andhra social reform was led mainly by which social group?
195.x: The reform movement began in Rajahmundry under the leadership of the English-educated middle class. It was not an exclusive movement of rulers, soldiers or European missionaries.
195.tq: Identify the social base of a movement rather than its geographical location.
xs: Andhra reform began at **Rajahmundry** under the **English-educated middle class** — option **(4)**.
It was not the work of princely families, a military aristocracy or missionaries alone; zamindari patrons such as the **Pithapuram Raja** only funded later work.
Its first guru was **Atmuri Lakshmi Narasimham**.
xa: Rajahmundry (**Godavari district**, today East Godavari) = Andhra's **first Renaissance centre**.
Peak period: **1870-1935**; other main centre **Kakinada**.
Veeresalingam used the **press, not politics**, for reform; by **1905** about **20** Telugu journals were in print.
Reform became institutional — **samajs, homes, journals** — and so outlived its founders.

195.s: Who is identified as the first guru associated with the early social reform movement in Andhra?
195.x: Atmuri Lakshmi Narasimham is identified as the first guru of the early Andhra social reform movement.
195.tq: Recall the specific title-holder among several reform-era personalities.
xs: **Atmuri Lakshmi Narasimham** is named the **first guru** of Andhra social reform — option **(1)**.
**Gidugu Ramamurthy** led the **vyavaharika** (spoken Telugu) movement; **Gurajada Apparao** wrote **Kanyasulkam**.
**Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Chowdary** was the rationalist poet called **Kavi Raju**.
xa: The early reform was led by the **English-educated middle class** of **Rajahmundry**.
Peak: **1870-1935**; main centres **Rajahmundry** and **Kakinada**.
First organised reform body: **Rajahmundry Social Reform Association** (Veeresalingam).

195.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with the place and year mentioned in the context of Andhra reform activity?
o: Sri Krishnadevaraya Andhra Bhasha Nilayam — Hyderabad, 1898
195.x: The Kavi Club was at Kumudavalli (West Godavari) in 1897. The traps: the 1882 Brahmo Samaj was at Machilipatnam (Guntur's Samaj came in 1898), the Sri Krishnadevaraya Andhra Bhasha Nilayam at Hyderabad dates to 1901, and the Kakinada Samaj was at Kakinada in 1888.
195.tq: Check both components of a place–year pair instead of accepting a familiar institution name.
xs: The **Kavi Club** was at **Kumudavalli** (West Godavari) in **1897** — option **(3)** is correctly matched.
The **1882** Brahmo Samaj was at **Machilipatnam**, not Guntur; the **Guntur Samaj** came in **1898**.
**Sri Krishnadevaraya Andhra Bhasha Nilayam** (Hyderabad) dates to **1901**, not 1898.
The **Kakinada Samaj** was at Kakinada in **1888**, not Rajahmundry in 1898.
xa: Kakinada Samaj founders: **Tayi Surya Prakasarao Naidu**, Duggirala Surya Prakasarao; Guntur Samaj: **Pillarisetty Sitaramayya**.
The Bhasha Nilayam was founded by **Komarraju Lakshmana Rao** with Ravichettu Ranga Rao and Nayani Venkata Ranga Rao.
**Bapatla** is linked with **Desiraju** (Peda Bapayya).

195.s: Which one of the following places became the centre of Telugu social reform, modern prose, journalism and the novel during the nineteenth century?
195.x: Rajahmundry emerged as the centre of Telugu social reform and the development of modern prose, journalism and the novel.
195.tq: Use the significance-based location clue and distinguish the reform centre from other Andhra places.
xs: **Rajahmundry** was the centre of Telugu **social reform, modern prose, journalism and the novel** — option **(4)**.
**Vizianagaram** was a cradle of the **language movement**; **Madanapalle** is the **Theosophy** link; **Kakinada** was the other reform centre.
xa: Rajahmundry (Godavari district) = Andhra's **first Renaissance centre**.
Firsts there: **Prarthana Samaj** (**1878**), first widow remarriage (**11 Dec 1881**).
Dowlaiswaram near it had the **first girls' school** (**1874**).

195.s: Which region was the cradle of the Telugu language movement?
o: South Coastal Andhra, especially Nellore and Ongole
North Coastal Andhra, especially Vizianagaram, Srikakulam and Parlakimidi
195.x: The language movement had its cradle in North Coastal Andhra, particularly Vizianagaram, Srikakulam and Parlakimidi.
195.tq: Use the region-and-example pairing to avoid confusing the cultural zones of Andhra.
xs: The cradle of the language movement was **North Coastal Andhra** — **Vizianagaram**, **Srikakulam**, **Parlakimidi** — option **(2)**.
⚠ The **Rajahmundry-Kakinada** belt was the cradle of social **reform**, not of the language movement.
xa: Gidugu was born at **Ponduru (Srikakulam)** and taught at **Parlakimidi**.
Kanyasulkam uses the **Srikakulam dialect** and was staged at **Vizianagaram** (**1892**).
The Samstha's founding meeting was at **Visakhapatnam** (**1910**).

195.s: Where was the Kavi Club founded in 1897?
195.x: The Kavi Club was set up at Kumudavalli in West Godavari in 1897.

195.s: Among the early Andhra reform centres, with whom is Bapatla associated?
195.x: Bapatla was the centre of Desiraju Pedda Bapayya; Sitaramayya was linked to Guntur and Ramakrishnayya and Surya Prakasarao Naidu to Kakinada.

195.s: What was the peak period of the Andhra social reform movement?
195.x: Andhra social reform peaked between 1870 and 1935, with Rajahmundry and Kakinada as the main centres.

195.s: Who founded the Ram Mohan Roy School (1909) for backward-class children?
195.x: Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham founded the Ram Mohan Roy School in 1909 for backward-class children.

195.s: Who among the following founded the Andhra Desa Library Association in 1914?
195.x: Iyyanki Venkata Ramanaiah founded the Andhra Desa Library Association in 1914.
195.tq: Distinguish the founder of the library movement from leaders of the spoken-Telugu movement.
xs: **Iyyanki Venkata Ramanaiah** founded the **Andhra Desa Library Association** (**1914**) — option **(2)**.
He led the **Library movement**.
**Gidugu** led the vyavaharika movement; **Acchamamba** founded Stree Samajam; **Gurajada** wrote Kanyasulkam.
xa: **Sri Krishnadevaraya Andhra Bhasha Nilayam**: Hyderabad, **1901**.
**Kavi Club, Kumudavalli** (West Godavari): **1897**.
**Madras Native Association**: **1852**.

195.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Dharmavaram Krishnamacharyulu — Father of Andhra Drama
Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu — Father of Andhra Drama
195.x: Dharmavaram Krishnamacharyulu was known as the Father of Andhra Drama. Andhra Ratna was the title of Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya, while Kavi Raju was associated with Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Chowdary.
195.tq: Use title-based elimination, especially where neighbouring personalities have similar reform credentials.
xs: **Dharmavaram Krishnamacharyulu** = **Father of Andhra Drama** — option **(1)**.
**Andhra Ratna** = **Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya**; **Kavi Raju** = **Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Chowdary**.
**Venkataratnam Naidu** was **Brahmarshi**, not Father of Andhra Drama.
xa: Veeresalingam = **Andhra Rammohan Roy**, **Gadya Tikkana**.
Gidugu = **Vyavaharika Bhashodyama Pitamaha**.
Tripuraneni was a **rationalist poet**.

195.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Bala Bharathi Samiti – Kokkonda Venkata Ratnam
Madras Native Association – Gajula Lakshminarasu Chetty
195.x: Gajula Lakshminarasu Chetty founded the Madras Native Association; the youth of Rajahmundry formed the Bala Bharathi Samiti, Kokkonda ran Hasyavardhani and Veeresalingam started Viveka Vardhini.
n: Golagi Math was founded by Sadbhana Sambhu. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 22-23]
Bala Bharathi Samiti was founded by the youth of Rajahmundry. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 22-23]
The Hasyavardhani Journal was founded by Kokkonda Venkata Ratnam. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 22-23]
xa: Madras Native Association: **1852**.
**Madras Mahajana Sabha**: **1884**.
Kokkonda also ran the orthodox **Andhra Bhasha Sanjeevini**.

195.s: How was Karunalayam, established by the Pithapuram Raja, described?
o: The first Brahmo Samaj in Andhra
The first girls' school in Andhra
195.x: Karunalayam was described as the only orphanage in Andhra and also provided vocational education.
195.tq: Test the distinctive numerical or superlative description.
xs: **Karunalayam** (**1909**), of the **Pithapuram Raja**, was the **only orphanage in Andhra** — option **(1)**.
The first Samaj in Andhra was the **Prarthana Samaj, Rajahmundry** (**1878**); the first girls' school was at **Dowlaiswaram** (**1874**).
xa: Pithapuram Raja: **Rao Venkatakumara Mahipati Suryarao** (**1885-1964**).
He also ran **orphan and vocational schools**; gave **Rs 1 lakh** to the Brahma Dharma Prachara Nidhi.
Karunalayam at **Kakinada** was set up with **Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu**.

195.s: In which year did Bhandaru Acchamamba found the Stree Samajam at Brundavanapuram, Machilipatnam?
195.x: Acchamamba founded the Stree Samajam in 1902.
xa: ⚠ **1902** = both Stree Samajam (Machilipatnam) and Hindu Sundari (**Kakinada**).
Acchamamba's women's biography series: **Abala Sachcharitra Ratnamala**.
Devadasi bill: **Dr. Muthulakshmi Reddy** + Chodagam Ammannaraja (**1937** → passed **1947**).

195.s: From where was Hindu Sundari, associated with Mosalikanti Ramabai and Vempati Shantabai, published?
195.x: Hindu Sundari was associated with Mosalikanti Ramabai and Vempati Shantabai and was published from Kakinada in 1902.
195.tq: Test a journal-place association using nearby Andhra reform centres as distractors.
xs: **Hindu Sundari** (**1902**) was published from **Kakinada** — option **(3)**.
**Machilipatnam** was the seat of **Acchamamba's Stree Samajam** (also **1902**) — the trap.
xa: Editors: **Mosalikanti Ramabai** + **Vempati Shantabai**.
⚠ **1902** = Stree Samajam (Machilipatnam) and Hindu Sundari (Kakinada).
Kakinada also had the Samaj (**1888**) and **Karunalayam**.

195.s: In which year was the Devadasi Bill associated with Dr. Muthulakshmi Reddy and Chodagam Ammannaraja passed?
195.x: The Devadasi Bill campaign was associated with Dr. Muthulakshmi Reddy and Chodagam Ammannaraja; the Bill was passed in 1947.
195.tq: Distinguish the year of the reform initiative from the year in which the legislation was passed.
xs: The **Devadasi bill** of **Dr. Muthulakshmi Reddy** and **Chodagam Ammannaraja** was passed in **1947** — option **(3)**.
**1937** is the year the bill was introduced, not passed.
xa: The anti-nautch (Devadasi) movement in Madras was begun by **Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu**.
**Desiraju Peda Bapayya** led the **boycott of Bhogam melas**.
Venkataratnam Naidu's anti-Devadasi journal: **People's Friend**.

195.s: In which year was the Madras Mahajana Sabha formed?
195.x: The Madras Mahajana Sabha was formed in 1884; the Madras Native Association of Gajula Lakshmi Narasu Chetty dates to 1852.
xa: **Sri Krishnadevaraya Andhra Bhasha Nilayam** (Hyderabad): **1901**, **Komarraju Lakshmana Rao**.
**Social Purity Association**: **1891**, Venkataratnam Naidu.
**Andhra Desa Library Association**: **1914**.

195.s: Sri Krishnadevaraya Andhra Bhasha Nilayam was established at Hyderabad in 1901 with the association of which group?
o: Komarraju Lakshmana Rao, Ravichettu Ranga Rao and Nayani Venkata Ranga Rao
Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu, Desiraju Peda Bapayya and Tayi Surya Prakasarao
Gajula Lakshmi Narasu Chetty, Paidah Ramakrishnayya and Atmuri Lakshmi Narasimham
Veeresalingam, Gurajada Apparao and Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy
195.x: Sri Krishnadevaraya Andhra Bhasha Nilayam at Hyderabad was established in 1901 with Komarraju Lakshmana Rao, Ravichettu Ranga Rao and Nayani Venkata Ranga Rao.
195.tq: Identify the correct founding group from closely related reform-era names.
xs: The **Bhasha Nilayam** (Hyderabad, **1901**) was set up by **Komarraju Lakshmana Rao**, **Ravichettu Ranga Rao** and **Nayani Venkata Ranga Rao** — option **(1)**.
The other groups mix reformers of the Brahmo, remarriage and language movements.
xa: **Varthamana Vyavaharikandhra Bhasha Parivartaka Samaj** — **Gidugu Ramamurthy** (APPSC **2017**).
**Andhra Desa Library Association** (**1914**) — **Iyyanki Venkata Ramanaiah**, leader of the **Library movement**.
⚠ APPSC-GS 2024: "Kanyasulkam written by **Kommaraju Lakshmana Rao**" is **false** — it is **Gurajada**'s.

195.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
195.x: Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya was known as Andhra Ratna. The title Brahma Rishi was associated with Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu.
195.tq: Find the swapped title–person pair among closely related reform personalities.
xs: "**Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya — Brahma Rishi**" is wrong — option **(4)**; he was **Andhra Ratna**.
**Brahma Rishi** (**1932**) was **Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu**'s, from his students.
The rest are correct: **Kavi Raju** — Tripuraneni; **Rao Bahadur, 1893** — Veeresalingam.
xa: Venkataratnam Naidu's **knighthood** (**1924**): first non-official educator knighted.
**Father of Andhra Drama** = **Dharmavaram Krishnamacharyulu**.
**Rao Saheb** = **Gidugu**.

195.s: Who was known as 'Andhra Ratna'?
195.x: Andhra Ratna was Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya; Prakasam was Andhra Kesari and Tripuraneni was Kavi Raju.

195.s: Who held the title 'Kavi Raju'?
195.x: Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Chowdary was called Kavi Raju; Dharmavaram Krishnamacharyulu was the Father of Andhra Drama.

195.s: In which year did the Pithapuram Raja establish Karunalayam, the only orphanage in Andhra?
195.x: The Pithapuram Raja set up Karunalayam in 1909, with vocational education.

195.s: Who founded the MIM in 1927?
195.x: Mahmood Nawaz Khan Qiledar founded the MIM at Hyderabad in 1927. It was later led by Bahadur Yar Jung and Kasim Razvi.
195.tq: Recall the founder of the MIM.
n: Mahmood Nawaz Khan Qiledar founded MIM. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 27-29]
MIM was established in 1927. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 27-29]
Bahadur Yar Jung later led MIM. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 27-29]
Kasim Razvi later led MIM during the Razakar phase. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 27-29]
xs: **Mahmood Nawaz Khan Qiledar** founded the **MIM** (**Ittehad-ul-Muslimeen**) in **1927** at **Hyderabad** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It was later led by **Bahadur Yar Jung**, and by **Kasim Razvi** in the **Razakar phase**.
xa: **Comrades Association** — **1940**, **Hyderabad**.
**Socialist Party Andhra Branch** — **1934**.
**Jatiya Andhra Mahasabha** — **Ravi Narayana Reddy**.

195.s: In which year did Gajula Lakshminarasu Chetty found the Madras Native Association?
195.x: The Madras Native Association was founded by Gajula Lakshminarasu Chetty in 1852; the Madras Mahajana Sabha came in 1884.

195.s: Whom did Christian mission schools in Andhra admit?
195.x: Mission schools admitted Sudras and Panchamas, extending education beyond the traditional upper-caste groups.
xa: **London Missionary Society**: **Jammalamadugu, 1805**.
**American Baptists**: Rayalaseema **1835**; schools in Guntur, Gurazala, Palnadu, **Ongole**, Nellore.
**Church Mission Society**: Krishna-Godavari from **1841**; Machilipatnam school became a college in **1864**.
The **Bellary Christian Mission** issued the first Telugu journal, **Satyaduta** (**1835**).

195.s: Where did the London Missionary Society begin its work in Andhra in 1805?
195.x: The London Missionary Society is associated with Jammalamadugu in Cuddapah, where it began work in Andhra in 1805.
195.tq: Apply the place-and-year pair rather than relying on the organisation alone.
xs: The **London Missionary Society** began at **Jammalamadugu** (Cuddapah) in **1805** — option **(3)**.
**Machilipatnam** was a **Church Mission Society** centre (from **1841**).
**Rajahmundry** was the social-reform base, not an LMS centre.
xa: LMS also worked in **Cuddapah, Kurnool and Bellary**.
⚠ **LMS** = Jammalamadugu **1805**; **CMS** = Krishna-Godavari **1841**.
**North German Mission** = Godavari; **Pennsylvania Synod** = Guntur, Prattipadu, Nallapadu.

195.s: The American Baptist Mission at Ongole was popularly known by which name?
195.x: The American Baptist Mission at Ongole, built up by Lyman Jewett and John E. Clough, was known as the Lone Star Mission.
195.tq: Recall the popular name of the Ongole mission.
n: The American Baptist Mission was known as the “Lone Star” Mission. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 27-29]
The American Baptist Mission was located in Ongole. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 27-29]
xs: The **American Baptist Mission** at **Ongole** was the "**Lone Star**" Mission — so option **(1)** is correct.
It was built up by **Lyman Jewett** and **John E. Clough** (**1866**).
xa: ⚠ Sources differ: American Baptist work began in **Rayalaseema** in **1835**.
Mission schools admitted **Sudras and Panchamas**.
**London Missionary Society** — **Jammalamadugu, 1805**.

195.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Pennsylvania Synod — Guntur, Prattipadu and Nallapadu
195.x: The Church Mission Society operated in the Krishna-Godavari region and had a school at Machilipatnam; it was not confined to Palnadu.
195.tq: Reject the option that narrows a mission’s area incorrectly.
xs: "**Church Mission Society — Palnadu only**" is wrong — option **(4)**; the CMS worked in **Krishna-Godavari** from **1841**.
Palnadu had schools of the **American Baptist** mission.
The other pairs are correct: **LMS — Jammalamadugu**, **Pennsylvania Synod — Guntur, Prattipadu, Nallapadu**, **North German Mission — Godavari**.
xa: CMS's **Machilipatnam school** (**1841**) became a college in **1864**.
⚠ **London Missionary Society** = **Jammalamadugu 1805**; **Church Mission Society** = Krishna-Godavari **1841**.
American Baptists: **Rayalaseema 1835**; schools in Guntur, Gurazala, Palnadu, Ongole, Nellore.

195.s: In which year did the Theosophical Society set up its headquarters at Adyar (Madras)?
195.x: Founded in New York in 1875, the Society moved its headquarters to Adyar in 1882.

195.s: Where was Jiddu Krishnamurti born in 1895?
195.x: Jiddu Krishnamurti was born at Madanapalle, now in Andhra Pradesh.

195.s: Who identified Jiddu Krishnamurti at Adyar in 1909 as the 'World Teacher'?
195.x: Leadbeater identified him in 1909; Krishnamurti left the Society in 1929.

195.s: In which region of Andhra did the Church Mission Society work from 1841?
195.x: The CMS worked in Krishna-Godavari from 1841, not Palnadu.

195.s: Where did the Lutheran Mission (Pennsylvania Synod) mainly work?
195.x: The Lutheran Mission worked in Guntur, Prattipadu and Nallapadu; Ongole was the American Baptists' Lone Star Mission.

195.s: Where was the Theosophical Society founded in 1875?
195.x: Blavatsky and Olcott founded the Theosophical Society at New York in 1875; its headquarters moved to Adyar in 1882.

195.s: In which year did Jiddu Krishnamurti leave the Theosophical Society?
195.x: Jiddu Krishnamurti, born at Madanapalle (1895) and hailed as 'World Teacher' in 1909, left the Society in 1929.

195.s: Lyman Jewett and John E. Clough are associated with which mission in Andhra?
195.x: The American Baptist 'Lone Star' Mission at Ongole is linked with Lyman Jewett and John E. Clough.

xs: The Extremists **turned nationalism into a mass movement** and **made Swaraj the goal** — so option **(1)** is correct.

**Atmashakti** (self-reliance): constructive work such as **cooperatives**.

234.x: Three were part of it: boycott of law courts and foreign cloth, strict non-violence, and panchayats for disputes. Titles were to be surrendered, not retained.

234.s:
Which among the following about Mahatma Gandhi Non-Cooperation Movement are correct?

234.s: Which one of the following was not actually part of the original plan of the non-co operation movement but acquired great popularity among the movement in many parts of the country.

Boycott of Government schools and colleges
Boycott of public transport and communication system

234.s: Under the Non-Cooperation programme, how were the November 1920 legislative elections treated?

239.s: Which among the following was not the provision of the Gandhi-Irwin Pact?

251.x: Article 32, which guarantees the Right to Constitutional Remedies, was described by Ambedkar as the ‘heart and soul’ of the Constitution.
251.tq: Match the famous phrase with the constitutional provision, not with the related social-justice articles.
xs: **Article 32** (**Right to Constitutional Remedies**) is the "**heart and soul**" of the Constitution — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Art. 356** he hoped would stay a "**dead letter**"; **Art. 17** abolishes untouchability; **Art. 46** is **SC/ST welfare**.
xa: ⚠ "Heart and soul" = **Art. 32**; "dead letter" = **Art. 356**.
**Arts. 330 and 332**: reserved seats.
**Arts. 15-16**: non-discrimination, equal opportunity.

251.s: Which Article of the Constitution abolishes untouchability?
251.x: Article 17 abolishes untouchability and makes it punishable; Articles 15-16 cover non-discrimination and Article 46 the welfare of SCs/STs.
xa: **Article 32** = "**heart and soul**".
**Art. 356** = hoped to be a "**dead letter**".
These embedded a "**social revolution**" — rights, reservation, abolition of untouchability.

251.s: What did Ambedkar hope the emergency provisions under Article 356 would remain?
o: Source of the Union’s power to secede
251.x: Ambedkar expressed the hope that Article 356 would remain a ‘dead letter’, indicating that it would not be used routinely.
251.tq: Match the distinctive quotation with the correct emergency provision.
xs: Ambedkar hoped **Art. 356** would remain a "**dead letter**" — so option **(3)** is correct.
States have **no right to secede**, so "power to secede" is wrong.
xa: ⚠ "Heart and soul" = **Art. 32**; "dead letter" = **Art. 356**.
India is a "**Union of States**", able to work as **unitary or federal**.
He favoured a **strong Centre** to protect weaker sections.

251.s:
Consider the following statements about Ambedkar's views in the Constituent Assembly:
1. He called the Directive Principles a novel feature, like the instruments of instructions.
2. He hoped Article 356 would remain a dead letter.
3. He called Article 17 the heart and soul of the Constitution.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
251.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The 'heart and soul' was Article 32, not Article 17, which abolishes untouchability.

251.s: During the debates on its making, the Indian Constitution was criticised as a copy of which Act?
251.x: Critics called it a 'copy of the Government of India Act, 1935' and a 'lawyers' paradise'.
xa: His reply came in the speech of **4 Nov 1948** (UPPSC 2015).
Same speech: **constitutional morality** "has to be cultivated".
The Draft had **315 Articles and 13 Schedules**.

251.s: From whom did Ambedkar borrow the term 'constitutional morality'?
251.x: Ambedkar took the term from George Grote and said constitutional morality has to be cultivated.
xa: Same speech: **no need to apologise** for borrowing from the **GoI Act 1935**.
Final speech: **25 November 1949**.
Warning against **bhakti or hero-worship** in politics.

251.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched regarding Ambedkar's view of Indian federalism?
o: System – unitary or federal as times require
Centre – strong, to protect weaker sections
States – right to secede from the Union
251.x: Ambedkar held the Union indestructible, so States have no right to secede; the other pairs reflect his views.
xa: He hoped **Art. 356** would remain a "**dead letter**".
**Universal adult suffrage** including women from the start.
He called **Article 32** the "**heart and soul**".

251.s: In Ambedkar's view, what did India being a 'Union of States' mean?
o: States could secede by a referendum
The Union is indestructible and states have no right to secede
States are sovereign units that formed a compact
The Centre can be dissolved by the states
251.x: Ambedkar said the Union is indestructible and the states have no right to secede.

251.s: On which date did Dr. B.R. Ambedkar deliver his final speech in the Constituent Assembly?
251.x: Ambedkar delivered his final speech in the Constituent Assembly on 25 November 1949.
251.tq: Separate the final speech date from Constitution Day and the date of commencement of the Constitution.
xs: Ambedkar's final speech in the Assembly was on **25 November 1949** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**4 November 1948** was his speech on the 1935 Act and **constitutional morality**; **26 January 1950** is when India entered "**a life of contradictions**".
xa: Three warnings: give up the "**grammar of anarchy**", avoid **hero-worship**, turn **political democracy into social democracy**.
"Political democracy cannot last unless there lies at the base of it **social and economic democracy**."
⚠ **4 Nov 1948** = 1935 Act reply; **25 November 1949** = three warnings.

251.s: Which of the following was NOT one of the three warnings given by Ambedkar in his final Constituent Assembly speech?
o: Turn political democracy into social democracy.
Abolish the parliamentary system in favour of a presidential system.
Give up the bloody methods of revolution and civil disobedience.
Do not lay liberties at the feet of a great man.
251.x: Ambedkar warned against violent and extra-constitutional methods, hero-worship in politics, and the failure to establish social democracy. He did not call for abolishing the parliamentary system.
251.tq: Find the option outside the recognised set of three warnings.
xs: **Abolishing the parliamentary system for a presidential one** was NOT a warning — so option **(2)** is the answer.
Warning 1: give up **bloody methods of revolution and civil disobedience** — "the **grammar of anarchy**".
Warning 2: do not lay liberties at the feet of a **great man** (**bhakti or hero-worship** → dictatorship).
Warning 3: turn **political democracy into social democracy**.
xa: Delivered on **25 November 1949**.
On **26 Jan 1950** India would enter "**a life of contradictions**".
Constitutional morality "**has to be cultivated**" (**4 Nov 1948**).

251.s: Ambedkar's reference to India entering 'a life of contradictions' on 26 January 1950 pointed to the coexistence of which of the following?
o: Federalism with the right of secession
Political equality with social and economic inequality
251.x: The contradiction lay in political equality coexisting with inequality in social and economic life. Ambedkar urged that political democracy be transformed into social democracy.
251.tq: Match each side of the contrast without reversing the domains of equality and inequality.
xs: "**A life of contradictions**" meant **political equality** alongside **social and economic inequality** — so option **(4)** is correct.
India would enter it on **26 Jan 1950**; he urged turning **political democracy into social democracy**.
Option (2) reverses the two.
xa: "Political democracy cannot last unless there lies at the base of it **social and economic democracy**."
Final speech: **25 November 1949**.
States have **no right to secede**, so option (1) is also wrong.

251.s: In his final speech, what did Dr. B.R. Ambedkar call civil disobedience, non-cooperation and satyagraha?
251.x: He said these methods were now the 'grammar of anarchy' and should be given up.

251.s: According to Ambedkar, what does bhakti or hero-worship in politics lead to?
251.x: His second warning: bhakti or hero-worship in politics leads to dictatorship.

251.s: In his final speech of 25 November 1949, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar said political democracy cannot last unless there lies at its base:
251.x: Ambedkar said political democracy cannot last unless social and economic democracy lies at its base.

251.s: Who among the following was not a member of the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly?
251.x: B.N. Rau was the Constitutional Adviser, not a Drafting Committee member; Ayyangar, Munshi and Saadullah were members.

251.s: Who was elected President of the Constituent Assembly on 11 December 1946?
251.x: Dr. Rajendra Prasad was elected President on 11 December 1946; Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee.

251.s: Who was the Constitutional Adviser to the Constituent Assembly?
251.x: B.N. Rau was Constitutional Adviser and prepared the initial draft in October 1947.

251.s: Who were the two Vice-Presidents of the Constituent Assembly?
251.x: H.C. Mukherjee and V.T. Krishnamachari were Vice-Presidents; T.T. Krishnamachari was a Drafting Committee member.

251.s: The Draft Constitution, published in February 1948, contained how many Articles?
251.x: The Draft Constitution was published on 21 February 1948 and contained 315 Articles.
xa: The Drafting Committee sat for only **141 days**; draft completed in **under six months**.
Ambedkar replied to the "copy of the 1935 Act" charge on **4 Nov 1948**.
Committee set up on **29 August 1947**.
251.fixed: Draft Constitution (Feb 1948) had 315 Articles and 8 Schedules; 13 Schedules was B.N. Rau's Oct 1947 draft

251.s: On which date was the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly set up?
251.x: It was set up on 29 August 1947 with seven members, including chairman Ambedkar; Nehru was not a member.
xa: "How many **other** members" = **6**.
It was the **most important** committee of the Assembly.
**Dr. K.M. Munshi** was originally its **only Congress member**.

251.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with reference to the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly?
o: N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar — Co-author of the Munshi-Ayyangar language formula
Syed Mohammad Saadullah — Representative from Bombay
N. Madhava Rao — Original member in place of B.L. Mitter
T.T. Krishnamachari — Replaced Dr. K.M. Munshi
251.x: N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar was associated with the Munshi-Ayyangar language formula. Saadullah was from Assam, Madhava Rao replaced B.L. Mitter, and T.T. Krishnamachari replaced D.P. Khaitan.
251.tq: Start from the sure member–role pair and eliminate swapped replacements and locations.
xs: **N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar** co-authored the **Munshi-Ayyangar language formula** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Syed Mohammad Saadullah** was from **Assam**, not Bombay.
**N. Madhava Rao** replaced **B.L. Mitter**; **T.T. Krishnamachari** replaced **D.P. Khaitan** (died **1948**), not Munshi.
xa: ⚠ **Madhava Rao** ← Mitter; **Krishnamachari** ← Khaitan.
The formula was adopted on **14 Sept 1949**, recalled on **Hindi Diwas (14 Sept)**.
The committee had **7 members** (chairman **Ambedkar** + **6** others).

251.s: Who was originally the only Congress member of the Drafting Committee?
251.x: K.M. Munshi, who also chaired the Order of Business Committee, was originally the only Congress member of the Drafting Committee.
xa: ⚠ Trap: **Jawaharlal Nehru** was **not a member** (UPPSC 2012).
Chairman: **Dr. B.R. Ambedkar**; set up on **29 August 1947**.
**Syed Mohammad Saadullah** was the member from **Assam**.

251.s: On which date was the Munshi-Ayyangar formula on the language of the Constitution adopted?
251.x: The Munshi-Ayyangar formula was adopted on 14 September 1949. The date is also associated with the observance of Hindi Diwas on 14 September.
251.tq: Distinguish the language formula’s adoption date from the Constitution’s adoption date.
xs: The **Munshi-Ayyangar formula** was adopted on **14 September 1949** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It is recalled on **Hindi Diwas (14 Sept)**.
xa: Named after two Drafting Committee members: **Dr. K.M. Munshi** and **N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar**.
Munshi also chaired the **Order of Business Committee**.
Ambedkar's final speech came on **25 November 1949**.

251.s: Apart from its chairman, how many other members did the Drafting Committee have?
251.x: The Drafting Committee had 7 members: the chairman plus 6 others.

251.s: For how many days did the Drafting Committee sit?
251.x: The Drafting Committee sat for 141 days.

251.s: Whom did T.T. Krishnamachari replace in the Drafting Committee?
251.x: T.T. Krishnamachari replaced D.P. Khaitan (died 1948); N. Madhava Rao replaced B.L. Mitter.

251.s: Which of the following was NOT a member of the Drafting Committee?
251.x: Nehru was not a member of the Drafting Committee; the other three were.

251.s: On which date was the Draft Constitution prepared by the Drafting Committee published?
251.x: The Draft Constitution was published on 21 February 1948 with 315 Articles and 8 Schedules.

251.s: Which member of the Drafting Committee chaired the Order of Business Committee of the Constituent Assembly?
251.x: K.M. Munshi, originally the only Congress member of the Drafting Committee, chaired the Order of Business Committee.

251.s: B.R. Ambedkar was elected to the Constituent Assembly from:
251.x: After his Bengal seat went to East Pakistan, Ambedkar was elected from the Bombay Presidency (1947), in M.R. Jayakar's vacated seat – the UPSC key.

251.s: From where was Dr. B.R. Ambedkar elected to the Constituent Assembly before Partition?
251.x: Before Partition, Ambedkar was elected from Bengal's Jessore-Khulna area with the support of Jogendra Nath Mandal.
xa: He lost the Bengal seat when those districts went to **East Pakistan**.
He then chaired the **Drafting Committee** (**29 August 1947**).

251.s: After Partition, in whose vacated seat was Dr. B.R. Ambedkar re-elected to the Constituent Assembly from the Bombay Presidency?
251.x: His Bengal seat went to East Pakistan, so he was re-elected from Bombay in the seat vacated by M.R. Jayakar.

251.s: Who among the following was the first Law Minister of India?
251.x: Nehru invited Ambedkar into his 1947 cabinet as the first Law Minister of independent India; Setalvad was the first Attorney-General.

251.s: The stalling of which Bill made Dr. B.R. Ambedkar resign as Law Minister in September 1951?
251.x: The omnibus Hindu Code Bill stalled in Parliament and Ambedkar resigned in September 1951.

251.s: Which law, passed in 1955 as part of the Hindu Code, introduced monogamy and divorce?
251.x: The Hindu Marriage Act 1955 brought monogamy and divorce; the Hindu Succession Act 1956 made daughters Class I heirs.

251.s:
Consider the following statements about the Hindu Code Bill:
1. It aimed at monogamy, divorce and inheritance rights of daughters and widows.
2. It was passed as one omnibus bill in 1951.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
251.x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the omnibus bill stalled and was later passed in parts in 1955-56.

251.s: In which year were daughters given equal coparcenary rights by an amendment to the Hindu Succession Act?
251.x: The 2005 amendment to the Hindu Succession Act gave daughters equal coparcenary rights.

251.s: Which Act of 1956, part of the Hindu Code, made daughters Class I heirs?
251.x: The Hindu Succession Act, 1956 made daughters Class I heirs; the 2005 amendment gave them equal coparcenary rights.

251.s: Which post held by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar earned him the title 'Father of the Indian Constitution'?
251.x: He is the Father / Chief Architect of the Constitution as Chairman of the Drafting Committee.

251.s: Which title was given to Dr. B.R. Ambedkar as the law-giver of modern India?
251.x: Ambedkar is called the 'Modern Manu', the law-giver of modern India.

252.s: The Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Orders (Amendment) Act, 1990 has extended the reservations to:
252.src: TSPSC Refractionist in Insurance Medical Service 2018
252.x: The Constitution (SC) Orders (Amendment) Act 1990 extended SC status to Buddhists (Sikhs had been added in 1956).

252.s: Who advocated 'Neo-Buddhism'?
252.x: Navayana or Neo-Buddhism is the reinterpretation of Buddhism founded by B.R. Ambedkar (Dalit Buddhist movement).

252.s: Who advocated ‘Neo-Buddhism’?
252.x: Ambedkar advocated Neo-Buddhism (Navayana, 'new vehicle'), adopted at Nagpur in 1956.

252.s:
Consider the following statements about Ambedkar's declaration that, though born a Hindu, he would not die a Hindu:
1. It was made at Yeola on 13 October 1935.
2. It was made at the Depressed Classes Conference.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
252.x: Ambedkar made this declaration at the Depressed Classes Conference at Yeola on 13 October 1935, so both statements are correct.

252.s: What is Ambedkar's reinterpretation of Buddhism known as?
252.x: Ambedkar's reinterpretation of Buddhism is called Navayana, meaning Neo-Buddhism. It gave rise to the Dalit Buddhist Movement.
252.tq: Distinguish Ambedkar's modern reinterpretation from the established Buddhist sects.
xs: His reinterpretation is **Navayana** ("**Neo-Buddhism**") — option **(4)** is correct.
**CGPSC 2019** asked it as Neo-Buddhism = Ambedkar.
Its basis is **The Buddha and His Dhamma** (posthumous, **1957**), a rational, social reading of Buddhism.
xa: It gave rise to the **Dalit Buddhist Movement**.
Conversion: **14 October 1956**, **Deekshabhoomi, Nagpur**, with **22 vows**.
Buddhists were added for SC status in **1990**.

252.s: According to the Supreme Court ruling of 24 March 2026, conversion out of which of the following religions results in the immediate loss of Scheduled Caste status under Clause 3 of the Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950?
252.x: The ruling held that conversion out of Hinduism, Sikhism or Buddhism leads to immediate loss of Scheduled Caste status under Clause 3 of the Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950.
252.tq: Identify the exact religious categories and the constitutional provision involved.
xs: Converting out of **Hinduism, Sikhism or Buddhism** brings immediate loss of SC status — option **(1)** is correct.
The basis is **Clause 3** of the **Constitution (SC) Order 1950**, per the SC ruling of **24 March 2026**.
The bench: Justices **P.K. Mishra** and **Manmohan**.
xa: **Buddhists** were added in **1990**; **Sikhs** in **1956**.
The case, **Chinthada Anand**, came from **Andhra Pradesh**.
It arose from an AP pastor's case under the **SC/ST Atrocities Act**.

252.s: Who supported Ambedkar's idea of considering Sikhism as an alternative to Hinduism?
252.x: B.S. Moonje supported the idea, while Gandhi, Rajagopalachari and Malaviya opposed it.
xa: He finally converted to **Buddhism** on **14 October 1956** at **Deekshabhoomi, Nagpur**.
The exit was announced at **Yeola** on **13 October 1935**.
SC status: **Sikhs** were added in **1956**, **Buddhists** in **1990**.

252.s: Which of the following pairs regarding Ambedkar's conversion to Buddhism is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Followers who accompanied him – about fifty thousand
252.x: About five lakh followers, mostly Mahars, accompanied him, not fifty thousand; the other pairs are correct.
xa: ⚠ Trap: **1935** was only the **Yeola declaration**, not the conversion.
He died on **6 December 1956**, weeks later, in Delhi.
**Navayana** ("Neo-Buddhism") → **Dalit Buddhist Movement**.

252.s: On which date did Ambedkar embrace Buddhism?
252.x: He converted on 14 October 1956 at Deekshabhoomi, Nagpur; 13 October 1935 was only the Yeola declaration.

252.s: Where did Ambedkar embrace Buddhism in 1956?
252.x: The conversion took place at Deekshabhoomi, Nagpur; Yeola was the place of the 1935 declaration and he died in Delhi.

252.s: How many vows did Ambedkar administer at his conversion to Buddhism?
252.x: Ambedkar prescribed 22 vows at the 1956 conversion.

252.s:
Consider the following statements about Ambedkar's conversion to Buddhism:
1. About 5 lakh followers converted with him.
2. Most of the followers were Mahars.
3. The conversion took place in 1935.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
252.x: About 5 lakh followers, mostly Mahars, converted with him in 1956; 1935 was only the Yeola declaration.

252.s: In which year were Buddhists brought under the Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950?
252.x: Sikhs were added in 1956 and Buddhists in 1990.

252.s: On which date did B.R. Ambedkar die?
252.x: Ambedkar died in Delhi on 6 December 1956, less than two months after his conversion at Nagpur.

252.s: Which of the following does Ambedkar's Navayana (Neo-Buddhism) reject?
252.x: Navayana rejects Karma, rebirth, monasticism, meditation and the four noble truths, and gives a rational, social reading of Buddhism.

252.s: In which year were Sikhs added to the Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950?
252.x: Sikhs were added to the SC Order in 1956; Buddhists were added in 1990.

252.s: Why Dr B.R.Ambedkar supported electorates for depressed classes?
o: Some sort of political power was necessary for the depressed classes to protect themselves
252.x: Ambedkar sought separate electorates because some political power was necessary for the depressed classes to protect their interests.

252.s: What was Ambedkar's critique of caste in Annihilation of Caste?
o: Only untouchability needed to be removed while the caste system could remain.
Caste had no connection with religious texts and could be reformed through charity alone.
The caste system as a whole had to be destroyed because it possessed religious sanction in the Shastras and Vedas.
Caste was an ideal division of labour that required only greater efficiency.
252.x: Ambedkar argued that caste had religious sanction in the Shastras and Vedas and that reform limited to untouchability was inadequate; the entire caste system had to go.
252.tq: Choose the option that captures both the source of caste sanction and the scope of the remedy.
xs: In **Annihilation of Caste**, the **caste system as a whole had to be destroyed** because it had **religious sanction in the Shastras and Vedas** — option **(3)** is correct.
Since the sanction was religious, Ambedkar held **reform within Hinduism futile**.
Removing only **untouchability** was not enough — the **whole caste system** must go, so option (1) is wrong.
Varna as an ideal **division of labour** was **Gandhi's** view, not Ambedkar's.
xa: The book was a **direct rebuke of Gandhi's approach**.
⚠ Gandhi: varna a **division of labour**; Ambedkar: caste a **division of labourers**.
"Nothing can emancipate the outcaste except the **destruction of the caste system**" — Ambedkar (**APPSC-G1 2018**).
Remedy prescribed: **inter-caste marriage**.

252.s: Who described caste as “not just a division of labour, but a division of labourers”?
252.x: The statement that caste is a division of labourers, rather than merely a division of labour, was made by B.R. Ambedkar.
252.tq: Use author-quotation matching, a common history question pattern.
xs: **B.R. Ambedkar** described caste as "not just a **division of labour**, but a **division of labourers**" — option **(3)** is correct.
**Gandhi** held the opposite: **varna** was an ideal **division of labour** and only untouchability a corruption.
**B.S. Moonje** and **Malaviya** appear in the notes only in the debate on Ambedkar's turn to **Sikhism** (Moonje for, Malaviya against).
xa: ⚠ Classic trap: Gandhi = division of **labour**; Ambedkar = division of **labourers**.
Ambedkar: "Nothing can emancipate the outcaste except the **destruction of the caste system**" (**APPSC-G1 2018**).
His remedy: **inter-caste marriage**, the "**real remedy**".

252.s: What was Ambedkar's position regarding political power for the Depressed Classes?
o: Political power was necessary to protect their interests.
Political power could be secured only through religious conversion.
Political power should remain exclusively with caste Hindus.
Political power was irrelevant because social reform alone was sufficient.
252.x: Ambedkar held that political power was necessary for the Depressed Classes to protect themselves and secure their rights.
252.tq: Test the central argument associated with a political thinker.
xs: Ambedkar held that **political power was necessary** for the depressed classes **to protect themselves** — option **(1)** is correct (**APPSC GS 2016**).
This is why he **demanded separate electorates**, against Gandhi.
He did not see social reform alone as enough: his method was **legal, constitutional, political rights** and state action.
xa: **Poona Pact (1932)**: he settled for joint electorates with **147** reserved seats.
Later he felt the Pact made Dalits **dependent on caste Hindus**.
He founded the **Independent Labour Party (1936)**.

252.s: For which organisation was Ambedkar's Annihilation of Caste (1936) prepared as an address?
252.x: It was an undelivered address for the Jat-Pat Todak Mandal, Lahore; the session was cancelled and Ambedkar published it himself.

252.s: In Annihilation of Caste, Ambedkar called which of the following the "real remedy" for caste?
252.x: Ambedkar held inter-caste marriage to be the real remedy; change of heart and temple entry were Gandhi's methods.

252.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Annihilation of Caste (1936)?
o: It held that caste has sanction in the Shastras and Vedas
It argued that the whole caste system must go
Gandhi replied to it in Harijan
It was delivered by Ambedkar at Lahore
252.x: The address was never delivered: the session was cancelled and Ambedkar published it himself.

252.s: Ambedkar later felt that the Poona Pact made the Dalits:
o: independent of caste Hindus in political matters
252.x: Ambedkar later felt the Pact made Dalits dependent on caste Hindus, although he had accepted joint electorates during the negotiations.
xa: **Poona Pact (1932)** followed Gandhi's **fast** against separate electorates.
Ambedkar accepted it to **save Gandhi's life**.
His underlying view: **political power** is necessary for the depressed classes to protect themselves (**APPSC GS 2016**).

252.s: What was a major criticism made by Ambedkar against the Indian National Congress?
o: It opposed all constitutional safeguards for minorities.
It supported separate electorates for the Scheduled Castes.
It refused to treat caste as a political issue.
It treated caste exclusively as an economic issue.
252.x: Ambedkar criticised Congress for refusing to recognise caste as a political issue. His work What Congress and Gandhi Have Done to the Untouchables was published in 1945.
252.tq: Identify the specific criticism rather than a broader political accusation.
xs: Ambedkar criticised Congress because it **refused to treat caste as a political issue** — option **(3)** is correct.
He set this out in "**What Congress and Gandhi Have Done to the Untouchables**" (**1945**).
Congress did not support separate electorates — **Gandhi opposed** them and fasted in **1932**.
xa: The **SCF** constitution declared its members **distinct from Hindus**.
**States and Minorities (1947)** was a memorandum to the Constituent Assembly for the **Scheduled Castes Federation**.
**Who Were the Shudras?** came in **1946** (**APPSC-GS 2019**).

252.s: Under the Poona Pact (1932), how many seats were reserved for the Depressed Classes?
252.x:
Most books (NextGen, PMF, NCERT): 148 seats. Spectrum p.424 gives 147.
The Poona Pact raised the depressed classes' reserved seats in provincial legislatures from 71 to 148.

252.s: According to Ambedkar's Who Were the Shudras?, who were the Shudras originally?
o: A Kshatriya community degraded after conflict with Brahmins
An occupational group created by British legislation
A group formed exclusively from foreign invaders
252.x: Ambedkar argued that the Shudras were originally Kshatriyas who were degraded after conflict with Brahmins, who denied them the upanayana.
252.tq: Test the proposed social origin and the specific cause of degradation together.
xs: The Shudras were originally a **Kshatriya community degraded after conflict with Brahmins** — option **(2)** is correct.
The Brahmins **denied them the upanayana**, causing the degradation.
The book appeared in **1946** (asked in **APPSC-GS 2019**).
xa: ⚠ Shudras = degraded **Kshatriyas**; Untouchables = "**broken men**" (The Untouchables, **1948**).
**The Buddha and His Dhamma** (**1957**) is the basis of **Navayana** — not about the Shudras.
**States and Minorities** came the next year, **1947**.

252.s: Which work of Ambedkar advanced the “broken men” theory regarding the origin of untouchability?
o: What Congress and Gandhi Have Done to the Untouchables
252.x: The Untouchables, published in 1948, dealt with the origin of untouchability and advanced the theory of “broken men.”
252.tq: Match the distinctive theory with the correct title.
xs: **The Untouchables** (**1948**) advanced the "**broken men**" theory of the origin of untouchability — option **(3)** is correct.
**Who Were the Shudras?** (**1946**) dealt with the origin of the **Shudras**, not untouchables.
**What Congress and Gandhi Have Done** (**1945**) attacked Congress; **The Buddha and His Dhamma** (**1957**) reread Buddhism.
xa: ⚠ Shudras = degraded **Kshatriyas**; Untouchables = "**broken men**".
**Thoughts on Linguistic States** — **1955**.
**Annihilation of Caste** — **1936**.

252.s:
Consider the following statements about Ambedkar's works:
1. Who Were the Shudras? was published in 1946.
2. The Untouchables was published in 1948.

**Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao** founded **Andhra Patrika**; **Konda Venkatappayya** co-founded **Krishna Patrika**; **Jonnavittula Gurunatham** wrote the **1911** series in **The Hindu**.
xa: His fast: **15 August to 20 September 1951**, **35 days**.
He led the **palm-tree cutting** campaign in the **Civil Disobedience Movement**.
⚠ **Swami Sitaram** = **35 days** (1951, ended by **Vinoba Bhave**); **Potti Sriramulu** = **58 days** (1952, died).

255.s: In which year was Nellore district renamed Sri Potti Sriramulu Nellore District?

xs: Nellore was renamed **"Sri Potti Sriramulu Nellore District"** in **2008** — so option **(3)** is correct.

xa: Sriramulu's ancestral village was **Gajula Dinne**, in Nellore district; he was born in Madras on **16 March 1901**.

Madras city's status to be settled within **three** years.

255.s: Which one of the following was NOT a demand associated with Swami Sitaram's 1951 fast?
o: Settlement of Madras city's status within three years
Immediate merger of Telangana with Andhra State
Formation of Andhra State by 2 October 1951
Neither Andhra nor Tamil interests controlling Madras city during the interim
255.x: The demands concerned the formation of Andhra State, settlement of Madras city's status, and an interim arrangement over the city. Merger of Telangana was not one of the stated demands.
255.tq: Find the option outside the specific demand set.
xs: **Immediate merger of Telangana** was **not** one of Swami Sitaram's demands — option **(2)** is the answer.
His demands: Andhra State by **2 October 1951**; Madras city's status settled within **three years**; **neither side** to control Madras meanwhile.
xa: Fast: **35 days**, **15 August to 20 September 1951**.
Ended on the appeal of **Vinoba Bhave**.
**Nehru criticised** the fast.

255.s: By what margin did Sanjiva Reddy defeat N.G. Ranga in the April 1951 APCC election?
255.x: Sanjiva Reddy won by five votes, after which Prakasam and Ranga formed the Kisan Mazdoor Praja Party.
xa: The split (**Prakasam and Ranga vs Pattabhi and Sanjiva Reddy**) **delayed the state**.
Swami Sitaram fasted **15 August to 20 September 1951**.
**Leadership splits** — **Circars vs Rayalaseema**, **Prakasam vs Pattabhi** — repeatedly slowed the movement.

255.s: To which community did Potti Sriramulu, born on 16 March 1901, belong?
255.x: Potti Sriramulu was born on 16 March 1901 in an Arya Vysya family. His ancestral village was Gajula Dinne in Nellore.
255.tq: Test a precise biographical detail carried in the heading and introductory account.
xs: Potti Sriramulu was born in an **Arya Vysya** family on **16 March 1901** — option **(4)** is correct.
Born in **Madras**; ancestral village **Gajula Dinne**, Nellore district.
xa: Some notes give **15 March**; older notes **15 March 1901 or 1911**.
125th birth anniversary: **16 March 2026** — **58-foot** "**Statue of Sacrifice**", **Sakhamuru Park, Amaravati**.
Titles: **Amarajeevi**; "**Andhra Martyra Martanda**".

255.s: The earlier fasts of Potti Sriramulu were primarily undertaken for which cause?
o: Demand for prohibition in Madras Presidency
255.x: His earlier fasts were undertaken for Harijan causes, including temple entry and Harijan welfare. The 1952 fast was his only fast for statehood.
255.tq: Separate the earlier Harijan fasts from the later statehood fast.
xs: His earlier fasts were for **Harijan causes** — including **temple entry** — option **(1)** is correct.
The **1952** fast was his **only fast for statehood**, so (3) is wrong for the earlier ones.
xa: **1946**: Nellore **Venugopala Swamy temple** — Harijan entry.
**1948**: **29 days**, **Wardha** — Harijan Day.
**1949**: **28 days** (January) — **Gandhi Smarak Din**.

255.s:
Assertion (A): Potti Sriramulu's constructive work included khadi, prohibition and Harijan uplift.
Reason (R): Potti Sriramulu was born in Nellore town, his ancestral village.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
255.x: A is true. R is false: he was born in Madras, and his ancestral village was Gajula Dinne in Nellore district.
xa: His work also covered **Hindu-Muslim unity**.
Earlier fasts were for **Harijan** causes; the **1952** fast was his only one for statehood.
**Potti Sreeramulu Telugu University** is in **Hyderabad**.

255.s: Potti Sriramulu's 29-day fast at Wardha in 1948 was associated with which combination?
o: Harijan Day and a grant of one crore rupees
Temple entry and the formation of Andhra State
Gandhi Smarak Din and the creation of Rayalaseema
Prohibition and the establishment of Andhra University
255.x: The Wardha fast in 1948 was associated with the observance of Harijan Day and a grant of one crore rupees. Madras also marked Harijan Welfare Day on the thirtieth of every month.
255.tq: Match the duration and place of a fast with its distinctive outcome.
xs: The **1948 Wardha** fast of **29 days** led Nehru to declare a **Harijan Day** and **₹1 crore** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Gandhi Smarak Din** came from the **1949** fast; **temple entry** from **1946**.
xa: **Madras** marks **Harijan Welfare Day** on the **30th** of every month (APP).
**1946**: **19 days** — temple-entry law for Harijans.

255.s: On 19 December 1952, from which areas did Jawaharlal Nehru announce that Andhra State would be formed?
o: Telangana and the coastal districts of Madras Presidency
The undisputed Telugu-speaking areas, excluding Madras city
All Telugu-speaking areas including Madras city
The entire Madras Presidency excluding Rayalaseema
255.x: Nehru announced that Andhra State would be formed from the undisputed Telugu areas, while Madras city would be excluded.
255.tq: Separate the accepted Telugu areas from the specifically excluded Madras city.
xs: On **19 December 1952**, Nehru told Parliament Andhra would be formed from the **undisputed Telugu areas, excluding Madras city** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Telangana** joined only in **1956** (Andhra Pradesh); Madras city was never included.
xa: ⚠ **19 December** is often misgiven as Sriramulu's death — he died on **15 December 1952**.
**25 March 1953**: Nehru — "**No question**" of Madras as the capital.
Andhra State formed **1 October 1953**.

255.s: After Potti Sriramulu's death, riots and police firing broke out. How many persons died in the firing?
255.x: Sriramulu's death was followed by riots and police firing in which seven people died; Nehru then announced Andhra State in Parliament on 19 December 1952.
xa: **Hartals, demonstrations, riots**; railway stations, post offices attacked.
MLA **Tenneti Viswanatham** and MLC **P. Sitaramayya** resigned.
Announcement in Parliament: **19 December 1952**.

255.s: Which one of the following was NOT one of the three conditions associated with Potti Sriramulu's demand?
o: Madras city should become a Chief Commissioner's State by agreement
The Andhra State should include the whole of the Madras Presidency
The Centre should announce the formation of Andhra State immediately
255.x: The three conditions concerned immediate announcement, unity among Andhra leaders and making Madras a Chief Commissioner's State by agreement. Inclusion of the entire Madras Presidency was not a condition.
255.tq: Find the option that goes beyond the precise three-condition formulation.
xs: Inclusion of **the whole Madras Presidency** was **not** a condition — option **(2)** is the answer.
The **three conditions**: Centre to **announce Andhra State at once**; Andhra leaders to **stay united**; **Madras city** → **Chief Commissioner's (C-class) state** by agreement.
xa: The C-class arrangement was also called a "**free state**".
On the **50th day**, Nehru offered Andhra **without Madras** if all parties agreed.
He died on the **58th day**.

255.s: Which of the following is a title associated with Potti Sriramulu?
255.x: Potti Sriramulu is known by the title Amarajeevi, meaning Immortal Martyr. He is also associated with the title “Andhra Martyra Martanda.”
255.tq: Test an exact honorific while using titles associated with other Andhra leaders as traps.
xs: Potti Sriramulu is known as **Amarajeevi** (Immortal Martyr) — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Andhra Ratna** = **Duggirala Gopalakrishnaiah**; **Desoddharaka** = **Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao**; **Andhra Kesari** = **Tanguturi Prakasam**.
xa: His other title: **"Andhra Martyra Martanda"**.
He got the title after dying on the **58th day** of his fast, **15 December 1952**.
⚠ **Andhra Kesari** is also the name of **Chilukuri Veerabhadra Rao's** paper (**1904**).
**Deshabhakta** = Konda Venkatappayya; **Swami Sitaram** = Gollapudi Sitarama Sastri.

255.s: Which anniversary of Potti Sriramulu was marked by the unveiling of his 58-foot 'Statue of Sacrifice' at Amaravati on 16 March 2026?
255.x: Born 16 March 1901, Sriramulu's 125th birth anniversary fell on 16 March 2026, when CM Chandrababu Naidu unveiled the statue.
xa: Memorial park of **6.80 acres**, about **₹150 crore**; **26 t** bronze + **42 t** iron.
Built by the **Amarajeevi Potti Sriramulu Memorial Trust**; phase 2 adds a **museum, auditorium** and skill centre.
The 58-foot height echoes his **58-day** fast of **1952**.

255.s: Potti Sriramulu sought the formation of a state comprising which of the following areas?
o: The Telugu-speaking districts along with the entire Madras city area
The Telugu-speaking districts of Coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema

xs: Sriramulu sought a state of the Telugu districts of **Coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Madras city** was left to **later negotiation** (APPSC 2019).
xa: His condition on Madras: a **Chief Commissioner's (C-class) state** by agreement.
Andhra State (**1953**): **Coastal Andhra (7)** + **Rayalaseema (4)** districts.
⚠ **Swami Sitaram's** 1951 demand: Madras's status settled within **three years**.

xs: **Amarajeevi** Potti Sriramulu died on **15 December 1952**, the **58th day** — option **(2)** is correct.
